“Dr. Waldron,” the woman said to me as I prepared to leave the exam room. “I have one more question. How can I lose this extra weight?”

I sighed inaudibly as I sat down to discuss the situation with her. Dealing with weight gain is not the sort of thing that is easy to tack onto the end of an office visit and there have been many lengthy books written on the subject.

Americans seem to struggle with this. They spend an average of 33 billion dollars on weight loss products every year and 65 percent of Americans are either overweight or obese.

The whole discussion is a challenging one. We want a quick fix—to take a pill or add in a fat-burning food or do a simple exercise that will melt the extra weight away simply and quickly. The reality is that while we gain weight quite easily, it is much more difficult to lose that same weight. Maintaining weight loss is harder yet.

In the Beginning

We don’t know much about life before the fall in Genesis 3. We do know that …God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good… –Genesis 1:31.

It is safe to assume that Adam and Eve did not struggle with their weight before sin entered the world. They were created perfectly which meant that they would not have struggled with metabolism issues. They also did not have the uncontrolled appetites for food that their descendants deal with today.

Two things happened with the fall of man in the Garden of Eden. First, humans started to have physical ailments—their bodies did not work as well as they did before. Adam and Eve were still able to live much longer lives than humans today, but metabolic diseases and other illnesses began to develop. The second thing that happened was that they began to have a sin nature.

Those two things have led to a lot of problems… Among them are metabolism and weight issues.

What the Bible Says About Food

Our bodies need to eat nutritious food—without eating they would deteriorate and eventually die. There is nothing better for a man, than that he should eat and drink, and that he should make his soul enjoy good in his labour. This also I saw, that it was from the hand of God –Ecclesiastes 2:24.

The Old Testament law was restrictive regarding what the Jewish people could eat. Under Kosher Law, the number of clean animals was far outweighed by the numbers of unclean animals. More than that, the book of Proverbs mentions several times that overeating is dangerous. Be not among winebibbers; among riotous eaters of flesh: For the drunkard and the glutton shall come to poverty: and drowsiness shall clothe a man with rags –Proverbs 23:20-21.

From the New Testament we find the early church no longer required Gentile Christians to follow Jewish laws regarding their diets. The Jerusalem council specifically required …that they abstain from pollutions of idols, and from fornication, and from things strangled, and from blood –Acts 15:20. Otherwise, it seems that they were free to eat whatever they wanted.

What did not change in the New Testament was the idea of self-control. The Fruit of the Spirit lists temperance as one of the things Christians should have and Paul made it clear that he was focused on controlling his desires, lest he become a castaway (see 1 Corinthians 9:27).

What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own? For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God’s –1 Corinthians 6:19-20.

Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you? If any man defile the temple of God, him shall God destroy; for the temple of God is holy, which temple ye are –1 Corinthians 3:16-17.

Scripture is clear that Christians should take care of their bodies, put their desires under the control of God, and avoid things that have anything to do with idolatry.

Reasons People Gain Weight

It is easy to break down reasons for weight gain into two big categories:

  1. problems with metabolism
  2. problems with excessive calories.

When we think about metabolic issues, these include things like thyroid problems and diabetes. These disorders affect the rate at which our bodies burn calories. One of the main ways we have to increase our metabolism is to increase our activity levels, particularly exercise that increases the heart rate—cardiovascular exercise.

Excess calories mainly come from overeating. It is important to remember that people eat for lots of reasons other than because they are hungry. People eat because they are bored, lonely, sad, and yes, sometimes because they are hungry. Some medications, particularly steroids, can increase appetite and negatively affect the metabolic rate.

We call the number of calories our bodies burn while at rest, the body’s metabolic rate. There are a couple of different formulas used to calculate our basal metabolic rates. They use height, weight, age, and gender to determine how many calories your body will burn in an average day. There are a few applications and websites that will do this calculation for you. https://www.active.com/fitness/calculators/bmr The important thing to know is that this is the number of calories you should consume to maintain your current body weight. Eat fewer calories than this number and you will tend to lose weight, take in more calories than this number and you will gain weight.

Is Weight Important?

From a medical standpoint, being overweight is associated with several different things. It tends to increase insulin resistance and it can lead to diabetes. It increases blood pressure. It can lead to obstructive sleep apnea, and it worsens arthritis in the back and legs.

Being overweight is not necessarily an indication of a spiritual problem and depending on a person’s genetics, it can be difficult to get it where it should be according to the charts. Even though most people feel much better when they are close to their ideal weight, Scripture does not indicate that there is a specific weight or body mass index (BMI) that Christians should not go over.

The important thing is that our lives are to be under the control of God if we have yielded ourselves, appetites, and all, to Him. We should try to be healthy in order that we can best participate in Kingdom building. More than that, we should attempt to set an example for others of a life that is yielded to God.

Myths About Weight Loss…

There are many things that people believe about weight loss. We will look at a list of things which people repeat. While there may be a grain of truth in them, they are not completely true and may discourage activities that can help a person who is struggling with his weight.

…Vigorous exercise is the only way to lose weight.

Many people believe that the reason that they can’t lose weight is because they can’t do enough exercise. They struggle with pain, arthritis, or some heart or lung condition that makes them unable to do vigorous athletic endeavors.

Maybe they know someone who took up running and lost a bunch of weight and that seems like the right way to do it. They just don’t feel able to take that path and feel hopeless about the whole endeavor.

Exercise is important. Most medical societies recommend that people exercise at least 150 minutes a week. While exercise does boost our metabolism and helps our hearts and lungs, it still may not change a person’s weight very much.

Most people burn between 200 and 300 calories with a half hour of exercise. While this may sound like a lot, a body must burn 3500 calories to lose one pound. In addition, most of us are hungrier after we exercise, and it is awfully easy to eat an extra 200 calories that basically negates whatever was burned during the exercise time.

…Carbohydrates make you gain weight.

Carbohydrate is the medical term for sugars. The calories we consume in our diets come from one of three sources: carbohydrates, fats, and proteins. Carbohydrates are present in desserts, but they are also present in many starchy foods like rice, corn, pasta, bread, and lots of other things.

There are several diets, like the Atkins Diet and the Keto Diet, that push those who follow them to cut out as many carbohydrates as possible. People often do lose weight on these sorts of diets. Unfortunately, these diets are difficult to maintain long term as they are quite restrictive.

The healthiest thing is to eat carbohydrates moderately and steer towards the healthier options. Using whole grains and more complex carbohydrates is important. A bowl of oatmeal may have a similar number of grams of carbohydrates as compared to a sugary breakfast cereal, but it will be broken down more slowly by our bodies and is easier for them to deal with.

…Starvation is the only way to lose weight.

Starvation does result in weight loss—there were no heavy-set people who came out of the concentration camps in World War II. This certainly is not the only way to lose weight, nor is it a healthy way to lose weight.

We know that when people starve for extended periods of time, they will begin to lose muscle mass, their bones will get weaker, and their metabolism will decrease. Most people who starve themselves will end up regaining all of the weight they lost within a few years and because their metabolism has been downgraded, in the long run it will be harder for them to keep weight off.

…You just need to eat ‘___’ fat burning food to lose weight!

I specifically left the food blank above because it seems that this is always changing. Maybe you’ve read that Greek yogurt, or cinnamon, or goji berry juice will help you lose weight. Studies indicate that there is no magic food that will melt fat away.

If these foods work, it is because you have replaced something unhealthy and rich in calories with something healthier. For example, if your normal breakfast consists of 5 strips of bacon, a glass of orange juice, 2 slices of toast, and two eggs and you replace that with a glass of water and a bowl of oatmeal, you will probably lose weight. It is not because the oatmeal is “burning fat,” but rather that it has significantly fewer calories than the breakfast you were eating before.

Some foods have almost no calories and probably take as much energy to eat and digest as humans get from them. Celery, iceberg lettuce, and mushrooms all fall into this category. The problem is that if you put peanut butter on the celery, salad dressing on the lettuce, and fry the mushrooms in butter or oil, then suddenly they aren’t the low-calorie foods they purport to be. We humans are very good at fixing low-cal foods so that they both taste better and are no longer low-calorie.

…Fat free and diet foods are the key to weight loss.

There are many foods and condiments on the market that have reduced fat and claim to be lower calorie than the normal versions of themselves. These often have a lot of different chemicals and sugar substitutes in them to get the taste and texture as similar to the regular versions as possible.

Sugar substitutes seem to be healthier than sugar when used moderately, but they also seem to encourage people to crave sweeter foods. Studies have linked artificial sweeteners with the onset of glucose intolerance—something that could lead to diabetes. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3095502/ Dieticians seem to think that of the various sugar substitutes, Stevia is the safest.

All in all, our goal should not be to try to eat all the same foods, just with fewer calories, but rather to eat a variety of healthy foods and moderate-sized portions. This is what will lead to a better metabolism and not simply getting reduced fat versions of our favorite foods.

…The solution is diet pills.

Over time I have seen many people take medications and supplements, both prescription and over the counter varieties, to try to help them lose weight. These medications and supplements are supposed to do a number of things—reduce appetite and increase the metabolic rate are several of these.

They often work in the short term. People lose quite a bit of weight in the first few weeks and think that they have conquered their struggles. The problem is that over time, they usually get used to whatever it is that they are taking, their appetite returns, and their metabolism goes back to normal.

While these sorts of solutions may give short-term help, being healthy in the long term, means figuring out a healthy eating plan and exercise schedule, then sticking with it long term. The goal should never be simply to “take off ten pounds,” but rather to be as healthy as possible.

We’ve covered a lot of things not to do and probably reading between the lines you can see some of the things that are helpful to do as well. A second part (Lord willing) will be coming with the next issue to discuss positive things that we can do to achieve a healthy weight.

With all of this, it is important to remember that our goal is not about achieving some sort of earthly beauty. The aim, rather, is to treat our body as the Temple of the Holy Ghost (1 Corinthians 6:19). I have heard this verse used to explain why we shouldn’t drink, smoke, or get tattoos, but we need to treat it with respect when it comes to eating and exercise, as well.

As we care for our bodies, we will be better able to meet the needs of the people around us and we will be prepared to meet whatever plan God has for our lives.

“월드런 박사님,” 진료실을 나서려던 제게 여성이 말했습니다. “질문이 하나 더 있어요. 어떻게 하면 이 군살을 뺄 수 있을까요?”

그녀와 이 문제를 의논하려고 자리에 앉으며 저는 소리 없이 한숨을 쉬었습니다. 체중 증가 문제를 진료가 끝날 무렵 간단히 덧붙여 다루는 것은 쉽지 않습니다. 이 주제에 관해서는 분량이 상당한 책도 많이 나와 있습니다.

미국인들은 이 문제로 고군분투하는 듯합니다. 미국인들은 체중 감량 제품에 매년 평균 330억 달러를 쓰며, 미국인의 65퍼센트는 과체중이거나 비만입니다.

이 문제는 전반적으로 다루기 어렵습니다. 우리는 알약을 먹거나 지방을 태우는 음식을 더하거나, 간단한 운동으로 군살을 손쉽고 빠르게 녹여 없애는 식의 빠른 해결책을 원합니다. 현실은 살이 찌기는 아주 쉽지만, 똑같은 체중을 빼기는 훨씬 어렵다는 것입니다. 감량한 체중을 유지하는 일은 더 어렵습니다.

태초에

창세기 3장에 나오는 타락 이전의 삶에 관해서는 우리가 아는 것이 많지 않습니다. 다만 하나님이 지으신 그 모든 것을 보시니 보시기에 심히 좋았더라… –창세기 1:31.

죄가 세상에 들어오기 전에 아담과 하와가 체중 문제로 고생하지 않았다고 보는 것이 타당합니다. 그들은 완전하게 창조되었으므로 신진대사 문제로 고생하지 않았을 것입니다. 또한 오늘날 그들의 후손들이 겪는 통제되지 않는 식욕도 없었습니다.

에덴동산에서 인간이 타락하면서 두 가지 일이 일어났습니다. 첫째, 인간은 신체적 질환을 겪기 시작했습니다. 몸은 이전처럼 잘 기능하지 않았습니다. 아담과 하와는 여전히 오늘날 인간보다 훨씬 오래 살 수 있었지만, 대사 질환과 다른 병들이 생기기 시작했습니다. 둘째, 그들은 죄성을 지니게 되었습니다.

이 두 가지는 많은 문제를 일으켰습니다… 그 가운데 신진대사와 체중 문제도 있습니다.

음식에 관해 성경이 말하는 것

우리 몸은 영양가 있는 음식을 먹어야 합니다. 먹지 않으면 몸은 쇠약해지고 결국 죽게 됩니다. 사람이 먹고 마시며 수고하는 가운데 자기 영혼으로 낙을 누리는 것보다 나은 것이 없나니, 내가 보니 이것도 하나님의 손에서 나는 것이로다 –전도서 2:24.

구약의 율법은 유대 민족이 먹을 수 있는 것을 제한했습니다. 정결법에 따라 먹을 수 있는 동물의 수보다 부정한 동물의 수가 훨씬 많았습니다. 그뿐 아니라 잠언은 과식이 위험하다고 여러 차례 언급합니다. 술을 즐기는 자들과 고기를 탐하는 자들과 함께하지 말라. 술 취하는 자와 탐식하는 자는 가난하게 되고, 잠자기를 좋아하는 자는 누더기를 입게 되리라 –잠언 23:20-21.

신약성경을 보면 초대 교회는 이방인 그리스도인들에게 유대인의 식사 규례를 더는 지키라고 요구하지 않았습니다. 예루살렘 공의회가 특별히 요구한 것은 …우상의 더러운 것과 음행과 목매어 죽인 것과 피를 멀리하라 –사도행전 15:20. 그 외에는 무엇이든 먹을 자유가 있었던 듯합니다.

신약에서 변하지 않은 것은 절제라는 생각이었습니다. 성령의 열매에는 그리스도인이 지녀야 할 것 가운데 절제가 포함되어 있으며, 바울은 자신이 버림받는 일이 없도록 자기 욕망을 다스리는 데 힘쓰고 있음을 분명히 했습니다(고린도전서 9:27 참조).

너희 몸은 너희가 하나님께로부터 받은 바 너희 안에 계신 성령의 전인 줄을 알지 못하느냐? 너희는 너희 자신의 것이 아니니, 값으로 산 것이 되었으니 그러므로 너희 몸으로 하나님께 영광을 돌리라. 너희의 몸과 영은 하나님의 것이니라 –고린도전서 6:19-20.

너희가 하나님의 성전인 것과 하나님의 영께서 너희 안에 거하시는 것을 알지 못하느냐? 누구든지 하나님의 성전을 더럽히면 하나님께서 그를 멸하시리니, 하나님의 성전은 거룩하니라. 너희가 바로 그 성전이니라 –고린도전서 3:16-17.

성경은 그리스도인들이 자기 몸을 돌보고, 자신의 욕망을 하나님의 통제 아래 두며, 우상 숭배와 관련된 것은 무엇이든 피해야 한다고 분명히 가르칩니다.

사람들이 살이 찌는 이유

체중 증가의 원인은 크게 두 가지로 나누어 생각할 수 있습니다.

  1. 신진대사 문제
  2. 과도한 열량 섭취 문제.

대사 문제에는 갑상선 질환이나 당뇨병 같은 것이 포함됩니다. 이러한 질환은 우리 몸이 열량을 태우는 속도에 영향을 줍니다. 신진대사를 높이는 주요 방법 가운데 하나는 활동량을 늘리는 것이며, 특히 심박수를 높이는 운동, 즉 심혈관 운동이 그렇습니다.

열량을 과도하게 섭취하는 것은 주로 과식에서 비롯됩니다. 사람들은 배고파서만 먹는 것이 아니라는 점을 기억하는 것이 중요합니다. 지루하거나 외롭거나 슬퍼서 먹기도 하고, 물론 때로는 배고파서 먹기도 합니다. 일부 약물, 특히 스테로이드는 식욕을 높이고 대사율에 부정적인 영향을 미칠 수 있습니다.

몸이 쉬고 있을 때 태우는 열량을 기초대사율이라고 합니다. 기초대사율을 계산하는 공식은 몇 가지가 있습니다. 키, 체중, 나이, 성별을 사용해 하루 평균 몸이 태울 열량을 계산합니다. 이 계산을 해주는 앱과 웹사이트도 몇 가지 있습니다. https://www.active.com/fitness/calculators/bmr 중요한 점은 이 수치가 현재 체중을 유지하기 위해 섭취해야 하는 열량이라는 것입니다. 이보다 적게 먹으면 대체로 체중이 줄고, 이보다 많이 섭취하면 체중이 늘게 됩니다.

체중은 중요한가?

의학적 관점에서 과체중은 여러 문제와 관련이 있습니다. 인슐린 저항성을 높이고 당뇨병으로 이어질 수 있습니다. 혈압을 높입니다. 폐쇄성 수면 무호흡증을 일으킬 수 있으며, 등과 다리의 관절염을 악화시킵니다.

과체중이라고 해서 반드시 영적인 문제가 있다는 뜻은 아닙니다. 유전적 요인에 따라서는 차트상 적정 체중에 도달하기 어려울 수 있습니다. 대부분의 사람은 이상적인 체중에 가까울 때 훨씬 기분이 좋지만, 그리스도인이 넘지 말아야 할 특정 체중이나 체질량지수(BMI)가 있다고 성경은 말하지 않습니다.

중요한 것은 우리 자신과 식욕을 비롯한 모든 것을 하나님께 맡겼다면, 우리의 삶이 하나님의 다스림을 받아야 한다는 점입니다. 하나님 나라를 세우는 일에 최대한 참여할 수 있도록 건강을 위해 노력해야 합니다. 그뿐 아니라 하나님께 삶을 맡긴 사람의 본을 다른 이들에게 보이도록 힘써야 합니다.

체중 감량에 관한 오해…

사람들이 체중 감량에 관해 믿는 것은 많습니다. 사람들이 되풀이하는 주장들을 살펴보겠습니다. 그 안에 어느 정도 진실이 있을 수는 있지만, 전적으로 사실은 아니며 체중 문제로 고생하는 사람에게 도움이 될 수 있는 활동을 단념하게 할 수도 있습니다.

…격렬한 운동만이 체중을 줄이는 유일한 방법이다.

많은 사람은 충분히 운동할 수 없어서 체중을 줄이지 못한다고 믿습니다. 통증이나 관절염, 또는 격렬한 운동을 할 수 없게 만드는 심장이나 폐 질환으로 고생하기도 합니다.

달리기를 시작해 살을 많이 뺀 사람을 알고 있어 그것이 올바른 방법이라고 생각할 수도 있습니다. 하지만 자신은 그 길을 갈 수 없다고 느끼며, 체중 감량 자체를 포기하고 싶어 합니다.

운동은 중요합니다. 대부분의 의학회는 일주일에 적어도 150분 운동할 것을 권합니다. 운동은 신진대사를 높이고 심장과 폐에 도움이 되지만, 사람의 체중을 크게 바꾸지 못할 수도 있습니다.

대부분의 사람은 30분 운동으로 200~300칼로리를 태웁니다. 많은 양처럼 들릴 수 있지만, 1파운드를 빼려면 몸이 3,500칼로리를 태워야 합니다. 게다가 운동을 하고 나면 대부분 더 배가 고파지며, 운동으로 태운 열량을 사실상 상쇄할 만큼 200칼로리를 더 먹기는 너무 쉽습니다.

…탄수화물을 먹으면 살이 찐다.

탄수화물은 당을 가리키는 의학 용어입니다. 우리가 식단에서 섭취하는 열량은 탄수화물, 지방, 단백질이라는 세 가지 공급원에서 나옵니다. 탄수화물은 디저트에 들어 있지만, 쌀, 옥수수, 파스타, 빵을 비롯한 많은 전분 식품에도 들어 있습니다.

앳킨스 다이어트와 케토 다이어트처럼 따르는 사람들에게 탄수화물을 최대한 줄이도록 하는 식단이 몇 가지 있습니다. 이런 식단을 하면 흔히 체중이 줄기도 합니다. 안타깝게도 상당히 제한적이어서 장기간 유지하기 어렵습니다.

가장 건강한 방법은 탄수화물을 적당히 먹고 더 건강한 선택지에 무게를 두는 것입니다. 통곡물과 복합 탄수화물을 사용하는 것이 중요합니다. 오트밀 한 그릇은 설탕이 많이 든 아침용 시리얼과 탄수화물 그램 수가 비슷할 수 있지만, 몸에서 더 천천히 분해되어 소화하기 쉽습니다.

…굶는 것만이 체중을 줄이는 유일한 방법이다.

굶으면 체중이 줄기는 합니다. 제2차 세계대전 중 강제수용소에서 나온 사람들 가운데 살찐 사람은 없었습니다. 그러나 굶는 것이 체중 감량의 유일한 방법은 아니며, 건강한 방법도 아닙니다.

사람들이 오랫동안 굶으면 근육량이 줄고 뼈가 약해지며 신진대사도 느려지기 시작한다는 것을 우리는 알고 있습니다. 스스로 굶는 사람 대부분은 몇 년 안에 감량한 체중을 모두 다시 얻게 됩니다. 신진대사까지 저하되었기 때문에 장기적으로는 체중을 유지하기가 더 어려워집니다.

…살을 빼려면 ‘___’ 지방 연소 식품만 먹으면 된다!

위 문장에서 음식 이름을 빈칸으로 남겨 둔 것은 그 음식이 늘 바뀌는 듯하기 때문입니다. 그릭 요거트나 계피, 구기자 주스가 체중 감량에 도움이 된다는 글을 읽었을 수도 있습니다. 연구에 따르면 지방을 녹여 없애는 마법의 음식은 없습니다.

이런 음식이 효과가 있다면, 그것은 건강에 좋지 않고 열량이 높은 것을 더 건강한 것으로 대체했기 때문입니다. 예를 들어 평소 아침으로 베이컨 다섯 조각, 오렌지 주스 한 잔, 토스트 두 쪽, 달걀 두 개를 먹다가 물 한 잔과 오트밀 한 그릇으로 바꾸면 아마 체중이 줄 것입니다. 오트밀이 “지방을 태워서”가 아니라, 이전에 먹던 아침 식사보다 열량이 훨씬 적기 때문입니다.

칼로리가 거의 없고, 먹고 소화하는 데 드는 에너지가 음식에서 얻는 에너지와 비슷할 법한 식품도 있습니다. 셀러리, 아이스버그 상추, 버섯이 모두 여기에 해당합니다. 문제는 셀러리에 땅콩버터를 바르고, 상추에 샐러드 드레싱을 뿌리고, 버섯을 버터나 기름에 볶으면 갑자기 더는 저칼로리 식품이 아니라는 것입니다. 우리 인간은 저칼로리 식품의 맛을 더 좋게 만들면서 더는 저칼로리가 아니게 만드는 데 아주 능숙합니다.

…무지방 식품과 다이어트 식품이 체중 감량의 핵심이다.

시중에는 지방을 줄였으며 원래 제품보다 칼로리가 낮다고 내세우는 식품과 양념이 많이 있습니다. 이런 제품에는 일반 제품과 가능한 한 비슷한 맛과 질감을 내기 위해 여러 화학물질과 설탕 대체제가 들어 있는 경우가 많습니다.

설탕 대체제는 적당히 사용하면 설탕보다 건강에 좋은 듯하지만, 사람들이 더 단 음식을 찾게 만들기도 하는 것 같습니다. 연구들은 인공 감미료와 포도당 불내증 발생 사이의 연관성을 밝혔는데, 이는 당뇨병으로 이어질 수 있는 문제입니다. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3095502/ 영양사들은 여러 설탕 대체제 가운데 스테비아가 가장 안전하다고 보는 듯합니다.

요컨대 목표는 칼로리만 줄여 똑같은 음식을 모두 먹으려는 것이 아니라, 여러 가지 건강한 음식을 적당한 양으로 먹는 것이어야 합니다. 그래야 신진대사가 더 좋아지며, 단지 좋아하는 음식의 저지방 제품을 고르는 것만으로는 충분하지 않습니다.

…해결책은 다이어트 약이다.

그동안 저는 체중 감량에 도움이 되기를 바라며 처방약과 일반의약품을 비롯한 여러 약과 보충제를 복용하는 사람들을 많이 보았습니다. 이런 약과 보충제는 식욕을 줄이고 대사율을 높이는 등 여러 가지 효과를 내도록 만들어졌습니다.

단기적으로는 효과가 있는 경우가 많습니다. 처음 몇 주 동안 체중이 꽤 줄어들면 어려움을 이겨냈다고 생각합니다. 문제는 시간이 흐르면 대개 복용 중인 것에 익숙해져 식욕이 돌아오고 신진대사도 정상으로 돌아간다는 것입니다.

이런 방법이 단기적인 도움을 줄 수는 있지만, 장기적으로 건강하려면 건강한 식사 계획과 운동 일정을 세우고 그것을 오랫동안 지켜야 합니다. 목표는 단지 “10파운드를 빼는 것”이 아니라, 가능한 한 건강해지는 것이어야 합니다.

하지 말아야 할 일을 많이 다뤘지만, 행간을 읽으면 도움이 되는 일도 몇 가지 짐작할 수 있을 것입니다. (주님께서 허락하신다면) 다음 호에 후속편을 실어 건강한 체중을 이루기 위해 할 수 있는 긍정적인 일들을 다루겠습니다.

이 모든 점에서 우리의 목표가 세상적인 미를 이루는 것이 아님을 기억하는 것이 중요합니다. 오히려 성령의 전인 우리 몸을 소중히 대하는 것이 목표입니다(고린도전서 6:19). 저는 이 구절이 술을 마시거나 담배를 피우거나 문신을 해서는 안 되는 이유를 설명하는 데 쓰이는 것을 들었지만, 식사와 운동에 관해서도 이 말씀을 존중해야 합니다.

우리 몸을 돌보면 주변 사람들의 필요를 더 잘 채울 수 있고, 하나님께서 우리 삶에 두신 어떤 계획에도 준비된 사람이 될 것입니다.

Lord, this pain seems unbearable.
Things once loved now must die.
So many hearts are bleeding.
No one has kept a dry eye.

We’ve wept and writhed and prayed
Asking, Lord, this cup to avoid.
We tried what we thought might change it,
But all attempts seemed to return to us void.

Father, we’ve cried out for mercy,
All would have escaped this pain.
But Lord, You bade us go through it;
Your hand in it all You’ve made plain.

Our minds seem to spin as we ponder,
Just exactly what You’re trying to do.
Yet we know that no matter our feelings,
There’s a reason we this storm must go through.

So Father, we bow at Your feet now,
Acknowledging Your omnipotent might.
We cannot discern all the details,
But we trust in the end, all will be right.

Help us, Father, to be broken,
Releasing our all up to You.
Our rights, dreams, ambitions, and possessions,
Making everything open to Your view.

Grow in us, Lord, a humility,
Quiet, yet deep and true.
It’s a jewel that nothing but trials can teach.
Lord, through this, make us more like You!

May our eyes be set on You, Father,
Not on this o’erwhelming gale.
For You have gone through these deep waters,
Nothing but what You plan will prevail.

Obedient even unto death, Lord,
No matter how high the cost may seem.
Give us a vision of the heavenly treasure,
For which no earthly price can exceed.

–By Adrianna H. Fanton

Bwana, maumivu haya yanaonekana hayawezi kuvumilika.
Vitu tulivyovipenda zamani sasa lazima vife.
Mioyo mingi sana inaumizwa.
Hakuna aliyebaki bila machozi.

Tumelia, tumeteseka na kuomba
Tukikuomba, Bwana, uliondoe kikombe hiki.
Tulijaribu tulichodhani kingeweza kubadili hali,
Lakini juhudi zote zilionekana kutuacha mikono mitupu.

Baba, tumekulilia utuhurumie,
Kila mtu angeepuka maumivu haya.
Lakini, Bwana, ulituagiza tupitie haya;
Umeweka wazi mkono wako katika yote haya.

Akili zetu zinaonekana kuzunguka tunapotafakari,
Hasa ni nini unachojaribu kufanya.
Hata hivyo, tunajua kwamba hata tuhisi vipi,
Kuna sababu inayotufanya tupitie dhoruba hii.

Basi, Baba, sasa tunainama miguuni pako,
Tukikiri uwezo wako mkuu usio na mipaka.
Hatuwezi kutambua kila jambo kwa undani,
Lakini tunaamini kwamba mwishowe, yote yatakuwa sawa.

Utusaidie, Baba, kujinyenyekeza,
Tukikukabidhi vyote tulivyo navyo.
Haki zetu, ndoto, matarajio na mali zetu,
Tukiyaweka yote wazi mbele zako.

Kuza ndani yetu, Bwana, unyenyekevu,
Wa utulivu, lakini wa kina na wa kweli.
Ni kito ambacho majaribu pekee yanaweza kufundisha.
Bwana, kupitia haya, utufanye tufanane nawe zaidi!

Macho yetu yaelekezwe kwako, Baba,
Si kwenye dhoruba hii kali inayotuzidi.
Kwa maana umepitia maji haya ya kina,
Hakuna kitakachoshinda isipokuwa kile ulichopanga.

Mtiifu hata kufa, Bwana,
Haidhuru gharama ionekane kubwa kiasi gani.
Tupe maono ya hazina ya mbinguni,
Ambayo hakuna bei ya duniani inayoweza kuizidi.

–Na Adrianna H. Fanton

We all have a story. Some feel like Job sometimes. Some have lost parents, or partners, or children, or siblings, or friends. Some suffer from severe illness. Some will never recover from their illnesses. Our loved ones might have a terminal illness. Maybe a husband or parent is abusive or unfaithful. Like Job, our friends might have turned against us. Maybe there are problems in the church that seem impossible to fix. It could be something like a colicky baby, or a hyper child. Maybe we just have a cold and are feeling like everything is going wrong. The list is endless. We can relate to the words of this song.

Till the Storm Passes By

In the dark of the midnight have I oft hid my face,
While the storm howls above me, and there’s no hiding place.
‘Mid the crash of the thunder, Precious Lord, hear my cry,
Keep me safe till the storm passes by.

refrain:

Till the storm passes over, till the thunder sounds no more,
Till the clouds roll forever from the sky;
Hold me fast, let me stand in the hollow of Thy hand,
Keep me safe till the storm passes by.

Many times Satan whispered, “There is no need to try,
For there’s no end of sorrow, there’s no hope by and by”
But I know Thou art with me, and tomorrow I’ll rise
Where the storms never darken the skies.

When the long night has ended and the storms come no more,
Let me stand in Thy presence on the bright peaceful shore;
In that land where the tempest, never comes, Lord, may I
Dwell with Thee when the storm passes by.

–by Mosie Lister

When I was a little girl, I thought the author was referring to thunderstorms. I was afraid of thunderstorms. Now I understand that he was referring to the storms of life we go through. On July 14, 2013, I suddenly ended up in the hospital with a life-threatening heart attack caused by a spontaneous coronary artery dissection. What a shock for a 40-year-old mother. The storm was howling, and the thunder was crashing. There was no hiding place from the danger, for it was within me. I only had one heart and it could not be trusted. What if it happens again? Would I die? Then my children would be motherless.

This song was one I’d pray in the dark of the midnight when I couldn’t sleep, and fear threatened to overwhelm me. The Lord’s presence was very real to me. I came through this storm with a greater awareness of how God reveals Himself to us in a deeper way when we are going through hard times. We must choose to yield ourselves completely to Him, and say, “Not my will, but Thine be done.”

When the disciples were out on the sea in the storm, Jesus was with them. He is with us too. We can trust Him. Nothing will happen that is not according to His will. We do not always understand why things happen, but that’s okay. An old preacher used to quote:

“Not now, but in the coming years,
It may be in the better land
We’ll read the meaning of our tears,
And there, sometime, we’ll understand.”

It is so important that we accept what God allows in our lives. Accepting does not mean we don’t do anything about it. We will go to the doctor if necessary. We will reach out to others for comfort and council. We will still have all kinds of feelings, but we should have peace. We can’t wallow in self-pity and have a “poor me” attitude. And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose –Romans 8:28. I believe that. I can’t always see the good, but God does.

Life is hard sometimes, but the song tells about the time when the long night has ended, and the storms come no more. Dear sisters, let’s remain faithful and lean hard on the Lord through the storms of life.

And I saw a new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth were passed away; and there was no more sea. And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God. And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away. Revelation 21:1-4.

Wir alle haben eine Geschichte. Manchmal fühlen sich manche von uns wie Hiob. Einige haben Eltern, Partner, Kinder, Geschwister oder Freunde verloren. Manche leiden an einer schweren Krankheit. Manche werden sich nie von ihrer Krankheit erholen. Unsere Lieben könnten unheilbar krank sein. Vielleicht ist ein Ehemann oder ein Elternteil misshandelnd oder untreu. Wie Hiob könnten sich unsere Freunde gegen uns gewandt haben. Vielleicht gibt es Probleme in der Gemeinde, die unlösbar scheinen. Es könnte etwas sein wie ein Baby mit Koliken oder ein überaus aktives Kind. Vielleicht haben wir auch nur eine Erkältung und das Gefühl, dass alles schiefläuft. Die Liste ist endlos. Wir können die Worte dieses Liedes nachempfinden.

Bis der Sturm vorüberzieht

In der dunklen Mitternacht verbarg ich oft mein Gesicht,
während der Sturm über mir tobt und es keinen Zufluchtsort gibt.
Mitten im Donnergrollen, lieber Herr, hör mein Rufen,
bewahre mich, bis der Sturm vorüberzieht.

Refrain:

Bis der Sturm vorüberzieht, bis der Donner nicht mehr grollt,
bis die Wolken für immer vom Himmel verschwinden;
halte mich fest, lass mich in der Höhlung deiner Hand stehen,
bewahre mich, bis der Sturm vorüberzieht.

Oft flüsterte Satan: „Es lohnt sich nicht, es zu versuchen,
denn das Leid nimmt kein Ende, und bald gibt es keine Hoffnung mehr.“
Doch ich weiß, du bist bei mir, und morgen werde ich aufstehen
an dem Ort, wo die Stürme niemals den Himmel verdunkeln.

Wenn die lange Nacht zu Ende ist und die Stürme nicht mehr kommen,
lass mich in deiner Gegenwart am hellen, friedlichen Ufer stehen;
in jenem Land, in das der Sturm niemals kommt, Herr, lass mich
bei dir wohnen, wenn der Sturm vorüberzieht.

– von Mosie Lister

Als kleines Mädchen dachte ich, der Verfasser meinte Gewitter. Ich hatte Angst vor Gewittern. Heute verstehe ich, dass er die Stürme des Lebens meinte, die wir durchmachen. Am 14. Juli 2013 landete ich plötzlich im Krankenhaus mit einem lebensbedrohlichen Herzinfarkt, verursacht durch eine spontane Dissektion einer Koronararterie. Was für ein Schock für eine 40-jährige Mutter. Der Sturm tobte, und der Donner krachte. Vor der Gefahr gab es kein Versteck, denn sie war in mir. Ich hatte nur ein Herz, und auf dieses war kein Verlass. Was, wenn es wieder passiert? Würde ich sterben? Dann wären meine Kinder ohne Mutter.

Dieses Lied betete ich in der dunklen Mitternacht, wenn ich nicht schlafen konnte und die Angst mich zu überwältigen drohte. Die Gegenwart des Herrn war für mich ganz real. Ich kam durch diesen Sturm und gewann ein größeres Bewusstsein dafür, wie Gott sich uns auf tiefere Weise offenbart, wenn wir schwere Zeiten durchmachen. Wir müssen uns ganz ihm hingeben und sagen: „Nicht mein Wille, sondern deiner geschehe.“

Als die Jünger im Sturm auf dem Meer waren, war Jesus bei ihnen. Auch bei uns ist er. Wir können ihm vertrauen. Nichts wird geschehen, was nicht seinem Willen entspricht. Wir verstehen nicht immer, warum Dinge geschehen, aber das ist in Ordnung. Ein alter Prediger pflegte zu zitieren:

„Nicht jetzt, doch in den kommenden Jahren,
vielleicht im besseren Land,
werden wir den Sinn unsrer Tränen erkennen,
und irgendwann dort verstehen.“

Es ist so wichtig, dass wir annehmen, was Gott in unserem Leben zulässt. Annehmen bedeutet nicht, dass wir nichts dagegen unternehmen. Wenn nötig, gehen wir zum Arzt. Wir wenden uns an andere, um Trost und Rat zu finden. Wir werden weiterhin alle möglichen Gefühle haben, doch wir sollten Frieden haben. Wir dürfen nicht in Selbstmitleid schwelgen und eine „Ich Arme“-Haltung einnehmen. Und wir wissen, dass denen, die Gott lieben, alle Dinge zum Guten dienen, denen, die nach seinem Vorsatz berufen sind – Römer 8:28. Das glaube ich. Ich kann das Gute nicht immer erkennen, aber Gott erkennt es.

Das Leben ist manchmal schwer, aber das Lied erzählt von der Zeit, wenn die lange Nacht zu Ende ist und die Stürme nicht mehr kommen. Liebe Schwestern, lasst uns treu bleiben und uns in den Stürmen des Lebens fest auf den Herrn stützen.

Und ich sah einen neuen Himmel und eine neue Erde; denn der erste Himmel und die erste Erde waren vergangen, und das Meer war nicht mehr. Und ich, Johannes, sah die heilige Stadt, das neue Jerusalem, von Gott aus dem Himmel herabkommen, bereit wie eine für ihren Mann geschmückte Braut. Und ich hörte eine laute Stimme aus dem Himmel sagen: Siehe, die Wohnung Gottes ist bei den Menschen, und er wird bei ihnen wohnen, und sie werden sein Volk sein, und Gott selbst wird bei ihnen sein und ihr Gott sein. Und Gott wird alle Tränen von ihren Augen abwischen, und der Tod wird nicht mehr sein, auch weder Trauer noch Geschrei noch Schmerz wird mehr sein; denn das Frühere ist vergangen. Offenbarung 21:1-4.

The night was still, the air was drear.

A man walked alone; his direction unclear.

A battle raged within his troubled soul.

He was at the crossroads, all his life as a whole.

He believed in God, or at least so he thought.

He obeyed what he knew—all that he’d been taught.

But something’s not right, there’s something I lack.

I’ve lived like most others, as my life plays back.

But I go to church! I sing and I pray!

I even helped the neighbor, just the other day!

He fought with his mind, justifying the wrong.

It was God that was working, He seemed quite strong.

The fact of the matter, it’s confidence I lack.

I believe in myself, not the God from way back.

God wants to show strong, in my life every day.

He wants me to be proved; He’s the Life and the Way.

There’s no better One, in Whom to put all your trust;

Than the almighty God. For all men it’s a must!

–by Barry Grant

A noite era silenciosa, o ar sombrio.

Um homem caminhava sozinho; sem saber para onde ir.

Uma batalha assolava sua alma conturbada.

Estava numa encruzilhada, diante de toda a sua vida.

Acreditava em Deus, ou ao menos era o que pensava.

Obedecia ao que sabia — a tudo o que lhe ensinaram.

Mas algo não está certo, há algo que me falta.

Tenho vivido como a maioria, ao rever minha vida.

Era Deus quem agia; Ele parecia bem forte.

O fato é que me falta confiança.

Creio em mim mesmo, não no Deus de outrora.

Deus quer mostrar-se poderoso, todos os dias em minha vida.

Ele quer que eu seja provado; Ele é a Vida e o Caminho.

Não há ninguém melhor em quem depositar toda a confiança;

do que no Deus Todo-Poderoso. Para todos os homens, isso é indispensável!

–por Barry Grant

There He was, the King Himself, standing before Pilate, awaiting His death sentence. A large crowd had gathered outside. There was no mistaking it, these people were angry. They wanted this man, Jesus of Nazareth, dead. “Crucify him! Crucify him!” was all that could be heard. This man must have done something terrible. But who were these people that were so angry at the Son of God? Maybe they were rapists, thieves, and murderers. Possibly they were the local liars, drunks, or some other evildoers. Actually, they were the religious people, the church goers, the ones claiming to be God’s people.

Ever since that infamous day, history has repeated itself. People claiming to be God’s people have seen those who love Jesus and try to follow His teachings as their enemies and have persecuted them any way they could. From the Jews, to the Roman Catholics, to the Protestants, the mainstream church of the day has always been the enemy of those who try to govern their everyday lives by the simple clarity of the Scriptures.

I am concerned that we have signed a deal with the mainstream church of our day—a deal for peace at all costs.

Any Scripture that teaches rebuke, reproof, or correction is considered out-of-date and is not allowed to be used to help shape the faith and practice of today’s Christian. Many individuals, church leaders, and even whole churches have begun to believe that love and acceptance alone is a better way to point others to Christ. Those who would raise a voice of warning are seen to be critical and stirring unrest, so they are quickly silenced.

As we search the Scriptures, we see that Jesus, then the disciples, then the early church, had nothing good to say or think about the false church.

While out witnessing or talking to people about the Lord, I’m amazed at the backlash from the mainstream church of our day. Mainly, the Protestant church.

A simple man walked up to a Christian concert holding a sign reading ‘Jesus saves from sin’. Without him ever saying a word, he was attacked. “Quit judging us!” “You don’t know our hearts!” “You’re a disgrace!” “Bigot!” The man slowly walked away.

Many times, the people who get angry when discussions involving God come up are actually folks who claim to know Jesus. The sinners seem to let the message penetrate their hearts. If you were to go to an intersection in a city and simply hold a sign proclaiming something about Christ, you would soon see that this is true.

As I was standing in line at a fast-food restaurant, I noticed that the young man preparing my sandwich had many interesting tattoos. Some were of tombstones, skulls, and other graphic designs. I calmly asked him if he could explain what the tattoos meant to him. He began going into detail about each one. I then asked the young man if he knew Jesus. He got sober and explained that he wanted to believe in God but couldn’t. I quoted a few Bible verses and told him that God was waiting for him. I noticed that God’s Word was having a great effect on the young man.

Meanwhile, I also noticed that the lady behind me was beginning to get frustrated. Finally, she interrupted our conversation and told the man, “Jesus loves you just the way you are. You don’t have to change for this man.” This lady later told me what church she went to and how judgmental she thought that I had acted. I was amazed. I had only told the young man about the Savior!

Before I left the restaurant, I walked back over to the young man to bid him farewell. As I approached, he looked up with tears in his eyes. “Thank you”, he said “I can tell that you truly care about me. I will go home and really think about what you said.”

That night, as I reflected on the day’s events, I wondered why that professing Christian woman had such a problem with my interaction with the young man. Why did she get so angry? I felt like the Lord gave me an answer: No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon –Matthew 6:24.

She was a nice young lady. And, yes, she professed that she was a Christian, but she clearly did not live a life that was in obedience to God’s Word. Rather, outside of going to church, one would not be able to tell at all that she was a follower of Christ. I’m sure if I would have met her at the park, we could have had a nice chat. I’m sure she would have been courteous and polite. I’m sure she would have presented herself as a good citizen and nice person. But when it came to being excited about Jesus, sharing the gospel, and talking about God’s Word, her true colors came out.

Am I saying that a person must be an Anabaptist to make it to heaven? Absolutely not, but I am saying we must obey the Bible and follow Christ to make it to heaven. Most professing Christians are super nice and seem godly, until you start talking about God.

Since when has the definition of a Christian been ‘a nice person’, or ‘a good citizen’? Is that all there is to it anymore—simply do what you want, find a fun church that doesn’t require anything from you, get a good job, get married, have a few children and just like that you’re a ‘Christian’? God help us!

When He was having a discussion with a group of people about whether or not they were true followers of God, Jesus said, …If ye were Abraham’s children, ye would do the works of Abraham. But now ye seek to kill me, a man that hath told you the truth … Ye do the deeds of your father … Ye are of your father the devil… –John 8:39-44.

Has the true church slipped so far as to not be able to call things as they are? God’s Word gives us clear understanding on the matter: Proving what is acceptable unto the Lord. And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather reprove them. For it is a shame even to speak of those things which are done of them in secret. But all things that are reproved are made manifest by the light: for whatsoever doth make manifest is light –Ephesians 5:10-13.

Jesus says Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid –Matthew 5:14. Do we expose sin and heresy in the same way that light exposes darkness? Or are we too attached to a comfortable life with no enemies? We do not need to be scared of the world, or of the false church, because we know that we have what they need! For years the mainstream churches have been getting farther and farther away from the truth of God’s Word. Are we afraid to recognize this? Are we afraid to separate ourselves from this? Will we stand up against it like the early church did?

There is a reason why the Protestant reformer, Martin Luther, died hating the Anabaptist people—because they rejected his interpretation of the Scriptures. The Anabaptist people were not respecters of people. Rather their only respect was for God and His Word, and that without compromise. It was for this that they were persecuted. It would have been much easier for those godly young men to just be quiet and try to get along with the Catholics and Protestants, but they refused and both groups sought to extinguish them. Still, they lived on, trusting only in their God. When we joined the church of Jesus Christ didn’t we promise to continue fighting the same fight—the same fight that Jesus fought; the same fight the early church fought—the fight against the false church? Or have we agreed to get along, for the sake of peace? After all isn’t it better for business, for friendships, and for reputation?! God forbid!

We can live a life that seems to be without sin, but still be living in disobedience. The Bible calls us to action! We are called to be lights, to be witnesses, to pursue godliness, and to live uprightly, not just to put on a good show. I believe this is what has become popular in our day. Lying, cheating, stealing, and killing are attributes that even the world rejects. It’s the ‘in thing’ to be respectable, to make a nice living, and to be upstanding citizens. But is this the life of a born-again believer? Should we fit in with the American dream? Should the only thing that’s different between us and the Protestant church be a head covering? I think we should prayerfully consider this move, the move to join hands with the mainstream church.

I personally know many Protestant Christians. I’m not trying to say they are bad people; many are good folks. But that is not what we are talking about. I believe we need to draw a line and slow down this draw to join them in any compromising manner. Let’s look at just a few of the differences between the Protestants and Anabaptists.

War

Can you believe in war, killing your enemies, and still be a New Testament Christian? Most Protestants are supporters of fighting for our freedoms and our rights. Many will go as far as calling Anabaptist people cowards for not fighting.

Years ago, a group of professing Christians gathered around the biggest bomb ever made. This bomb was about to be sent into a foreign land to destroy an entire city; this bomb was meant to kill everything in its path. Men, women, and children alike would perish because of this bomb; that was the plan. As this group was gathered around this bomb they began to pray, they asked God’s blessing on this bombing mission. They then thanked Him for its success—killing nearly one quarter of a million souls.

Jesus calls us to love our enemies. This topic clearly separated the churches during the various wars. Most of the ‘Christian’ churches in the world supported the war effort of their country. The Anabaptists would not, and they were sorely persecuted for it. So, can we be a Christian and continue to support war? If we support war, where will it stop? Will we also prepare to defend ourselves and our families against violence and lawlessness? The American church calls ‘defending ourselves’, our families, and our country, heroism or bravery; the Bible calls it.

Entertainment

It seems that most Christians in America have no problem watching as many ballgames and sports events as they desire. Movies and television are found in nearly every home. Going to the beach, casinos, and festivals are commonplace. Spending thousands on big hunting trips and expensive vacations is completed without a second thought. To be honest, there really are no limits to what the Christian in America can do, as long as it seems right to them. Jesus tells us multiple times to deny ourselves. It seems that we look for any loophole possible to indulge in all the self-gratifying activities we want! It’s no wonder the church is struggling with pornography and many other sins of the flesh. When we learn how to deny ourselves, pick up the cross, and follow Jesus, then we will start to see a clear, distinct, and large separation between us and the mainstream church of our day.

Non-conformity

It is common to conform to one’s surroundings. This is one reason we don’t send our children to public schools. Jesus is also very clear that we need to come out from among them and be separate, to say “No” to evil communication and the ways of this world, and to not be afraid of identifying ourselves with the people of God. It almost seems that dress is really the only thing that separates many of us, and that is changing also.

Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world. If any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him. For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world –1 John 2:15-16. Where are the people that hate the world? Where are the people that want to be as separated as possible? Where are the people that are not afraid to be laughed at? Where are the people that are not afraid to be different? Oh, where are God’s people?! If history repeats itself, there will soon be no difference between the church and the world. Oh, where are the men?!

I’ve heard many Anabaptist people say they can’t say that those in the worldly church are not Christians; they just don’t want to go in that direction. Is that truthful? Is that the message we want to send to our youth, and to our children? I don’t believe so. The Bible says that few will make it. If we pass on to our children that the Protestant church is also ok, and that they just do things differently, we are destroying everything that Jesus preached. We are saying that we do what we do, not because the Bible says, but rather we decide what we do based on our circumstances and what others around us think! No wonder our children are more interested in the modern church of today than ever before—there’s no line drawn!

There was a modern church that caught my attention. They seemed to be on fire for the Lord! The pastor preached as a dying man. They were very interested in reaching the lost. But there were so many Bible teachings that they simply ignored! I finally took it to the Lord. “What is going on here God!” It was as if God told me to ‘just wait’.

Soon after that, the pastor was released from his position because he was having an affair. Then it all became clear to me—you can have a nice church, you can preach a good message, and you can help the poor, but if you’re not willing to obey ALL of the New Testament teachings, you’re not a true Christian, and you will not find victory. It’s easy to take Christianity so far, but it is not easy to sell all that you have, put your all on the altar, and follow your Master. I know this is bold, but it is the truth of God’s Word.

I was speaking to a young lady in a Protestant setting, who wanted to give her life to the Lord. She was ready to do what it took, or so she said. I asked her if she was ready to suffer for Jesus, if she was ready to separate herself from her old friends, if she was ready to be hated by the world, and ready to be different. I asked her if she was willing to change how she looked. It didn’t take long before she shockingly responded with an emphatic “No!” “I want to start going to church, but not all that other stuff.” I later noticed her with her friends pointing and laughing at me. Being cool does not define a true Christian but being rejected for the sake of the Gospel does.

This is a tough article to write. It’s not a popular message and not very encouraging. But I think it’s a message we must consider today, not only for our sake, but for our children’s sake, and that of the church of tomorrow. We must draw clear lines of separation, without any compromise. We must honestly evaluate the modern church of our day with the clear teachings of the New Testament. We must call sin, sin. We must call disobedience, sin. We must call compromise, sin. We must once again choose to suffer with the true people of God. This does not mean that we shun people or act distasteful towards them, but with love in our hearts, and a message on our lips, we point the masses to Christ!

For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek –Romans 1:16.

Der sto han, kongen selv, foran Pilatus og ventet på dødsdommen. En stor folkemengde hadde samlet seg utenfor. Det var ingen tvil om det: Disse menneskene var sinte. De ville ha denne mannen, Jesus fra Nasaret, drept. «Korsfest ham! Korsfest ham!» var alt som kunne høres. Denne mannen måtte ha gjort noe forferdelig. Men hvem var disse menneskene som var så sinte på Guds Sønn? Kanskje var de voldtektsmenn, tyver og mordere. Kanskje var de lokale løgnere, fylliker eller andre ugjerningsmenn. Faktisk var de religiøse mennesker, kirkegjengere, de som hevdet at de var Guds folk.

Helt siden den beryktede dagen har historien gjentatt seg. Mennesker som hevder at de er Guds folk, har sett dem som elsker Jesus og prøver å følge hans lære, som fiender, og har forfulgt dem på alle måter de kunne. Fra jødene til romersk-katolikkene og protestantene har den etablerte kirken til enhver tid alltid vært fienden til dem som prøver å styre hverdagslivet sitt etter Skriftens enkle og klare ord.

Jeg er bekymret for at vi har inngått en avtale med vår tids etablerte kirke – en avtale om fred for enhver pris.

Ethvert skriftsted som lærer oss å irettesette, formane eller korrigere, blir ansett som utdatert og får ikke brukes til å forme troen og praksisen til kristne i dag. Mange enkeltpersoner, kirkeledere og til og med hele kirker har begynt å tro at kjærlighet og aksept alene er en bedre måte å vise andre til Kristus på. De som vil heve en advarende røst, blir sett på som kritiske og som noen som skaper uro, og blir derfor raskt brakt til taushet.

Når vi gransker Skriftene, ser vi at Jesus, deretter disiplene og så den tidlige kirken ikke hadde noe godt å si eller mene om den falske kirken.

Når jeg er ute og vitner eller snakker med folk om Herren, blir jeg forbløffet over motreaksjonene fra vår tids etablerte kirke. Først og fremst fra protestantiske kirker.

En enkel mann gikk bort til en kristen konsert med et skilt der det sto «Jesus frelser fra synd». Uten at han hadde sagt et eneste ord, ble han angrepet. «Slutt å dømme oss!» «Du kjenner ikke hjertene våre!» «Du er en skam!» «Fanatiker!» Mannen gikk langsomt bort.

Ofte er det faktisk folk som hevder at de kjenner Jesus, som blir sinte når samtaler om Gud kommer opp. Det virker som om budskapet trenger inn i hjertene til synderne. Hvis du gikk til et veikryss i en by og bare holdt opp et skilt som forkynte noe om Kristus, ville du snart se at dette stemmer.

Mens jeg sto i kø på en hurtigmatrestaurant, la jeg merke til at den unge mannen som laget sandwichen min, hadde mange interessante tatoveringer. Noen forestilte gravsteiner, hodeskaller og andre grafiske motiver. Jeg spurte ham rolig om han kunne forklare hva tatoveringene betydde for ham. Han begynte å fortelle detaljert om hver enkelt. Så spurte jeg den unge mannen om han kjente Jesus. Han ble alvorlig og forklarte at han ønsket å tro på Gud, men ikke kunne. Jeg siterte noen bibelvers og fortalte ham at Gud ventet på ham. Jeg merket at Guds ord gjorde sterkt inntrykk på den unge mannen.

Samtidig la jeg også merke til at kvinnen bak meg begynte å bli utålmodig. Til slutt avbrøt hun samtalen vår og sa til mannen: «Jesus elsker deg akkurat slik du er. Du trenger ikke å forandre deg for denne mannen.» Senere fortalte kvinnen meg hvilken kirke hun gikk i, og hvor dømmende hun syntes jeg hadde oppført meg. Jeg ble forbløffet. Jeg hadde bare fortalt den unge mannen om Frelseren!

Før jeg dro fra restauranten, gikk jeg bort til den unge mannen igjen for å ta farvel. Da jeg nærmet meg, så han opp med tårer i øynene. «Takk», sa han. «Jeg kan se at du virkelig bryr deg om meg. Jeg skal dra hjem og virkelig tenke over det du sa.»

Den kvelden, mens jeg tenkte tilbake på dagens hendelser, undret jeg meg over hvorfor denne kvinnen, som bekjente seg som kristen, hadde så store problemer med samtalen min med den unge mannen. Hvorfor ble hun så sint? Jeg følte at Herren ga meg et svar: Ingen kan tjene to herrer. For enten vil han hate den ene og elske den andre, eller holde seg til den ene og forakte den andre. Dere kan ikke tjene både Gud og mammon – Matteus 6:24.

Hun var en hyggelig ung kvinne. Og ja, hun bekjente at hun var kristen, men hun levde tydeligvis ikke i lydighet mot Guds ord. Bortsett fra at hun gikk i kirken, ville man ikke kunne se at hun var en Kristi etterfølger. Jeg er sikker på at hvis jeg hadde møtt henne i parken, kunne vi ha hatt en hyggelig prat. Jeg er sikker på at hun ville vært høflig og vennlig. Jeg er sikker på at hun ville ha framstått som en god borger og et godt menneske. Men når det gjaldt å være begeistret for Jesus, dele evangeliet og snakke om Guds ord, kom hennes sanne natur fram.

Sier jeg at man må være anabaptist for å komme til himmelen? Absolutt ikke, men jeg sier at vi må adlyde Bibelen og følge Kristus for å komme til himmelen. De fleste som bekjenner seg som kristne, er svært hyggelige og virker gudfryktige, helt til man begynner å snakke om Gud.

Når ble definisjonen på en kristen «et hyggelig menneske» eller «en god borger»? Er det virkelig alt som skal til nå – bare gjøre som man vil, finne en morsom kirke som ikke krever noe av en, få en god jobb, gifte seg, få noen barn, og dermed er man «kristen»? Gud hjelpe oss!

Da Jesus diskuterte med en gruppe mennesker om de var sanne etterfølgere av Gud eller ikke, sa han: … Hvis dere var Abrahams barn, ville dere gjøre Abrahams gjerninger. Men nå søker dere å drepe meg, en mann som har fortalt dere sannheten … Dere gjør deres fars gjerninger … Dere har djevelen til far … – Johannes 8:39–44.

Har den sanne kirken sunket så dypt at den ikke lenger klarer å kalle ting ved deres rette navn? Guds ord gir oss klar forståelse av saken: Prøv hva som er til behag for Herren. Ta ikke del i mørkets ufruktbare gjerninger, men avslør dem heller. For det er skammelig selv å tale om det de gjør i det skjulte. Men alt som blir avslørt, blir synlig i lyset; for alt som avslører, er lys – Efeserne 5:10–13.

Jesus sier: Dere er verdens lys. En by som ligger på et fjell, kan ikke skjules – Matteus 5:14. Avslører vi synd og kjetteri på samme måte som lyset avslører mørket? Eller er vi for knyttet til et behagelig liv uten fiender? Vi trenger ikke være redde for verden eller den falske kirken, for vi vet at vi har det de trenger! I årevis har de etablerte kirkene fjernet seg mer og mer fra sannheten i Guds ord. Er vi redde for å erkjenne dette? Er vi redde for å skille oss fra dem? Vil vi stå opp mot det, slik den tidlige kirken gjorde?

Det er en grunn til at den protestantiske reformatoren Martin Luther døde med hat mot anabaptistene – fordi de forkastet hans tolkning av Skriftene. Anabaptistene gjorde ikke forskjell på folk. Deres eneste respekt var for Gud og hans ord, uten kompromisser. Det var derfor de ble forfulgt. Det ville ha vært mye enklere for disse gudfryktige unge mennene bare å tie og prøve å komme overens med katolikkene og protestantene, men de nektet, og begge gruppene forsøkte å utslette dem. Likevel levde de videre og stolte bare på sin Gud. Da vi ble en del av Jesu Kristi kirke, lovet vi vel å fortsette å kjempe den samme kampen – den samme kampen som Jesus kjempet, den samme kampen som den tidlige kirken kjempet – kampen mot den falske kirken? Eller har vi gått med på å komme overens for fredens skyld? Tross alt er det vel bedre for forretningene, vennskapene og ryktet vårt?! Gud forby!

Vi kan leve et liv som ser ut til å være uten synd, men likevel leve i ulydighet. Bibelen kaller oss til handling! Vi er kalt til å være lys, vitner, søke gudsfrykt og leve rettskaffent, ikke bare til å sette opp et pent skue. Jeg tror dette er blitt populært i vår tid. Løgn, juks, tyveri og drap er ting selv verden tar avstand fra. Det er blitt «in» å være respektabel, ha en god inntekt og være en aktverdig borger. Men er dette livet til en gjenfødt troende? Bør vi passe inn i den amerikanske drømmen? Bør det eneste som skiller oss fra protestantiske kirker, være et hodeplagg? Jeg synes vi bør tenke grundig og be over dette trekket – å slå oss sammen med den etablerte kirken.

Jeg kjenner personlig mange protestantiske kristne. Jeg prøver ikke å si at de er dårlige mennesker; mange er gode folk. Men det er ikke det vi snakker om. Jeg mener vi må trekke en grense og bremse denne tendensen til å slutte oss til dem på en måte som innebærer kompromisser. La oss se på bare noen få av forskjellene mellom protestantene og anabaptistene.

Krig

Kan man støtte krig, drepe fiendene sine og likevel være en nytestamentlig kristen? De fleste protestanter støtter å kjempe for frihetene og rettighetene våre. Mange går så langt som til å kalle anabaptistene feiginger fordi de ikke kjemper.

For mange år siden samlet en gruppe mennesker som bekjente seg som kristne seg rundt den største bomben som noen gang var laget. Denne bomben skulle sendes til et fremmed land for å ødelegge en hel by; den var ment å drepe alt som kom i dens vei. Både menn, kvinner og barn skulle dø på grunn av denne bomben; det var planen. Mens denne gruppen sto samlet rundt bomben, begynte de å be. De ba Gud velsigne bombetoktet. Deretter takket de ham for at det var vellykket – for at nesten en kvart million mennesker var drept.

Jesus kaller oss til å elske fiendene våre. Dette spørsmålet skilte kirkene tydelig fra hverandre under de ulike krigene. De fleste «kristne» kirkene i verden støttet sitt lands krigsinnsats. Anabaptistene ville ikke gjøre det, og ble hardt forfulgt for det. Så kan vi være kristne og samtidig fortsette å støtte krig? Hvis vi støtter krig, hvor stopper det? Vil vi også forberede oss på å forsvare oss selv og familiene våre mot vold og lovløshet? Den amerikanske kirken kaller det å «forsvare oss selv», familiene våre og landet vårt, for heltemot eller tapperhet; Bibelen kaller det.

Underholdning

Det virker som om de fleste kristne i Amerika ikke har noe problem med å se så mange ballkamper og idrettsarrangementer som de ønsker. Nesten alle hjem har filmer og fjernsyn. Det er vanlig å dra på stranden, på kasinoer og festivaler. Man bruker tusenvis på store jaktturer og dyre ferier uten å tenke seg om to ganger. For å være ærlig er det egentlig ingen grenser for hva en kristen i Amerika kan gjøre, så lenge det virker riktig for vedkommende. Jesus sier gjentatte ganger at vi skal fornekte oss selv. Det virker som om vi leter etter enhver mulig utvei for å hengi oss til alle de selvtilfredsstillende aktivitetene vi ønsker! Det er ikke rart at kirken sliter med pornografi og mange andre kjødelige synder. Når vi lærer å fornekte oss selv, ta opp korset og følge Jesus, vil vi begynne å se et klart, tydelig og stort skille mellom oss og vår tids etablerte kirke.

Å ikke tilpasse seg

Det er vanlig å tilpasse seg omgivelsene sine. Dette er én grunn til at vi ikke sender barna våre på offentlige skoler. Jesus sier også tydelig at vi må komme ut fra dem og skille oss ut, si «nei» til ond tale og denne verdens veier, og ikke være redde for å identifisere oss med Guds folk. Det virker nesten som om klærne er det eneste som skiller mange av oss fra andre, og også det er i ferd med å endre seg.

Elsk ikke verden, heller ikke det som er i verden. Om noen elsker verden, er ikke Faderens kjærlighet i ham. For alt som er i verden – kjødets lyst, øynenes lyst og livets stolthet – er ikke av Faderen, men av verden – 1. Johannes 2:15–16. Hvor er menneskene som hater verden? Hvor er menneskene som ønsker å skille seg ut så mye som mulig? Hvor er menneskene som ikke er redde for å bli ledd av? Hvor er menneskene som ikke er redde for å være annerledes? Å, hvor er Guds folk?! Hvis historien gjentar seg, vil det snart ikke være noen forskjell mellom kirken og verden. Å, hvor er mennene?!

Jeg har hørt mange anabaptister si at de ikke kan si at de som tilhører den verdslige kirken, ikke er kristne; de vil bare ikke gå i den retningen. Er det santferdig? Er det budskapet vi ønsker å formidle til ungdommene våre og barna våre? Det tror jeg ikke. Bibelen sier at få vil bli frelst. Hvis vi gir barna våre videre at den protestantiske kirken også er grei, og at de bare gjør ting annerledes, ødelegger vi alt Jesus forkynte. Vi sier at vi gjør som vi gjør, ikke fordi Bibelen sier det, men fordi vi selv bestemmer hva vi gjør ut fra omstendighetene og hva folk rundt oss mener! Ikke rart barna våre er mer interessert i vår tids moderne kirke enn noen gang – det er ingen tydelig grense!

Det var en moderne kirke som fanget oppmerksomheten min. Det virket som om de brant for Herren! Pastoren forkynte som en døende mann. De var svært opptatt av å nå de fortapte. Men det var så mange bibelske læresetninger de rett og slett ignorerte! Til slutt la jeg det fram for Herren. «Hva er det som foregår her, Gud!» Det var som om Gud sa til meg: «Bare vent.»

Kort tid etterpå ble pastoren løst fra stillingen sin fordi han hadde et forhold til en annen kvinne. Da ble alt klart for meg – du kan ha en hyggelig kirke, forkynne et godt budskap og hjelpe de fattige, men hvis du ikke er villig til å adlyde ALLE læresetningene i Det nye testamentet, er du ikke en sann kristen, og du vil ikke seire. Det er lett å gå et stykke på den kristne veien, men det er ikke lett å selge alt du har, legge alt på alteret og følge Mesteren din. Jeg vet at dette er sterkt sagt, men det er sannheten i Guds ord.

Jeg snakket med en ung kvinne i et protestantisk miljø som ønsket å gi livet sitt til Herren. Hun sa at hun var klar til å gjøre det som måtte til. Jeg spurte henne om hun var klar til å lide for Jesus, om hun var klar til å skille seg fra de gamle vennene sine, om hun var klar til å bli hatet av verden og til å være annerledes. Jeg spurte henne om hun var villig til å forandre utseendet sitt. Det tok ikke lang tid før hun svarte sjokkert med et ettertrykkelig «Nei!» «Jeg vil begynne å gå i kirken, men ikke alt det andre.» Senere så jeg henne sammen med vennene sine, mens de pekte på meg og lo. Å være kul definerer ikke en sann kristen, men å bli avvist for evangeliets skyld gjør det.

Dette er en vanskelig artikkel å skrive. Det er ikke et populært budskap og heller ikke særlig oppmuntrende. Men jeg tror det er et budskap vi må ta på alvor i dag, ikke bare for vår egen skyld, men også for barnas skyld og for morgendagens kirke. Vi må trekke klare skillelinjer, uten kompromisser. Vi må oppriktig vurdere vår tids moderne kirke opp mot Det nye testamentets tydelige lære. Vi må kalle synd for synd. Vi må kalle ulydighet for synd. Vi må kalle kompromisser for synd. Vi må igjen velge å lide sammen med Guds sanne folk. Dette betyr ikke at vi skal sky mennesker eller behandle dem dårlig, men med kjærlighet i hjertet og et budskap på leppene viser vi folkemassene til Kristus!

For jeg skammer meg ikke over Kristi evangelium. Det er en Guds kraft til frelse for hver den som tror, først for jøde og så for greker – Romerne 1:16.
