Editor’s Note: Many of our readers may at first be convinced that this topic doesn’t pertain to them. If this is correct, we rejoice with you. However, before simply passing over this article we urge the reader to carefully read what is written here then start asking questions of family, friends, and acquaintances. We are hearing that especially the younger generation is being drawn into para-church events (such as concerts, seminars, Bible Schools, etc.) or special services at neighboring churches, which involve this type of content to one degree or another. Especially prominent are special music groups/concerts, ventriloquism, religious films, and skits. We wish to raise awareness on this issue and stimulate a discussion on the matter.

Religious drama—what is it?

A serious story by actors performing or impersonating any given dialogue in a theatrical manner, or an event of real life with emotional effects which are characteristics of a play, patterned after a religious theme. (American Heritage College Dictionary)

Is this something the church needs to be concerned about? It should be. It usually seems to get its beginning in extended “prayer and praise” services between Sunday school and church services. Or in special services other than on a Sunday morning. It can include such things as instrumental presentations, puppet shows, skits, plays, dances, and religious films.

Religious drama is not something new. It was introduced during the Dark Ages (A.D. 400 to 1200) as dramatic performances with religious themes known as “miracle plays.” These plays became so corrupt that the Catholic Church tried to put a stop to them, but to no avail. In 1242, the Passion play, a performance that depicts the death of Christ, started in Germany and it is still being performed around the world today.

An interesting observation, as we look back through time, is that religious drama was introduced during the darkest time of history (the Dark Ages), but the church emerged from this long era of moral decay through Spirit-filled, Bible-based, New Covenant-focused preaching of the Anabaptist Revival during the Reformation time period.

I. Why Drama Violates True Worship

a. Drama is a violation of the law of hearing.

In a spiritual world, seeing is not as important as hearing (2 Corinthians 4:18). The words hear, heareth, and heard are found over 1,000 times in the Bible. As a matter of fact, the whole Bible is God speaking to man. He wants mankind to hear! “Thus, saith the Lord” is a constant refrain throughout Scripture.

On Mount Sinai (Exodus 19:9), the people heard the message of God through His spokesman, Moses. God’s voice was frightening to them (Exodus 20:18-19) but hearing from Him was essential so that they “sin not.” In Exodus 20, God gave some detailed instructions of what the worship pattern was to be. Ye shall not make with me gods of silver, neither shall ye make unto you gods of gold –Exodus 20:23. These visual aids (idols) were a violation of God’s law of hearing. Through the eye gate comes the temptation to build idols. The altars that God did permit were to be plain and uncut (vss. 24-25). What they did see was not to distract from that which was heard from the altar! What is seen, especially immodesty, tends to be a distraction from what is heard (v. 26).

The preaching of Jesus appealed to the hearing: Who hath ears to hear, let him hear –Matthew 13:9. While He did not use visual aids like speakers do today, Jesus did use verbal aids (parables) as a tool to appeal to the hearing (Mat 13:18).

On the Mount of Transfiguration (Matthew 17), Peter wanted to reinvent the worship experience by building three shrines. He wanted something to see! But the voice in the clouds alerted the disciples to the importance of hearing (v. 5). Worship with visual aids is not endorsed by God!

Jesus said, Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life … The hour is coming, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God: and they that hear shall live. John 5:24-25. Salvation comes by hearing the Word of God, but only when one believes what is heard!

Paul raises some sobering questions: How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher? –Romans 10:14. He answers his own questions: So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God –Romans 10:17. God’s law to experience salvation is either by hearing God’s Word or by reading God’s Word!

In the 2nd and 3rd chapters of Revelation, Jesus repeats seven times: “He that hath an ear, let him hear.” Religious drama is superficial in that it appeals to the soulish part of man, not the spiritual part. The soulish part of man (emotions) can have a great time while the spirit within man remains untouched and unmoved. Satan uses the eye gate to distract man from his real heart issues.

Hebrews 11:6 tells us, “Faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen (or demonstrated).” Real faith comes to the human heart by hearing, not by demonstration. Therefore, religious drama borders on being anti-Christ because it is counterproductive to God’s law of hearing.

b. Drama is a violation of sincerity.

The Scriptures teach the importance of sincerity in all of life (1 Corinthians 5:8; 2 Corinthians 1:12, 2:17; Philippians 1:10). In maintaining our sincerity, it is important for each person to recognize that God has created us as unique individuals (Psalm 139:14-15). We are not and cannot be someone else! To try to be someone else violates our individual uniqueness. And, when one does so, he becomes insincere.

How does this connect with religious drama? Drama employs playacting. Jesus had a constant controversy with the Pharisees. They were constantly playacting, or pretending to be something that they were not. Jesus repeatedly called them hypocrites. The original Greek word means “play actor.”

The Pharisees’ sole motivation to pray in public was to be seen of men (Matthew 6:5-7). They were conscious of their audience, thus their performance. Jesus made it very clear that religious devotion was to be private, in “thy closet.” When a person who expresses his piety becomes more concerned about his performance than his message, he is no longer worshiping, but putting on a show! This can happen to preachers, quartets, choruses, etc. “Prayer walks” also usually fall into this same category of playacting.

When a person makes play-acting a regular habit, he becomes a hypocrite. He violates his own soul, because he injures his own uniqueness, which was given by God.

Jesus addressed the Pharisees as hypocrites seven times in Matthew 23. He informed them that they were walking dead men (Matthew 23:27-28). They had playacted for so long that they did not know the difference between the real and the unreal!

This deception is one reason that professional actors become such extremists about the issues of life. Professionally, they become increasingly detached from truth, sincerity, and reality. In such matters as ecology, animal rights, abortion, gay rights, and global warming, many of them have taken positions that are disconnected from the foundations of truth and are no longer sincere.

To pretend to pray or worship or to act out Bible characters in a play is not only insincere, but it borders on being sacrilegious. Imagine pretending to be Jesus in a play! To pretend to be Jesus is blasphemous because no Christian has ever come anywhere close to His perfection! Or, what about pretending to be the devil? Why, pray tell, would anyone who is sincerely following the teachings of Jesus take upon himself the embodiment of evil? A. W. Tozer concludes, “Playacting embodies a gross moral contradiction in that it calls a lie to the service of the truth.”

Religious drama, those who involve themselves in it, and for that matter those who approve of the very hypocrisy that Jesus condemned, are frauds. The Holy Spirit does not honor pretense and showmanship!

The reason multitudes followed Jesus was that His sincerity was so refreshing in comparison to the constant playacting of the Pharisees.

II. Practical Reasons Why Religious Drama is a Menace

a. Religious drama demoralizes reverence for God.

A person who pretends to be Jesus Christ or any other Bible character erodes his reverence for the Lord. When one playacts enough, his fear of God slowly dies within. After all, if a person can pretend to be equal to Christ, what is the need for reverence to a higher being? The Pharisees did not even suspect that they were walking dead men (Matthew 23:27).

b. Religious drama identifies worship with the theatrical world.

Hollywood has effectively proven that the theatrical world cannot produce godly moral values. Pairing a man and a woman as a pretend husband and wife breaks down the sanctity of marriage. The theatrical world also endorses courtship practices that violate the biblical standards of purity. The theatrical world has become the pacesetter of moral standards in today’s society, and many are following their ungodly pattern.

c. Religious drama does not satisfy the inner man.

When a person’s senses are titillated by outward show, the emotions keep seeking a new high and another feel-good worship experience. It creates a desire within to see yet another show that is more satisfying than the previous one. The emotions are having fun, but the inner man starves and slowly dies because the heart and mind have not been fed with real substance.

d. Religious drama ruins the preacher.

Drama is a friend to the lazy preacher. He no longer needs to: Study to shew thyself approved unto God… –2 Timothy 2:15. It requires no Holy Spirit unction to substitute a play for the sermon. Instead of commanding men to be “the light of the world,” he commands them to “lower the lights, please!” When the projector replaces the prophet, the primary means for man to find salvation is lost (1 Corinthians 1:21).

“As long as the preacher can fall back upon entertainment, the pressure that makes preachers will be wanting. The habit and rhythm which belongs to great preaching will be missing from their ministry.” –A. W. Tozer.

The use of religious drama will doom the preacher to mediocrity! The menace that we face today is that as religious drama multiplies, the heaven-sent revivals of the past will become extinct.

e. True worship will be viewed as inferior.

By using drama in a worship service, churches are training the youth to think that true worship is just another inferior form of amusement. When worship and drama are fused into one, worship is reduced to the lowest common denominator. The danger is that the next generation will not know what true worship is!

III. Patterns of True Worship

a. Prayer

Prayer is a vast subject, a worship pattern that too many times remains untapped. Public prayer in the congregational life is squeezed into our man-made time constraints.

In the early church, public prayers held a consistent pattern in their worship experiences. There was public prayer immediately after Christ’s ascension (Acts 1:14) and the first ordination (Acts 1:24). And they continued stedfastly … in prayers –Acts 2:42. No spirit of apathy was present! Prayer meetings were an evangelistic tool, a means of implementing the fear of God, and a great unifier for the whole church (Acts 2:41-44).

Peter and John attended a midafternoon prayer meeting (Acts 3:1). (Say, fellow saint, when was the last time that you attended a midafternoon prayer meeting?) Their prayer meeting had seismic results (Acts 4:31)! The power and presence of the Holy Spirit in our worship services brings results!

Prayer meeting attendance was not a monthly or a bimonthly option (Act 6:4)! When Peter was in prison, they had a voluntary, round-the-clock, prayer chain (Acts 12:5). They laid hands on their missionaries and prayed for them (Acts 13:3). They gathered at the river for a prayer meeting (Acts 16:13). Please note: this gathering at the river was not for the purpose of any kind of water sports; it was a prayer meeting! They gathered …prayer was wont to be made… –Acts 16:13. They understood that wherever Christians happened to meet, it was a normal activity to pray together.

b. Preaching

Preaching is a worship pattern that dates back to the time of Jonah (Jonah 3:2) and Moses (Acts 15:21). In the Old Testament, preaching was God’s pattern for communicating the will of God to man. When Jesus came on the scene, …[He] came into Galilee, preaching the gospel of the kingdom of God –Mark 1:14. He used the same worship pattern. Jesus used parables as verbal illustrations (not visual ones), which caught the attention of His hearers.

Near the end of His ministry, Jesus extended preaching as a worship pattern to future generations and all world cultures: …Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature –Mark 16:15.

Paul’s call was to preach the gospel (1 Corinthians 1:17-21). Preaching was not to be embellished by the cleverness of man. It pleased God to use the foolishness and simplicity of preaching to minister salvation to those who dared to believe. For this reason, preaching needs to be the focal point of every worship service. Praise services, concerts, and musicals are robbers of time that instead ought to be invested in listening to Holy Spirit-inspired preaching. When religious drama is used to present truth, it bypasses God’s ordained pattern of bringing the message of salvation to man.

Blessed is he that readeth, and they that hear the words of this prophecy, and keep those things which are written therein… –Revelation 1:3. God’s method of communication is the written or spoken Word. Not a picture! Not a play! Not a pageant!

c. Singing

The New Testament leaves no hint of professional singers, choirs, or musical performances. Meaningful singing requires participation by all, and an intelligent involvement of the mind (1 Corinthians 14:15). The context clearly implies that worship or singing is not only an individual experience; it is for the edification of all present. Soloists, who tend to be self-exalting, prohibit the remainder of the audience from entering into a corporate worship experience.

Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord –Colossians 3:16. Spiritual songs move the heart, while soulish songs move the feet and the emotions. Our singing is “to the Lord.” Preaching is from God to man, but singing is from man to God, containing expressions of praise, adoration, honor, and thanksgiving. Singing is for worship, not for entertainment.

Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord –Ephesians 5:19. Spirit-filled singing brings mutual edification, inspiration, and encouragement. Participation in singing has a way of ministering to heartfelt needs, where other methods fail. “Making melody in your heart” involves the accompaniment of the heart. External instrumentation tends to focus on a person’s abilities rather than on the heart. If our singing is not accompanied by our hearts, it becomes just another pharisaical worship show.

Old Testament worship was acceptable to God; nevertheless, it was also ritualistic with animal sacrifices, burning incense, using musical instruments, and dancing before the Lord. New Testament worship, however, is quite different. Jesus teaches us that we …must worship him in spirit and in truth –John 4:24. The spirit of worship replaces the rituals. When we move from intrinsic methods of worship to extrinsic methods, we violate the New Testament “spirit” of worship. Our worship is not to be stimulated by the extrinsic, but rather by the Holy Spirit (Ephesians 5:18).

IV. Essence of True Worship

When Jesus met the woman at the well, she expressed a concern about His change in worship format (John 4:20). She was concerned about how her fathers worshiped. In other words, “this is the way that we have always done it!” Every generation of worshipers must guard against formalistic worship.

There are two attitudes that affect true worship in a wrong way:

  • Formal –becoming so accustomed to the way that we have always done it, that we end up merely going through the motions and losing focus on the One being worshiped.
  • Casual –becoming so aloof to any form of worship that the One being worshiped becomes obscured by indifference.

Both formal and casual worship styles have one root problem: lack of reverence for God!

The fathers of the woman at the well had lost both the focus and the concept of worship: “Ye worship ye know not what” (John 4:22a). Jesus clearly indicated that worship is not thoughtless: “We know what we worship” (4:22b). True worship is the exercise of our mind and intellect. True worship has something to offer: “Salvation is of Jesus” (4:22c). It is life-changing!

The worship location is not as important as the attitude (John 4:23). The emphasis that Jesus gives is not on the outward ceremony, but on the state of the mind and spirit.

God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth –John 4:24. Note the word must! The only acceptable worship is in spirit and in truth. Our attitude must be such that it is in harmony with the Spirit of God. True worship also involves our response to truth. If our spirits are not responding to truth, we are not worshiping! If our minds are somewhere else, or on anything else, our worship is merely cold, dead ritualism!

Conclusion

In the observation of the principles of Scripture, it is clear that religious drama is not God’s pattern to bring faith and life into the human soul!

The pattern of true worship in the New Testament is to gather to hear the Word preached; to pray together and for each other; and to sing songs, hymns, and spiritual songs.

The temptation to introduce new things to worship is very real today. The appeal of Jesus is to worship in spirit and in truth. When each of us sincerely does his part to keep worship services meaningful and spiritual, it reduces the temptation to reintroduce the formal (“the way our fathers worshiped”) or to introduce the casual (any new irreverent worship).

Redakteursnota: Baie van ons lesers is dalk aanvanklik daarvan oortuig dat hierdie onderwerp nie op hulle van toepassing is nie. As dit inderdaad so is, is ons saam met julle bly. Voordat julle egter hierdie artikel bloot oorslaan, moedig ons die leser aan om noukeurig te lees wat hier geskryf staan en dan vrae aan familie, vriende en kennisse te begin stel. Ons hoor dat veral die jonger geslag ingetrek word by geleenthede van organisasies buite die kerk (soos konserte, seminare, Bybelskole, ens.) of spesiale dienste by naburige kerke, waar hierdie soort inhoud in ’n mindere of meerdere mate voorkom. Spesiale musiekgroepe/konserte, buikspraak, godsdienstige films en sketse is veral opvallend. Ons wil bewustheid oor hierdie kwessie kweek en ’n bespreking daaroor aanmoedig.

Godsdienstige drama—wat is dit?

’n Ernstige verhaal wat deur akteurs opgevoer word deur enige bepaalde dialoog op ’n teatermatige manier uit te beeld of na te boots, of ’n gebeurtenis uit die werklike lewe met emosionele uitwerkings wat kenmerkend van ’n toneelstuk is, volgens ’n godsdienstige tema. (American Heritage College Dictionary)

Is dit iets waaroor die kerk besorg behoort te wees? Dit behoort. Dit lyk gewoonlik of dit begin tydens lang “gebed-en-lofdienstye” tussen Sondagskool en kerkdienste. Of by spesiale dienste op ander tye as Sondagoggend. Dit kan dinge soos instrumentale uitvoerings, poppespel, sketse, toneelstukke, danse en godsdienstige films insluit.

Godsdienstige drama is nie iets nuuts nie. Dit is gedurende die Donker Eeue (n.C. 400 tot 1200) ingevoer as dramatiese opvoerings met godsdienstige temas, bekend as “wonderwerke”. Hierdie toneelstukke het so korrup geword dat die Katolieke Kerk probeer het om hulle stop te sit, maar sonder sukses. In 1242 het die Passiespel, ’n opvoering wat Christus se dood uitbeeld, in Duitsland begin, en dit word vandag steeds regoor die wêreld opgevoer.

’n Interessante waarneming wanneer ons terugkyk deur die geskiedenis, is dat godsdienstige drama gedurende die donkerste tydperk in die geskiedenis (die Donker Eeue) ingevoer is, maar dat die kerk uit hierdie lang tydperk van morele verval te voorskyn gekom het deur die Geesvervulde, Bybelgegronde prediking, gerig op die Nuwe Verbond, van die Anabaptistiese Herlewing gedurende die tyd van die Hervorming.

I. Waarom drama ware aanbidding skend

a. Drama skend die wet van hoor.

In ’n geestelike wêreld is sien nie so belangrik soos hoor nie (2 Korintiërs 4:18). Die woorde hoor, hoor en gehoor kom meer as 1 000 keer in die Bybel voor. Trouens, die hele Bybel is God wat met die mens praat. Hy wil hê dat die mensdom moet hoor! “So sê die Here” is ’n voortdurende refrein regdeur die Skrif.

Op die berg Sinai (Eksodus 19:9) het die volk God se boodskap deur sy woordvoerder, Moses, gehoor. God se stem het hulle bang gemaak (Eksodus 20:18-19), maar dit was noodsaaklik dat hulle Hom hoor sodat hulle “nie sondig nie”. In Eksodus 20 het God uitvoerige instruksies gegee oor hoe die aanbiddingspatroon moes wees. Julle mag nie vir My gode van silwer maak nie, en ook mag julle nie vir julle gode van goud maak nie –Eksodus 20:23. Hierdie visuele hulpmiddels (afgode) was ’n skending van God se wet van hoor. Deur die oogpoort kom die versoeking om afgode te bou. Die altare wat God wel toegelaat het, moes eenvoudig en ongekap wees (vss. 24-25). Wat hulle gesien het, moes nie aflei van dit wat vanaf die altaar gehoor is nie! Wat ’n mens sien, veral onbeskeidenheid, is geneig om af te lei van wat gehoor word (v. 26).

Jesus se prediking het ’n beroep op die gehoor gedoen: Wie ore het om te hoor, laat hom hoor –Matteus 13:9. Hoewel Hy nie visuele hulpmiddels gebruik het soos sprekers vandag nie, het Jesus wel verbale hulpmiddels (gelykenisse) as ’n manier gebruik om ’n beroep op die gehoor te doen (Mat 13:18).

Op die berg van Verheerliking (Matteus 17) wou Petrus die aanbiddingservaring herontwerp deur drie heiligdomme te bou. Hy wou iets hê om te sien! Maar die stem uit die wolk het die dissipels op die belangrikheid van hoor gewys (v. 5). Aanbidding met visuele hulpmiddels word nie deur God goedgekeur nie!

Jesus het gesê: Voorwaar, voorwaar, Ek sê vir julle: Wie my woord hoor en Hom glo wat My gestuur het, het die ewige lewe … Die uur kom, en dit is nou, wanneer die dooies die stem van die Seun van God sal hoor, en dié wat dit hoor, sal lewe. Johannes 5:24-25. Verlossing kom deur die Woord van God te hoor, maar slegs wanneer iemand glo wat hy hoor!

Paulus stel ’n paar ernstige vrae: Hoe kan hulle Hom dan aanroep in wie hulle nie geglo het nie? En hoe kan hulle in Hom glo van wie hulle nie gehoor het nie? En hoe kan hulle hoor sonder iemand wat preek? –Romeine 10:14. Hy beantwoord sy eie vrae: Die geloof is dus uit die gehoor, en die gehoor is deur die woord van God –Romeine 10:17. God se wet vir die belewing van verlossing is dat dit óf deur God se Woord te hoor óf deur God se Woord te lees, kom!

In die 2de en 3de hoofstukke van Openbaring herhaal Jesus sewe keer: “Wie ’n oor het, laat hom hoor.” Godsdienstige drama is oppervlakkig omdat dit ’n beroep doen op die sielse deel van die mens, nie die geestelike deel nie. Die sielse deel van die mens (emosies) kan dit baie geniet terwyl die gees binne-in die mens onaangeraak en onbeweeg bly. Satan gebruik die oogpoort om die mens se aandag van sy werklike hartsake af te lei.

Hebreërs 11:6 sê vir ons: “Geloof is die vaste vertroue op die dinge wat gehoop word, die bewys van die dinge wat nie gesien word nie (of gedemonstreer word nie).” Ware geloof kom deur te hoor in die mens se hart, nie deur demonstrasie nie. Daarom grens godsdienstige drama aan anti-Christelik wees, want dit werk teen God se wet van hoor.

b. Drama skend opregtheid.

Die Skrif leer hoe belangrik opregtheid in elke aspek van die lewe is (1 Korintiërs 5:8; 2 Korintiërs 1:12, 2:17; Filippense 1:10). Om ons opregtheid te behou, is dit belangrik dat elkeen erken dat God ons as unieke individue geskep het (Psalm 139:14-15). Ons is nie iemand anders nie en kan dit ook nie wees nie! Om iemand anders te probeer wees, skend ons individuele uniekheid. En wanneer iemand dit doen, raak hy onopreg.

Hoe hou dit verband met godsdienstige drama? Drama behels toneelspel. Jesus was voortdurend in konflik met die Fariseërs. Hulle het gedurig toneelgespeel, of voorgegee dat hulle iets is wat hulle nie was nie. Jesus het hulle herhaaldelik geveinsdes genoem. Die oorspronklike Griekse woord beteken “toneelspeler”.

Die Fariseërs se enigste beweegrede om in die openbaar te bid, was om deur mense gesien te word (Matteus 6:5-7). Hulle was bewus van hulle gehoor en het dus hulle optrede in ag geneem. Jesus het dit baie duidelik gestel dat godsdienstige toewyding privaat moes wees, in “jou binnekamer”. Wanneer iemand wat sy vroomheid uitdruk, meer besorg raak oor sy optrede as oor sy boodskap, aanbid hy nie meer nie, maar voer hy ’n vertoning op! Dit kan met predikers, kwartette, kore, ens. gebeur. “Gebedswandelings” val gewoonlik ook in hierdie selfde kategorie van toneelspel.

Wanneer iemand toneelspel ’n gereelde gewoonte maak, word hy ’n geveinsde. Hy skend sy eie siel, want hy skaad sy eie uniekheid, wat God aan hom gegee het.

Jesus het die Fariseërs sewe keer in Matteus 23 geveinsdes genoem. Hy het hulle ingelig dat hulle wandelende dooies was (Matteus 23:27-28). Hulle het so lank toneelgespeel dat hulle nie meer die verskil tussen die werklike en die onwerklike geken het nie!

Hierdie misleiding is een rede waarom professionele akteurs sulke uiterste standpunte oor lewenskwessies inneem. Professioneel raak hulle toenemend verwyderd van waarheid, opregtheid en werklikheid. Oor sake soos ekologie, diereregte, aborsie, gayregte en aardverwarming het baie van hulle standpunte ingeneem wat losstaan van die grondbeginsels van waarheid en nie meer opreg is nie.

Om voor te gee dat jy bid of aanbid, of om Bybelkarakters in ’n toneelstuk uit te beeld, is nie net onopreg nie, maar grens aan heiligskennis. Stel jou voor dat jy in ’n toneelstuk voorgee om Jesus te wees! Om voor te gee dat jy Jesus is, is godslasterlik, want geen Christen het ooit naastenby sy volmaaktheid bereik nie! Of wat van voorgee om die duiwel te wees? Waarom, vra ek, sou iemand wat Jesus se leer opreg volg, die beliggaming van die bose op homself neem? A. W. Tozer kom tot die gevolgtrekking: “Toneelspel beliggaam ’n growwe morele teenstrydigheid deurdat dit ’n leuen in diens van die waarheid stel.”

Godsdienstige drama, diegene wat daaraan deelneem, en trouens diegene wat die einste skynheiligheid goedkeur wat Jesus veroordeel het, is bedrieërs. Die Heilige Gees eer nie voorwendsels en vertoon nie!

Die rede waarom menigtes Jesus gevolg het, was dat sy opregtheid so verfrissend was in vergelyking met die Fariseërs se voortdurende toneelspel.

II. Praktiese redes waarom godsdienstige drama ’n bedreiging is

a. Godsdienstige drama ondermyn eerbied vir God.

Iemand wat voorgee om Jesus Christus of enige ander Bybelkarakter te wees, ondermyn sy eerbied vir die Here. Wanneer iemand genoeg toneelspel, sterf sy vrees vir God stadig binne-in hom. As iemand immers kan voorgee dat hy gelyk is aan Christus, waarom sou daar dan ’n behoefte wees aan eerbied vir ’n hoër wese? Die Fariseërs het nie eens vermoed dat hulle wandelende dooies was nie (Matteus 23:27).

b. Godsdienstige drama vereenselwig aanbidding met die teaterwêreld.

Hollywood het doeltreffend bewys dat die teaterwêreld nie godvrugtige morele waardes kan voortbring nie. Wanneer ’n man en ’n vrou as ’n voorgewende man en vrou saamgepaar word, word die heiligheid van die huwelik afgebreek. Die teaterwêreld keur ook hofmakerypraktyke goed wat die Bybelse standaarde van reinheid skend. Die teaterwêreld het die maatstaf vir morele standaarde in vandag se samelewing geword, en baie volg hierdie goddelose patroon.

c. Godsdienstige drama bevredig nie die innerlike mens nie.

Wanneer iemand se sintuie deur uiterlike vertoon geprikkel word, bly sy emosies na ’n nuwe hoogtepunt en nog ’n goedvoel-aanbiddingservaring soek. Dit skep ’n begeerte na nog ’n vertoning wat meer bevredigend is as die vorige een. Die emosies geniet hulleself, maar die innerlike mens ly honger en sterf stadig omdat die hart en verstand nie met werklike inhoud gevoed is nie.

d. Godsdienstige drama ruïneer die prediker.

Drama is ’n vriend van die lui prediker. Hy hoef nie meer: Hom daarop toe te lê om jou beproef voor God te stel… –2 Timoteus 2:15. Dit verg geen salwing deur die Heilige Gees om ’n toneelstuk in die plek van die preek te stel nie. In plaas daarvan om mense opdrag te gee om “die lig van die wêreld” te wees, beveel hy hulle: “Dim asseblief die ligte!” Wanneer die projektor die profeet vervang, gaan die vernaamste manier waarop die mens verlossing kan vind, verlore (1 Korintiërs 1:21).

“Solank die prediker op vermaak kan terugval, sal die druk wat predikers voortbring, ontbreek. Die gewoonte en ritme wat by kragtige prediking hoort, sal in hulle bediening ontbreek.” –A. W. Tozer.

Die gebruik van godsdienstige drama sal die prediker tot middelmatigheid verdoem! Die bedreiging waarvoor ons vandag staan, is dat die hemelgestuurde herlewings van die verlede sal uitsterf namate godsdienstige drama vermeerder.

e. Ware aanbidding sal as minderwaardig beskou word.

Deur drama in ’n aanbiddingsdiens te gebruik, leer kerke die jeug om te dink dat ware aanbidding maar net nog ’n minderwaardige vorm van vermaak is. Wanneer aanbidding en drama saamgesmelt word, word aanbidding tot die laagste gemene deler afgebring. Die gevaar is dat die volgende geslag nie sal weet wat ware aanbidding is nie!

III. Patrone van ware aanbidding

a. Gebed

Gebed is ’n omvangryke onderwerp, ’n aanbiddingspatroon wat te dikwels onbenut bly. Openbare gebed in die gemeentelike lewe word binne ons mensgemaakte tydsbeperkings ingedruk.

In die vroeë kerk het openbare gebede ’n vaste patroon in hulle aanbiddingservarings gevolg. Daar was openbare gebed onmiddellik ná Christus se hemelvaart (Handelinge 1:14) en die eerste bevestiging in die amp (Handelinge 1:24). En hulle het volhard … in die gebede –Handelinge 2:42. Geen gees van apatie was aanwesig nie! Gebedsbyeenkomste was ’n evangelisasiehulpmiddel, ’n manier om die vrees vir God te bevorder, en ’n kragtige verenigende faktor vir die hele kerk (Handelinge 2:41-44).

Petrus en Johannes het ’n gebedsbyeenkoms in die middel van die middag bygewoon (Handelinge 3:1). (Sê nou, medegelowige, wanneer het jy laas ’n gebedsbyeenkoms in die middel van die middag bygewoon?) Hulle gebedsbyeenkoms het aardbewingagtige gevolge gehad (Handelinge 4:31)! Die krag en teenwoordigheid van die Heilige Gees in ons aanbiddingsdienste bring resultate!

Om gebedsbyeenkomste by te woon, was nie ’n maandelikse of tweemaandelikse opsie nie (Hand 6:4)! Toe Petrus in die tronk was, het hulle vrywillig ’n gebedsketting gehad wat dag en nag voortgeduur het (Handelinge 12:5). Hulle het hulle hande op hulle sendelinge gelê en vir hulle gebid (Handelinge 13:3). Hulle het by die rivier bymekaargekom vir ’n gebedsbyeenkoms (Handelinge 16:13). Let wel: hierdie byeenkoms by die rivier was nie vir enige soort watersport nie; dit was ’n gebedsbyeenkoms! Hulle het bymekaargekom; …daar waar die gebed gewoonlik gedoen is… –Handelinge 16:13. Hulle het begryp dat dit ’n normale gebruik is om saam te bid, waar Christene ook al bymekaar kom.

b. Prediking

Prediking is ’n aanbiddingspatroon wat terugdateer tot die tyd van Jona (Jona 3:2) en Moses (Handelinge 15:21). In die Ou Testament was prediking God se patroon om sy wil aan die mens bekend te maak. Toe Jesus op die toneel verskyn, het …[Hy] in Galilea gekom en die evangelie van die koninkryk van God verkondig –Markus 1:14. Hy het dieselfde aanbiddingspatroon gebruik. Jesus het gelykenisse as mondelinge illustrasies gebruik (nie visuele illustrasies nie), wat die aandag van sy hoorders getrek het.

Naby die einde van sy bediening het Jesus prediking as ’n aanbiddingspatroon uitgebrei na toekomstige geslagte en alle kulture wêreldwyd: …Gaan die hele wêreld in en verkondig die evangelie aan die ganse mensdom –Markus 16:15.

Paulus se roeping was om die evangelie te verkondig (1 Korintiërs 1:17-21). Prediking moes nie met menslike vernuf opgesmuk word nie. Dit het God behaag om die dwaasheid en eenvoud van die prediking te gebruik om verlossing te bedien aan dié wat dit durf glo het. Om hierdie rede moet prediking die fokuspunt van elke aanbiddingsdiens wees. Lofprysingsdienste, konserte en musiekuitvoerings steel tyd wat eerder bestee behoort te word aan luister na prediking wat deur die Heilige Gees geïnspireer is. Wanneer godsdienstige drama gebruik word om waarheid oor te dra, omseil dit God se verordende patroon om die boodskap van verlossing aan die mens te bring.

Salig is hy wat lees, en hulle wat die woorde van hierdie profesie hoor en bewaar wat daarin geskrywe staan… –Openbaring 1:3. God se manier van kommunikeer is die geskrewe of gesproke Woord. Nie ’n prent nie! Nie ’n toneelstuk nie! Nie ’n skouspel nie!

c. Sang

Die Nuwe Testament gee geen aanduiding van professionele sangers, kore of musikale uitvoerings nie. Betekenisvolle sang vereis dat almal deelneem en dat die verstand met begrip betrokke is (1 Korintiërs 14:15). Die konteks impliseer duidelik dat aanbidding of sang nie net ’n individuele ervaring is nie; dit is tot stigting van almal wat teenwoordig is. Soliste, wat geneig is om hulleself te verhef, verhinder die res van die gehoor om aan ’n gesamentlike aanbiddingservaring deel te neem.

Laat die woord van Christus ryklik in julle woon in alle wysheid, terwyl julle mekaar leer en vermaan met psalms en lofsange en geestelike liedere, en met genade in julle harte tot eer van die Here sing –Kolossense 3:16. Geestelike liedere beweeg die hart, terwyl sielse liedere die voete en emosies beweeg. Ons sing “tot eer van die Here”. Prediking is van God tot die mens, maar sang is van die mens tot God, met uitdrukkings van lof, aanbidding, eer en danksegging. Sang is vir aanbidding, nie vir vermaak nie.

Praat met mekaar met psalms en lofsange en geestelike liedere, en sing en psalmsing in julle hart tot eer van die Here –Efesiërs 5:19. Geesvervulde sang bring wedersydse stigting, inspirasie en bemoediging. Deelname aan sang het ’n manier om in behoeftes van die hart te voorsien waar ander metodes misluk. “Psalmsing in julle hart” behels dat die hart begelei. Uiterlike instrumente is geneig om die aandag op iemand se vermoëns eerder as op die hart te vestig. As ons sang nie deur ons harte begelei word nie, word dit maar net nog ’n Farisese aanbiddingsvertoning.

Aanbidding in die Ou Testament was vir God aanvaarbaar; dit was nietemin ook ritualisties, met diereoffers, wierook wat gebrand is, musiekinstrumente wat gebruik is en dans voor die Here. Nuwe-Testamentiese aanbidding is egter heeltemal anders. Jesus leer ons dat ons …Hom in gees en waarheid moet aanbid –Johannes 4:24. Die gees van aanbidding vervang die rituele. Wanneer ons van innerlike aanbiddingsmetodes na uiterlike metodes oorgaan, skend ons die Nuwe-Testamentiese “gees” van aanbidding. Ons aanbidding moet nie deur die uiterlike aangevuur word nie, maar eerder deur die Heilige Gees (Efesiërs 5:18).

IV. Die wese van ware aanbidding

Toe Jesus die vrou by die put ontmoet het, het sy haar kommer uitgespreek oor die verandering in die aanbiddingswyse (Johannes 4:20). Sy was besorg oor hoe haar vaders aanbid het. Met ander woorde: “Dit is hoe ons dit nog altyd gedoen het!” Elke geslag aanbidders moet waak teen formalistiese aanbidding.

Daar is twee gesindhede wat ware aanbidding op ’n verkeerde manier beïnvloed:

  • Formeel –om so gewoond te raak aan die manier waarop ons dit nog altyd gedoen het, dat ons uiteindelik bloot die bewegings deurgaan en die fokus verloor op die Een wat aanbid word.
  • Gemaklik –om so afsydig te raak teenoor enige vorm van aanbidding dat die Een wat aanbid word deur onverskilligheid verduister word.

Beide formele en informele aanbiddingstyle het een grondliggende probleem: ’n gebrek aan eerbied vir God!

Die vrou by die put se vaders het sowel die fokus as die begrip van aanbidding verloor: “Julle aanbid wat julle nie ken nie” (Johannes 4:22a). Jesus het duidelik aangedui dat aanbidding nie onnadenkend is nie: “Ons aanbid wat ons ken” (4:22b). Ware aanbidding behels die gebruik van ons verstand en intellek. Ware aanbidding het iets om te bied: “Die verlossing is uit Jesus” (4:22c). Dit verander ’n mens se lewe!

Die plek van aanbidding is nie so belangrik soos die gesindheid nie (Johannes 4:23). Die klem wat Jesus lê, is nie op die uiterlike seremonie nie, maar op die toestand van die verstand en gees.

God is Gees; en dié wat Hom aanbid, moet Hom in gees en waarheid aanbid –Johannes 4:24. Let op die woord “moet”! Die enigste aanvaarbare aanbidding is in gees en waarheid. Ons gesindheid moet in ooreenstemming wees met die Gees van God. Ware aanbidding behels ook ons reaksie op die waarheid. As ons gees nie op die waarheid reageer nie, aanbid ons nie! As ons verstand elders is, of met iets anders besig is, is ons aanbidding bloot koue, dooie ritualisme!

Gevolgtrekking

Wanneer die beginsels van die Skrif in ag geneem word, is dit duidelik dat godsdienstige drama nie God se patroon is om geloof en lewe in die menslike siel te bring nie!

Die patroon van ware aanbidding in die Nuwe Testament is om bymekaar te kom om die Woord te hoor verkondig; om saam en vir mekaar te bid; en om liedere, lofsange en geestelike liedere te sing.

Die versoeking om nuwe dinge by aanbidding in te voer, is vandag baie werklik. Jesus se oproep is om in gees en waarheid te aanbid. Wanneer elkeen van ons opreg sy deel doen om aanbiddingsdienste betekenisvol en geestelik te hou, verminder dit die versoeking om die formele (“die manier waarop ons vaders aanbid het”) weer in te voer, of die informele (enige nuwe oneerbiedige aanbidding) in te voer.

We all have a story. Some feel like Job sometimes. Some have lost parents, or partners, or children, or siblings, or friends. Some suffer from severe illness. Some will never recover from their illnesses. Our loved ones might have a terminal illness. Maybe a husband or parent is abusive or unfaithful. Like Job, our friends might have turned against us. Maybe there are problems in the church that seem impossible to fix. It could be something like a colicky baby, or a hyper child. Maybe we just have a cold and are feeling like everything is going wrong. The list is endless. We can relate to the words of this song.

Till the Storm Passes By

In the dark of the midnight have I oft hid my face,
While the storm howls above me, and there’s no hiding place.
‘Mid the crash of the thunder, Precious Lord, hear my cry,
Keep me safe till the storm passes by.

refrain:

Till the storm passes over, till the thunder sounds no more,
Till the clouds roll forever from the sky;
Hold me fast, let me stand in the hollow of Thy hand,
Keep me safe till the storm passes by.

Many times Satan whispered, “There is no need to try,
For there’s no end of sorrow, there’s no hope by and by”
But I know Thou art with me, and tomorrow I’ll rise
Where the storms never darken the skies.

When the long night has ended and the storms come no more,
Let me stand in Thy presence on the bright peaceful shore;
In that land where the tempest, never comes, Lord, may I
Dwell with Thee when the storm passes by.

–by Mosie Lister

When I was a little girl, I thought the author was referring to thunderstorms. I was afraid of thunderstorms. Now I understand that he was referring to the storms of life we go through. On July 14, 2013, I suddenly ended up in the hospital with a life-threatening heart attack caused by a spontaneous coronary artery dissection. What a shock for a 40-year-old mother. The storm was howling, and the thunder was crashing. There was no hiding place from the danger, for it was within me. I only had one heart and it could not be trusted. What if it happens again? Would I die? Then my children would be motherless.

This song was one I’d pray in the dark of the midnight when I couldn’t sleep, and fear threatened to overwhelm me. The Lord’s presence was very real to me. I came through this storm with a greater awareness of how God reveals Himself to us in a deeper way when we are going through hard times. We must choose to yield ourselves completely to Him, and say, “Not my will, but Thine be done.”

When the disciples were out on the sea in the storm, Jesus was with them. He is with us too. We can trust Him. Nothing will happen that is not according to His will. We do not always understand why things happen, but that’s okay. An old preacher used to quote:

“Not now, but in the coming years,
It may be in the better land
We’ll read the meaning of our tears,
And there, sometime, we’ll understand.”

It is so important that we accept what God allows in our lives. Accepting does not mean we don’t do anything about it. We will go to the doctor if necessary. We will reach out to others for comfort and council. We will still have all kinds of feelings, but we should have peace. We can’t wallow in self-pity and have a “poor me” attitude. And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose –Romans 8:28. I believe that. I can’t always see the good, but God does.

Life is hard sometimes, but the song tells about the time when the long night has ended, and the storms come no more. Dear sisters, let’s remain faithful and lean hard on the Lord through the storms of life.

Sote tuna hadithi yetu. Nyakati nyingine wengine huhisi kama Ayubu. Wengine wamewapoteza wazazi, au wenzi wao, au watoto, au ndugu, au marafiki. Wengine wanateseka kwa magonjwa makali. Wengine hawatapona kamwe kutokana na magonjwa yao. Wapendwa wetu huenda wana ugonjwa usiotibika. Labda mume au mzazi ni mnyanyasaji au si mwaminifu. Kama ilivyokuwa kwa Ayubu, huenda marafiki zetu wametugeuka. Labda kuna matatizo kanisani ambayo yanaonekana hayawezekani kutatuliwa. Huenda ni jambo kama mtoto mchanga mwenye maumivu ya tumbo, au mtoto mwenye uchangamfu kupita kiasi. Labda tuna mafua tu na tunahisi kana kwamba kila kitu kinaenda vibaya. Orodha haina mwisho. Tunaweza kuelewa maneno ya wimbo huu.

Mpaka Dhoruba Ipite

Katika giza la usiku wa manane mara nyingi nimejificha uso wangu,
Dhoruba inapounguruma juu yangu, nami sina pa kujisitiri.
Katikati ya mlipuko wa ngurumo, Bwana mpendwa, sikia kilio changu,
Unilinde salama mpaka dhoruba ipite.

kiitikio:

Mpaka dhoruba ipite, mpaka ngurumo zisiwe tena,
Mpaka mawingu yatoweke milele angani;
Nishike imara, uniache nisimame katika kiganja cha mkono Wako,
Unilinde salama mpaka dhoruba ipite.

Mara nyingi Shetani alinong’ona, “Hakuna haja ya kujaribu,
Kwa maana huzuni haina mwisho, hakuna tumaini linalokuja”
Lakini najua uko pamoja nami, na kesho nitaamka
Mahali ambapo dhoruba hazitawahi kutia giza angani.

Usiku mrefu utakapokwisha na dhoruba zisipokuwepo tena,
Uniache nisimame mbele zako kwenye ufuo angavu na wenye amani;
Katika nchi ile ambako tufani haziji kamwe, Bwana, naomba
Nikae pamoja nawe dhoruba inapopita.

–na Mosie Lister

Nilipokuwa msichana mdogo, nilidhani mwandishi alikuwa akizungumzia ngurumo na radi. Niliogopa ngurumo na radi. Sasa ninaelewa kwamba alikuwa akizungumzia dhoruba za maisha tunazopitia. Mnamo Julai 14, 2013, nilijikuta ghafla hospitalini baada ya kupata mshtuko wa moyo uliotishia maisha yangu, uliosababishwa na mpasuko wa ghafla wa ateri ya moyo. Ilikuwa mshtuko mkubwa kwa mama wa miaka 40. Dhoruba ilikuwa ikivuma kwa nguvu, na ngurumo zilikuwa zikipiga. Hakukuwa na mahali pa kujificha dhidi ya hatari, kwa maana ilikuwa ndani yangu. Nilikuwa na moyo mmoja tu, na sikuweza kuutegemea. Je, ingetokea tena? Je, ningekufa? Basi watoto wangu wangekuwa bila mama.

Huu ulikuwa wimbo ambao ningeuomba katika giza la usiku wa manane niliposhindwa kulala, na hofu ilipotishia kunilemea. Uwepo wa Bwana ulikuwa halisi sana kwangu. Nilipitia dhoruba hii nikiwa na ufahamu mkubwa zaidi wa jinsi Mungu anavyojidhihirisha kwetu kwa undani zaidi tunapopitia nyakati ngumu. Ni lazima tuchague kujikabidhi kikamilifu Kwake, na kusema, “Si mapenzi yangu, bali yako yatimizwe.”

Wanafunzi walipokuwa baharini katika dhoruba, Yesu alikuwa pamoja nao. Yeye yuko pamoja nasi pia. Tunaweza kumtumaini. Hakuna kitakachotokea kisicholingana na mapenzi Yake. Hatuielewi daima sababu ya mambo kutokea, lakini hilo si tatizo. Mhubiri mmoja wa zamani alikuwa akikariri:

“Si sasa, bali katika miaka ijayo,
Huenda katika nchi iliyo bora zaidi
Tutaelewa maana ya machozi yetu,
Na huko, siku moja, tutaelewa.”

Ni muhimu sana tukubali yale ambayo Mungu anaruhusu yatokee maishani mwetu. Kukubali hakumaanishi kwamba hatufanyi chochote kuyahusu. Tutaenda kwa daktari ikihitajika. Tutawafikia wengine ili tupate faraja na ushauri. Bado tutakuwa na hisia za kila aina, lakini tunapaswa kuwa na amani. Hatuwezi kujifungia katika kujionea huruma na kuwa na mtazamo wa “maskini mimi.” Nasi twajua ya kuwa katika mambo yote Mungu hufanya kazi pamoja na wale wampendao katika kuwapatia mema, yaani, wale walioitwa kwa kusudi lake —Warumi 8:28. Ninaamini hivyo. Siwezi kuona mema kila wakati, lakini Mungu anaweza.

Maisha huwa magumu nyakati nyingine, lakini wimbo unasimulia wakati ambapo usiku mrefu utakuwa umekwisha, na dhoruba hazitakuwepo tena. Dada wapendwa, na tubaki waaminifu na kumtegemea sana Bwana katika dhoruba za maisha.

Kisha nikaona mbingu mpya na nchi mpya; kwa maana mbingu za kwanza na nchi ya kwanza zimekwisha kupita, wala hapana bahari tena. Nami, Yohana, nikauona mji ule mtakatifu, Yerusalemu mpya, ukishuka kutoka mbinguni kwa Mungu, umewekwa tayari kama bibi-arusi aliyepambwa kwa mumewe. Nikasikia sauti kubwa kutoka mbinguni ikisema, Tazama, maskani ya Mungu iko pamoja na wanadamu, naye atakaa pamoja nao, nao watakuwa watu wake, naye atakuwa Mungu wao. Naye Mungu atafuta kila chozi katika macho yao, wala mauti haitakuwapo tena; wala maombolezo, wala kilio, wala maumivu hayatakuwapo tena; kwa kuwa mambo ya kwanza yamekwisha kupita. Ufunuo 21:1-4.

Editor’s Note: Many of our readers may at first be convinced that this topic doesn’t pertain to them. If this is correct, we rejoice with you. However, before simply passing over this article we urge the reader to carefully read what is written here then start asking questions of family, friends, and acquaintances. We are hearing that especially the younger generation is being drawn into para-church events (such as concerts, seminars, Bible Schools, etc.) or special services at neighboring churches, which involve this type of content to one degree or another. Especially prominent are special music groups/concerts, ventriloquism, religious films, and skits. We wish to raise awareness on this issue and stimulate a discussion on the matter.

Religious drama—what is it?

A serious story by actors performing or impersonating any given dialogue in a theatrical manner, or an event of real life with emotional effects which are characteristics of a play, patterned after a religious theme. (American Heritage College Dictionary)

Is this something the church needs to be concerned about? It should be. It usually seems to get its beginning in extended “prayer and praise” services between Sunday school and church services. Or in special services other than on a Sunday morning. It can include such things as instrumental presentations, puppet shows, skits, plays, dances, and religious films.

Religious drama is not something new. It was introduced during the Dark Ages (A.D. 400 to 1200) as dramatic performances with religious themes known as “miracle plays.” These plays became so corrupt that the Catholic Church tried to put a stop to them, but to no avail. In 1242, the Passion play, a performance that depicts the death of Christ, started in Germany and it is still being performed around the world today.

An interesting observation, as we look back through time, is that religious drama was introduced during the darkest time of history (the Dark Ages), but the church emerged from this long era of moral decay through Spirit-filled, Bible-based, New Covenant-focused preaching of the Anabaptist Revival during the Reformation time period.

I. Why Drama Violates True Worship

a. Drama is a violation of the law of hearing.

In a spiritual world, seeing is not as important as hearing (2 Corinthians 4:18). The words hear, heareth, and heard are found over 1,000 times in the Bible. As a matter of fact, the whole Bible is God speaking to man. He wants mankind to hear! “Thus, saith the Lord” is a constant refrain throughout Scripture.

On Mount Sinai (Exodus 19:9), the people heard the message of God through His spokesman, Moses. God’s voice was frightening to them (Exodus 20:18-19) but hearing from Him was essential so that they “sin not.” In Exodus 20, God gave some detailed instructions of what the worship pattern was to be. Ye shall not make with me gods of silver, neither shall ye make unto you gods of gold –Exodus 20:23. These visual aids (idols) were a violation of God’s law of hearing. Through the eye gate comes the temptation to build idols. The altars that God did permit were to be plain and uncut (vss. 24-25). What they did see was not to distract from that which was heard from the altar! What is seen, especially immodesty, tends to be a distraction from what is heard (v. 26).

The preaching of Jesus appealed to the hearing: Who hath ears to hear, let him hear –Matthew 13:9. While He did not use visual aids like speakers do today, Jesus did use verbal aids (parables) as a tool to appeal to the hearing (Mat 13:18).

On the Mount of Transfiguration (Matthew 17), Peter wanted to reinvent the worship experience by building three shrines. He wanted something to see! But the voice in the clouds alerted the disciples to the importance of hearing (v. 5). Worship with visual aids is not endorsed by God!

Jesus said, Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life … The hour is coming, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God: and they that hear shall live. John 5:24-25. Salvation comes by hearing the Word of God, but only when one believes what is heard!

Paul raises some sobering questions: How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher? –Romans 10:14. He answers his own questions: So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God –Romans 10:17. God’s law to experience salvation is either by hearing God’s Word or by reading God’s Word!

In the 2nd and 3rd chapters of Revelation, Jesus repeats seven times: “He that hath an ear, let him hear.” Religious drama is superficial in that it appeals to the soulish part of man, not the spiritual part. The soulish part of man (emotions) can have a great time while the spirit within man remains untouched and unmoved. Satan uses the eye gate to distract man from his real heart issues.

Hebrews 11:6 tells us, “Faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen (or demonstrated).” Real faith comes to the human heart by hearing, not by demonstration. Therefore, religious drama borders on being anti-Christ because it is counterproductive to God’s law of hearing.

b. Drama is a violation of sincerity.

The Scriptures teach the importance of sincerity in all of life (1 Corinthians 5:8; 2 Corinthians 1:12, 2:17; Philippians 1:10). In maintaining our sincerity, it is important for each person to recognize that God has created us as unique individuals (Psalm 139:14-15). We are not and cannot be someone else! To try to be someone else violates our individual uniqueness. And, when one does so, he becomes insincere.

How does this connect with religious drama? Drama employs playacting. Jesus had a constant controversy with the Pharisees. They were constantly playacting, or pretending to be something that they were not. Jesus repeatedly called them hypocrites. The original Greek word means “play actor.”

The Pharisees’ sole motivation to pray in public was to be seen of men (Matthew 6:5-7). They were conscious of their audience, thus their performance. Jesus made it very clear that religious devotion was to be private, in “thy closet.” When a person who expresses his piety becomes more concerned about his performance than his message, he is no longer worshiping, but putting on a show! This can happen to preachers, quartets, choruses, etc. “Prayer walks” also usually fall into this same category of playacting.

When a person makes play-acting a regular habit, he becomes a hypocrite. He violates his own soul, because he injures his own uniqueness, which was given by God.

Jesus addressed the Pharisees as hypocrites seven times in Matthew 23. He informed them that they were walking dead men (Matthew 23:27-28). They had playacted for so long that they did not know the difference between the real and the unreal!

This deception is one reason that professional actors become such extremists about the issues of life. Professionally, they become increasingly detached from truth, sincerity, and reality. In such matters as ecology, animal rights, abortion, gay rights, and global warming, many of them have taken positions that are disconnected from the foundations of truth and are no longer sincere.

To pretend to pray or worship or to act out Bible characters in a play is not only insincere, but it borders on being sacrilegious. Imagine pretending to be Jesus in a play! To pretend to be Jesus is blasphemous because no Christian has ever come anywhere close to His perfection! Or, what about pretending to be the devil? Why, pray tell, would anyone who is sincerely following the teachings of Jesus take upon himself the embodiment of evil? A. W. Tozer concludes, “Playacting embodies a gross moral contradiction in that it calls a lie to the service of the truth.”

Religious drama, those who involve themselves in it, and for that matter those who approve of the very hypocrisy that Jesus condemned, are frauds. The Holy Spirit does not honor pretense and showmanship!

The reason multitudes followed Jesus was that His sincerity was so refreshing in comparison to the constant playacting of the Pharisees.

II. Practical Reasons Why Religious Drama is a Menace

a. Religious drama demoralizes reverence for God.

A person who pretends to be Jesus Christ or any other Bible character erodes his reverence for the Lord. When one playacts enough, his fear of God slowly dies within. After all, if a person can pretend to be equal to Christ, what is the need for reverence to a higher being? The Pharisees did not even suspect that they were walking dead men (Matthew 23:27).

b. Religious drama identifies worship with the theatrical world.

Hollywood has effectively proven that the theatrical world cannot produce godly moral values. Pairing a man and a woman as a pretend husband and wife breaks down the sanctity of marriage. The theatrical world also endorses courtship practices that violate the biblical standards of purity. The theatrical world has become the pacesetter of moral standards in today’s society, and many are following their ungodly pattern.

c. Religious drama does not satisfy the inner man.

When a person’s senses are titillated by outward show, the emotions keep seeking a new high and another feel-good worship experience. It creates a desire within to see yet another show that is more satisfying than the previous one. The emotions are having fun, but the inner man starves and slowly dies because the heart and mind have not been fed with real substance.

d. Religious drama ruins the preacher.

Drama is a friend to the lazy preacher. He no longer needs to: Study to shew thyself approved unto God… –2 Timothy 2:15. It requires no Holy Spirit unction to substitute a play for the sermon. Instead of commanding men to be “the light of the world,” he commands them to “lower the lights, please!” When the projector replaces the prophet, the primary means for man to find salvation is lost (1 Corinthians 1:21).

“As long as the preacher can fall back upon entertainment, the pressure that makes preachers will be wanting. The habit and rhythm which belongs to great preaching will be missing from their ministry.” –A. W. Tozer.

The use of religious drama will doom the preacher to mediocrity! The menace that we face today is that as religious drama multiplies, the heaven-sent revivals of the past will become extinct.

e. True worship will be viewed as inferior.

By using drama in a worship service, churches are training the youth to think that true worship is just another inferior form of amusement. When worship and drama are fused into one, worship is reduced to the lowest common denominator. The danger is that the next generation will not know what true worship is!

III. Patterns of True Worship

a. Prayer

Prayer is a vast subject, a worship pattern that too many times remains untapped. Public prayer in the congregational life is squeezed into our man-made time constraints.

In the early church, public prayers held a consistent pattern in their worship experiences. There was public prayer immediately after Christ’s ascension (Acts 1:14) and the first ordination (Acts 1:24). And they continued stedfastly … in prayers –Acts 2:42. No spirit of apathy was present! Prayer meetings were an evangelistic tool, a means of implementing the fear of God, and a great unifier for the whole church (Acts 2:41-44).

Peter and John attended a midafternoon prayer meeting (Acts 3:1). (Say, fellow saint, when was the last time that you attended a midafternoon prayer meeting?) Their prayer meeting had seismic results (Acts 4:31)! The power and presence of the Holy Spirit in our worship services brings results!

Prayer meeting attendance was not a monthly or a bimonthly option (Act 6:4)! When Peter was in prison, they had a voluntary, round-the-clock, prayer chain (Acts 12:5). They laid hands on their missionaries and prayed for them (Acts 13:3). They gathered at the river for a prayer meeting (Acts 16:13). Please note: this gathering at the river was not for the purpose of any kind of water sports; it was a prayer meeting! They gathered …prayer was wont to be made… –Acts 16:13. They understood that wherever Christians happened to meet, it was a normal activity to pray together.

b. Preaching

Preaching is a worship pattern that dates back to the time of Jonah (Jonah 3:2) and Moses (Acts 15:21). In the Old Testament, preaching was God’s pattern for communicating the will of God to man. When Jesus came on the scene, …[He] came into Galilee, preaching the gospel of the kingdom of God –Mark 1:14. He used the same worship pattern. Jesus used parables as verbal illustrations (not visual ones), which caught the attention of His hearers.

Near the end of His ministry, Jesus extended preaching as a worship pattern to future generations and all world cultures: …Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature –Mark 16:15.

Paul’s call was to preach the gospel (1 Corinthians 1:17-21). Preaching was not to be embellished by the cleverness of man. It pleased God to use the foolishness and simplicity of preaching to minister salvation to those who dared to believe. For this reason, preaching needs to be the focal point of every worship service. Praise services, concerts, and musicals are robbers of time that instead ought to be invested in listening to Holy Spirit-inspired preaching. When religious drama is used to present truth, it bypasses God’s ordained pattern of bringing the message of salvation to man.

Blessed is he that readeth, and they that hear the words of this prophecy, and keep those things which are written therein… –Revelation 1:3. God’s method of communication is the written or spoken Word. Not a picture! Not a play! Not a pageant!

c. Singing

The New Testament leaves no hint of professional singers, choirs, or musical performances. Meaningful singing requires participation by all, and an intelligent involvement of the mind (1 Corinthians 14:15). The context clearly implies that worship or singing is not only an individual experience; it is for the edification of all present. Soloists, who tend to be self-exalting, prohibit the remainder of the audience from entering into a corporate worship experience.

Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord –Colossians 3:16. Spiritual songs move the heart, while soulish songs move the feet and the emotions. Our singing is “to the Lord.” Preaching is from God to man, but singing is from man to God, containing expressions of praise, adoration, honor, and thanksgiving. Singing is for worship, not for entertainment.

Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord –Ephesians 5:19. Spirit-filled singing brings mutual edification, inspiration, and encouragement. Participation in singing has a way of ministering to heartfelt needs, where other methods fail. “Making melody in your heart” involves the accompaniment of the heart. External instrumentation tends to focus on a person’s abilities rather than on the heart. If our singing is not accompanied by our hearts, it becomes just another pharisaical worship show.

Old Testament worship was acceptable to God; nevertheless, it was also ritualistic with animal sacrifices, burning incense, using musical instruments, and dancing before the Lord. New Testament worship, however, is quite different. Jesus teaches us that we …must worship him in spirit and in truth –John 4:24. The spirit of worship replaces the rituals. When we move from intrinsic methods of worship to extrinsic methods, we violate the New Testament “spirit” of worship. Our worship is not to be stimulated by the extrinsic, but rather by the Holy Spirit (Ephesians 5:18).

IV. Essence of True Worship

When Jesus met the woman at the well, she expressed a concern about His change in worship format (John 4:20). She was concerned about how her fathers worshiped. In other words, “this is the way that we have always done it!” Every generation of worshipers must guard against formalistic worship.

There are two attitudes that affect true worship in a wrong way:

  • Formal –becoming so accustomed to the way that we have always done it, that we end up merely going through the motions and losing focus on the One being worshiped.
  • Casual –becoming so aloof to any form of worship that the One being worshiped becomes obscured by indifference.

Both formal and casual worship styles have one root problem: lack of reverence for God!

The fathers of the woman at the well had lost both the focus and the concept of worship: “Ye worship ye know not what” (John 4:22a). Jesus clearly indicated that worship is not thoughtless: “We know what we worship” (4:22b). True worship is the exercise of our mind and intellect. True worship has something to offer: “Salvation is of Jesus” (4:22c). It is life-changing!

The worship location is not as important as the attitude (John 4:23). The emphasis that Jesus gives is not on the outward ceremony, but on the state of the mind and spirit.

God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth –John 4:24. Note the word must! The only acceptable worship is in spirit and in truth. Our attitude must be such that it is in harmony with the Spirit of God. True worship also involves our response to truth. If our spirits are not responding to truth, we are not worshiping! If our minds are somewhere else, or on anything else, our worship is merely cold, dead ritualism!

Conclusion

In the observation of the principles of Scripture, it is clear that religious drama is not God’s pattern to bring faith and life into the human soul!

The pattern of true worship in the New Testament is to gather to hear the Word preached; to pray together and for each other; and to sing songs, hymns, and spiritual songs.

The temptation to introduce new things to worship is very real today. The appeal of Jesus is to worship in spirit and in truth. When each of us sincerely does his part to keep worship services meaningful and spiritual, it reduces the temptation to reintroduce the formal (“the way our fathers worshiped”) or to introduce the casual (any new irreverent worship).

宗教戏剧——是什么？

由演员以戏剧方式演出或模仿某段对话的严肃故事，或现实生活中具有戏剧特征、带有情感效果的事件，并以宗教主题为范本。（《美国传统学院词典》）

这是教会需要关注的事吗？是的。它通常似乎始于主日学与教会礼拜之间延长的“祷告与赞美”聚会，或主日早晨以外的特别聚会。内容可能包括器乐演奏、木偶戏、短剧、戏剧、舞蹈和宗教电影。

宗教戏剧并非新事物。它在黑暗时代（公元400年至1200年）以宗教主题戏剧表演的形式出现，这些表演被称为“奇迹剧”。这些戏剧后来变得如此腐败，以致天主教会试图制止，却毫无成效。1242年，描绘基督之死的受难剧在德国兴起，至今仍在世界各地演出。

回顾历史时有一个有趣的观察：宗教戏剧是在历史最黑暗的时期（黑暗时代）引入的，但在宗教改革时期，教会借着重洗派复兴运动中充满圣灵、以圣经为根基、以新约为核心的讲道，走出了这段漫长的道德衰败时期。

I. 戏剧为何违背真正的敬拜

a. 戏剧违背聆听的法则。

在属灵的世界里，看见没有聆听那么重要（哥林多后书4:18）。圣经中“听”“听见”和“听了”等词出现了一千多次。事实上，整本圣经都是神向人说话。祂要人类听见！“主如此说”这句话贯穿整本圣经，反复出现。

在西奈山上（出埃及记19:9），百姓借着神的代言人摩西听见了神的信息。神的声音使他们害怕（出埃及记20:18-19），但听见祂的话至关重要，使他们“免得犯罪”。出埃及记20章中，神详细指示了敬拜应当遵循的模式。你们不可与我一同做什么神像，也不可为自己做金像。——出埃及记20:23。这些视觉辅助物（偶像）违背了神聆听的法则。眼目之门带来建造偶像的试探。神所许可的祭坛必须朴素，不可凿过（24-25节）。他们所看见的，不应使他们分心，不去听祭坛上所传讲的话！人所看见的，尤其是不端庄的衣着，往往会使人分心，无法专注聆听（26节）。

耶稣的讲道诉诸聆听：有耳可听的，就应当听！——马太福音13:9。祂没有像今天的讲员那样使用视觉辅助物，却使用了口头辅助方式（比喻），以此让人专心聆听（马太福音13:18）。

在登山变像时（马太福音17章），彼得想要重新塑造敬拜体验，建造三座棚。他想要有东西可以看！但云彩中的声音提醒门徒聆听的重要性（5节）。神并不认可借助视觉辅助物的敬拜！

耶稣说：我实实在在地告诉你们，那听我话、又信差我来者的，就有永生……时候将到，现在就是了，死人要听见神儿子的声音，听见的人就要活了。约翰福音5:24-25。救恩借着听见神的话而来，但只有人在所听见的话上相信时才如此！

保罗提出了一些发人深省的问题：然而，人未曾信他，怎能求他呢？未曾听见他，怎能信他呢？没有传道的，怎能听见呢？——罗马书10:14。他自己回答了这些问题：可见信道是从听道来的，听道是从神的话来的。——罗马书10:17。神所定、使人经历救恩的法则，就是听神的话或读神的话！

在《启示录》第2章和第3章中，耶稣七次重复说：“有耳可听的，就应当听。”宗教戏剧流于表面，因为它诉诸人的属魂部分，而不是属灵部分。人的属魂部分（情感）可以尽情享受，而人里面的灵却毫无触动，无动于衷。撒但利用眼目之门，使人偏离自己真正的内心问题。

希伯来书11:6告诉我们：“信就是所盼望之事的实底，是未见之事（或未展示之事）的确据。”真正的信心是借着聆听进入人的内心，而不是借着展示。因此，宗教戏剧近乎敌基督，因为它与神聆听的法则背道而驰。

b. 戏剧违背真诚。

圣经教导我们，人生各方面都要真诚（哥林多前书5:8；哥林多后书1:12，2:17；腓立比书1:10）。要保持真诚，每个人都必须明白，神创造我们各有独特之处（诗篇139:14-15）。我们不是、也不可能成为别人！试图成为别人，就是违背我们个人的独特性。人若如此行，就变得不真诚。

这与宗教戏剧有什么关系？戏剧包含表演。耶稣与法利赛人之间不断发生争论。他们一直在演戏，假装自己是他们实际上并非的样子。耶稣一次又一次称他们为假冒为善的人。这个希腊原文词的意思是“戏剧演员”。

法利赛人在公众面前祷告，唯一的动机就是要让人看见（马太福音6:5-7）。他们在意观众，因此在意自己的表演。耶稣清楚指出，虔诚的敬拜应当私下进行，在“你的内室”里。一个表达虔诚的人若比起信息本身更关心自己的表现，他就不再是在敬拜，而是在作秀！传道人、四重唱团、合唱团等都可能如此。“祷告漫步”通常也属于这种假装表演。

一个人若把表演变成习惯，就会成为假冒为善的人。他违背自己的灵魂，因为他损害了神所赐予自己的独特性。

耶稣在马太福音23章七次称法利赛人为假冒为善的人。祂告诉他们，他们是行走的死人（马太福音23:27-28）。他们演戏演了太久，甚至分不清真实与虚假！

这种欺骗是职业演员在生活议题上变得如此极端的原因之一。在职业生涯中，他们越来越脱离真理、真诚和现实。在生态、动物权利、堕胎、同性恋权利和全球变暖等问题上，他们当中许多人所持的立场已经脱离真理的根基，不再真诚。

假装祷告或敬拜，或在戏剧中扮演圣经人物，不仅不真诚，而且近乎亵渎。想象一下在戏剧中假扮耶稣！假扮耶稣是亵渎，因为没有基督徒曾接近过祂的完全！或者，假扮魔鬼又如何？请问，一个真心遵从耶稣教导的人，为什么要让自己成为邪恶的化身？A. W. 陶泽总结说：“表演包含着严重的道德矛盾，因为它让谎言为真理效劳。”

宗教戏剧、参与其中的人，以及赞同耶稣所谴责的虚伪的人，都是骗子。圣灵不会悦纳伪装和作秀！

众人跟随耶稣的原因，是与法利赛人不断的假意表演相比，祂的真诚令人耳目一新。

II. 宗教戏剧构成威胁的实际原因

a. 宗教戏剧削弱人对神的敬畏。

假扮耶稣基督或其他圣经人物的人，会削弱自己对主的敬畏。一个人表演得够多，心中的敬畏神之情就会渐渐消失。毕竟，如果一个人能假装与基督平起平坐，又何必敬畏更高的存在？法利赛人甚至没有意识到自己是行走的死人（马太福音23:27）。

b. 宗教戏剧把敬拜与戏剧界联系起来。

好莱坞已经充分证明，戏剧界无法培养敬虔的道德价值观。让一男一女假扮夫妻，会破坏婚姻的神圣性。戏剧界也认可违反圣经纯洁标准的恋爱方式。戏剧界已经成为当今社会道德标准的领头者，许多人正追随它们不敬虔的模式。

c. 宗教戏剧无法满足内里的人。

一个人的感官若被外在的表演撩动，情感就会不断寻求新的高潮和另一种令人愉悦的敬拜体验。它会在人里面产生渴望，想看一场比之前更令人满足的表演。情感固然乐在其中，但内里的人却挨饿并渐渐枯死，因为心灵和思想没有得到真正实质的喂养。

d. 宗教戏剧毁坏传道人。

戏剧是懒惰传道人的帮手。他不再需要：你当竭力在神面前得蒙喜悦……——提摩太后书2:15。用戏剧代替讲道，不需要圣灵的恩膏。他不再吩咐人“作世上的光”，反而吩咐他们“请把灯光调暗！”当放映机取代先知，人得救的主要途径就失去了（哥林多前书1:21）。

“只要传道人还能依靠娱乐，促使传道人产生的压力就会消失。伟大讲道所具备的习惯和节奏，将从他们的事奉中消失。”——A. W. 陶泽。

使用宗教戏剧会使传道人注定平庸！我们今天面临的威胁是，随着宗教戏剧不断增加，过去那些从天而来的复兴将会绝迹。

e. 真正的敬拜会被视为低劣。

教会在敬拜聚会中使用戏剧，就是在训练年轻人认为真正的敬拜不过是另一种低劣的娱乐方式。敬拜与戏剧一旦融合为一，敬拜就被降低到最浅薄的层次。危险在于，下一代将不知道真正的敬拜是什么！

III. 真正敬拜的模式

a. 祷告

祷告是一个广阔的主题，也是一种常常未被充分运用的敬拜模式。会众生活中的公开祷告，被挤压进我们人为设定的时间限制之中。

在早期教会，公开祷告在他们的敬拜中始终有固定的模式。基督升天后立即有公开祷告（使徒行传1:14），第一次按立时也有公开祷告（使徒行传1:24）。他们都恒心……祈祷。——使徒行传2:42。当时没有冷淡漠然的心态！祷告会是传福音的工具，是使人敬畏神的途径，也是整个教会极好的合一之道（使徒行传2:41-44）。

彼得和约翰参加了下午中段的祷告会（使徒行传3:1）。（请问，亲爱的圣徒，你上一次参加下午中段的祷告会是什么时候？）他们的祷告会带来了震撼性的结果（使徒行传4:31）！敬拜聚会中圣灵的能力和同在会带来果效！

参加祷告会并非每月或每两个月一次的选择（使徒行传6:4）！彼得被关在监狱时，他们自发地昼夜不停地接力祷告（使徒行传12:5）。他们为宣教士按手并为他们祷告（使徒行传13:3）。他们聚集在河边举行祷告会（使徒行传16:13）。请注意：他们在河边聚集不是为了任何水上活动，而是为了祷告会！他们聚集在那里，……素常有一个祷告的地方……——使徒行传16:13。他们明白，基督徒无论在哪里相遇，一同祷告都是很自然的事。

b. 讲道

讲道这一敬拜模式，可以追溯到约拿（约拿书3:2）和摩西的时代（使徒行传15:21）。在旧约中，讲道是神向人传达神旨意的模式。耶稣出来传道时，……到了加利利，宣传神的福音。——马可福音1:14。祂采用了同样的敬拜模式。耶稣用比喻作口头说明（而非视觉说明），吸引听众的注意。

在事奉接近尾声时，耶稣把讲道这一敬拜模式延伸到后世和世界各地的文化：……你们往普天下去，传福音给万民听。——马可福音16:15。

保罗蒙召传福音（哥林多前书1:17-21）。讲道不应以人的巧智加以修饰。神乐意使用讲道的愚拙和简朴，把救恩传给那些敢于相信的人。因此，讲道必须成为每场敬拜聚会的焦点。赞美聚会、音乐会和音乐剧都占用时间，而这些时间本应投入聆听受圣灵启发的讲道。使用宗教戏剧来呈现真理，就是绕过神所设立、把救恩信息带给人的模式。

念这书上预言的，和那些听见又遵守其中所记载的，都是有福的……——启示录1:3。神传达信息的方式是书写或宣讲的话语。不是图画！不是戏剧！不是盛大演出！

c. 歌唱

新约没有留下任何专业歌手、合唱团或音乐表演的迹象。有意义的歌唱需要所有人参与，并且需要思想上的明白领会（哥林多前书14:15）。上下文清楚表明，敬拜或歌唱不只是个人的体验；它是为了造就所有在场的人。独唱者往往会高举自己，使其余听众无法参与共同敬拜。

当用各样的智慧，把基督的道理丰丰富富地存在心里，用诗章、颂词、灵歌彼此教导，互相劝戒，心被恩感歌颂神。——歌罗西书3:16。属灵的诗歌感动人心，属魂的歌曲则带动人的脚步和情感。我们的歌唱是“归给主的”。讲道是神向人说话，歌唱则是人向神说话，其中包含赞美、敬拜、尊荣和感谢。歌唱是为了敬拜，不是为了娱乐。

当用诗章、颂词、灵歌彼此对说，口唱心和地赞美主。——以弗所书5:19。被圣灵充满的歌唱能带来彼此造就、激励和鼓舞。参与歌唱能满足内心深处的需要，而其他方法却做不到。“心被恩感歌颂”意味着心也一同伴奏。外在的乐器往往使人关注一个人的技巧，而不是内心。如果歌唱没有我们的心相伴，就会成为另一场法利赛式的敬拜表演。

旧约敬拜蒙神悦纳；然而，它也带有仪式性，包括献动物为祭、焚香、使用乐器和在主面前跳舞。但新约敬拜则截然不同。耶稣教导我们，……必须用心灵和诚实拜他。——约翰福音4:24。敬拜的属灵实质取代了仪式。当我们从内在的敬拜方式转向外在的敬拜方式时，就违背了新约敬拜的“属灵”实质。我们的敬拜不应由外在事物激发，而应由圣灵激发（以弗所书5:18）。

IV. 真正敬拜的实质

耶稣在井旁遇见那妇人时，她对祂改变敬拜方式表示担忧（约翰福音4:20）。她在意的是她祖先如何敬拜。换句话说，“我们一直都是这样做的！”每一代敬拜者都必须提防形式主义的敬拜。

有两种态度会以错误的方式影响真正的敬拜：

  • 形式主义——过于习惯我们一贯的做法，结果只是照章行事，并失去对敬拜对象的专注。
  • 随便——对任何形式的敬拜都漠不关心，以致敬拜对象被冷漠掩盖。

形式主义和随便的敬拜方式都有一个根本问题：缺乏对神的敬畏！

井旁妇人的祖先既失去了敬拜的焦点，也失去了敬拜的观念：“你们所拜的，你们不知道”（约翰福音4:22上）。耶稣清楚指出，敬拜不是不假思索的：“我们所拜的，我们知道”（约翰福音4:22中）。真正的敬拜是运用我们的思想和理智。真正的敬拜有所献上：“救恩是从耶稣来的”（约翰福音4:22下）。它会改变生命！

敬拜的地点不如态度重要（约翰福音4:23）。耶稣强调的不是外在仪式，而是心思和灵的状态。

神是个灵，所以拜他的，必须用心灵和诚实拜他。——约翰福音4:24。请留意“必须”这个词！唯一蒙悦纳的敬拜，就是用心灵和诚实敬拜。我们的态度必须与神的灵和谐一致。真正的敬拜也包含我们对真理的回应。若我们的灵没有回应真理，我们就不是在敬拜！若我们的思想在别处，或想着其他事，我们的敬拜就只是冷淡、死气沉沉的仪式主义！

结论

遵循圣经的原则就会清楚看出，宗教戏剧并非神把信心和生命带进人灵魂里的模式！

新约中真正的敬拜模式是聚集起来聆听讲道，彼此一同祷告并为彼此祷告，以及歌唱诗歌、颂词和灵歌。

今天，人们确实很容易受到诱惑，想在敬拜中引入新事物。耶稣呼召人用心灵和诚实敬拜。当我们每个人都真诚地尽自己的本分，使敬拜聚会保持有意义且属灵，就能减少重新引入形式主义（“我们祖先敬拜的方式”）或引入随便的做法（任何新的不敬虔敬拜）的诱惑。

We all have a story. Some feel like Job sometimes. Some have lost parents, or partners, or children, or siblings, or friends. Some suffer from severe illness. Some will never recover from their illnesses. Our loved ones might have a terminal illness. Maybe a husband or parent is abusive or unfaithful. Like Job, our friends might have turned against us. Maybe there are problems in the church that seem impossible to fix. It could be something like a colicky baby, or a hyper child. Maybe we just have a cold and are feeling like everything is going wrong. The list is endless. We can relate to the words of this song.

Till the Storm Passes By

In the dark of the midnight have I oft hid my face,
While the storm howls above me, and there’s no hiding place.
‘Mid the crash of the thunder, Precious Lord, hear my cry,
Keep me safe till the storm passes by.

refrain:

Till the storm passes over, till the thunder sounds no more,
Till the clouds roll forever from the sky;
Hold me fast, let me stand in the hollow of Thy hand,
Keep me safe till the storm passes by.

Many times Satan whispered, “There is no need to try,
For there’s no end of sorrow, there’s no hope by and by”
But I know Thou art with me, and tomorrow I’ll rise
Where the storms never darken the skies.

When the long night has ended and the storms come no more,
Let me stand in Thy presence on the bright peaceful shore;
In that land where the tempest, never comes, Lord, may I
Dwell with Thee when the storm passes by.

–by Mosie Lister

When I was a little girl, I thought the author was referring to thunderstorms. I was afraid of thunderstorms. Now I understand that he was referring to the storms of life we go through. On July 14, 2013, I suddenly ended up in the hospital with a life-threatening heart attack caused by a spontaneous coronary artery dissection. What a shock for a 40-year-old mother. The storm was howling, and the thunder was crashing. There was no hiding place from the danger, for it was within me. I only had one heart and it could not be trusted. What if it happens again? Would I die? Then my children would be motherless.

This song was one I’d pray in the dark of the midnight when I couldn’t sleep, and fear threatened to overwhelm me. The Lord’s presence was very real to me. I came through this storm with a greater awareness of how God reveals Himself to us in a deeper way when we are going through hard times. We must choose to yield ourselves completely to Him, and say, “Not my will, but Thine be done.”

When the disciples were out on the sea in the storm, Jesus was with them. He is with us too. We can trust Him. Nothing will happen that is not according to His will. We do not always understand why things happen, but that’s okay. An old preacher used to quote:

“Not now, but in the coming years,
It may be in the better land
We’ll read the meaning of our tears,
And there, sometime, we’ll understand.”

It is so important that we accept what God allows in our lives. Accepting does not mean we don’t do anything about it. We will go to the doctor if necessary. We will reach out to others for comfort and council. We will still have all kinds of feelings, but we should have peace. We can’t wallow in self-pity and have a “poor me” attitude. And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose –Romans 8:28. I believe that. I can’t always see the good, but God does.

Life is hard sometimes, but the song tells about the time when the long night has ended, and the storms come no more. Dear sisters, let’s remain faithful and lean hard on the Lord through the storms of life.

Jusqu’à ce que la tempête passe

Dans l’obscurité de minuit, souvent j’ai caché mon visage,
Tandis que l’orage grondait au-dessus de moi, sans aucun abri.
Au milieu du fracas du tonnerre, Seigneur précieux, entends mon cri,
Garde-moi en sûreté jusqu’à ce que la tempête passe.

Refrain :

Jusqu’à ce que la tempête soit passée, jusqu’à ce que le tonnerre ne résonne plus,
Jusqu’à ce que les nuages aient disparu à jamais du ciel ;
Tiens-moi fermement, laisse-moi me tenir dans le creux de ta main,
Garde-moi en sûreté jusqu’à ce que la tempête passe.

Bien des fois, Satan m’a murmuré : « Inutile d’essayer,
Car le chagrin n’a pas de fin, et il n’y a aucun espoir pour l’avenir. »
Mais je sais que tu es avec moi, et demain je me relèverai,
Là où les tempêtes n’assombrissent jamais le ciel.

Quand la longue nuit sera finie et que les tempêtes ne reviendront plus,
Laisse-moi me tenir en ta présence, sur le rivage paisible et lumineux ;
Dans ce pays où jamais ne vient la tempête, Seigneur, puissé-je
Habiter avec toi lorsque la tempête sera passée.

– de Mosie Lister

Quand j’étais petite, je pensais que l’auteur parlait des orages. J’avais peur des orages. Maintenant, je comprends qu’il parlait des tempêtes de la vie que nous traversons. Le 14 juillet 2013, je me suis soudain retrouvée à l’hôpital, victime d’une crise cardiaque potentiellement mortelle causée par une dissection spontanée d’une artère coronaire. Quel choc pour une mère de 40 ans ! La tempête faisait rage et le tonnerre grondait. Il n’y avait aucun refuge contre le danger, car il se trouvait en moi. Je n’avais qu’un seul cœur, et on ne pouvait pas lui faire confiance. Et si cela se reproduisait ? Allais-je mourir ? Mes enfants se retrouveraient alors sans mère.

Je priais souvent avec ce cantique dans l’obscurité de minuit, lorsque je n’arrivais pas à dormir et que la peur menaçait de m’envahir. La présence du Seigneur était bien réelle pour moi. J’ai traversé cette tempête en prenant davantage conscience de la manière dont Dieu se révèle à nous plus profondément lorsque nous traversons des moments difficiles. Nous devons choisir de nous abandonner entièrement à lui et dire : « Que ma volonté ne se fasse pas, mais la tienne. »

Lorsque les disciples étaient en mer pendant la tempête, Jésus était avec eux. Il est aussi avec nous. Nous pouvons lui faire confiance. Rien n’arrivera qui ne soit conforme à sa volonté. Nous ne comprenons pas toujours pourquoi certaines choses arrivent, mais ce n’est pas grave. Un vieux prédicateur avait l’habitude de citer ces vers :

« Pas maintenant, mais dans les années à venir,
Peut-être dans le meilleur des pays,
Nous comprendrons le sens de nos larmes,
Et là, un jour, nous comprendrons. »

Il est si important que nous acceptions ce que Dieu permet dans nos vies. Accepter ne signifie pas que nous ne faisons rien pour y remédier. Nous irons chez le médecin si nécessaire. Nous chercherons auprès d’autres personnes du réconfort et des conseils. Nous éprouverons toutes sortes de sentiments, mais nous devrions avoir la paix. Nous ne pouvons pas nous complaire dans l’apitoiement sur nous-mêmes et adopter une attitude de « pauvre de moi ». Et nous savons que toutes choses concourent au bien de ceux qui aiment Dieu, de ceux qui sont appelés selon son dessein – Romains 8:28. Je le crois. Je ne vois pas toujours le bien, mais Dieu, lui, le voit.

La vie est parfois difficile, mais le chant parle du moment où la longue nuit sera terminée et où les tempêtes ne reviendront plus. Chères sœurs, restons fidèles et appuyons-nous de tout notre poids sur le Seigneur au milieu des tempêtes de la vie.

Et je vis un nouveau ciel et une nouvelle terre ; car le premier ciel et la première terre avaient disparu, et la mer n’était plus. Et moi, Jean, je vis la ville sainte, la nouvelle Jérusalem, qui descendait du ciel, d’auprès de Dieu, préparée comme une épouse parée pour son époux. Et j’entendis du ciel une voix forte qui disait : Voici le tabernacle de Dieu avec les hommes ! Il habitera avec eux, et ils seront son peuple, et Dieu lui-même sera avec eux, et sera leur Dieu. Et Dieu essuiera toute larme de leurs yeux ; la mort ne sera plus, et il n’y aura plus ni deuil, ni cri, ni douleur, car les premières choses ont disparu. Apocalypse 21:1-4.
