Editor’s Note: Many of our readers may at first be convinced that this topic doesn’t pertain to them. If this is correct, we rejoice with you. However, before simply passing over this article we urge the reader to carefully read what is written here then start asking questions of family, friends, and acquaintances. We are hearing that especially the younger generation is being drawn into para-church events (such as concerts, seminars, Bible Schools, etc.) or special services at neighboring churches, which involve this type of content to one degree or another. Especially prominent are special music groups/concerts, ventriloquism, religious films, and skits. We wish to raise awareness on this issue and stimulate a discussion on the matter.

Religious drama—what is it?

A serious story by actors performing or impersonating any given dialogue in a theatrical manner, or an event of real life with emotional effects which are characteristics of a play, patterned after a religious theme. (American Heritage College Dictionary)

Is this something the church needs to be concerned about? It should be. It usually seems to get its beginning in extended “prayer and praise” services between Sunday school and church services. Or in special services other than on a Sunday morning. It can include such things as instrumental presentations, puppet shows, skits, plays, dances, and religious films.

Religious drama is not something new. It was introduced during the Dark Ages (A.D. 400 to 1200) as dramatic performances with religious themes known as “miracle plays.” These plays became so corrupt that the Catholic Church tried to put a stop to them, but to no avail. In 1242, the Passion play, a performance that depicts the death of Christ, started in Germany and it is still being performed around the world today.

An interesting observation, as we look back through time, is that religious drama was introduced during the darkest time of history (the Dark Ages), but the church emerged from this long era of moral decay through Spirit-filled, Bible-based, New Covenant-focused preaching of the Anabaptist Revival during the Reformation time period.

I. Why Drama Violates True Worship

a. Drama is a violation of the law of hearing.

In a spiritual world, seeing is not as important as hearing (2 Corinthians 4:18). The words hear, heareth, and heard are found over 1,000 times in the Bible. As a matter of fact, the whole Bible is God speaking to man. He wants mankind to hear! “Thus, saith the Lord” is a constant refrain throughout Scripture.

On Mount Sinai (Exodus 19:9), the people heard the message of God through His spokesman, Moses. God’s voice was frightening to them (Exodus 20:18-19) but hearing from Him was essential so that they “sin not.” In Exodus 20, God gave some detailed instructions of what the worship pattern was to be. Ye shall not make with me gods of silver, neither shall ye make unto you gods of gold –Exodus 20:23. These visual aids (idols) were a violation of God’s law of hearing. Through the eye gate comes the temptation to build idols. The altars that God did permit were to be plain and uncut (vss. 24-25). What they did see was not to distract from that which was heard from the altar! What is seen, especially immodesty, tends to be a distraction from what is heard (v. 26).

The preaching of Jesus appealed to the hearing: Who hath ears to hear, let him hear –Matthew 13:9. While He did not use visual aids like speakers do today, Jesus did use verbal aids (parables) as a tool to appeal to the hearing (Mat 13:18).

On the Mount of Transfiguration (Matthew 17), Peter wanted to reinvent the worship experience by building three shrines. He wanted something to see! But the voice in the clouds alerted the disciples to the importance of hearing (v. 5). Worship with visual aids is not endorsed by God!

Jesus said, Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life … The hour is coming, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God: and they that hear shall live. John 5:24-25. Salvation comes by hearing the Word of God, but only when one believes what is heard!

Paul raises some sobering questions: How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher? –Romans 10:14. He answers his own questions: So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God –Romans 10:17. God’s law to experience salvation is either by hearing God’s Word or by reading God’s Word!

In the 2nd and 3rd chapters of Revelation, Jesus repeats seven times: “He that hath an ear, let him hear.” Religious drama is superficial in that it appeals to the soulish part of man, not the spiritual part. The soulish part of man (emotions) can have a great time while the spirit within man remains untouched and unmoved. Satan uses the eye gate to distract man from his real heart issues.

Hebrews 11:6 tells us, “Faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen (or demonstrated).” Real faith comes to the human heart by hearing, not by demonstration. Therefore, religious drama borders on being anti-Christ because it is counterproductive to God’s law of hearing.

b. Drama is a violation of sincerity.

The Scriptures teach the importance of sincerity in all of life (1 Corinthians 5:8; 2 Corinthians 1:12, 2:17; Philippians 1:10). In maintaining our sincerity, it is important for each person to recognize that God has created us as unique individuals (Psalm 139:14-15). We are not and cannot be someone else! To try to be someone else violates our individual uniqueness. And, when one does so, he becomes insincere.

How does this connect with religious drama? Drama employs playacting. Jesus had a constant controversy with the Pharisees. They were constantly playacting, or pretending to be something that they were not. Jesus repeatedly called them hypocrites. The original Greek word means “play actor.”

The Pharisees’ sole motivation to pray in public was to be seen of men (Matthew 6:5-7). They were conscious of their audience, thus their performance. Jesus made it very clear that religious devotion was to be private, in “thy closet.” When a person who expresses his piety becomes more concerned about his performance than his message, he is no longer worshiping, but putting on a show! This can happen to preachers, quartets, choruses, etc. “Prayer walks” also usually fall into this same category of playacting.

When a person makes play-acting a regular habit, he becomes a hypocrite. He violates his own soul, because he injures his own uniqueness, which was given by God.

Jesus addressed the Pharisees as hypocrites seven times in Matthew 23. He informed them that they were walking dead men (Matthew 23:27-28). They had playacted for so long that they did not know the difference between the real and the unreal!

This deception is one reason that professional actors become such extremists about the issues of life. Professionally, they become increasingly detached from truth, sincerity, and reality. In such matters as ecology, animal rights, abortion, gay rights, and global warming, many of them have taken positions that are disconnected from the foundations of truth and are no longer sincere.

To pretend to pray or worship or to act out Bible characters in a play is not only insincere, but it borders on being sacrilegious. Imagine pretending to be Jesus in a play! To pretend to be Jesus is blasphemous because no Christian has ever come anywhere close to His perfection! Or, what about pretending to be the devil? Why, pray tell, would anyone who is sincerely following the teachings of Jesus take upon himself the embodiment of evil? A. W. Tozer concludes, “Playacting embodies a gross moral contradiction in that it calls a lie to the service of the truth.”

Religious drama, those who involve themselves in it, and for that matter those who approve of the very hypocrisy that Jesus condemned, are frauds. The Holy Spirit does not honor pretense and showmanship!

The reason multitudes followed Jesus was that His sincerity was so refreshing in comparison to the constant playacting of the Pharisees.

II. Practical Reasons Why Religious Drama is a Menace

a. Religious drama demoralizes reverence for God.

A person who pretends to be Jesus Christ or any other Bible character erodes his reverence for the Lord. When one playacts enough, his fear of God slowly dies within. After all, if a person can pretend to be equal to Christ, what is the need for reverence to a higher being? The Pharisees did not even suspect that they were walking dead men (Matthew 23:27).

b. Religious drama identifies worship with the theatrical world.

Hollywood has effectively proven that the theatrical world cannot produce godly moral values. Pairing a man and a woman as a pretend husband and wife breaks down the sanctity of marriage. The theatrical world also endorses courtship practices that violate the biblical standards of purity. The theatrical world has become the pacesetter of moral standards in today’s society, and many are following their ungodly pattern.

c. Religious drama does not satisfy the inner man.

When a person’s senses are titillated by outward show, the emotions keep seeking a new high and another feel-good worship experience. It creates a desire within to see yet another show that is more satisfying than the previous one. The emotions are having fun, but the inner man starves and slowly dies because the heart and mind have not been fed with real substance.

d. Religious drama ruins the preacher.

Drama is a friend to the lazy preacher. He no longer needs to: Study to shew thyself approved unto God… –2 Timothy 2:15. It requires no Holy Spirit unction to substitute a play for the sermon. Instead of commanding men to be “the light of the world,” he commands them to “lower the lights, please!” When the projector replaces the prophet, the primary means for man to find salvation is lost (1 Corinthians 1:21).

“As long as the preacher can fall back upon entertainment, the pressure that makes preachers will be wanting. The habit and rhythm which belongs to great preaching will be missing from their ministry.” –A. W. Tozer.

The use of religious drama will doom the preacher to mediocrity! The menace that we face today is that as religious drama multiplies, the heaven-sent revivals of the past will become extinct.

e. True worship will be viewed as inferior.

By using drama in a worship service, churches are training the youth to think that true worship is just another inferior form of amusement. When worship and drama are fused into one, worship is reduced to the lowest common denominator. The danger is that the next generation will not know what true worship is!

III. Patterns of True Worship

a. Prayer

Prayer is a vast subject, a worship pattern that too many times remains untapped. Public prayer in the congregational life is squeezed into our man-made time constraints.

In the early church, public prayers held a consistent pattern in their worship experiences. There was public prayer immediately after Christ’s ascension (Acts 1:14) and the first ordination (Acts 1:24). And they continued stedfastly … in prayers –Acts 2:42. No spirit of apathy was present! Prayer meetings were an evangelistic tool, a means of implementing the fear of God, and a great unifier for the whole church (Acts 2:41-44).

Peter and John attended a midafternoon prayer meeting (Acts 3:1). (Say, fellow saint, when was the last time that you attended a midafternoon prayer meeting?) Their prayer meeting had seismic results (Acts 4:31)! The power and presence of the Holy Spirit in our worship services brings results!

Prayer meeting attendance was not a monthly or a bimonthly option (Act 6:4)! When Peter was in prison, they had a voluntary, round-the-clock, prayer chain (Acts 12:5). They laid hands on their missionaries and prayed for them (Acts 13:3). They gathered at the river for a prayer meeting (Acts 16:13). Please note: this gathering at the river was not for the purpose of any kind of water sports; it was a prayer meeting! They gathered …prayer was wont to be made… –Acts 16:13. They understood that wherever Christians happened to meet, it was a normal activity to pray together.

b. Preaching

Preaching is a worship pattern that dates back to the time of Jonah (Jonah 3:2) and Moses (Acts 15:21). In the Old Testament, preaching was God’s pattern for communicating the will of God to man. When Jesus came on the scene, …[He] came into Galilee, preaching the gospel of the kingdom of God –Mark 1:14. He used the same worship pattern. Jesus used parables as verbal illustrations (not visual ones), which caught the attention of His hearers.

Near the end of His ministry, Jesus extended preaching as a worship pattern to future generations and all world cultures: …Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature –Mark 16:15.

Paul’s call was to preach the gospel (1 Corinthians 1:17-21). Preaching was not to be embellished by the cleverness of man. It pleased God to use the foolishness and simplicity of preaching to minister salvation to those who dared to believe. For this reason, preaching needs to be the focal point of every worship service. Praise services, concerts, and musicals are robbers of time that instead ought to be invested in listening to Holy Spirit-inspired preaching. When religious drama is used to present truth, it bypasses God’s ordained pattern of bringing the message of salvation to man.

Blessed is he that readeth, and they that hear the words of this prophecy, and keep those things which are written therein… –Revelation 1:3. God’s method of communication is the written or spoken Word. Not a picture! Not a play! Not a pageant!

c. Singing

The New Testament leaves no hint of professional singers, choirs, or musical performances. Meaningful singing requires participation by all, and an intelligent involvement of the mind (1 Corinthians 14:15). The context clearly implies that worship or singing is not only an individual experience; it is for the edification of all present. Soloists, who tend to be self-exalting, prohibit the remainder of the audience from entering into a corporate worship experience.

Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord –Colossians 3:16. Spiritual songs move the heart, while soulish songs move the feet and the emotions. Our singing is “to the Lord.” Preaching is from God to man, but singing is from man to God, containing expressions of praise, adoration, honor, and thanksgiving. Singing is for worship, not for entertainment.

Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord –Ephesians 5:19. Spirit-filled singing brings mutual edification, inspiration, and encouragement. Participation in singing has a way of ministering to heartfelt needs, where other methods fail. “Making melody in your heart” involves the accompaniment of the heart. External instrumentation tends to focus on a person’s abilities rather than on the heart. If our singing is not accompanied by our hearts, it becomes just another pharisaical worship show.

Old Testament worship was acceptable to God; nevertheless, it was also ritualistic with animal sacrifices, burning incense, using musical instruments, and dancing before the Lord. New Testament worship, however, is quite different. Jesus teaches us that we …must worship him in spirit and in truth –John 4:24. The spirit of worship replaces the rituals. When we move from intrinsic methods of worship to extrinsic methods, we violate the New Testament “spirit” of worship. Our worship is not to be stimulated by the extrinsic, but rather by the Holy Spirit (Ephesians 5:18).

IV. Essence of True Worship

When Jesus met the woman at the well, she expressed a concern about His change in worship format (John 4:20). She was concerned about how her fathers worshiped. In other words, “this is the way that we have always done it!” Every generation of worshipers must guard against formalistic worship.

There are two attitudes that affect true worship in a wrong way:

  • Formal –becoming so accustomed to the way that we have always done it, that we end up merely going through the motions and losing focus on the One being worshiped.
  • Casual –becoming so aloof to any form of worship that the One being worshiped becomes obscured by indifference.

Both formal and casual worship styles have one root problem: lack of reverence for God!

The fathers of the woman at the well had lost both the focus and the concept of worship: “Ye worship ye know not what” (John 4:22a). Jesus clearly indicated that worship is not thoughtless: “We know what we worship” (4:22b). True worship is the exercise of our mind and intellect. True worship has something to offer: “Salvation is of Jesus” (4:22c). It is life-changing!

The worship location is not as important as the attitude (John 4:23). The emphasis that Jesus gives is not on the outward ceremony, but on the state of the mind and spirit.

God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth –John 4:24. Note the word must! The only acceptable worship is in spirit and in truth. Our attitude must be such that it is in harmony with the Spirit of God. True worship also involves our response to truth. If our spirits are not responding to truth, we are not worshiping! If our minds are somewhere else, or on anything else, our worship is merely cold, dead ritualism!

Conclusion

In the observation of the principles of Scripture, it is clear that religious drama is not God’s pattern to bring faith and life into the human soul!

The pattern of true worship in the New Testament is to gather to hear the Word preached; to pray together and for each other; and to sing songs, hymns, and spiritual songs.

The temptation to introduce new things to worship is very real today. The appeal of Jesus is to worship in spirit and in truth. When each of us sincerely does his part to keep worship services meaningful and spiritual, it reduces the temptation to reintroduce the formal (“the way our fathers worshiped”) or to introduce the casual (any new irreverent worship).

Redaktørens merknad: Mange av leserne våre vil kanskje først være overbevist om at dette temaet ikke angår dem. Hvis det stemmer, gleder vi oss sammen med dere. Men før dere ganske enkelt hopper over denne artikkelen, oppfordrer vi leseren til å lese nøye det som står her, og deretter begynne å stille spørsmål til familie, venner og bekjente. Vi hører at særlig den yngre generasjonen trekkes med på arrangementer i organisasjoner ved siden av kirken (som konserter, seminarer, bibelskoler osv.) eller spesielle gudstjenester i nabokirker, der denne typen innhold inngår i større eller mindre grad. Særlig fremtredende er spesielle musikkgrupper/konserter, buktaling, religiøse filmer og sketsjer. Vi ønsker å øke bevisstheten om dette spørsmålet og stimulere til en diskusjon om saken.

Religiøst drama – hva er det?

En alvorlig fortelling framført av skuespillere som fremfører eller etterligner en gitt dialog på en teatralsk måte, eller en hendelse fra virkeligheten med følelsesmessige virkninger som kjennetegner et skuespill, utformet etter et religiøst tema. (American Heritage College Dictionary)

Er dette noe kirken bør være bekymret for? Det bør den. Det ser vanligvis ut til å begynne med utvidede «bønn- og lovprisningssamlinger» mellom søndagsskolen og gudstjenestene. Eller ved spesielle samlinger på andre tidspunkter enn søndag morgen. Det kan omfatte slike ting som instrumentale innslag, dukketeater, sketsjer, skuespill, danser og religiøse filmer.

Religiøst drama er ikke noe nytt. Det ble innført i den mørke middelalderen (400–1200 e.Kr.) som dramatiske framføringer med religiøse temaer, kjent som «mirakelspill». Disse skuespillene ble så fordervet at den katolske kirke forsøkte å sette en stopper for dem, men uten hell. I 1242 begynte pasjonsspillet, en framføring som skildrer Kristi død, i Tyskland, og det framføres fremdeles over hele verden i dag.

En interessant observasjon når vi ser tilbake i tid, er at religiøst drama ble innført i historiens mørkeste periode (den mørke middelalderen), men at kirken kom ut av denne lange epoken med moralsk forfall gjennom den åndsfylte, bibelbaserte forkynnelsen med fokus på den nye pakt under den anabaptistiske vekkelsen i reformasjonstiden.

I. Hvorfor drama krenker sann gudsdyrkelse

a. Drama er et brudd på prinsippet om å høre.

I den åndelige verden er det å se ikke like viktig som det å høre (2. Korinter 4:18). Ordene «høre», «hører» og «hørte» forekommer over 1000 ganger i Bibelen. Faktisk er hele Bibelen Gud som taler til mennesket. Han vil at menneskeheten skal høre! «Så sier Herren» er et gjennomgående omkved i hele Skriften.

På Sinai-fjellet (2. Mosebok 19:9) hørte folket Guds budskap gjennom hans talsmann Moses. Guds stemme skremte dem (2. Mosebok 20:18–19), men det var nødvendig å høre fra ham, så de «ikke skulle synde». I 2. Mosebok 20 ga Gud detaljerte instrukser om hvordan gudsdyrkelsen skulle foregå. Dere skal ikke lage guder av sølv ved siden av meg, og dere skal ikke lage guder av gull til dere selv – 2. Mosebok 20:23. Disse visuelle hjelpemidlene (avgudene) var et brudd på Guds prinsipp om å høre. Gjennom øyet kommer fristelsen til å lage avguder. Alterne Gud tillot, skulle være enkle og ikke tilhogde (vers 24–25). Det de så, skulle ikke distrahere fra det som ble hørt fra alteret! Det som sees, særlig uanstendig påkledning, har en tendens til å distrahere fra det som høres (vers 26).

Jesu forkynnelse appellerte til hørselen: Den som har ører, han høre! – Matteus 13:9. Selv om han ikke brukte visuelle hjelpemidler slik forkynnere gjør i dag, brukte Jesus verbale hjelpemidler (lignelser) for å appellere til hørselen (Matt 13:18).

På forklarelsens berg (Matteus 17) ønsket Peter å finne opp gudstjenesteopplevelsen på nytt ved å bygge tre helligdommer. Han ville ha noe å se på! Men stemmen fra skyen gjorde disiplene oppmerksomme på hvor viktig det er å høre (vers 5). Gud godkjenner ikke gudsdyrkelse med visuelle hjelpemidler!

Jesus sa: Sannelig, sannelig sier jeg dere: Den som hører mitt ord og tror ham som har sendt meg, har evig liv … Timen kommer, ja, den er nå, da de døde skal høre Guds Sønns røst, og de som hører, skal leve. Johannes 5:24–25. Frelse kommer ved å høre Guds ord, men bare når man tror det man hører!

Paulus stiller noen alvorlige spørsmål: Hvordan kan de da påkalle en de ikke er kommet til tro på? Og hvordan kan de tro på en de ikke har hørt om? Og hvordan kan de høre uten at noen forkynner? – Romerne 10:14. Han besvarer sine egne spørsmål: Så kommer da troen av det en hører, og det en hører, kommer ved Guds ord – Romerne 10:17. Guds regel for å erfare frelse er enten å høre Guds ord eller å lese Guds ord!

I det andre og tredje kapitlet i Johannes' åpenbaring gjentar Jesus sju ganger: «Den som har ører, han høre.» Religiøst drama er overfladisk fordi det appellerer til menneskets sjelsliv, ikke den åndelige delen. Menneskets sjelsliv (følelsene) kan ha det svært hyggelig mens ånden i mennesket forblir uberørt og upåvirket. Satan bruker øyet til å distrahere mennesket fra dets egentlige hjerteanliggender.

Hebreerne 11:6 forteller oss: «Tro er en fast tillit til det en håper på, en overbevisning om ting en ikke ser (eller får demonstrert).» Sann tro kommer til menneskehjertet ved å høre, ikke ved demonstrasjon. Derfor grenser religiøst drama til å være antikristelig, fordi det motarbeider Guds prinsipp om å høre.

b. Drama er et brudd på oppriktigheten.

Skriften lærer hvor viktig oppriktighet er i alle livets forhold (1. Korinter 5:8; 2. Korinter 1:12, 2:17; Filipperne 1:10). For å bevare vår oppriktighet er det viktig at hver enkelt erkjenner at Gud har skapt oss som unike individer (Salme 139:14–15). Vi er ikke, og kan ikke være, noen andre! Å forsøke å være noen andre krenker vår individuelle egenart. Og når man gjør det, blir man uoppriktig.

Hvordan henger dette sammen med religiøst drama? Drama innebærer skuespill. Jesus var stadig i konflikt med fariseerne. De spilte hele tiden skuespill eller lot som om de var noe de ikke var. Jesus kalte dem gjentatte ganger hyklere. Det opprinnelige greske ordet betyr «skuespiller».

Fariseernes eneste motiv for å be offentlig var å bli sett av mennesker (Matteus 6:5–7). De var opptatt av tilskuerne sine, og dermed av framføringen. Jesus gjorde det helt klart at religiøs hengivenhet skulle være privat, «i ditt lønnkammer». Når en person som gir uttrykk for fromhet, blir mer opptatt av sin opptreden enn av budskapet sitt, tilber han ikke lenger, men setter opp et show! Dette kan skje med forkynnere, kvartetter, kor osv. «Bønnevandringer» havner også vanligvis i samme kategori av skuespill.

Når en person gjør skuespill til en fast vane, blir han en hykler. Han krenker sin egen sjel fordi han skader sin egenart, som Gud har gitt ham.

Jesus omtalte fariseerne som hyklere sju ganger i Matteus 23. Han fortalte dem at de var levende døde (Matteus 23:27–28). De hadde spilt skuespill så lenge at de ikke lenger kjente forskjell på det virkelige og det uvirkelige!

Dette bedraget er én grunn til at profesjonelle skuespillere blir så ytterliggående i livets spørsmål. Profesjonelt blir de stadig mer løsrevet fra sannhet, oppriktighet og virkelighet. I saker som miljøvern, dyrs rettigheter, abort, homofiles rettigheter og global oppvarming har mange av dem inntatt standpunkter som er løsrevet fra sannhetens grunnvoll og ikke lenger er oppriktige.

Å late som man ber eller tilber, eller å spille bibelske personer i et skuespill, er ikke bare uoppriktig, men grenser til helligbrøde. Tenk deg å late som om du er Jesus i et skuespill! Å utgi seg for å være Jesus er blasfemisk fordi ingen kristen har kommet i nærheten av hans fullkommenhet! Eller hva med å late som man er djevelen? Hvorfor i all verden skulle noen som oppriktig følger Jesu lære, påta seg å legemliggjøre det onde? A. W. Tozer konkluderer: «Skuespill innebærer en grov moralsk selvmotsigelse ved at det setter en løgn i sannhetens tjeneste.»

Religiøst drama, dem som deltar i det, og for den saks skyld dem som godkjenner selve hykleriet Jesus fordømte, er bedragere. Den Hellige Ånd anerkjenner ikke skuespill og show!

Grunnen til at så mange fulgte Jesus, var at hans oppriktighet var så forfriskende sammenlignet med fariseernes stadige skuespill.

II. Praktiske grunner til at religiøst drama er en trussel

a. Religiøst drama svekker ærbødigheten for Gud.

En person som later som han er Jesus Kristus eller en annen bibelsk person, undergraver sin ærbødighet for Herren. Når man spiller skuespill ofte nok, dør gudsfrykten langsomt ut inni en. Når alt kommer til alt, hvis en person kan late som han er lik Kristus, hvorfor trenger han da å vise ærbødighet for et høyere vesen? Fariseerne ante ikke engang at de var levende døde (Matteus 23:27).

b. Religiøst drama knytter gudsdyrkelse til teaterverdenen.

Hollywood har tydelig bevist at teaterverdenen ikke kan frembringe gudfryktige moralske verdier. Når en mann og en kvinne settes sammen som liksom-ektemann og -hustru, brytes ekteskapets hellighet ned. Teaterverdenen går også inn for kjærestepraksiser som bryter med Bibelens renhetsnormer. Teaterverdenen har blitt rettesnoren for moralske normer i dagens samfunn, og mange følger dens ugudelige mønster.

c. Religiøst drama tilfredsstiller ikke det indre mennesket.

Når sansene til en person pirres av ytre show, søker følelsene stadig etter en ny rus og en ny godfølelse i gudsdyrkelsen. Det skaper et ønske om å se enda et show som er mer tilfredsstillende enn det forrige. Følelsene har det gøy, men det indre mennesket sulter og dør langsomt fordi hjertet og sinnet ikke har fått næring av virkelig innhold.

d. Religiøst drama ødelegger forkynneren.

Drama er en venn av den late forkynneren. Han trenger ikke lenger å: Legg vinn på å framstille deg selv for Gud som en som holder prøve … – 2. Timoteus 2:15. Det krever ingen salvelse fra Den Hellige Ånd å erstatte prekenen med et skuespill. I stedet for å befale mennesker å være «verdens lys», ber han dem om å «dempe lyset, vær så snill!» Når projektoren erstatter profeten, går det viktigste middelet mennesket har for å finne frelse, tapt (1. Korinter 1:21).

«Så lenge forkynneren kan falle tilbake på underholdning, vil presset som skaper forkynnere, mangle. Vanen og rytmen som kjennetegner stor forkynnelse, vil være fraværende i tjenesten deres.» – A. W. Tozer.

Bruk av religiøst drama vil dømme forkynneren til middelmådighet! Trusselen vi står overfor i dag, er at etter hvert som religiøst drama blir mer utbredt, vil de himmelsendte vekkelsene fra fortiden dø ut.

e. Sann gudsdyrkelse vil bli betraktet som underlegen.

Ved å bruke drama i gudstjenesten lærer kirkene ungdommen å tro at sann gudsdyrkelse bare er en annen, mindreverdig form for underholdning. Når gudsdyrkelse og drama smeltes sammen, reduseres gudsdyrkelsen til det laveste felles multiplum. Faren er at den neste generasjonen ikke vil vite hva sann gudsdyrkelse er!

III. Mønstre for sann gudsdyrkelse

a. Bønn

Bønn er et omfattende tema, et mønster for gudsdyrkelse som altfor ofte ikke blir tatt i bruk. Offentlig bønn i menighetens liv presses inn i våre menneskeskapte tidsrammer.

I den tidlige kirken fulgte offentlige bønner et fast mønster i gudstjenestene. Det ble bedt offentlig umiddelbart etter Kristi himmelfart (Apostlenes gjerninger 1:14) og ved den første ordinasjonen (Apostlenes gjerninger 1:24). De holdt urokkelig fast … ved bønnene – Apostlenes gjerninger 2:42. Det fantes ingen ånd av likegyldighet! Bønnemøtene var et evangeliseringsredskap, et middel til å innprente gudsfrykt og en sterk samlende kraft for hele kirken (Apostlenes gjerninger 2:41–44).

Peter og Johannes deltok på et bønnemøte midt på ettermiddagen (Apostlenes gjerninger 3:1). (Si meg, kjære hellige, når var du sist på et bønnemøte midt på ettermiddagen?) Bønnemøtet deres fikk seismiske følger (Apostlenes gjerninger 4:31)! Den Hellige Ånds kraft og nærvær i gudstjenestene våre gir resultater!

Å delta på bønnemøter var ikke noe man kunne velge å gjøre én gang i måneden eller annenhver måned (Apostlenes gjerninger 6:4)! Da Peter satt i fengsel, hadde de en frivillig bønnekjede som gikk døgnet rundt (Apostlenes gjerninger 12:5). De la hendene på misjonærene sine og ba for dem (Apostlenes gjerninger 13:3). De samlet seg ved elven til et bønnemøte (Apostlenes gjerninger 16:13). Merk: Denne samlingen ved elven var ikke for å drive med noen form for vannsport; det var et bønnemøte! De samlet seg … der det pleide å være et bønnested … – Apostlenes gjerninger 16:13. De forsto at det var vanlig å be sammen hvor enn kristne møttes.

b. Forkynnelse

Forkynnelse er et mønster for gudsdyrkelse som går tilbake til Jonas' tid (Jona 3:2) og Moses' tid (Apostlenes gjerninger 15:21). I Det gamle testamentet var forkynnelse Guds mønster for å formidle Guds vilje til mennesket. Da Jesus trådte fram, … kom [han] til Galilea og forkynte evangeliet om Guds rike – Markus 1:14. Han brukte det samme mønsteret for gudsdyrkelse. Jesus brukte lignelser som verbale illustrasjoner (ikke visuelle), og fanget dermed tilhørernes oppmerksomhet.

Mot slutten av sin tjeneste utvidet Jesus forkynnelsen som mønster for gudsdyrkelse til framtidige generasjoner og alle verdens kulturer: … Gå ut i hele verden og forkynn evangeliet for alt som Gud har skapt – Markus 16:15.

Paulus' kall var å forkynne evangeliet (1. Korinter 1:17–21). Forkynnelsen skulle ikke pyntes på med menneskelig kløkt. Det behaget Gud å bruke forkynnelsens dårskap og enkelhet til å formidle frelse til dem som våget å tro. Av denne grunn må forkynnelsen være midtpunktet i enhver gudstjeneste. Lovprisningssamlinger, konserter og musikaler stjeler tid som i stedet burde brukes på å lytte til forkynnelse inspirert av Den Hellige Ånd. Når religiøst drama brukes til å formidle sannheten, omgår det mønsteret Gud har fastsatt for å bringe frelsens budskap til mennesket.

Salig er den som leser ordene i denne profetien, og de som hører dem og tar vare på det som står skrevet i den … – Johannes' åpenbaring 1:3. Guds formidlingsmåte er det skrevne eller talte ord. Ikke et bilde! Ikke et skuespill! Ikke en tablåframstilling!

c. Sang

Det nye testamentet gir ikke det minste tegn til profesjonelle sangere, kor eller musikalske framføringer. Meningsfull sang krever at alle deltar, og at sinnet engasjeres på en bevisst måte (1. Korinter 14:15). Sammenhengen viser tydelig at gudsdyrkelse eller sang ikke bare er en individuell opplevelse; den er til oppbyggelse for alle som er til stede. Solister, som gjerne opphøyer seg selv, hindrer resten av forsamlingen i å delta i felles gudsdyrkelse.

La Kristi ord bo rikelig blant dere, så dere med all visdom lærer og rettleder hverandre med salmer, hymner og åndelige sanger, og synger med nåde i hjertene for Herren – Kolosserne 3:16. Åndelige sanger beveger hjertet, mens sjelslige sanger beveger føttene og følelsene. Vi synger «for Herren». Forkynnelsen går fra Gud til mennesket, men sangen går fra mennesket til Gud og uttrykker lovprisning, tilbedelse, ære og takksigelse. Sang er til gudsdyrkelse, ikke til underholdning.

La salmer, hymner og åndelige sanger lyde blant dere. Syng og spill av hjertet for Herren – Efeserne 5:19. Åndsfylt sang gir gjensidig oppbyggelse, inspirasjon og oppmuntring. Det å delta i sangen har en egen evne til å betjene hjertets behov, der andre metoder ikke strekker til. «Å spille av hjertet» innebærer at hjertet følger med. Ytre instrumentering har en tendens til å rette oppmerksomheten mot en persons ferdigheter snarere enn hjertet. Hvis sangen vår ikke ledsages av hjertet, blir den enda et fariseisk gudsdyrkelsesshow.

Gudsdyrkelse i Det gamle testamentet var til behag for Gud; likevel var den også ritualpreget, med dyreofringer, røkelse, musikkinstrumenter og dans for Herren. Gudsdyrkelsen i Det nye testamentet er imidlertid ganske annerledes. Jesus lærer oss at vi … må tilbe ham i ånd og sannhet – Johannes 4:24. Gudsdyrkelsens ånd erstatter ritualene. Når vi går fra indre former for gudsdyrkelse til ytre former, bryter vi med Det nye testamentets «ånd» i gudsdyrkelsen. Gudsdyrkelsen vår skal ikke stimuleres av det ytre, men av Den Hellige Ånd (Efeserne 5:18).

IV. Sann gudsdyrkelses vesen

Da Jesus møtte kvinnen ved brønnen, uttrykte hun bekymring over at han endret formen for gudsdyrkelse (Johannes 4:20). Hun var opptatt av hvordan fedrene hennes hadde tilbedt. Med andre ord: «Slik har vi alltid gjort det!» Hver generasjon av gudsdyrkere må vokte seg for formalistisk gudsdyrkelse.

Det er to holdninger som påvirker sann gudsdyrkelse på en gal måte:

  • Formell – å bli så vant til måten vi alltid har gjort det på at vi ender opp med bare å utføre handlingene og mister blikket for ham vi tilber.
  • Uformell – å bli så likegyldig til enhver form for gudsdyrkelse at han vi tilber, blir skjult av likegyldighet.

Både formell og uformell gudsdyrkelse har det samme grunnproblemet: mangel på ærbødighet for Gud!

Kvinnens fedre ved brønnen hadde mistet både fokus og forståelse av gudsdyrkelsen: «Dere tilber det dere ikke kjenner» (Johannes 4:22a). Jesus viste tydelig at gudsdyrkelse ikke er tankeløs: «Vi tilber det vi kjenner» (4:22b). Sann gudsdyrkelse innebærer at vi bruker sinnet og forstanden. Sann gudsdyrkelse har noe å tilby: «Frelsen kommer fra Jesus» (4:22c). Den forandrer livet!

Hvor gudsdyrkelsen finner sted, er ikke like viktig som holdningen (Johannes 4:23). Jesus legger ikke vekt på den ytre seremonien, men på sinnets og åndens tilstand.

Gud er ånd, og de som tilber ham, må tilbe i ånd og sannhet – Johannes 4:24. Legg merke til ordet «må»! Den eneste godkjente gudsdyrkelsen er i ånd og sannhet. Holdningen vår må være i harmoni med Guds Ånd. Sann gudsdyrkelse innebærer også vår respons på sannheten. Hvis åndene våre ikke svarer på sannheten, tilber vi ikke! Hvis tankene våre er et annet sted, eller opptatt av noe annet, er gudsdyrkelsen vår bare kald, død ritualisme!

Konklusjon

Når vi betrakter prinsippene i Skriften, er det tydelig at religiøst drama ikke er Guds mønster for å bringe tro og liv inn i menneskesjelen!

Mønsteret for sann gudsdyrkelse i Det nye testamentet er å samles for å høre Ordet forkynt, be sammen og for hverandre, og synge sanger, hymner og åndelige sanger.

Fristelsen til å innføre nye ting i gudsdyrkelsen er svært reell i dag. Jesus oppfordrer oss til å tilbe i ånd og sannhet. Når hver av oss oppriktig gjør sin del for å holde gudstjenestene meningsfulle og åndelige, reduserer det fristelsen til å gjeninnføre det formelle («slik fedrene våre tilba») eller innføre det uformelle (enhver ny, respektløs form for gudsdyrkelse).

Greetings in the worthy name of our Lord and Saviour, Jesus Christ. I trust that amid the present uncertainties in the world our hearts echo with the Psalmist: In God is my salvation and my glory: the rock of my strength, and my refuge, is in God –Psalm 62:7. And, God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble –Psalm 46:1.

We are facing unprecedented and challenging times. More so than many of us can remember in our lifetime. I’m sure that each generation has faced challenges unique to their time in history. The same is true of us. But what is our ‘time’ in history? Most god-fearing individuals believe we are on the threshold of what the Scriptures refer to as “the time of the end”. (See Daniel 8:17; 11:35; 11:40; 12:4; & 12:9)

Maybe it is just me, or perhaps it has a lot to do with how fast news is broadcast around the world now a days. But it sure seems like there is a lot more chaos and violent acts of nature than there was five or ten years ago. Hurricanes, tornadoes, wildfires, earthquakes, drought, flooding, political unrest, wars, and rumors of war. Did I miss anything? Oh yes, there’s the ever-present issue of a worldwide pestilence—Covid-19.

Much of the world today seems to have a sense that “something is up”, or that “something is about to happen”. We should not be surprised by this, Jesus foretold it. We should not be overcome and distracted by fear, Jesus has told us what to do. In the following Scripture I have underlined three things that I see Jesus wants us to be active in doing as long as time continues.

And Jesus answered and said unto them, Take heed that no man deceive you. For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and shall deceive many. And ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars: see that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet. For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom: and there shall be famines, and pestilences, and earthquakes, in divers places. All these are the beginning of sorrows. Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name’s sake. And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another. And many false prophets shall rise, and shall deceive many. And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold. But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved. And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations; and then shall the end come –Matthew 24:4-14.

Take heed that no man deceive you

I find it interesting that Jesus mentions this before telling us what He wants us to do. Someone has said that spiritual blindness is different than physical blindness in that when someone is physically blind, they know it, but when someone is spiritually blind, they don’t know it. In fact, that is the foundation of being spiritually blind—to no longer be aware of one’s own spiritual condition.

What all can we be deceived by? Who all might try to deceive us? Let’s always remember that Satan wants to use whoever he can, however he can, to deceive as many as he can. Job’s friends turned against him and even his own wife offered Satan’s own words as a way out (See Job 1;11; 2:5; and 2:9). We should not be surprised if we find ourselves in similar situations; Christ predicted that this would happen (See Matthew 10:35-36; and Luke 12:53).

Let’s never forget that God has given some clear solutions that we can follow to prevent ourselves from becoming deceived. Take heed, brethren, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God. But exhort one another daily, while it is called To day; lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin. For we are made partakers of Christ, if we hold the beginning of our confidence stedfast unto the end; While it is said, To day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts, as in the provocation –Hebrews 3:12-15.

Endure unto the end

This is one of the more interesting Scriptures that I think of whenever there is a heated discussion about whether or not someone who is once saved is then always saved and therefore never able to become unsaved. Doesn’t Scripture assure us …that ye may know that ye have eternal life… –1 John 5:13. However, Peter tells us to …beware lest ye also, being led away with the error of the wicked, fall from your own stedfastness –2 Peter 3:17.

So how do we bring this together so that Scripture harmonizes? First, we need to be saved initially so we can have eternal life which provides us with the power to walk in obedience to God’s Word. Secondly, we stay saved as long as we continue walking in obedience to the Scriptures. Then lastly, we are finally saved forever, IF we endure through life faithfully until the end (the end of our life here on earth).

Preach the Gospel in all the world

Preach the Gospel? Yes. Maybe we can’t all personally do the preaching, but we can all do our part to help the church fulfil this mandate. Some folks God has ordained to spend hours in their prayer closet in earnest intercessory prayer. Some have been called to give of their finances to support others who have been chosen to be on the front lines preaching the Gospel. This is a group effort. It is the church as a whole working together with each local church doing their part and everyone doing their individual part.

Let’s not allow the chaos and confusion around us to cause us to become distracted and disoriented. Let’s pull together as brothers and sisters with a common goal—not being deceived, enduring unto the end, and preaching the Gospel in all the world.

Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy, To the only wise God our Saviour, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, both now and ever. Amen. –Jude 1:24-25.

Приветствую вас достойным именем нашего Господа и Спасителя Иисуса Христа. Надеюсь, что среди нынешней неопределённости в мире наши сердца вторят псалмопевцу: В Боге спасение моё и слава моя; крепость силы моей и прибежище моё — в Боге. — Псалом 62:7. И ещё: Бог нам прибежище и сила, скорая помощь в бедах. — Псалом 46:1.

Мы переживаем беспрецедентные и тяжёлые времена. Более тяжёлые, чем многие из нас могут припомнить за всю свою жизнь. Уверен, каждое поколение сталкивалось с испытаниями, присущими его исторической эпохе. То же верно и для нас. Но какова наша «эпоха» в истории? Большинство богобоязненных людей верят, что мы стоим на пороге того, что Писание называет «временем конца». (См. Даниил 8:17; 11:35; 11:40; 12:4; и 12:9)

Может быть, это только мне так кажется, а может быть, дело в том, как быстро сегодня новости распространяются по всему миру. Но создаётся впечатление, что хаоса и разрушительных природных явлений стало гораздо больше, чем пять или десять лет назад. Ураганы, торнадо, лесные пожары, землетрясения, засухи, наводнения, политические волнения, войны и слухи о войнах. Я что-нибудь упустил? Ах да, есть ещё постоянно присутствующая угроза всемирной эпидемии — COVID-19.

Сегодня многим людям во всём мире кажется, что «что-то происходит» или что «вот-вот что-то случится». Нас это не должно удивлять: Иисус предсказал это. Мы не должны поддаваться страху и отвлекаться: Иисус сказал нам, что делать. В следующем отрывке из Писания я подчеркнул три вещи, которыми, как я считаю, Иисус хочет, чтобы мы занимались всё то время, пока продолжается нынешняя эпоха.

Иисус сказал им в ответ: смотрите, не обольстил бы вас кто; ибо многие придут под именем Моим, и будут говорить: «я Христос», и многих прельстят. Также услышите о войнах и о военных слухах. Смотрите, не ужасайтесь, ибо надлежит всему тому быть, но это ещё не конец. Ибо восстанет народ на народ, и царство на царство; и будут глады, моры и землетрясения по местам; всё же это — начало болезней. Тогда будут предавать вас на мучения и убивать вас; и вы будете ненавидимы всеми народами за имя Моё; и тогда соблазнятся многие; и друг друга будут предавать, и возненавидят друг друга; и многие лжепророки восстанут, и прельстят многих; и, по причине умножения беззакония, во многих охладеет любовь; претерпевший же до конца спасётся. И проповедано будет сие Евангелие Царствия по всей вселенной, во свидетельство всем народам; и тогда придёт конец. — Матфея 24:4-14.

Смотрите, не обольстил бы вас кто

Мне кажется интересным, что Иисус говорит об этом прежде, чем рассказывает, что Он хочет, чтобы мы делали. Кто-то сказал, что духовная слепота отличается от физической тем, что физически слепой человек знает о своей слепоте, а духовно слепой — нет. По сути, в этом и заключается основа духовной слепоты: человек перестаёт осознавать собственное духовное состояние.

Чем нас могут обольстить? Кто может попытаться нас обмануть? Будем всегда помнить, что сатана хочет использовать любого, кого сможет, и как угодно, чтобы обмануть как можно больше людей. Друзья Иова отвернулись от него, и даже его собственная жена предложила ему слова самого сатаны как выход из положения (см. Иов 1;11; 2:5; и 2:9). Не следует удивляться, если мы окажемся в подобных ситуациях: Христос предсказал, что так и будет (см. Матфея 10:35-36; и Луки 12:53).

Будем помнить, что Бог дал нам ясные способы не дать себя обмануть, и мы можем им следовать. Смотрите, братия, чтобы не было в ком из вас злого сердца неверия, дабы вам не отступить от Бога живого. Но наставляйте друг друга каждый день, доколе можно говорить: «ныне», чтобы кто из вас не ожесточился, обольстившись грехом. Ибо мы сделались причастниками Христу, если только до конца сохраним твёрдость нашей первоначальной уверенности, доколе говорится: «ныне, когда услышите глас Его, не ожесточите сердец ваших, как во время ропота». — Евреям 3:12-15.

Претерпеть до конца

Это одно из тех мест Писания, о которых я вспоминаю всякий раз, когда разгорается спор о том, спасён ли человек навсегда, если однажды был спасён, и потому уже никогда не может утратить спасение. Разве Писание не уверяет нас: …дабы вы знали, что вы, веруя в Сына Божия, имеете жизнь вечную… — 1 Иоанна 5:13. Однако Пётр говорит нам: …берегитесь, чтобы вам не увлечься заблуждением беззаконников и не отпасть от своего утверждения. — 2 Петра 3:17.

Как же согласовать это, чтобы Писание не противоречило само себе? Во-первых, мы должны изначально обрести спасение, чтобы иметь вечную жизнь, которая даёт нам силу жить в послушании Слову Божьему. Во-вторых, мы остаёмся спасёнными, пока продолжаем жить в послушании Писанию. И наконец, мы обретаем окончательное спасение навеки, ЕСЛИ до конца жизни будем верны и претерпим до конца (то есть до конца нашей земной жизни).

Проповедовать Евангелие по всему миру

Проповедовать Евангелие? Да. Возможно, не все мы можем лично проповедовать, но каждый может внести свой вклад, помогая церкви исполнить это поручение. Некоторых Бог призвал проводить часы в молитвенной комнате, усердно ходатайствуя в молитве. Других призвал отдавать свои средства, поддерживая тех, кого Он избрал проповедовать Евангелие на передовой. Это общее дело. Вся церковь трудится сообща: каждая поместная церковь вносит свой вклад, и каждый делает то, что ему надлежит.

Не позволим окружающим нас хаосу и смятению отвлечь нас и сбить с пути. Будем сплочённо трудиться, как братья и сёстры, ради общей цели: не поддаваться обману, претерпеть до конца и проповедовать Евангелие по всему миру.

Могущему же соблюсти вас от падения и поставить пред славою Своею непорочными в радости, Единому Премудрому Богу, Спасителю нашему, слава и величие, сила и власть ныне и во веки. Аминь. — Иуды 1:24-25.

“Could you come with me to visit my sister and her husband?” a friend asked my husband. “They’re having serious marriage problems. My brother-in-law saw how God is working in our marriage and asked me how it happened. Can you tell them how God could change their marriage, too?”

At dusk that evening, my husband, and I, waited with our friend outside his sister’s home. Half an hour later a dilapidated red pickup chugged up and shuddered to a stop. An overweight man with grease-covered clothes and a perpetual smile heaved himself out from behind the steering wheel, while his pretty, fashionably dressed wife hopped out of the passenger seat.

“Come in! Come in!” they invited, guiding us to the stairway which led to their living quarters.

“Excuse the mess,” the wife apologized, swiping clothes from the couches so we could take seats. The room was elaborately furnished but dirty. A deep layer of dust covered the top of the large-screen television set, the end tables… everything.

“Lord, give us wisdom,” I silently implored as we took seats across from the couple. How could we connect with folks we scarcely knew, and who did not have God in their lives?

The husband talked. His wife had failed him miserably and had cheated on him many times. She was presently meeting with a new boyfriend, a young chap she had learned to know on the street. “But I’ll forgive you all that,” promised the husband, “If you are willing to start over, be my wife, and be a mom to our children. I know you’ve failed, but we all fail. Let’s start over, Dear.”

The wife sat in stony silence. Our friend talked, pleading with his sister and brother-in-law to be reconciled. My husband talked about God and His plan for marriage, urging them to turn to Him.

Finally, the wife opened her mouth. Bitterness poured out; dishonor; old dirt. “You never show me that you care. You never buy me anything. Why should I try to please you anymore?”

The husband joined the fray. Both talked at once, on and on, louder and louder.

We sat with sagging hearts, listening, praying, thinking. I tried to imagine how the wife must have felt. She was pretty and young. Why stay at home to clean, cook, and wash clothes for a hulk of a husband who spent his days leaning over greasy motors and crawling under dirty cars? Why, when she could have fun on the street with a cool, young fellow who made her feel so-o-o special?

Finally, the couple ran out of steam. We sat in sad silence. “I’m sorry,” my husband stated finally, “but we can’t help you. The only one who can help you is God. And if you don’t want His help, there’s no hope for your marriage.”

“Yeah, I really should go to church,” mumbled the husband.

“Ha, ha,” sneered the wife. “Just see you become a Mennonite yet!” We rose and shook hands, promised our prayers, and left.

After we left that evening, more harsh words flew between the couple. Their two children came upon the scene and, siding with their father, drove their mother from the house.

From far in the distance came a sound of music—and what else? Singing. Joyful shouting. A wife threw open the shutter from a window facing the street, leaned out, and peered up the road. Oh, yes, today is the day my husband went to bring the Ark of the Covenant home. But why are they making such a ruckus over it?

Into the city danced the parade, singing, shouting, and blowing trumpets. David danced with all his might, his heart overflowing with thanks to God. After agonizing years of fleeing from Saul, God had established him as king. And now the Ark of the Lord was finally returning to its proper dwelling place… God be praised!

As David leaped and shouted his way up the street, his wife looked down from her perch at the window with a dark scowl on her face. Just look at how his robe flies around as he dances. Doesn’t he have any shame?! And hollering like that… what a way for a king to act! Doesn’t he care what others think?!

David returned home several hours later—tired, but happy—to bless his household. It had been a good day. He could tell his wife, Michal, all about it at the supper table.

But she beat him to the subject. [“My, but didn’t you act gloriously today,”] were her frosty words. David must have looked confused. [“I mean, jumping around like that in front of the maidens, just like a vain fellow from off the streets!”]

David must have been smitten. [“I was doing it to the Lord, to the one who chose me to be king instead of your father.”]

I imagine Michal wincing. Ouch! [“Why do you have to throw that in my face?”]

[“I know I am low in your esteem,”]* continued David, [“but those maidens you mentioned, they esteem me.”]

I think of the wayward lady in town who was chased from home by her children, and I wonder who will care for her forty years from now when her pretty face is wrinkled, and her back is bent.

I picture Michal’s lonely old age. The account ends by saying she had no children until her dying day. I doubt if her king-husband bothered to stop in with her anymore. Why would he? He received honor aplenty from others. I also wonder if Michal’s dishonor and their fall-out weakened King David. Several chapters later tell of his eyes roving to a neighbor’s wife and the resulting sin.

All wives are tempted to dishonor their husbands. We are tempted to dishonor regardless of whether our husband is a king or a mechanic, godly or ungodly.

Every day I choose to honor or dishonor the husband God gave me. I can skip alongside him, supporting with enthusiasm, or I can hang out the window, watching with scorn in my heart. I can focus on what he does well and compliment him, or I can nag about what he does wrong. My choice determines the reciprocating favor or loss. My choice affects, not only my husband and me, but also a cloud of witnesses… my children, my sisters in Christ, and my neighbors.

“And the wife see that she reverence her husband.”
(Ephesians 5:33b)

* This is how the Spanish Bible says it; the thought is clearer than in the English translation.

«Не мог бы ты пойти со мной навестить мою сестру и её мужа?» — спросил моего мужа один наш друг. «У них серьёзные проблемы в браке. Мой зять увидел, как Бог действует в нашем браке, и спросил меня, как это произошло. Можешь рассказать им, как Бог может изменить и их брак?»

В тот вечер, в сумерках, мы с мужем ждали нашего друга у дома его сестры. Через полчаса подъехал старый красный пикап, тарахтя и дрожа, и остановился. Из-за руля с трудом выбрался полный мужчина в одежде, покрытой машинной смазкой, с неизменной улыбкой на лице, а его хорошенькая, модно одетая жена выпрыгнула с пассажирского сиденья.

«Заходите! Заходите!» — пригласили они, проводив нас к лестнице, ведущей в их жилые комнаты.

«Простите за беспорядок», — извинилась жена, убирая с диванов одежду, чтобы мы могли сесть. Комната была обставлена с большим вкусом, но грязная. Толстый слой пыли покрывал большой телевизор с плоским экраном, журнальные столики… всё.

«Господи, дай нам мудрости», — молча взывала я, садясь напротив супругов. Как найти общий язык с людьми, которых мы едва знали и в чьей жизни не было Бога?

Говорил муж. Его жена жестоко подвела его и много раз изменяла ему. Сейчас она встречалась с новым парнем — молодым человеком, с которым познакомилась на улице. «Но я всё тебе прощу, — пообещал муж, — если ты согласишься начать всё сначала, быть моей женой и матерью наших детей. Я знаю, ты поступала неправильно, но все мы ошибаемся. Давай начнём сначала, дорогая».

Жена сидела молча, окаменев. Наш друг говорил, умоляя сестру и зятя примириться. Мой муж рассказывал о Боге и Его замысле о браке, призывая их обратиться к Нему.

Наконец жена заговорила. Из неё полились горечь, упрёки, старые обиды. «Ты никогда не показываешь, что тебе не всё равно. Ты никогда ничего мне не покупаешь. Почему я должна и дальше стараться тебе угодить?»

Муж тоже включился в перепалку. Оба говорили одновременно, всё без умолку, всё громче и громче.

Мы сидели с тяжёлым сердцем, слушали, молились, размышляли. Я пыталась представить, что чувствовала жена. Она была молодой и хорошенькой. Зачем оставаться дома, чтобы убирать, готовить и стирать для громилы-мужа, который целыми днями склонялся над залитыми смазкой моторами и ползал под грязными машинами? Зачем, если можно веселиться на улице с классным молодым парнем, рядом с которым чувствуешь себя такой-и-и особенной?

Наконец у супругов иссякли силы. Мы сидели в печальном молчании. «Мне жаль, — наконец сказал мой муж, — но мы не можем вам помочь. Помочь вам может только Бог. И если вы не хотите Его помощи, у вашего брака нет надежды».

«Да, мне и правда стоило бы ходить в церковь», — пробормотал муж.

«Ха-ха, — насмешливо сказала жена. — Ещё посмотрим, как ты станешь меннонитом!» Мы встали, пожали им руки, пообещали молиться за них и ушли.

После нашего ухода тем вечером супруги продолжили обмениваться резкими словами. Их двое детей застали эту сцену и, приняв сторону отца, выгнали мать из дома.

Издалека донеслись звуки музыки — а что ещё? Пение. Радостные возгласы. Жена распахнула ставню окна, выходившего на улицу, высунулась и посмотрела вверх по дороге. Ах да, сегодня мой муж должен привезти домой ковчег завета. Но почему из-за него подняли такой шум?

В город въехала танцующая процессия — люди пели, кричали и трубили в трубы. Давид танцевал изо всех сил, и сердце его переполняла благодарность Богу. После мучительных лет бегства от Саула Бог утвердил его царём. И вот ковчег Господень наконец возвращался на своё подобающее место… Слава Богу!

Пока Давид, прыгая и крича, поднимался по улице, жена смотрела на него сверху из окна, мрачно нахмурившись. Только посмотрите, как развевается на нём плащ, когда он танцует. Разве ему совсем не стыдно?! И ещё кричит… разве так должен вести себя царь? Разве ему всё равно, что подумают другие?!

Несколько часов спустя Давид вернулся домой — уставший, но счастливый, — чтобы благословить свой дом. День выдался чудесный. За ужином он мог рассказать жене, Мелхоле, обо всём.

Но она заговорила первой. [«Ну и прославил же ты себя сегодня!»] — произнесла она ледяным тоном. Наверное, Давид растерянно посмотрел на неё. [«Я имею в виду: прыгал перед служанками, словно какой-то пустой человек с улицы!»]

Наверное, Давид был потрясён. [«Я делал это для Господа, для Того, Кто избрал меня царём вместо твоего отца»].

Представляю, как Мелхола поморщилась. Ой! [«Зачем ты бросаешь мне это в лицо?»]

[«Я знаю, что пал в твоих глазах»,]* — продолжил Давид, — [«но те служанки, о которых ты говорила, ценят меня»].

Я думаю о заблудшей женщине из нашего города, которую дети выгнали из дома, и задаюсь вопросом: кто позаботится о ней через сорок лет, когда её хорошенькое лицо покроется морщинами, а спина согнётся?

Я представляю одинокую старость Мелхолы. Рассказ завершается словами, что до самой смерти у неё не было детей. Сомневаюсь, что её муж-царь и дальше заходил к ней. Зачем бы ему? Другие воздавали ему более чем достаточно почестей. Мне также интересно, ослабили ли неуважение Мелхолы к Давиду и их размолвка царя Давида. Несколько глав спустя рассказывается, как его взгляд блуждал по жене соседа и к какому греху это привело.

Каждая жена испытывает искушение бесчестить своего мужа. Нас искушает проявлять неуважение независимо от того, царь наш муж или механик, благочестив он или нет.

Каждый день я выбираю: чтить или бесчестить мужа, которого дал мне Бог. Я могу идти рядом с ним, с воодушевлением поддерживая его, а могу высунуться из окна и смотреть на него с презрением в сердце. Я могу замечать, что он делает хорошо, и хвалить его, а могу пилить за то, что он делает не так. От моего выбора зависит, ответит ли он мне взаимной благосклонностью или отвернётся. Мой выбор влияет не только на меня и моего мужа, но и на целое облако свидетелей… на моих детей, сестёр во Христе и соседей.

«А жена да уважает своего мужа».
(Ефесянам 5:33б)

“Could you come with me to visit my sister and her husband?” a friend asked my husband. “They’re having serious marriage problems. My brother-in-law saw how God is working in our marriage and asked me how it happened. Can you tell them how God could change their marriage, too?”

At dusk that evening, my husband, and I, waited with our friend outside his sister’s home. Half an hour later a dilapidated red pickup chugged up and shuddered to a stop. An overweight man with grease-covered clothes and a perpetual smile heaved himself out from behind the steering wheel, while his pretty, fashionably dressed wife hopped out of the passenger seat.

“Come in! Come in!” they invited, guiding us to the stairway which led to their living quarters.

“Excuse the mess,” the wife apologized, swiping clothes from the couches so we could take seats. The room was elaborately furnished but dirty. A deep layer of dust covered the top of the large-screen television set, the end tables… everything.

“Lord, give us wisdom,” I silently implored as we took seats across from the couple. How could we connect with folks we scarcely knew, and who did not have God in their lives?

The husband talked. His wife had failed him miserably and had cheated on him many times. She was presently meeting with a new boyfriend, a young chap she had learned to know on the street. “But I’ll forgive you all that,” promised the husband, “If you are willing to start over, be my wife, and be a mom to our children. I know you’ve failed, but we all fail. Let’s start over, Dear.”

The wife sat in stony silence. Our friend talked, pleading with his sister and brother-in-law to be reconciled. My husband talked about God and His plan for marriage, urging them to turn to Him.

Finally, the wife opened her mouth. Bitterness poured out; dishonor; old dirt. “You never show me that you care. You never buy me anything. Why should I try to please you anymore?”

The husband joined the fray. Both talked at once, on and on, louder and louder.

We sat with sagging hearts, listening, praying, thinking. I tried to imagine how the wife must have felt. She was pretty and young. Why stay at home to clean, cook, and wash clothes for a hulk of a husband who spent his days leaning over greasy motors and crawling under dirty cars? Why, when she could have fun on the street with a cool, young fellow who made her feel so-o-o special?

Finally, the couple ran out of steam. We sat in sad silence. “I’m sorry,” my husband stated finally, “but we can’t help you. The only one who can help you is God. And if you don’t want His help, there’s no hope for your marriage.”

“Yeah, I really should go to church,” mumbled the husband.

“Ha, ha,” sneered the wife. “Just see you become a Mennonite yet!” We rose and shook hands, promised our prayers, and left.

After we left that evening, more harsh words flew between the couple. Their two children came upon the scene and, siding with their father, drove their mother from the house.

From far in the distance came a sound of music—and what else? Singing. Joyful shouting. A wife threw open the shutter from a window facing the street, leaned out, and peered up the road. Oh, yes, today is the day my husband went to bring the Ark of the Covenant home. But why are they making such a ruckus over it?

Into the city danced the parade, singing, shouting, and blowing trumpets. David danced with all his might, his heart overflowing with thanks to God. After agonizing years of fleeing from Saul, God had established him as king. And now the Ark of the Lord was finally returning to its proper dwelling place… God be praised!

As David leaped and shouted his way up the street, his wife looked down from her perch at the window with a dark scowl on her face. Just look at how his robe flies around as he dances. Doesn’t he have any shame?! And hollering like that… what a way for a king to act! Doesn’t he care what others think?!

David returned home several hours later—tired, but happy—to bless his household. It had been a good day. He could tell his wife, Michal, all about it at the supper table.

But she beat him to the subject. [“My, but didn’t you act gloriously today,”] were her frosty words. David must have looked confused. [“I mean, jumping around like that in front of the maidens, just like a vain fellow from off the streets!”]

David must have been smitten. [“I was doing it to the Lord, to the one who chose me to be king instead of your father.”]

I imagine Michal wincing. Ouch! [“Why do you have to throw that in my face?”]

[“I know I am low in your esteem,”]* continued David, [“but those maidens you mentioned, they esteem me.”]

I think of the wayward lady in town who was chased from home by her children, and I wonder who will care for her forty years from now when her pretty face is wrinkled, and her back is bent.

I picture Michal’s lonely old age. The account ends by saying she had no children until her dying day. I doubt if her king-husband bothered to stop in with her anymore. Why would he? He received honor aplenty from others. I also wonder if Michal’s dishonor and their fall-out weakened King David. Several chapters later tell of his eyes roving to a neighbor’s wife and the resulting sin.

All wives are tempted to dishonor their husbands. We are tempted to dishonor regardless of whether our husband is a king or a mechanic, godly or ungodly.

Every day I choose to honor or dishonor the husband God gave me. I can skip alongside him, supporting with enthusiasm, or I can hang out the window, watching with scorn in my heart. I can focus on what he does well and compliment him, or I can nag about what he does wrong. My choice determines the reciprocating favor or loss. My choice affects, not only my husband and me, but also a cloud of witnesses… my children, my sisters in Christ, and my neighbors.

“And the wife see that she reverence her husband.”
(Ephesians 5:33b)

« Pourrais-tu m’accompagner rendre visite à ma sœur et à son mari ? » demanda un ami à mon mari. « Ils ont de graves problèmes conjugaux. Mon beau-frère a vu comment Dieu agit dans notre mariage et m’a demandé comment cela s’était passé. Peux-tu leur dire comment Dieu pourrait, lui aussi, transformer leur mariage ? »

Ce soir-là, au crépuscule, mon mari et moi avons attendu avec notre ami devant la maison de sa sœur. Une demi-heure plus tard, un vieux pick-up rouge bringuebalant a pétaradé jusqu’à nous et s’est immobilisé dans un soubresaut. Un homme corpulent, vêtu de vêtements couverts de graisse et arborant un sourire perpétuel, s’est extirpé du siège du conducteur, tandis que sa jolie épouse, habillée à la dernière mode, sautait du siège passager.

« Entrez ! Entrez ! » nous ont-ils invités, en nous guidant vers l’escalier qui menait à leurs pièces d’habitation.

« Excusez le désordre », s’est excusée l’épouse en retirant des vêtements des canapés pour que nous puissions nous asseoir. La pièce était meublée avec faste, mais sale. Une épaisse couche de poussière recouvrait le dessus du grand téléviseur, les guéridons… tout.

« Seigneur, donne-nous de la sagesse », ai-je imploré en silence tandis que nous prenions place en face du couple. Comment pouvions-nous établir un lien avec des gens que nous connaissions à peine et qui n’avaient pas Dieu dans leur vie ?

Le mari a pris la parole. Sa femme l’avait terriblement déçu et l’avait trompé à maintes reprises. En ce moment, elle fréquentait un nouveau petit ami, un jeune homme qu’elle avait appris à connaître dans la rue. « Mais je te pardonnerai tout cela, promettait le mari, si tu es prête à repartir à zéro, à être ma femme et la mère de nos enfants. Je sais que tu as failli, mais nous faisons tous des erreurs. Repartons à zéro, ma chérie. »

La femme est restée assise, silencieuse comme une pierre. Notre ami a pris la parole, suppliant sa sœur et son beau-frère de se réconcilier. Mon mari a parlé de Dieu et de son plan pour le mariage, les exhortant à se tourner vers lui.

Enfin, la femme a ouvert la bouche. L’amertume s’est déversée ; le manque de respect ; de vieilles rancœurs. « Tu ne me montres jamais que tu tiens à moi. Tu ne m’achètes jamais rien. Pourquoi devrais-je encore essayer de te faire plaisir ? »

Le mari s’est mêlé à la dispute. Tous deux parlaient en même temps, sans arrêt, de plus en plus fort.

Nous étions assis, le cœur lourd, à écouter, prier, réfléchir. J’ai essayé d’imaginer ce que la femme devait ressentir. Elle était jolie et jeune. Pourquoi rester à la maison pour nettoyer, cuisiner et laver les vêtements d’un mari baraqué qui passait ses journées penché sur des moteurs graisseux et à ramper sous des voitures sales ? Pourquoi, alors qu’elle pouvait s’amuser dans la rue avec un jeune gars branché qui la faisait se sentir siiii spéciale ?

Finalement, le couple n’a plus eu la force de continuer. Nous sommes restés assis dans un silence triste. « Je suis désolé, a fini par dire mon mari, mais nous ne pouvons pas vous aider. Le seul qui puisse vous aider, c’est Dieu. Et si vous ne voulez pas de son aide, il n’y a aucun espoir pour votre mariage. »

« Oui, je devrais vraiment aller à l’église », a marmonné le mari.

« Ha, ha », a ricané la femme. « On verra si tu deviens mennonite, tiens ! » Nous nous sommes levés et avons échangé une poignée de main, promis de prier pour eux, puis nous sommes partis.

Après notre départ, ce soir-là, les paroles blessantes ont continué de fuser entre les époux. Leurs deux enfants sont arrivés sur les lieux et, prenant le parti de leur père, ont chassé leur mère de la maison.

Du lointain nous parvenait un son de musique… et quoi d’autre ? Des chants. Des cris de joie. Une femme a ouvert le volet d’une fenêtre donnant sur la rue, s’est penchée et a regardé au loin. Ah oui, aujourd’hui, c’est le jour où mon mari est allé chercher l’Arche de l’Alliance pour la ramener. Mais pourquoi font-ils tant de vacarme ?

Le cortège a dansé en entrant dans la ville, chantant, criant et faisant retentir les trompettes. David dansait de toutes ses forces, le cœur débordant de reconnaissance envers Dieu. Après des années d’angoisse à fuir Saül, Dieu l’avait établi roi. Et maintenant, l’Arche du Seigneur allait enfin retrouver sa demeure légitime… Loué soit Dieu !

Tandis que David bondissait et criait dans la rue, sa femme le regardait d’en haut, depuis son poste à la fenêtre, le visage assombri par une moue méprisante. Regarde donc comme son manteau vole autour de lui pendant qu’il danse. N’a-t-il donc aucune honte ?! Et ces hurlements… quelle façon de se comporter pour un roi ! Se soucie-t-il donc de ce que pensent les autres ?!

David est rentré chez lui plusieurs heures plus tard — fatigué, mais heureux — pour bénir les siens. C’était une belle journée. Il pourrait tout raconter à sa femme, Mical, à table, au souper.

Mais elle a abordé le sujet la première. [« Eh bien, tu t’es couvert de gloire aujourd’hui »,] lui a-t-elle lancé froidement. David a dû avoir l’air perplexe. [« Je veux dire, à sauter ainsi devant les jeunes filles, comme un vulgaire vaurien de la rue ! »]

David a dû se sentir blessé. [« Je le faisais pour le Seigneur, celui qui m’a choisi pour être roi à la place de ton père. »]

J’imagine Mical grimacer. Aïe ! [« Pourquoi faut-il que tu me jettes cela au visage ? »]

[« Je sais que je suis peu estimé à tes yeux »,]* a poursuivi David, [« mais ces jeunes filles dont tu parles, elles, m’estiment. »]

Je pense à cette femme égarée de la ville, que ses enfants ont chassée de la maison, et je me demande qui prendra soin d’elle dans quarante ans, quand son joli visage sera ridé et son dos courbé.

J’imagine la vieillesse solitaire de Mical. Le récit se termine en disant qu’elle n’eut pas d’enfant jusqu’au jour de sa mort. Je doute que son époux, le roi, ait encore pris la peine de venir la voir. Pourquoi l’aurait-il fait ? Il recevait déjà amplement d’honneurs de la part des autres. Je me demande aussi si le mépris de Mical et leur brouille ont affaibli le roi David. Quelques chapitres plus loin, le récit raconte que son regard s’est porté sur la femme de son voisin et qu’il a commis un péché à la suite de cela.

Toutes les épouses sont tentées de manquer de respect à leur mari. Nous sommes tentées de lui manquer de respect, que notre mari soit roi ou mécanicien, pieux ou impie.

Chaque jour, je choisis d’honorer ou de déshonorer le mari que Dieu m’a donné. Je peux gambader à ses côtés et le soutenir avec enthousiasme, ou rester à la fenêtre, à l’observer avec mépris dans le cœur. Je peux mettre l’accent sur ce qu’il fait bien et le complimenter, ou le harceler à propos de ce qu’il fait mal. Mon choix détermine la faveur qu’il me rendra ou la perte de cette faveur. Mon choix a des conséquences non seulement pour mon mari et moi, mais aussi pour une nuée de témoins… mes enfants, mes sœurs en Christ et mes voisins.

« Et que la femme respecte son mari. »
(Éphésiens 5:33b)

* C’est ainsi que le dit la Bible espagnole ; l’idée est plus claire que dans la traduction anglaise.

“제 여동생과 남편을 만나러 저와 함께 가 주실 수 있을까요?” 한 친구가 남편에게 물었습니다. “두 사람이 심각한 결혼 문제를 겪고 있어요. 제 매제는 하나님께서 우리 결혼 생활 가운데 어떻게 일하시는지 보고, 어떻게 그런 일이 일어났는지 제게 물었어요. 하나님께서 그들의 결혼 생활도 어떻게 변화시키실 수 있는지 말해 주시겠어요?”

그날 저녁 해 질 무렵, 남편과 나는 친구의 여동생 집 밖에서 친구와 함께 기다렸습니다. 30분쯤 지나자 낡은 빨간 픽업트럭 한 대가 덜컹거리며 다가와 덜덜 떨다가 멈춰 섰습니다. 기름때가 묻은 옷을 입고 늘 웃는 얼굴을 한 뚱뚱한 남자가 운전석에서 몸을 힘겹게 빼냈고, 예쁘고 유행에 맞게 차려입은 아내는 조수석에서 폴짝 뛰어내렸습니다.

“어서 들어오세요! 들어오세요!” 그들은 우리를 생활공간으로 이어지는 계단으로 안내했습니다.

“집이 어수선해서 죄송해요.” 아내는 우리가 앉을 수 있도록 소파 위의 옷가지들을 치우며 사과했습니다. 방에는 가구가 화려하게 갖춰져 있었지만 더러웠습니다. 대형 텔레비전 위며 사이드 테이블이며… 모든 곳에 먼지가 두껍게 쌓여 있었습니다.

부부와 마주 앉으며 나는 속으로 간구했습니다. “주님, 저희에게 지혜를 주소서.” 하나님을 삶에 모시지 않은, 거의 알지도 못하는 사람들과 어떻게 마음을 나눌 수 있을까요?

남편이 이야기를 했습니다. 아내는 그를 몹시 실망시켰고 여러 번 바람을 피웠습니다. 지금은 거리에서 알게 된 젊은 남자친구를 만나고 있었습니다. “하지만 그 모든 걸 용서할게.” 남편이 약속했습니다. “네가 새로 시작해서 내 아내가 되고 우리 아이들의 엄마가 될 마음이 있다면 말이야. 네가 잘못한 건 알아. 하지만 우리 모두 잘못을 하잖아. 다시 시작하자, 여보.”

아내는 돌처럼 굳은 채 말없이 앉아 있었습니다. 친구는 여동생과 매제에게 화해하라고 간청하며 이야기했습니다. 남편은 하나님과 그분의 결혼 계획에 대해 말하며, 하나님께로 돌아오라고 권했습니다.

마침내 아내가 입을 열었습니다. 원망과 모욕, 묵은 불만이 쏟아져 나왔습니다. “당신은 내가 소중하다는 걸 한 번도 보여 주지 않아. 내게 뭘 사 준 적도 없잖아. 내가 더는 왜 당신을 기쁘게 하려고 애써야 해?”

남편도 말다툼에 끼어들었습니다. 두 사람은 동시에 말했고, 쉬지 않고 점점 더 큰 소리로 말했습니다.

우리는 마음이 무거운 채 앉아 듣고, 기도하고, 생각했습니다. 아내의 마음이 어떨지 상상해 보았습니다. 그녀는 예쁘고 젊었습니다. 기름때 묻은 모터에 몸을 숙이고 더러운 차 밑을 기어 다니며 하루를 보내는 거구 같은 남편을 위해 집에 남아 청소하고 요리하고 빨래를 해야 할 이유가 있을까요? 자신을 아주 특별한 사람처럼 느끼게 해 주는 멋진 젊은이와 거리에서 즐겁게 지낼 수 있는데 말입니다.

마침내 부부는 더는 할 말을 잃었습니다. 우리는 슬픔에 잠긴 채 말없이 앉아 있었습니다. “죄송하지만,” 마침내 남편이 말했습니다. “저희는 도와드릴 수 없습니다. 여러분을 도울 수 있는 분은 하나님뿐입니다. 그리고 하나님의 도움을 원하지 않는다면, 여러분 결혼 생활에는 희망이 없습니다.”

“그래요, 정말 교회에 나가야겠어요.” 남편이 중얼거렸습니다.

“하, 하.” 아내가 비웃었습니다. “두고 봐요, 당신도 결국 메노나이트가 되겠지!” 우리는 일어나 악수를 나누고 기도하겠다고 약속한 뒤 떠났습니다.

그날 저녁 우리가 떠난 뒤에도 부부 사이에는 더 거친 말들이 오갔습니다. 두 아이가 그 광경을 보고 아버지 편을 들어 어머니를 집에서 내쫓았습니다.

저 멀리서 음악 소리가 들려왔습니다. 그리고 또 무엇이 들렸을까요? 노랫소리였습니다. 기쁨에 찬 함성도 들렸습니다. 거리 쪽으로 난 창의 덧문을 아내가 활짝 열고 몸을 내밀어 길 위쪽을 바라보았습니다. 아, 맞다. 오늘 남편이 언약궤를 집으로 모셔 오는 날이지. 그런데 그 일로 왜 저렇게 야단법석을 떠는 거지?

노래하고 외치며 나팔을 부는 행렬이 춤추듯 도시 안으로 들어왔습니다. 다윗은 온 힘을 다해 춤을 추었고, 하나님께 드리는 감사로 마음이 넘쳤습니다. 사울에게 쫓겨 다니며 괴로웠던 세월이 지나고 하나님께서 그를 왕으로 세우셨습니다. 이제 주님의 궤가 마침내 제자리에 있는 거처로 돌아오고 있었습니다… 하나님을 찬양하라!

다윗이 길을 따라 뛰고 외치며 올라가자, 아내는 창가에 선 자리에서 얼굴을 어둡게 찌푸리고 그를 내려다보았습니다. 춤춘다고 겉옷이 펄럭이는 꼴 좀 봐. 부끄러운 줄도 모르나?! 저렇게 고함까지 지르다니… 왕이 할 짓이야? 남들이 어떻게 생각할지는 신경도 안 쓰나?!

몇 시간 뒤 다윗은 피곤했지만 기쁜 마음으로 집에 돌아와 가족을 축복했습니다. 좋은 하루였습니다. 저녁 식탁에서 아내 미갈에게 그날 있었던 일을 모두 들려줄 수 있었습니다.

하지만 미갈이 먼저 말을 꺼냈습니다. [“오늘 참 영광스럽게도 행동하셨더군요.”] 그녀의 말은 차가웠습니다. 다윗은 어리둥절했을 것입니다. [“아가씨들 앞에서 그렇게 폴짝폴짝 뛰시다니, 길거리에서 온 허영심 많은 사람이나 할 짓을 하셨잖아요!”]

다윗은 마음이 상했을 것입니다. [“나는 주님을 위해 그렇게 한 것이오. 당신 아버지가 아니라 나를 왕으로 택하신 분을 위해서 말이오.”]

미갈이 움찔했으리라 생각합니다. 아야! [“왜 그런 말까지 해서 나를 아프게 해야 해요?”]

[“나는 당신 눈에 하찮은 사람인 줄 알고 있소,”]* 다윗은 말을 이었습니다. [“하지만 당신이 말한 그 아가씨들은 나를 존중하오.”]

아이들에게 집에서 쫓겨난 동네의 방탕한 여인을 생각하면, 예쁜 얼굴에 주름이 지고 등이 굽을 마흔 해 뒤에 누가 그녀를 돌봐 줄지 궁금해집니다.

나는 미갈이 외롭게 늙어 가는 모습을 그려 봅니다. 기록은 미갈이 죽는 날까지 자녀가 없었다고 끝맺습니다. 왕인 남편이 더는 그녀를 찾아 들를 마음이 있었을지 의문입니다. 그럴 이유가 어디 있겠습니까? 그는 다른 이들에게서 충분히 존경을 받았습니다. 미갈이 남편을 존중하지 않은 일과 두 사람의 불화가 다윗 왕을 약하게 했는지도 궁금합니다. 몇 장 뒤에는 다윗의 눈길이 이웃의 아내에게 향하고, 그 결과 죄를 짓는 이야기가 나옵니다.

모든 아내는 남편을 존중하지 않으려는 유혹을 받습니다. 남편이 왕이든 정비공이든, 경건하든 경건하지 않든 우리는 남편을 존중하지 않으려는 유혹을 받습니다.

나는 매일 하나님께서 내게 주신 남편을 존중할지 존중하지 않을지 선택합니다. 기쁜 마음으로 남편 곁을 뛰어가며 응원할 수도 있고, 창밖으로 몸을 내밀어 마음속에 경멸을 품은 채 지켜볼 수도 있습니다. 남편이 잘하는 일에 초점을 맞추어 칭찬할 수도 있고, 잘못하는 일을 두고 잔소리할 수도 있습니다. 나의 선택은 호의가 되돌아오거나 사라지는 결과를 낳습니다. 나의 선택은 남편과 나뿐 아니라 증인들의 구름, 곧 자녀와 그리스도 안의 자매들, 이웃들에게도 영향을 미칩니다…

“아내도 자기 남편을 경외할지니라.”
(에베소서 5:33b)
