Matthew 11:15, Matthew 13:9, Matthew 13:43, Mark 4:9, Mark 4:23, Mark 7:16, Luke 8:8, Luke 14:35
Matthew 11:15; 13:9, 43, Mark 4:9, 23; 7:16, Luke 8:8; 14:35

If there ever was a catch phrase of our Lord Jesus Christ, this would surely be it. Sometimes in the beginning of a discourse and sometimes at the conclusion, the audience would observe Him pause during the address, glance around His company, and say, “He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.” It was a solemn summons to reflect upon that which was being brought to their attention. It was a deft reminder to those within the sound of His voice to take full responsibility for what they had heard. All were listening, but not all were hearing. Christ knew it intuitively. He could read it from the look on their faces. All ears were subject unto the same words, but every heart was handling the discourse differently.

There was once a lad who responded to his mother, “Sure, I heard you calling, but you didn’t sound like you meant it yet.” Thus, we come to understand that hearing is not a mere physical activity. Rather, it is the reaction of the soul to the audibles which have been placed before it. Just as two men may gaze upon the same event yet see in it very different things, likewise, they may listen to the same set of words and conclude the most dissimilar of perceptions. For it is not with the ear that we hear but rather with the soul. We cannot choose everything that rides the air waves and penetrates our ears, but our soul can pass verdict on it all. What we hear is not only a revelation of the tongue of another, but of our own character as well. It exposes our loves and our hates. It excites or resists our ruling passions. It unveils our character and paves our destiny. Two men looked through the prison bars. The one saw mud, the other saw stars –unknown.

Of course, there is a literal sense in which our hearing is independent of our will. We cannot choose entirely what we hear any more than we can choose everything that we see. Every day there are thousands of vibrations hurled toward us in rapid succession, and we hear them whether we want to or not. Some are bold and obvious. Others are subliminal, and only our subconscious mind receives them. Those who dwell in the city are bombarded by the multiplicity of sounds of the street. Those stationed by the ocean cannot escape the droning music of the sea.

Our minds are accustomed to turn off monotonous tones no matter how loud the input. Still, when matters of import break our realm, we listen with keen interest. While the driver of an automobile may only hear the steady modulation of engine beneath his controls, the seasoned mechanic may hear a dozen other sounds coming from the same vehicle. Is it a blemish in the virtue of the first who cannot hear the misfiring cylinder or the rasping brakes? Yes, for it is not by the ear that we hear, but by the character of our will. If he were to care, he could also learn to hear. So, it is true in spiritual matters. A sermon that litigates the soul is a revelation of the preacher. How we respond to the motivation and challenge is a revelation of the hearer.

Our Unique Personality

Those disinterested in mathematics, motors, or music can get along in life just fine, though they fail to assimilate ninety percent of the sounds that enter their realm of hearing concerning these topics. It is when our major interests fall outside the realm of God that our ability to hear is considered to be handicapped. We may possess the best of intentions to be a sincere believer, but without the innate quickening of the Spirit, we will fail to comprehend the things that God would have us to hear.

The things that we set our hearts upon, and intuitively give our energies to, will determine what we hear. Every temptation we have ever met, and every sin we have ever fought and mastered, determines the kinds of thing that we shall hear as we take our pilgrimage. Live sparingly and you shall hear sparingly, though you be listening to an angel from heaven. Live nobly and you will hear nobly, though all that the ear catches is but mediocrity.

There was a crowd of people who had the golden opportunity to hear the voice of the Creator Himself. The people therefore, that stood by, and heard it, said that it thundered: others said, An angel spake to him –John 12:29. It was the same voice that resonated upon every ear, and, yet, to one it sounded like the angels, and to another there was nothing in it save the garbled roll of the thunder in the hills. If only the human ear had been involved, there would be no diversity of testimony. But these men were not hearing with the ear; they were hearing by what they were. Their heart’s orientation, enhanced by all their past, their habits, their traditions, and their manner of taking in the common things of life drew their own conclusion subconsciously concerning the interpretation of the Lord’s voice.

This happens to all on a constant daily basis. Our verdict of others is our own verdict. Often our judgment of a minister or a sermon is really the judgment of ourselves. We are listening, not with the bodily ear, but with our loves and hates, our grudges and preferences. We are listening through the hidden recesses within our heart. When Christ said, …ye cannot hear my word –John 8:43, it was not due to the lack of a microphone. There was no physical barrier. The hurdle was spiritual. Prejudices, jealousies, and antagonisms made the message of Christ inaudible to them, though every syllable fell upon their ears.

Why do ye not understand my speech? even because ye cannot hear my word. Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do … He that is of God heareth God’s words: ye therefore hear them not, because ye are not of God –John 8:43-47.

There is an elusive and gnawing factor corroding the moral fiber of this nation. While some would conclude that attention deficit disorder is a disease relentlessly attacking its victims against their will, honesty will surely deem it otherwise. It could very well be considered spiritual attention deficit. This is nominally just selective interest. Place a smart phone or video game before the eyes of most of these individuals and there is no lack of attention given to it. Our interests are trained by our environment. Those who spend countless hours in front of a television and video images are crippling their ability to hear a solemn message. The more our ears are exposed to decrepit signals the more surely we will handicap them from hearing the Word of God.

Fat Hearts

And he said, Go, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not. Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and convert, and be healed –Isaiah 6:9-10.

While some resign themselves to this fate, others will guard themselves from the ears’ greatest enemies…

…Distraction

We live in a society where people thrive on activity and are loathe to sit still. They have been trained to give their attention to the gadgetry of the electronic world and social input. If a text message falls upon their device, it will surely take their immediate attention while any prayerful meditation must wait on the back burner. Those who spend much time before a video screen will have their ears deadened by the encroachment of a new scene every five seconds (on average). Place this up against an hour of in-depth preaching and these souls will be gasping for air. For many of us, solitude has become nearly extinct since the advent of the cell phone and social media, while our attention span has fatefully eroded.

…Perfection

We play only the finest recorded music in our headset. This can deafen our ears to the message of the sincere and humble offerings of common singing. The message often becomes despised and discarded because the package is imperfect. As the intellectual standard is raised, often the heart sinks lower still. Who today would be stirred by the message from the lips of foolish and unlearned fishermen? If an orator must be articulate and schooled in the professional world in order to hold our attention, it is doubtful that we would be impressed by the fuzzy rumblings from heaven. Those who need the gospel offered to them upon a silver platter will surely grow leaner in spirit while their hearts grow fatter.

…Fiction

From movies to novels, we have been bombarded with the ideals of greener pastures elsewhere. A girl feeding on romance stories will surely be disappointed once she’s married. That which is common will never stir our appetite so long as it is being fed by fictitious elements without. …A prophet is not without honour, save in his own country, and in his own house –Matthew 13:57. We know the imperfections of our home minister, brother, or family member. If they should bring us a message from the throne of God, dull ears will miss it. People will flock to hear inspirational preaching and seminar propaganda in an ecumenical setting. While great truth may be presented, the environment is surreal and often only serves to the fattening of the heart and eventual disappointment at home.

…Reputation

Many people will listen to a myriad of voices in order to preserve their self-image. We call it open-mindedness. But heaven knows that the many questionable things that people bring to our attention really depend upon our meager character and would never reach us if Christ were our full devotion. There are those with whom we would never dream of sharing our gossip. They do not hear it because of a principle they hold within. Nobody brings them nasty or lewd tales simply because of their known character. If someone were to tell me an objectionable story, I should be very much ashamed. Not only of the narrator, but of myself also. I should be ashamed that he had such thoughts of me and of the kind of thing that I love to hear that he should venture to bring such garbage to my attention. So, very often, the sort of thing we hear depends on the sort of character we bear. Thus, we are ultimately responsible for what we allow to enter our soul through our ears.

Burning Hearts

As two bedraggled disciples trudged the road to Emmaus, they were overtaken by a heavenly visitor who inquired into their melancholy mood. They had read the prophets, heard Christ speak, perhaps had seen the miracles, and then had watched Him suffer and die. While they marveled at this newcomer’s oblivious ignorance to the current events, He described them as …slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken –Luke 24:25. As the evening continued and they realized that they had been face to face with the resurrected Savior, …they said one to another, Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures? –Luke 24:32.

Some may claim that to ‘make hearts burn’ is the responsibility of every faithful minister. This must be reconsidered. There is certainly no room for halfhearted preaching from halfhearted ministers. Those who are called to such a noble position should take the responsibility seriously enough to make it their utmost concern to provide solid milk and meat to their listeners. But those who find it their responsibility to make the hearts of the audience burn will often fall prey to animated preaching (call louder, perhaps they will respond; touch the emotional chords, perhaps they will weep). But speaking techniques can only administer earthly dynamics. It is the truth, alone, that can shake the bedrock of the never-dying soul.

To make the hearts burn is primarily the responsibility of the Holy Spirit and the ears upon which the oration falls. Christ could have spoken the same words to the hardened Roman soldiers and been met with sordid indifference. Had he laid his message upon the ears of a pair of young lovers out on an evening stroll, they would have exited His presence at the first opportunity. Had He revealed Himself to the proud religious zealots, perhaps they would have attempted to kill Him again. No, this sermon fell upon the voracious appetite of devout seekers, and their hearts burned with the rapturous revelation falling upon their ears. So ardent was their love that …they rose up the same hour, and returned to Jerusalem, and found the eleven gathered together, and them that were with them –Luke 24:33.

All our hope is in our hearing and all selfishness is in our hearing—all the right that we have ever sought and all the wrong we have ever done. Love a person and his speech is sweet. Hate him and his every word is barbed. It is by love and hate, generosity and envy that we ingest each and every utterance. Thus, it is vital to self-knowledge not only to take heed to the words we say, but also to what we hear. My sheep hear my voice –John 10:27, says our Master—they hear it because they love the Shepherd. Those who will accept this responsibility must purge themselves from the rabble of earth-linked daydreams in order to give ear to the rising Day Star as His glowing rays dawn upon their burning hearts. We have also a more sure word of prophecy; whereunto ye do well that ye take heed, as unto a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts: –2 Peter 1:19.

Mateo 11:15, Mateo 13:9, Mateo 13:43, Marcos 4:9, Marcos 4:23, Marcos 7:16, Lucas 8:8, Lucas 14:35
Mateo 11:15; 13:9, 43, Marcos 4:9, 23; 7:16, Lucas 8:8; 14:35

Si alguna vez hubo una frase característica de nuestro Señor Jesucristo, seguramente sería esta. A veces al comienzo de un discurso y otras veces al concluirlo, el público lo veía hacer una pausa mientras hablaba, mirar a su alrededor y decir: «El que tiene oídos para oír, que oiga». Era un solemne llamado a reflexionar sobre aquello que se les estaba señalando. Era un hábil recordatorio para quienes estaban al alcance de su voz de que debían asumir plena responsabilidad por lo que habían oído. Todos escuchaban, pero no todos oían. Cristo lo sabía intuitivamente. Podía leerlo en sus rostros. Todos los oídos estaban expuestos a las mismas palabras, pero cada corazón recibía el discurso de manera diferente.

Una vez hubo un muchacho que le respondió a su madre: «Claro que te oí llamarme, pero no sonabas como si realmente lo dijeras en serio». Así llegamos a entender que oír no es una mera actividad física. Más bien, es la reacción del alma a los sonidos que se le presentan. Así como dos hombres pueden mirar el mismo acontecimiento y, sin embargo, ver cosas muy distintas en él, también pueden escuchar las mismas palabras y llegar a las percepciones más dispares. Porque no oímos con el oído, sino con el alma. No podemos elegir todo lo que viaja por las ondas y nos penetra los oídos, pero nuestra alma puede emitir un juicio sobre todo ello. Lo que oímos no solo revela la lengua de otra persona, sino también nuestro propio carácter. Pone al descubierto nuestros amores y nuestros odios. Estimula o resiste nuestras pasiones dominantes. Desvela nuestro carácter y allana el camino de nuestro destino. Dos hombres miraron a través de los barrotes de la prisión. Uno vio barro; el otro, estrellas —desconocido.

Por supuesto, hay un sentido literal en que nuestro oído es independiente de nuestra voluntad. No podemos elegir por completo lo que oímos, como tampoco podemos elegir todo lo que vemos. Cada día nos llegan miles de vibraciones en rápida sucesión, y las oímos queramos o no. Algunas son fuertes y evidentes. Otras son subliminales, y solo nuestra mente subconsciente las recibe. Quienes viven en la ciudad son bombardeados por la multitud de sonidos de la calle. Quienes residen junto al océano no pueden escapar de la música monótona del mar.

Nuestra mente está acostumbrada a desconectarse de los tonos monótonos, por muy fuerte que sea el estímulo. Sin embargo, cuando asuntos importantes irrumpen en nuestro ámbito, escuchamos con vivo interés. Mientras que el conductor de un automóvil quizá solo oiga la modulación constante del motor bajo su control, el mecánico experimentado puede oír una docena de sonidos más procedentes del mismo vehículo. ¿Es una falla en la virtud del primero que no pueda oír el cilindro que falla o el chirrido de los frenos? Sí, porque no oímos con el oído, sino con el carácter de nuestra voluntad. Si le importara, también podría aprender a oír. Lo mismo ocurre en los asuntos espirituales. Un sermón que examina el alma es una revelación del predicador. Nuestra respuesta al estímulo y al desafío revela al oyente.

Nuestra personalidad singular

Quienes no tienen interés en las matemáticas, los motores o la música pueden desenvolverse perfectamente en la vida, aunque no asimilen el noventa por ciento de los sonidos que llegan a su ámbito auditivo sobre esos temas. Nuestra capacidad de oír se considera discapacitada cuando nuestros principales intereses están fuera del ámbito de Dios. Podemos tener las mejores intenciones de ser creyentes sinceros, pero sin la vivificación innata del Espíritu, no lograremos comprender las cosas que Dios quiere que oigamos.

Las cosas en las que ponemos el corazón y a las que intuitivamente dedicamos nuestras energías determinarán lo que oímos. Cada tentación que hayamos enfrentado y cada pecado contra el que hayamos luchado y que hayamos dominado determinan el tipo de cosas que oiremos en nuestra peregrinación. Vive con moderación y oirás con moderación, aunque estés escuchando a un ángel del cielo. Vive con nobleza y oirás con nobleza, aunque todo lo que capte el oído no sea más que mediocridad.

Hubo una multitud de personas que tuvo la oportunidad de oro de oír la voz del Creador mismo. La gente, pues, que estaba allí y había oído, decía que había sido un trueno; otros decían: Un ángel le ha hablado —Juan 12:29. Fue la misma voz la que resonó en todos los oídos y, sin embargo, a unos les sonó como la voz de los ángeles, mientras que otros no oyeron en ella más que el estruendo confuso del trueno en las colinas. Si solo hubiera intervenido el oído humano, no habría diversidad de testimonios. Pero aquellos hombres no oían con el oído; oían según lo que eran. La orientación de su corazón, moldeada por todo su pasado, sus hábitos, sus tradiciones y su manera de asimilar las cosas cotidianas de la vida, los llevó inconscientemente a sacar sus propias conclusiones sobre la interpretación de la voz del Señor.

Esto les sucede a todos constantemente, día tras día. Nuestro juicio de los demás es nuestro propio juicio. A menudo, nuestro juicio de un ministro o de un sermón es en realidad un juicio de nosotros mismos. Escuchamos, no con el oído físico, sino con nuestros amores y odios, nuestros resentimientos y preferencias. Escuchamos a través de los recovecos ocultos de nuestro corazón. Cuando Cristo dijo: …no podéis oír mi palabra —Juan 8:43, no fue por falta de micrófono. No había ninguna barrera física. El obstáculo era espiritual. Los prejuicios, los celos y las hostilidades hicieron que el mensaje de Cristo les resultara inaudible, aunque cada sílaba llegaba a sus oídos.

¿Por qué no entendéis mi lenguaje? Porque no podéis oír mi palabra. Vosotros sois de vuestro padre el diablo, y queréis hacer los deseos de vuestro padre… El que es de Dios oye las palabras de Dios; por eso vosotros no las oís, porque no sois de Dios —Juan 8:43-47.

Hay un factor esquivo y persistente que corroe la fibra moral de esta nación. Aunque algunos concluyen que el trastorno por déficit de atención es una enfermedad que ataca implacablemente a sus víctimas contra su voluntad, la honestidad seguramente dictará otra cosa. Muy bien podría considerarse un déficit de atención espiritual. En términos sencillos, no es más que un interés selectivo. Pongan un teléfono inteligente o un videojuego frente a los ojos de la mayoría de estas personas y no les faltará atención para dedicársela. Nuestro entorno moldea nuestros intereses. Quienes pasan incontables horas frente al televisor y viendo imágenes de video están debilitando su capacidad de oír un mensaje solemne. Cuanto más se exponen nuestros oídos a señales degradantes, más seguramente les impedimos oír la Palabra de Dios.

Corazones endurecidos

Y dijo: Anda, y di a este pueblo: Oíd bien, pero no entendáis; mirad bien, pero no percibáis. Engruesa el corazón de este pueblo, y agrava sus oídos, y ciega sus ojos; no sea que vea con sus ojos, y oiga con sus oídos, y entienda con su corazón, y se convierta y sea sanado —Isaías 6:9-10.

Mientras que algunos se resignan a este destino, otros se protegerán de los mayores enemigos del oído…

…La distracción

Vivimos en una sociedad en la que la gente prospera con la actividad y detesta quedarse quieta. Se la ha entrenado para prestar atención a los aparatos del mundo electrónico y a los estímulos sociales. Si llega un mensaje de texto a su dispositivo, sin duda captará su atención de inmediato, mientras que cualquier meditación en oración tendrá que esperar. Quienes pasan mucho tiempo frente a una pantalla de video tendrán los oídos adormecidos por la aparición de una nueva escena cada cinco segundos (en promedio). Pónganlo frente a una hora de predicación profunda y estas almas estarán jadeando en busca de aire. Para muchos de nosotros, la soledad casi se ha extinguido desde la llegada del teléfono celular y las redes sociales, mientras que nuestra capacidad de atención se ha erosionado fatalmente.

…La perfección

Solo escuchamos la mejor música grabada en nuestros auriculares. Esto puede ensordecer nuestros oídos al mensaje de las ofrendas sinceras y humildes del canto común. A menudo se desprecia y desecha el mensaje porque el envoltorio es imperfecto. A medida que se eleva el nivel intelectual, el corazón suele hundirse aún más. ¿A quién conmovería hoy el mensaje pronunciado por labios de pescadores necios e ignorantes? Si un orador tiene que ser elocuente y estar formado en el ámbito profesional para captar nuestra atención, es dudoso que nos impresione el confuso retumbar del cielo. Quienes necesitan que se les sirva el evangelio en bandeja de plata seguramente se empobrecerán de espíritu mientras sus corazones engordan.

…La ficción

Desde las películas hasta las novelas, hemos sido bombardeados con ideales de pastos más verdes en otros lugares. Una muchacha que se alimenta de historias románticas seguramente se decepcionará una vez casada. Lo común nunca despertará nuestro apetito mientras este se alimente de elementos ficticios externos. …No hay profeta sin honra sino en su propia tierra y en su casa —Mateo 13:57. Conocemos las imperfecciones del ministro, hermano o familiar de nuestra iglesia. Si nos trajeran un mensaje del trono de Dios, los oídos apagados no lo captarían. La gente acudirá en masa a escuchar predicación inspiradora y la promoción de seminarios en un entorno ecuménico. Aunque se presente una gran verdad, el ambiente es irreal y a menudo solo sirve para engordar el corazón y provocar, finalmente, decepción en casa.

…La reputación

Muchas personas escucharán una multitud de voces para preservar su propia imagen. Lo llamamos mentalidad abierta. Pero el cielo sabe que las muchas cosas cuestionables que la gente nos presenta dependen realmente de nuestro escaso carácter y nunca nos llegarían si Cristo fuera nuestra plena devoción. Hay personas con quienes jamás soñaríamos compartir nuestros chismes. No los oyen por un principio que llevan dentro. Nadie les cuenta historias desagradables o indecentes, sencillamente por el carácter que se les conoce. Si alguien me contara una historia objetable, me avergonzaría mucho. No solo del narrador, sino también de mí mismo. Debería avergonzarme de que él tuviera esa opinión de mí y de las cosas que me gusta oír, hasta el punto de atreverse a traerme semejante basura. Así pues, muy a menudo, el tipo de cosas que oímos depende del tipo de carácter que tenemos. Por tanto, somos en última instancia responsables de lo que permitimos que entre en nuestra alma por los oídos.

Corazones ardientes

Mientras dos discípulos andrajosos avanzaban penosamente por el camino a Emaús, se les acercó un visitante celestial que les preguntó por su tristeza. Habían leído a los profetas, habían oído hablar a Cristo, quizá habían visto los milagros y luego lo habían visto sufrir y morir. Mientras se maravillaban de la ignorancia de este recién llegado sobre los acontecimientos recientes, él los describió como …tardos de corazón para creer todo lo que los profetas han dicho —Lucas 24:25. Al avanzar la noche y darse cuenta de que habían estado cara a cara con el Salvador resucitado, …se dijeron el uno al otro: ¿No ardía nuestro corazón en nosotros, mientras nos hablaba en el camino y cuando nos abría las Escrituras? —Lucas 24:32.

Algunos quizá afirmen que «hacer arder los corazones» es responsabilidad de todo ministro fiel. Esto debe reconsiderarse. Desde luego, no hay lugar para una predicación tibia por parte de ministros tibios. Quienes han sido llamados a tan noble posición deben asumir la responsabilidad con la suficiente seriedad para hacer de su máxima preocupación ofrecer leche y alimento sólido a sus oyentes. Pero quienes consideran que es su responsabilidad hacer arder los corazones del público a menudo caerán presa de una predicación teatral (hablar más fuerte, quizá respondan; tocar las fibras emocionales, quizá lloren). Pero las técnicas de oratoria solo pueden producir dinámicas terrenales. Solo la verdad puede sacudir los cimientos del alma inmortal.

Hacer arder los corazones es principalmente responsabilidad del Espíritu Santo y de los oídos a los que llega el discurso. Cristo podría haber dicho las mismas palabras a los endurecidos soldados romanos y haber recibido a cambio una indiferencia abyecta. Si hubiera dirigido su mensaje a los oídos de una pareja de jóvenes enamorados que paseaban al atardecer, se habrían marchado de su presencia en la primera oportunidad. Si se hubiera revelado a los orgullosos fanáticos religiosos, quizá habrían intentado matarlo otra vez. No; este sermón llegó al apetito voraz de unos buscadores devotos, y sus corazones ardieron con la revelación arrebatadora que llegaba a sus oídos. Su amor era tan ferviente que …se levantaron a la misma hora y regresaron a Jerusalén, y hallaron reunidos a los once y a los que estaban con ellos —Lucas 24:33.

Toda nuestra esperanza está en lo que oímos, y todo egoísmo también; todo el bien que hemos buscado y todo el mal que hemos hecho. Ama a una persona y sus palabras te parecerán dulces. Ódiala y cada palabra suya tendrá espinas. Es mediante el amor y el odio, la generosidad y la envidia, que asimilamos cada expresión. Por eso, para conocernos a nosotros mismos, es vital prestar atención no solo a las palabras que decimos, sino también a lo que oímos. Mis ovejas oyen mi voz —Juan 10:27, dice nuestro Maestro; la oyen porque aman al Pastor. Quienes acepten esta responsabilidad deben purificarse del tumulto de las ensoñaciones terrenales para prestar oído a la Estrella de la Mañana que se alza, mientras sus rayos resplandecientes amanecen sobre sus corazones ardientes. Tenemos también la palabra profética más segura; a la cual hacéis bien en estar atentos como a una lámpara que alumbra en un lugar oscuro, hasta que el día esclarezca y el lucero de la mañana salga en vuestros corazones: —2 Pedro 1:19.

We all have a story. Some feel like Job sometimes. Some have lost parents, or partners, or children, or siblings, or friends. Some suffer from severe illness. Some will never recover from their illnesses. Our loved ones might have a terminal illness. Maybe a husband or parent is abusive or unfaithful. Like Job, our friends might have turned against us. Maybe there are problems in the church that seem impossible to fix. It could be something like a colicky baby, or a hyper child. Maybe we just have a cold and are feeling like everything is going wrong. The list is endless. We can relate to the words of this song.

Till the Storm Passes By

In the dark of the midnight have I oft hid my face,
While the storm howls above me, and there’s no hiding place.
‘Mid the crash of the thunder, Precious Lord, hear my cry,
Keep me safe till the storm passes by.

refrain:

Till the storm passes over, till the thunder sounds no more,
Till the clouds roll forever from the sky;
Hold me fast, let me stand in the hollow of Thy hand,
Keep me safe till the storm passes by.

Many times Satan whispered, “There is no need to try,
For there’s no end of sorrow, there’s no hope by and by”
But I know Thou art with me, and tomorrow I’ll rise
Where the storms never darken the skies.

When the long night has ended and the storms come no more,
Let me stand in Thy presence on the bright peaceful shore;
In that land where the tempest, never comes, Lord, may I
Dwell with Thee when the storm passes by.

–by Mosie Lister

When I was a little girl, I thought the author was referring to thunderstorms. I was afraid of thunderstorms. Now I understand that he was referring to the storms of life we go through. On July 14, 2013, I suddenly ended up in the hospital with a life-threatening heart attack caused by a spontaneous coronary artery dissection. What a shock for a 40-year-old mother. The storm was howling, and the thunder was crashing. There was no hiding place from the danger, for it was within me. I only had one heart and it could not be trusted. What if it happens again? Would I die? Then my children would be motherless.

This song was one I’d pray in the dark of the midnight when I couldn’t sleep, and fear threatened to overwhelm me. The Lord’s presence was very real to me. I came through this storm with a greater awareness of how God reveals Himself to us in a deeper way when we are going through hard times. We must choose to yield ourselves completely to Him, and say, “Not my will, but Thine be done.”

When the disciples were out on the sea in the storm, Jesus was with them. He is with us too. We can trust Him. Nothing will happen that is not according to His will. We do not always understand why things happen, but that’s okay. An old preacher used to quote:

“Not now, but in the coming years,
It may be in the better land
We’ll read the meaning of our tears,
And there, sometime, we’ll understand.”

It is so important that we accept what God allows in our lives. Accepting does not mean we don’t do anything about it. We will go to the doctor if necessary. We will reach out to others for comfort and council. We will still have all kinds of feelings, but we should have peace. We can’t wallow in self-pity and have a “poor me” attitude. And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose –Romans 8:28. I believe that. I can’t always see the good, but God does.

Life is hard sometimes, but the song tells about the time when the long night has ended, and the storms come no more. Dear sisters, let’s remain faithful and lean hard on the Lord through the storms of life.

Todos tenemos una historia. A veces, algunos se sienten como Job. Algunos han perdido a sus padres, a su pareja, a sus hijos, a sus hermanos o a sus amigos. Algunos padecen enfermedades graves. Algunos nunca se recuperarán de sus enfermedades. Nuestros seres queridos podrían padecer una enfermedad terminal. Quizá un esposo o uno de los padres sea abusivo o infiel. Como le sucedió a Job, nuestros amigos podrían haberse vuelto contra nosotros. Quizá haya problemas en la iglesia que parezcan imposibles de resolver. Podría tratarse de algo como un bebé con cólicos o un niño hiperactivo. Quizá simplemente tengamos un resfriado y sintamos que todo va mal. La lista no tiene fin. Podemos identificarnos con las palabras de este canto.

Hasta que pase la tormenta

En la oscuridad de la medianoche, a menudo he escondido mi rostro,
mientras la tormenta bramaba sobre mí y no había dónde esconderme.
Entre el estruendo de los truenos, precioso Señor, oye mi clamor,
mantenme a salvo hasta que pase la tormenta.

estribillo:

Hasta que pase la tormenta, hasta que no suene más el trueno,
hasta que las nubes se alejen para siempre del cielo;
sostenme firme, déjame estar en el hueco de tu mano,
mantenme a salvo hasta que pase la tormenta.

Muchas veces Satanás susurró: «No hay razón para intentarlo,
pues el dolor no tendrá fin, no habrá esperanza en el futuro».
Pero sé que estás conmigo, y mañana me levantaré
donde las tormentas nunca oscurecen los cielos.

Cuando haya terminado la larga noche y ya no vengan tormentas,
déjame estar en tu presencia, en la luminosa y apacible orilla;
en esa tierra donde nunca llega la tempestad, Señor, que pueda
morar contigo cuando pase la tormenta.

–por Mosie Lister

Cuando era una niña pequeña, pensaba que el autor se refería a las tormentas eléctricas. Les tenía miedo. Ahora entiendo que se refería a las tormentas de la vida que atravesamos. El 14 de julio de 2013, terminé repentinamente en el hospital por un infarto potencialmente mortal causado por una disección espontánea de una arteria coronaria. ¡Qué impacto para una madre de 40 años! La tormenta rugía y los truenos retumbaban. No había dónde esconderse del peligro, porque estaba dentro de mí. Solo tenía un corazón y no podía confiar en él. ¿Y si volvía a pasar? ¿Moriría? Entonces mis hijos se quedarían sin madre.

Este era un canto con el que oraba en la oscuridad de la medianoche, cuando no podía dormir y el miedo amenazaba con abrumarme. La presencia del Señor era muy real para mí. Atravesé esta tormenta con una mayor conciencia de cómo Dios se nos revela de una manera más profunda cuando pasamos por momentos difíciles. Debemos elegir entregarnos por completo a Él y decir: «No se haga mi voluntad, sino la tuya».

Cuando los discípulos estaban en el mar durante la tormenta, Jesús estaba con ellos. Él también está con nosotros. Podemos confiar en Él. Nada sucederá que no esté de acuerdo con su voluntad. No siempre entendemos por qué suceden las cosas, pero está bien. Un predicador de antaño solía citar:

«No ahora, sino en los años venideros,
quizá en la tierra mejor
comprendamos el significado de nuestras lágrimas,
y allí, algún día, entenderemos».

Es muy importante que aceptemos lo que Dios permite en nuestra vida. Aceptar no significa que no hagamos nada al respecto. Iremos al médico si es necesario. Buscaremos el consuelo y la orientación de otras personas. Seguiremos teniendo toda clase de sentimientos, pero debemos tener paz. No podemos revolcarnos en la autocompasión y adoptar una actitud de «pobre de mí». Y sabemos que Dios hace que todas las cosas cooperen para el bien de quienes aman a Dios, de quienes son llamados conforme a su propósito –Romanos 8:28. Yo lo creo. No siempre puedo ver el bien, pero Dios sí.

A veces la vida es difícil, pero el canto habla del momento en que la larga noche habrá terminado y ya no vendrán más tormentas. Queridas hermanas, permanezcamos fieles y apoyémonos firmemente en el Señor durante las tormentas de la vida.

Y vi un cielo nuevo y una tierra nueva; porque el primer cielo y la primera tierra habían pasado, y el mar ya no existía. Y yo, Juan, vi la ciudad santa, la nueva Jerusalén, que descendía de Dios, desde el cielo, dispuesta como una novia ataviada para su esposo. Y oí una gran voz del cielo que decía: He aquí el tabernáculo de Dios con los hombres, y él morará con ellos; y ellos serán su pueblo, y Dios mismo estará con ellos y será su Dios. Y Dios enjugará toda lágrágrima de sus ojos; y ya no habrá muerte, ni tristeza, ni llanto, ni habrá más dolor, porque las cosas anteriores han pasado. Apocalipsis 21:1-4.

Lord, this pain seems unbearable.
Things once loved now must die.
So many hearts are bleeding.
No one has kept a dry eye.

We’ve wept and writhed and prayed
Asking, Lord, this cup to avoid.
We tried what we thought might change it,
But all attempts seemed to return to us void.

Father, we’ve cried out for mercy,
All would have escaped this pain.
But Lord, You bade us go through it;
Your hand in it all You’ve made plain.

Our minds seem to spin as we ponder,
Just exactly what You’re trying to do.
Yet we know that no matter our feelings,
There’s a reason we this storm must go through.

So Father, we bow at Your feet now,
Acknowledging Your omnipotent might.
We cannot discern all the details,
But we trust in the end, all will be right.

Help us, Father, to be broken,
Releasing our all up to You.
Our rights, dreams, ambitions, and possessions,
Making everything open to Your view.

Grow in us, Lord, a humility,
Quiet, yet deep and true.
It’s a jewel that nothing but trials can teach.
Lord, through this, make us more like You!

May our eyes be set on You, Father,
Not on this o’erwhelming gale.
For You have gone through these deep waters,
Nothing but what You plan will prevail.

Obedient even unto death, Lord,
No matter how high the cost may seem.
Give us a vision of the heavenly treasure,
For which no earthly price can exceed.

–By Adrianna H. Fanton

اے خداوند، یہ درد ناقابلِ برداشت لگتا ہے۔
جن چیزوں سے کبھی محبت تھی، اب انہیں مرنا ہے۔
کتنے ہی دل لہولہان ہیں۔
کسی کی آنکھ خشک نہیں رہی۔

ہم روئے، تڑپے اور دعا کی،
اے خداوند، التجا کی کہ یہ پیالہ ٹل جائے۔
ہم نے وہ سب کیا جس سے ہمیں لگا کہ شاید کچھ بدل جائے،
مگر ہر کوشش کا نتیجہ خالی ہاتھ لوٹنا ہی لگا۔

اے باپ، ہم نے رحم کے لیے فریاد کی،
کاش سب اس درد سے بچ نکلتے۔
مگر اے خداوند، تو نے ہمیں اس سے گزرنے کو کہا؛
اس سب میں تیرا ہاتھ تو نے ہم پر واضح کر دیا۔

غور کرتے ہوئے ہمارے ذہن چکرا جاتے ہیں،
کہ آخر تو کیا کرنے کی کوشش کر رہا ہے۔
پھر بھی ہم جانتے ہیں کہ ہمارے احساسات جیسے بھی ہوں،
کوئی سبب ہے کہ ہمیں اس طوفان سے گزرنا ہے۔

سو اے باپ، اب ہم تیرے قدموں میں جھکتے ہیں،
تیری قادرِ مطلق قوت کو تسلیم کرتے ہوئے۔
ہم ہر تفصیل کو سمجھ نہیں سکتے،
مگر بھروسا ہے کہ آخرکار سب ٹھیک ہو جائے گا۔

اے باپ، ہماری مدد کر کہ ہم تیرے حضور شکستہ و فروتن ہوں،
اپنا سب کچھ تیرے سپرد کرتے ہوئے۔
اپنے حقوق، خواب، آرزوئیں اور مال و اسباب،
ہر چیز تیرے سامنے کھول کر رکھتے ہوئے۔

اے خداوند، ہم میں فروتنی بڑھا،
خاموش، مگر گہری اور سچی۔
یہ ایسا گوہر ہے جسے آزمائشوں کے سوا کوئی نہیں سکھا سکتا۔
اے خداوند، اس کے ذریعے ہمیں اپنے جیسا بنا دے!

اے باپ، ہماری نگاہیں تجھ پر جمی رہیں،
اس ہولناک آندھی پر نہیں۔
کیونکہ تو خود ان گہرے پانیوں سے گزرا ہے،
تیرے ارادے کے سوا کچھ بھی غالب نہ آئے گا۔

اے خداوند، موت تک فرمانبردار،
خواہ اس کی قیمت کتنی ہی بڑی کیوں نہ لگے۔
ہمیں آسمانی خزانے کا دیدار عطا کر،
جس کے مقابلے میں کوئی زمینی قیمت بڑھ کر نہیں۔

– از Adrianna H. Fanton

There He was, the King Himself, standing before Pilate, awaiting His death sentence. A large crowd had gathered outside. There was no mistaking it, these people were angry. They wanted this man, Jesus of Nazareth, dead. “Crucify him! Crucify him!” was all that could be heard. This man must have done something terrible. But who were these people that were so angry at the Son of God? Maybe they were rapists, thieves, and murderers. Possibly they were the local liars, drunks, or some other evildoers. Actually, they were the religious people, the church goers, the ones claiming to be God’s people.

Ever since that infamous day, history has repeated itself. People claiming to be God’s people have seen those who love Jesus and try to follow His teachings as their enemies and have persecuted them any way they could. From the Jews, to the Roman Catholics, to the Protestants, the mainstream church of the day has always been the enemy of those who try to govern their everyday lives by the simple clarity of the Scriptures.

I am concerned that we have signed a deal with the mainstream church of our day—a deal for peace at all costs.

Any Scripture that teaches rebuke, reproof, or correction is considered out-of-date and is not allowed to be used to help shape the faith and practice of today’s Christian. Many individuals, church leaders, and even whole churches have begun to believe that love and acceptance alone is a better way to point others to Christ. Those who would raise a voice of warning are seen to be critical and stirring unrest, so they are quickly silenced.

As we search the Scriptures, we see that Jesus, then the disciples, then the early church, had nothing good to say or think about the false church.

While out witnessing or talking to people about the Lord, I’m amazed at the backlash from the mainstream church of our day. Mainly, the Protestant church.

A simple man walked up to a Christian concert holding a sign reading ‘Jesus saves from sin’. Without him ever saying a word, he was attacked. “Quit judging us!” “You don’t know our hearts!” “You’re a disgrace!” “Bigot!” The man slowly walked away.

Many times, the people who get angry when discussions involving God come up are actually folks who claim to know Jesus. The sinners seem to let the message penetrate their hearts. If you were to go to an intersection in a city and simply hold a sign proclaiming something about Christ, you would soon see that this is true.

As I was standing in line at a fast-food restaurant, I noticed that the young man preparing my sandwich had many interesting tattoos. Some were of tombstones, skulls, and other graphic designs. I calmly asked him if he could explain what the tattoos meant to him. He began going into detail about each one. I then asked the young man if he knew Jesus. He got sober and explained that he wanted to believe in God but couldn’t. I quoted a few Bible verses and told him that God was waiting for him. I noticed that God’s Word was having a great effect on the young man.

Meanwhile, I also noticed that the lady behind me was beginning to get frustrated. Finally, she interrupted our conversation and told the man, “Jesus loves you just the way you are. You don’t have to change for this man.” This lady later told me what church she went to and how judgmental she thought that I had acted. I was amazed. I had only told the young man about the Savior!

Before I left the restaurant, I walked back over to the young man to bid him farewell. As I approached, he looked up with tears in his eyes. “Thank you”, he said “I can tell that you truly care about me. I will go home and really think about what you said.”

That night, as I reflected on the day’s events, I wondered why that professing Christian woman had such a problem with my interaction with the young man. Why did she get so angry? I felt like the Lord gave me an answer: No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon –Matthew 6:24.

She was a nice young lady. And, yes, she professed that she was a Christian, but she clearly did not live a life that was in obedience to God’s Word. Rather, outside of going to church, one would not be able to tell at all that she was a follower of Christ. I’m sure if I would have met her at the park, we could have had a nice chat. I’m sure she would have been courteous and polite. I’m sure she would have presented herself as a good citizen and nice person. But when it came to being excited about Jesus, sharing the gospel, and talking about God’s Word, her true colors came out.

Am I saying that a person must be an Anabaptist to make it to heaven? Absolutely not, but I am saying we must obey the Bible and follow Christ to make it to heaven. Most professing Christians are super nice and seem godly, until you start talking about God.

Since when has the definition of a Christian been ‘a nice person’, or ‘a good citizen’? Is that all there is to it anymore—simply do what you want, find a fun church that doesn’t require anything from you, get a good job, get married, have a few children and just like that you’re a ‘Christian’? God help us!

When He was having a discussion with a group of people about whether or not they were true followers of God, Jesus said, …If ye were Abraham’s children, ye would do the works of Abraham. But now ye seek to kill me, a man that hath told you the truth … Ye do the deeds of your father … Ye are of your father the devil… –John 8:39-44.

Has the true church slipped so far as to not be able to call things as they are? God’s Word gives us clear understanding on the matter: Proving what is acceptable unto the Lord. And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather reprove them. For it is a shame even to speak of those things which are done of them in secret. But all things that are reproved are made manifest by the light: for whatsoever doth make manifest is light –Ephesians 5:10-13.

Jesus says Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid –Matthew 5:14. Do we expose sin and heresy in the same way that light exposes darkness? Or are we too attached to a comfortable life with no enemies? We do not need to be scared of the world, or of the false church, because we know that we have what they need! For years the mainstream churches have been getting farther and farther away from the truth of God’s Word. Are we afraid to recognize this? Are we afraid to separate ourselves from this? Will we stand up against it like the early church did?

There is a reason why the Protestant reformer, Martin Luther, died hating the Anabaptist people—because they rejected his interpretation of the Scriptures. The Anabaptist people were not respecters of people. Rather their only respect was for God and His Word, and that without compromise. It was for this that they were persecuted. It would have been much easier for those godly young men to just be quiet and try to get along with the Catholics and Protestants, but they refused and both groups sought to extinguish them. Still, they lived on, trusting only in their God. When we joined the church of Jesus Christ didn’t we promise to continue fighting the same fight—the same fight that Jesus fought; the same fight the early church fought—the fight against the false church? Or have we agreed to get along, for the sake of peace? After all isn’t it better for business, for friendships, and for reputation?! God forbid!

We can live a life that seems to be without sin, but still be living in disobedience. The Bible calls us to action! We are called to be lights, to be witnesses, to pursue godliness, and to live uprightly, not just to put on a good show. I believe this is what has become popular in our day. Lying, cheating, stealing, and killing are attributes that even the world rejects. It’s the ‘in thing’ to be respectable, to make a nice living, and to be upstanding citizens. But is this the life of a born-again believer? Should we fit in with the American dream? Should the only thing that’s different between us and the Protestant church be a head covering? I think we should prayerfully consider this move, the move to join hands with the mainstream church.

I personally know many Protestant Christians. I’m not trying to say they are bad people; many are good folks. But that is not what we are talking about. I believe we need to draw a line and slow down this draw to join them in any compromising manner. Let’s look at just a few of the differences between the Protestants and Anabaptists.

War

Can you believe in war, killing your enemies, and still be a New Testament Christian? Most Protestants are supporters of fighting for our freedoms and our rights. Many will go as far as calling Anabaptist people cowards for not fighting.

Years ago, a group of professing Christians gathered around the biggest bomb ever made. This bomb was about to be sent into a foreign land to destroy an entire city; this bomb was meant to kill everything in its path. Men, women, and children alike would perish because of this bomb; that was the plan. As this group was gathered around this bomb they began to pray, they asked God’s blessing on this bombing mission. They then thanked Him for its success—killing nearly one quarter of a million souls.

Jesus calls us to love our enemies. This topic clearly separated the churches during the various wars. Most of the ‘Christian’ churches in the world supported the war effort of their country. The Anabaptists would not, and they were sorely persecuted for it. So, can we be a Christian and continue to support war? If we support war, where will it stop? Will we also prepare to defend ourselves and our families against violence and lawlessness? The American church calls ‘defending ourselves’, our families, and our country, heroism or bravery; the Bible calls it.

Entertainment

It seems that most Christians in America have no problem watching as many ballgames and sports events as they desire. Movies and television are found in nearly every home. Going to the beach, casinos, and festivals are commonplace. Spending thousands on big hunting trips and expensive vacations is completed without a second thought. To be honest, there really are no limits to what the Christian in America can do, as long as it seems right to them. Jesus tells us multiple times to deny ourselves. It seems that we look for any loophole possible to indulge in all the self-gratifying activities we want! It’s no wonder the church is struggling with pornography and many other sins of the flesh. When we learn how to deny ourselves, pick up the cross, and follow Jesus, then we will start to see a clear, distinct, and large separation between us and the mainstream church of our day.

Non-conformity

It is common to conform to one’s surroundings. This is one reason we don’t send our children to public schools. Jesus is also very clear that we need to come out from among them and be separate, to say “No” to evil communication and the ways of this world, and to not be afraid of identifying ourselves with the people of God. It almost seems that dress is really the only thing that separates many of us, and that is changing also.

Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world. If any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him. For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world –1 John 2:15-16. Where are the people that hate the world? Where are the people that want to be as separated as possible? Where are the people that are not afraid to be laughed at? Where are the people that are not afraid to be different? Oh, where are God’s people?! If history repeats itself, there will soon be no difference between the church and the world. Oh, where are the men?!

I’ve heard many Anabaptist people say they can’t say that those in the worldly church are not Christians; they just don’t want to go in that direction. Is that truthful? Is that the message we want to send to our youth, and to our children? I don’t believe so. The Bible says that few will make it. If we pass on to our children that the Protestant church is also ok, and that they just do things differently, we are destroying everything that Jesus preached. We are saying that we do what we do, not because the Bible says, but rather we decide what we do based on our circumstances and what others around us think! No wonder our children are more interested in the modern church of today than ever before—there’s no line drawn!

There was a modern church that caught my attention. They seemed to be on fire for the Lord! The pastor preached as a dying man. They were very interested in reaching the lost. But there were so many Bible teachings that they simply ignored! I finally took it to the Lord. “What is going on here God!” It was as if God told me to ‘just wait’.

Soon after that, the pastor was released from his position because he was having an affair. Then it all became clear to me—you can have a nice church, you can preach a good message, and you can help the poor, but if you’re not willing to obey ALL of the New Testament teachings, you’re not a true Christian, and you will not find victory. It’s easy to take Christianity so far, but it is not easy to sell all that you have, put your all on the altar, and follow your Master. I know this is bold, but it is the truth of God’s Word.

I was speaking to a young lady in a Protestant setting, who wanted to give her life to the Lord. She was ready to do what it took, or so she said. I asked her if she was ready to suffer for Jesus, if she was ready to separate herself from her old friends, if she was ready to be hated by the world, and ready to be different. I asked her if she was willing to change how she looked. It didn’t take long before she shockingly responded with an emphatic “No!” “I want to start going to church, but not all that other stuff.” I later noticed her with her friends pointing and laughing at me. Being cool does not define a true Christian but being rejected for the sake of the Gospel does.

This is a tough article to write. It’s not a popular message and not very encouraging. But I think it’s a message we must consider today, not only for our sake, but for our children’s sake, and that of the church of tomorrow. We must draw clear lines of separation, without any compromise. We must honestly evaluate the modern church of our day with the clear teachings of the New Testament. We must call sin, sin. We must call disobedience, sin. We must call compromise, sin. We must once again choose to suffer with the true people of God. This does not mean that we shun people or act distasteful towards them, but with love in our hearts, and a message on our lips, we point the masses to Christ!

For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek –Romans 1:16.

Da stand Er, der König selbst, vor Pilatus und erwartete sein Todesurteil. Draußen hatte sich eine große Menschenmenge versammelt. Es war unverkennbar: Diese Menschen waren wütend. Sie wollten, dass dieser Mann, Jesus von Nazareth, starb. „Kreuzige ihn! Kreuzige ihn!“ war alles, was zu hören war. Dieser Mann musste etwas Schreckliches getan haben. Doch wer waren diese Menschen, die so wütend auf den Sohn Gottes waren? Vielleicht waren es Vergewaltiger, Diebe und Mörder. Möglicherweise waren es die örtlichen Lügner, Trunkenbolde oder andere Übeltäter. Tatsächlich waren es die religiösen Menschen, die Kirchgänger, diejenigen, die behaupteten, Gottes Volk zu sein.

Seit jenem berüchtigten Tag hat sich die Geschichte wiederholt. Menschen, die behaupteten, Gottes Volk zu sein, betrachteten diejenigen, die Jesus lieben und versuchen, seinen Lehren zu folgen, als ihre Feinde und verfolgten sie auf jede erdenkliche Weise. Von den Juden über die römischen Katholiken bis zu den Protestanten war die etablierte Kirche ihrer Zeit stets der Feind derer, die versuchen, ihren Alltag nach der schlichten Klarheit der Schrift auszurichten.

Ich mache mir Sorgen, dass wir mit der etablierten Kirche unserer Zeit einen Handel geschlossen haben – einen Handel, der Frieden um jeden Preis verspricht.

Jede Schriftstelle, die Zurechtweisung, Überführung oder Korrektur lehrt, gilt als überholt und darf nicht dazu verwendet werden, den Glauben und die Praxis heutiger Christen mitzuprägen. Viele Einzelne, Gemeindeleiter und sogar ganze Gemeinden haben begonnen zu glauben, dass allein Liebe und Annahme ein besserer Weg seien, andere auf Christus hinzuweisen. Wer eine warnende Stimme erhebt, gilt als kritisch und als jemand, der Unruhe stiftet, und wird deshalb schnell zum Schweigen gebracht.

Wenn wir die Schrift erforschen, sehen wir, dass Jesus, dann die Jünger und später die frühe Kirche nichts Gutes über die falsche Kirche zu sagen oder zu denken hatten.

Wenn ich unterwegs Zeugnis gebe oder mit Menschen über den Herrn spreche, erstaunt mich die heftige Gegenreaktion der etablierten Kirche unserer Zeit. Vor allem der protestantischen Kirche.

Ein einfacher Mann kam zu einem christlichen Konzert und hielt ein Schild hoch, auf dem stand: „Jesus rettet von der Sünde.“ Ohne dass er auch nur ein Wort gesagt hatte, wurde er angegriffen. „Hör auf, uns zu verurteilen!“ „Du kennst unsere Herzen nicht!“ „Du bist eine Schande!“ „Fanatiker!“ Der Mann ging langsam davon.

Oft sind es gerade diejenigen, die wütend werden, wenn Gespräche über Gott aufkommen, die behaupten, Jesus zu kennen. Die Sünder scheinen die Botschaft in ihre Herzen eindringen zu lassen. Wenn du an eine Straßenkreuzung in einer Stadt gehen und einfach ein Schild mit einer Botschaft über Christus hochhalten würdest, würdest du bald sehen, dass das stimmt.

Als ich in einem Fast-Food-Restaurant in der Schlange stand, bemerkte ich, dass der junge Mann, der mein Sandwich zubereitete, viele interessante Tätowierungen hatte. Einige zeigten Grabsteine, Totenköpfe und andere drastische Motive. Ruhig fragte ich ihn, ob er mir erklären könne, was die Tätowierungen für ihn bedeuteten. Er begann, jede einzelne ausführlich zu erläutern. Dann fragte ich den jungen Mann, ob er Jesus kenne. Er wurde ernst und erklärte, dass er an Gott glauben wolle, es aber nicht könne. Ich zitierte ein paar Bibelverse und sagte ihm, dass Gott auf ihn warte. Ich bemerkte, dass Gottes Wort eine große Wirkung auf den jungen Mann hatte.

Währenddessen bemerkte ich auch, dass die Frau hinter mir langsam ungeduldig wurde. Schließlich unterbrach sie unser Gespräch und sagte zu dem Mann: „Jesus liebt dich genau so, wie du bist. Du musst dich für diesen Mann nicht ändern.“ Später erzählte mir die Frau, welche Gemeinde sie besuchte und wie verurteilend sie mein Verhalten gefunden hatte. Ich war verblüfft. Ich hatte dem jungen Mann doch nur von dem Erlöser erzählt!

Bevor ich das Restaurant verließ, ging ich noch einmal zu dem jungen Mann hinüber, um mich zu verabschieden. Als ich näher kam, blickte er mit Tränen in den Augen auf. „Danke“, sagte er. „Ich merke, dass du dich wirklich um mich sorgst. Ich werde nach Hause gehen und ernsthaft über das nachdenken, was du gesagt hast.“

An jenem Abend, als ich über die Ereignisse des Tages nachdachte, fragte ich mich, warum diese Frau, die sich zum christlichen Glauben bekannte, ein solches Problem mit meinem Gespräch mit dem jungen Mann hatte. Warum wurde sie so wütend? Ich hatte das Gefühl, der Herr gab mir eine Antwort: Niemand kann zwei Herren dienen; denn entweder wird er den einen hassen und den anderen lieben, oder er wird dem einen anhangen und den anderen verachten. Ihr könnt nicht Gott und dem Mammon dienen –Matthäus 6:24.

Sie war eine nette junge Frau. Und ja, sie bekannte sich zum Christentum, aber sie lebte ganz offensichtlich nicht in Gehorsam gegenüber Gottes Wort. Abgesehen davon, dass sie in die Kirche ging, hätte man überhaupt nicht erkennen können, dass sie eine Nachfolgerin Christi war. Ich bin sicher, wenn ich sie im Park getroffen hätte, hätten wir uns nett unterhalten können. Ich bin sicher, sie wäre zuvorkommend und höflich gewesen. Ich bin sicher, sie hätte sich als gute Bürgerin und nette Person präsentiert. Doch als es darum ging, sich für Jesus zu begeistern, das Evangelium weiterzugeben und über Gottes Wort zu sprechen, zeigte sie ihr wahres Gesicht.

Behaupte ich, dass man täuferisch sein muss, um in den Himmel zu kommen? Absolut nicht. Aber ich sage, dass wir der Bibel gehorchen und Christus nachfolgen müssen, um in den Himmel zu kommen. Die meisten, die sich zum Christentum bekennen, sind ausgesprochen nett und wirken gottesfürchtig – bis man anfängt, über Gott zu sprechen.

Seit wann besteht die Definition eines Christen aus „einem netten Menschen“ oder „einem guten Bürger“? Ist das inzwischen alles, was dazugehört – einfach tun, was man will, eine nette Gemeinde finden, die nichts von einem verlangt, einen guten Job bekommen, heiraten, ein paar Kinder haben, und schon ist man „Christ“? Gott helfe uns!

Als Jesus mit einer Gruppe von Menschen darüber sprach, ob sie wahre Nachfolger Gottes seien, sagte er: …Wenn ihr Abrahams Kinder wärt, würdet ihr Abrahams Werke tun. Nun aber sucht ihr mich zu töten, einen Menschen, der euch die Wahrheit gesagt hat … Ihr tut die Werke eures Vaters … Ihr seid von eurem Vater, dem Teufel … –Johannes 8:39-44.

Ist die wahre Kirche so weit abgeglitten, dass sie die Dinge nicht mehr beim Namen nennen kann? Gottes Wort gibt uns darüber klare Erkenntnis: Prüft, was dem Herrn wohlgefällig ist. Und habt keine Gemeinschaft mit den unfruchtbaren Werken der Finsternis, sondern deckt sie vielmehr auf. Denn es ist schon schändlich, von dem zu reden, was sie heimlich tun. Alles aber, was aufgedeckt wird, wird durch das Licht offenbar; denn alles, was offenbar wird, ist Licht –Epheser 5:10-13.

Jesus sagt: Ihr seid das Licht der Welt. Eine Stadt, die auf einem Hügel steht, kann nicht verborgen bleiben –Matthäus 5:14. Decken wir Sünde und Irrlehre auf, so wie Licht die Finsternis sichtbar macht? Oder hängen wir zu sehr an einem bequemen Leben ohne Feinde? Wir brauchen uns weder vor der Welt noch vor der falschen Kirche zu fürchten, denn wir wissen, dass wir das haben, was sie brauchen! Seit Jahren entfernen sich die etablierten Kirchen immer weiter von der Wahrheit des Wortes Gottes. Haben wir Angst, das anzuerkennen? Haben wir Angst, uns davon abzusondern? Werden wir uns dagegenstellen, wie es die frühe Kirche tat?

Es gibt einen Grund, warum der protestantische Reformator Martin Luther starb, während er das täuferische Volk hasste: weil sie seine Auslegung der Schrift ablehnten. Das täuferische Volk nahm keine Rücksicht auf Menschen. Seine einzige Ehrfurcht galt vielmehr Gott und seinem Wort, und zwar ohne Kompromisse. Dafür wurden sie verfolgt. Für jene gottesfürchtigen jungen Männer wäre es viel einfacher gewesen, einfach zu schweigen und zu versuchen, mit den Katholiken und Protestanten auszukommen. Doch sie weigerten sich, und beide Gruppen versuchten, sie auszurotten. Trotzdem lebten sie weiter und vertrauten allein auf ihren Gott. Als wir uns der Kirche Jesu Christi anschlossen, versprachen wir da nicht, denselben Kampf weiterzuführen – denselben Kampf, den Jesus kämpfte, denselben Kampf, den die frühe Kirche kämpfte: den Kampf gegen die falsche Kirche? Oder haben wir uns darauf geeinigt, um des Friedens willen miteinander auszukommen? Ist das schließlich nicht besser fürs Geschäft, für Freundschaften und für den Ruf?! Gott bewahre!

Wir können ein Leben führen, das sündlos zu sein scheint, und dennoch in Ungehorsam leben. Die Bibel ruft uns zum Handeln auf! Wir sind dazu berufen, Lichter und Zeugen zu sein, nach Gottesfurcht zu streben und aufrichtig zu leben – und nicht bloß eine gute Show abzuziehen. Ich glaube, dass dies in unserer Zeit populär geworden ist. Lügen, Betrügen, Stehlen und Töten sind Verhaltensweisen, die sogar die Welt ablehnt. Es ist „in“, angesehen zu sein, gut zu verdienen und ein vorbildlicher Bürger zu sein. Aber ist das das Leben eines wiedergeborenen Gläubigen? Sollten wir uns dem amerikanischen Traum anpassen? Sollte der einzige Unterschied zwischen uns und der protestantischen Kirche eine Kopfbedeckung sein? Ich denke, wir sollten diese Entwicklung, den Schritt, uns mit der etablierten Kirche zusammenzutun, im Gebet bedenken.

Ich kenne persönlich viele protestantische Christen. Ich will nicht sagen, dass sie schlechte Menschen sind; viele sind gute Leute. Aber darum geht es nicht. Ich glaube, wir müssen eine klare Grenze ziehen und diesen Drang, uns ihnen auf irgendeine kompromissvolle Weise anzuschließen, bremsen. Sehen wir uns nur einige der Unterschiede zwischen Protestanten und Täufern an.

Krieg

Kann man den Krieg befürworten, seine Feinde töten und dennoch ein Christ des Neuen Testaments sein? Die meisten Protestanten unterstützen den Kampf für unsere Freiheiten und Rechte. Viele gehen so weit, die Täufer Feiglinge zu nennen, weil sie nicht kämpfen.

Vor Jahren versammelte sich eine Gruppe von Menschen, die sich zum Christentum bekannten, um die größte je gebaute Bombe. Diese Bombe sollte in ein fremdes Land geschickt werden, um eine ganze Stadt zu zerstören; sie sollte alles töten, was in ihrem Weg lag. Männer, Frauen und Kinder würden gleichermaßen durch diese Bombe umkommen; das war der Plan. Während diese Gruppe um die Bombe versammelt war, begannen sie zu beten und baten Gott um seinen Segen für diesen Bombenangriff. Danach dankten sie ihm für dessen Erfolg – für den Tod von beinahe einer Viertelmillion Menschen.

Jesus ruft uns dazu auf, unsere Feinde zu lieben. Dieses Thema trennte die Kirchen während der verschiedenen Kriege deutlich voneinander. Die meisten „christlichen“ Kirchen der Welt unterstützten die Kriegsanstrengungen ihres Landes. Die Täufer taten es nicht, und wurden dafür schwer verfolgt. Können wir also Christen sein und weiterhin den Krieg unterstützen? Wenn wir den Krieg unterstützen, wo wird das enden? Werden wir uns auch darauf vorbereiten, uns selbst und unsere Familien gegen Gewalt und Gesetzlosigkeit zu verteidigen? Die amerikanische Kirche nennt die „Verteidigung“ unserer selbst, unserer Familien und unseres Landes Heldentum oder Tapferkeit; die Bibel nennt es.

Unterhaltung

Es scheint, dass die meisten Christen in Amerika kein Problem damit haben, so viele Ballspiele und Sportveranstaltungen anzusehen, wie sie wollen. Filme und Fernsehen gibt es in fast jedem Haushalt. An den Strand, ins Kasino und auf Festivals zu gehen, ist alltäglich. Tausende für große Jagdausflüge und teure Urlaube auszugeben, geschieht ohne den geringsten Gedanken daran. Ehrlich gesagt gibt es für Christen in Amerika wirklich keine Grenzen dessen, was sie tun können, solange es ihnen richtig erscheint. Jesus sagt uns wiederholt, dass wir uns selbst verleugnen sollen. Es scheint, als suchten wir nach jedem erdenklichen Schlupfloch, um all den selbstgefälligen Aktivitäten nachzugehen, die wir wollen! Kein Wunder, dass die Kirche mit Pornografie und vielen anderen Sünden des Fleisches zu kämpfen hat. Wenn wir lernen, uns selbst zu verleugnen, das Kreuz auf uns zu nehmen und Jesus nachzufolgen, dann werden wir eine klare, deutliche und große Trennung zwischen uns und der etablierten Kirche unserer Zeit erkennen.

Keine Anpassung an die Welt

Es ist üblich, sich seiner Umgebung anzupassen. Das ist ein Grund, warum wir unsere Kinder nicht auf öffentliche Schulen schicken. Jesus sagt auch ganz klar, dass wir aus ihrer Mitte herauskommen und abgesondert sein müssen, zum bösen Umgang und zu den Wegen dieser Welt „Nein“ sagen und keine Angst davor haben sollen, uns mit Gottes Volk zu identifizieren. Es scheint fast so, als sei die Kleidung wirklich das Einzige, was viele von uns unterscheidet, und auch das ändert sich.

Liebt nicht die Welt und auch nicht die Dinge, die in der Welt sind. Wenn jemand die Welt liebt, ist die Liebe des Vaters nicht in ihm. Denn alles, was in der Welt ist – die Begierde des Fleisches, die Begierde der Augen und der Hochmut des Lebens – ist nicht vom Vater, sondern von der Welt –1. Johannes 2:15-16. Wo sind die Menschen, die die Welt hassen? Wo sind die Menschen, die so abgesondert wie möglich sein wollen? Wo sind die Menschen, die keine Angst haben, ausgelacht zu werden? Wo sind die Menschen, die keine Angst haben, anders zu sein? Ach, wo ist Gottes Volk?! Wenn sich die Geschichte wiederholt, wird es bald keinen Unterschied mehr zwischen der Kirche und der Welt geben. Ach, wo sind die Männer?!

Ich habe viele Täufer sagen hören, sie könnten nicht behaupten, dass diejenigen in der weltlichen Kirche keine Christen seien; sie wollten nur nicht in diese Richtung gehen. Ist das ehrlich? Ist das die Botschaft, die wir unseren Jugendlichen und Kindern vermitteln wollen? Ich glaube nicht. Die Bibel sagt, dass nur wenige es schaffen werden. Wenn wir unseren Kindern vermitteln, dass auch die protestantische Kirche in Ordnung sei und die Menschen dort einfach andere Dinge täten, zerstören wir alles, was Jesus gepredigt hat. Wir sagen damit, dass wir nicht deshalb tun, was wir tun, weil die Bibel es sagt, sondern dass wir selbst entscheiden, was wir tun, je nach unseren Umständen und der Meinung der Menschen um uns herum! Kein Wunder, dass sich unsere Kinder mehr denn je für die moderne Kirche von heute interessieren – es wurde keine Grenze gezogen!

Eine moderne Kirche erregte meine Aufmerksamkeit. Sie schienen für den Herrn zu brennen! Der Pastor predigte wie ein sterbender Mann. Es lag ihnen sehr daran, die Verlorenen zu erreichen. Doch so viele Lehren der Bibel ignorierten sie einfach! Schließlich brachte ich es vor den Herrn. „Was geht hier vor, Gott?“ Es war, als sagte Gott mir: „Warte einfach ab.“

Bald darauf wurde der Pastor von seinem Amt entlassen, weil er eine Affäre hatte. Da wurde mir alles klar: Man kann eine nette Gemeinde haben, eine gute Botschaft predigen und den Armen helfen; aber wenn du nicht bereit bist, ALLEN Lehren des Neuen Testaments zu gehorchen, bist du kein wahrer Christ und wirst keinen Sieg finden. Es ist leicht, mit dem Christentum ein Stück weit zu gehen; aber es ist nicht leicht, alles, was man hat, zu verkaufen, sein ganzes Leben auf den Altar zu legen und seinem Meister nachzufolgen. Ich weiß, das ist eine deutliche Aussage, aber es ist die Wahrheit von Gottes Wort.

Ich sprach in einem protestantischen Umfeld mit einer jungen Frau, die ihr Leben dem Herrn hingeben wollte. Sie war bereit zu tun, was nötig war – oder so sagte sie. Ich fragte sie, ob sie bereit sei, für Jesus zu leiden, ob sie bereit sei, sich von ihren alten Freunden zu trennen, ob sie bereit sei, von der Welt gehasst zu werden und anders zu sein. Ich fragte sie, ob sie bereit sei, ihr Aussehen zu verändern. Es dauerte nicht lange, bis sie schockierend und nachdrücklich mit „Nein!“ antwortete. „Ich möchte anfangen, in die Kirche zu gehen, aber nicht all das andere Zeug.“ Später sah ich sie bei ihren Freunden, wie sie auf mich zeigten und über mich lachten. Cool zu sein macht einen nicht zum wahren Christen, aber um des Evangeliums willen abgelehnt zu werden, schon.

Es fällt schwer, diesen Artikel zu schreiben. Es ist keine beliebte Botschaft und nicht gerade ermutigend. Aber ich denke, es ist eine Botschaft, die wir heute bedenken müssen – nicht nur um unserer selbst willen, sondern auch um unserer Kinder und der Kirche von morgen willen. Wir müssen klare Trennungslinien ziehen, ohne jeden Kompromiss. Wir müssen die moderne Kirche unserer Zeit ehrlich an den klaren Lehren des Neuen Testaments messen. Wir müssen Sünde Sünde nennen. Wir müssen Ungehorsam Sünde nennen. Wir müssen Kompromiss Sünde nennen. Wir müssen uns aufs Neue dafür entscheiden, mit Gottes wahrem Volk zu leiden. Das bedeutet nicht, dass wir Menschen meiden oder ihnen mit Widerwillen begegnen; doch mit Liebe im Herzen und einer Botschaft auf den Lippen weisen wir die Menschenmassen auf Christus hin!

Denn ich schäme mich des Evangeliums Christi nicht; denn es ist Gottes Kraft zur Errettung für jeden, der glaubt, zuerst für den Juden und auch für den Griechen –Römer 1:16.

We all have a story. Some feel like Job sometimes. Some have lost parents, or partners, or children, or siblings, or friends. Some suffer from severe illness. Some will never recover from their illnesses. Our loved ones might have a terminal illness. Maybe a husband or parent is abusive or unfaithful. Like Job, our friends might have turned against us. Maybe there are problems in the church that seem impossible to fix. It could be something like a colicky baby, or a hyper child. Maybe we just have a cold and are feeling like everything is going wrong. The list is endless. We can relate to the words of this song.

Till the Storm Passes By

In the dark of the midnight have I oft hid my face,
While the storm howls above me, and there’s no hiding place.
‘Mid the crash of the thunder, Precious Lord, hear my cry,
Keep me safe till the storm passes by.

refrain:

Till the storm passes over, till the thunder sounds no more,
Till the clouds roll forever from the sky;
Hold me fast, let me stand in the hollow of Thy hand,
Keep me safe till the storm passes by.

Many times Satan whispered, “There is no need to try,
For there’s no end of sorrow, there’s no hope by and by”
But I know Thou art with me, and tomorrow I’ll rise
Where the storms never darken the skies.

When the long night has ended and the storms come no more,
Let me stand in Thy presence on the bright peaceful shore;
In that land where the tempest, never comes, Lord, may I
Dwell with Thee when the storm passes by.

–by Mosie Lister

When I was a little girl, I thought the author was referring to thunderstorms. I was afraid of thunderstorms. Now I understand that he was referring to the storms of life we go through. On July 14, 2013, I suddenly ended up in the hospital with a life-threatening heart attack caused by a spontaneous coronary artery dissection. What a shock for a 40-year-old mother. The storm was howling, and the thunder was crashing. There was no hiding place from the danger, for it was within me. I only had one heart and it could not be trusted. What if it happens again? Would I die? Then my children would be motherless.

This song was one I’d pray in the dark of the midnight when I couldn’t sleep, and fear threatened to overwhelm me. The Lord’s presence was very real to me. I came through this storm with a greater awareness of how God reveals Himself to us in a deeper way when we are going through hard times. We must choose to yield ourselves completely to Him, and say, “Not my will, but Thine be done.”

When the disciples were out on the sea in the storm, Jesus was with them. He is with us too. We can trust Him. Nothing will happen that is not according to His will. We do not always understand why things happen, but that’s okay. An old preacher used to quote:

“Not now, but in the coming years,
It may be in the better land
We’ll read the meaning of our tears,
And there, sometime, we’ll understand.”

It is so important that we accept what God allows in our lives. Accepting does not mean we don’t do anything about it. We will go to the doctor if necessary. We will reach out to others for comfort and council. We will still have all kinds of feelings, but we should have peace. We can’t wallow in self-pity and have a “poor me” attitude. And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose –Romans 8:28. I believe that. I can’t always see the good, but God does.

Life is hard sometimes, but the song tells about the time when the long night has ended, and the storms come no more. Dear sisters, let’s remain faithful and lean hard on the Lord through the storms of life.

Tutti abbiamo una storia. A volte qualcuno di noi si sente come Giobbe. Alcuni hanno perso i genitori, il coniuge, i figli, i fratelli o le sorelle, oppure degli amici. Alcuni soffrono di gravi malattie. Alcuni non guariranno mai dalle loro malattie. I nostri cari potrebbero avere una malattia terminale. Forse un marito o un genitore è violento o infedele. Come Giobbe, i nostri amici potrebbero essersi rivoltati contro di noi. Forse ci sono problemi nella chiesa che sembrano impossibili da risolvere. Potrebbe trattarsi di qualcosa come un neonato con le coliche o un bambino iperattivo. Forse abbiamo solo il raffreddore e ci sembra che tutto vada storto. L’elenco è infinito. Possiamo identificarci con le parole di questo canto.

Finché la tempesta non sarà passata

Nel buio della mezzanotte spesso ho nascosto il viso,
mentre la tempesta ulula sopra di me e non c’è riparo.
Tra il fragore del tuono, prezioso Signore, ascolta il mio grido,
tienimi al sicuro finché la tempesta non sarà passata.

ritornello:

Finché la tempesta non sarà passata, finché il tuono non risuonerà più,
finché le nuvole non scompariranno per sempre dal cielo;
stringimi forte, fa’ che io resti nel cavo della tua mano,
tienimi al sicuro finché la tempesta non sarà passata.

Molte volte Satana sussurrava: «Non serve provare,
il dolore non avrà fine, non ci sarà speranza in futuro».
Ma so che Tu sei con me, e domani sorgerò
là dove le tempeste non oscurano mai il cielo.

Quando la lunga notte sarà finita e le tempeste non torneranno più,
fa’ che io resti alla tua presenza sulla riva luminosa e serena;
in quella terra dove la tempesta non arriva mai, Signore, possa io
dimorare con Te quando la tempesta sarà passata.

–di Mosie Lister

Quando ero una bambina, pensavo che l’autore si riferisse ai temporali. Avevo paura dei temporali. Ora capisco che si riferiva alle tempeste della vita che attraversiamo. Il 14 luglio 2013 finii all’improvviso in ospedale per un infarto potenzialmente letale, causato da una dissezione spontanea di un’arteria coronaria. Che shock per una madre di 40 anni. La tempesta ululava e il tuono rimbombava. Non c’era riparo dal pericolo, perché era dentro di me. Avevo un solo cuore e non ci si poteva fidare. E se fosse successo di nuovo? Sarei morta? Allora i miei figli sarebbero rimasti senza madre.

Pregavo con questo canto nel buio della mezzanotte, quando non riuscivo a dormire e la paura minacciava di sopraffarmi. La presenza del Signore era molto reale per me. Sono uscita da questa tempesta con una maggiore consapevolezza di come Dio si riveli a noi più profondamente quando attraversiamo momenti difficili. Dobbiamo scegliere di abbandonarci completamente a Lui e dire: «Non la mia volontà, ma la tua sia fatta».

Quando i discepoli erano in mare durante la tempesta, Gesù era con loro. È con noi anche Lui. Possiamo fidarci di Lui. Non accadrà nulla che non sia secondo la Sua volontà. Non sempre capiamo perché accadono le cose, ma va bene così. Un vecchio predicatore era solito citare:

«Non ora, ma negli anni a venire,
forse nella terra migliore,
comprenderemo il significato delle nostre lacrime,
e un giorno, là, capiremo.»

È molto importante accettare ciò che Dio permette nella nostra vita. Accettare non significa che non facciamo nulla al riguardo. Se necessario, andremo dal medico. Ci rivolgeremo agli altri per ricevere conforto e consiglio. Proveremo comunque ogni sorta di emozioni, ma dovremmo avere pace. Non possiamo crogiolarci nell’autocommiserazione e avere un atteggiamento del tipo «poveri noi». E noi sappiamo che tutte le cose cooperano al bene di quelli che amano Dio, i quali sono chiamati secondo il suo proposito – Romani 8:28. Ci credo. Non sempre riesco a vedere il bene, ma Dio sì.

A volte la vita è dura, ma il canto parla del tempo in cui la lunga notte sarà finita e le tempeste non torneranno più. Care sorelle, restiamo fedeli e appoggiamoci con forza al Signore attraverso le tempeste della vita.

E vidi un nuovo cielo e una nuova terra, perché il primo cielo e la prima terra erano passati, e il mare non c’era più. E io, Giovanni, vidi la santa città, la nuova Gerusalemme, scendere dal cielo, da presso Dio, pronta come una sposa adorna per il suo sposo. E udii una gran voce dal cielo, che diceva: «Ecco il tabernacolo di Dio con gli uomini! Egli abiterà con loro, essi saranno suoi popoli e Dio stesso sarà con loro e sarà il loro Dio. Egli asciugherà ogni lacrima dai loro occhi e non ci sarà più la morte, né cordoglio, né grido, né dolore, perché le cose di prima sono passate». Apocalisse 21:1-4.
