« Dr Waldron, me dit la femme alors que je m’apprêtais à quitter la salle d’examen, j’ai encore une question. Comment puis-je perdre ce poids en trop ? »

Je soupirai intérieurement en m’asseyant pour discuter de la situation avec elle. La prise de poids n’est pas le genre de sujet qu’on peut facilement aborder à la fin d’une consultation, et de nombreux livres volumineux ont été écrits sur la question.

Les Américains semblent avoir du mal avec cela. Ils dépensent en moyenne 33 milliards de dollars par an en produits amaigrissants et 65 % des Américains sont en surpoids ou obèses.

La question est complexe. Nous voulons une solution rapide : prendre une pilule, ajouter un aliment brûle-graisse ou faire un exercice simple qui fera fondre rapidement et facilement les kilos en trop. En réalité, si nous prenons du poids assez facilement, il est beaucoup plus difficile de perdre ces mêmes kilos. Et maintenir la perte de poids l’est encore davantage.

Au commencement

Nous savons peu de choses sur la vie avant la chute décrite dans Genèse 3. Nous savons que … Dieu vit tout ce qu’il avait fait et voici, cela était très bon… – Genèse 1:31.

On peut raisonnablement supposer qu’Adam et Ève n’avaient pas de problèmes de poids avant que le péché n’entre dans le monde. Ils avaient été créés parfaitement, ce qui signifie qu’ils n’auraient pas eu de problèmes de métabolisme. Ils n’avaient pas non plus les appétits incontrôlés pour la nourriture auxquels leurs descendants sont confrontés aujourd’hui.

La chute de l’homme dans le jardin d’Éden a entraîné deux choses. Premièrement, les êtres humains ont commencé à souffrir de problèmes physiques : leur corps ne fonctionnait plus aussi bien qu’avant. Adam et Ève ont tout de même pu vivre beaucoup plus longtemps que les humains d’aujourd’hui, mais des maladies métaboliques et d’autres maladies ont commencé à apparaître. La deuxième chose qui s’est produite, c’est qu’ils ont commencé à avoir une nature pécheresse.

Ces deux choses ont entraîné beaucoup de problèmes… Parmi eux, des problèmes de métabolisme et de poids.

Ce que la Bible dit de la nourriture

Notre corps a besoin d’aliments nutritifs : sans nourriture, il dépérirait et finirait par mourir. Il n’y a rien de mieux pour l’homme que de manger, de boire et que son âme jouisse du bien dans son travail. J’ai vu que cela aussi vient de la main de Dieu – Ecclésiaste 2:24.

La loi de l’Ancien Testament imposait des restrictions aux aliments que le peuple juif pouvait manger. Selon la loi casher, les animaux purs étaient bien moins nombreux que les animaux impurs. De plus, le livre des Proverbes mentionne à plusieurs reprises que trop manger est dangereux. Ne sois pas parmi les buveurs de vin, parmi ceux qui font excès de viande : car l’ivrogne et le glouton tomberont dans la pauvreté, et le sommeil les vêtira de haillons – Proverbes 23:20-21.

Dans le Nouveau Testament, nous voyons que l’Église primitive n’exigeait plus des chrétiens non juifs qu’ils suivent les lois juives concernant leur alimentation. Le concile de Jérusalem a expressément exigé … qu’ils s’abstiennent des souillures des idoles, de l’impudicité, des animaux étouffés et du sang – Actes 15:20. Autrement, il semble qu’ils étaient libres de manger ce qu’ils voulaient.

Ce qui n’a pas changé dans le Nouveau Testament, c’est le principe de la maîtrise de soi. La liste du fruit de l’Esprit mentionne la tempérance parmi les qualités que les chrétiens devraient avoir, et Paul a clairement indiqué qu’il s’efforçait de maîtriser ses désirs, de peur d’être lui-même disqualifié (voir 1 Corinthiens 9:27).

Quoi ! Ne savez-vous pas que votre corps est le temple du Saint-Esprit qui est en vous, que vous avez reçu de Dieu, et que vous ne vous appartenez point à vous-mêmes ? Car vous avez été rachetés à un grand prix ; glorifiez donc Dieu dans votre corps et dans votre esprit, qui appartiennent à Dieu – 1 Corinthiens 6:19-20.

Ne savez-vous pas que vous êtes le temple de Dieu, et que l’Esprit de Dieu habite en vous ? Si quelqu’un profane le temple de Dieu, Dieu le détruira ; car le temple de Dieu est saint, et c’est ce que vous êtes – 1 Corinthiens 3:16-17.

L’Écriture dit clairement que les chrétiens devraient prendre soin de leur corps, soumettre leurs désirs au contrôle de Dieu et éviter tout ce qui a un rapport avec l’idolâtrie.

Pourquoi prend-on du poids ?

On peut facilement répartir les raisons de la prise de poids en deux grandes catégories :

  1. des problèmes de métabolisme
  2. un apport calorique excessif.

Parmi les problèmes métaboliques, on trouve notamment les troubles de la thyroïde et le diabète. Ces troubles influent sur la vitesse à laquelle notre corps brûle les calories. L’un des principaux moyens d’augmenter notre métabolisme consiste à accroître notre niveau d’activité, en particulier en pratiquant un exercice qui accélère le rythme cardiaque — un exercice cardiovasculaire.

Les calories en excès proviennent principalement d’une alimentation excessive. Il est important de se rappeler que les gens mangent pour de nombreuses raisons autres que la faim. Ils mangent parce qu’ils s’ennuient, se sentent seuls ou sont tristes et, oui, parfois parce qu’ils ont faim. Certains médicaments, notamment les stéroïdes, peuvent augmenter l’appétit et avoir un effet négatif sur le métabolisme.

On appelle métabolisme basal le nombre de calories que notre corps brûle au repos. Il existe plusieurs formules différentes pour calculer notre métabolisme basal. Elles utilisent la taille, le poids, l’âge et le sexe pour déterminer combien de calories votre corps brûlera au cours d’une journée moyenne. Quelques applications et sites Internet effectuent ce calcul pour vous. https://www.active.com/fitness/calculators/bmr Il est important de savoir que ce chiffre correspond au nombre de calories que vous devriez consommer pour maintenir votre poids actuel. Si vous mangez moins de calories que ce chiffre, vous aurez tendance à perdre du poids ; si vous en consommez davantage, vous prendrez du poids.

Le poids est-il important ?

D’un point de vue médical, le surpoids est associé à plusieurs problèmes. Il tend à augmenter la résistance à l’insuline et peut conduire au diabète. Il augmente la tension artérielle. Il peut entraîner l’apnée obstructive du sommeil et aggrave l’arthrite du dos et des jambes.

Le surpoids n’est pas nécessairement le signe d’un problème spirituel et, selon la génétique d’une personne, il peut être difficile d’atteindre le poids indiqué par les tableaux. Même si la plupart des gens se sentent beaucoup mieux lorsqu’ils sont proches de leur poids idéal, l’Écriture n’indique pas qu’il existe un poids ou un indice de masse corporelle (IMC) précis que les chrétiens ne devraient pas dépasser.

L’important, c’est que nos vies soient sous le contrôle de Dieu si nous nous sommes livrés à lui, avec nos appétits et tout le reste. Nous devrions chercher à être en bonne santé afin de pouvoir participer au mieux à l’édification du Royaume. De plus, nous devrions essayer de donner aux autres l’exemple d’une vie consacrée à Dieu.

Les idées reçues sur la perte de poids…

Beaucoup de choses sont tenues pour vraies au sujet de la perte de poids. Nous allons examiner une liste d’affirmations que les gens répètent. Même si elles peuvent contenir une part de vérité, elles ne sont pas entièrement exactes et peuvent décourager des activités qui aideraient une personne aux prises avec son poids.

… Un exercice vigoureux est le seul moyen de perdre du poids.

Beaucoup de gens pensent qu’ils n’arrivent pas à perdre du poids parce qu’ils ne peuvent pas faire assez d’exercice. Ils souffrent de douleurs, d’arthrite ou d’un problème cardiaque ou pulmonaire qui les empêche de pratiquer des activités sportives intenses.

Ils connaissent peut-être quelqu’un qui s’est mis à courir et a perdu beaucoup de poids, et cela leur semble être la bonne méthode. Mais ils ne se sentent tout simplement pas capables de suivre cette voie et désespèrent de pouvoir y arriver.

L’exercice est important. La plupart des sociétés médicales recommandent de faire au moins 150 minutes d’exercice par semaine. L’exercice stimule notre métabolisme et aide notre cœur et nos poumons, mais il ne changera peut-être pas beaucoup le poids d’une personne.

La plupart des gens brûlent entre 200 et 300 calories en faisant une demi-heure d’exercice. Cela peut sembler beaucoup, mais le corps doit brûler 3 500 calories pour perdre une livre. De plus, la plupart d’entre nous ont davantage faim après avoir fait de l’exercice, et il est très facile de manger 200 calories de plus, ce qui annule en gros les calories brûlées pendant l’exercice.

… Les glucides font prendre du poids.

Le terme médical « glucides » désigne les sucres. Les calories que nous consommons proviennent de l’une de ces trois sources : les glucides, les lipides et les protéines. Les glucides sont présents dans les desserts, mais aussi dans de nombreux aliments riches en amidon, comme le riz, le maïs, les pâtes, le pain et bien d’autres aliments.

Plusieurs régimes, comme le régime Atkins et le régime cétogène, incitent leurs adeptes à supprimer autant de glucides que possible. Les gens perdent souvent du poids avec ce genre de régimes. Malheureusement, il est difficile de les suivre à long terme, car ils sont assez restrictifs.

Le plus sain est de consommer des glucides avec modération et de privilégier les options les plus saines. Il est important de choisir des céréales complètes et des glucides plus complexes. Un bol de flocons d’avoine peut contenir à peu près autant de grammes de glucides qu’un bol de céréales sucrées pour le petit-déjeuner, mais notre corps le décomposera plus lentement et le digérera plus facilement.

… La famine est le seul moyen de perdre du poids.

La famine entraîne effectivement une perte de poids : il n’y avait pas de personnes corpulentes parmi celles qui sont sorties des camps de concentration après la Seconde Guerre mondiale. Ce n’est certainement pas le seul moyen de perdre du poids, ni une façon saine de le faire.

Nous savons que lorsque les gens sont privés de nourriture pendant de longues périodes, ils commencent à perdre de la masse musculaire, leurs os s’affaiblissent et leur métabolisme ralentit. La plupart des personnes qui s’affament finissent par reprendre en quelques années tout le poids qu’elles ont perdu et, comme leur métabolisme a ralenti, il leur sera à long terme plus difficile de ne pas reprendre de poids.

… Il suffit de manger tel ou tel aliment brûle-graisse pour perdre du poids !

J’ai volontairement laissé en blanc l’aliment ci-dessus, car il semble que cela change tout le temps. Vous avez peut-être lu que le yaourt grec, la cannelle ou le jus de baies de goji vous aideront à perdre du poids. Les études indiquent qu’il n’existe pas d’aliment magique qui fasse fondre les graisses.

Si ces aliments sont efficaces, c’est parce que vous avez remplacé quelque chose de malsain et riche en calories par quelque chose de plus sain. Par exemple, si votre petit-déjeuner habituel se compose de 5 tranches de bacon, d’un verre de jus d’orange, de 2 tranches de pain grillé et de deux œufs, et que vous remplacez tout cela par un verre d’eau et un bol de flocons d’avoine, vous perdrez probablement du poids. Ce ne sera pas parce que les flocons d’avoine « brûlent les graisses », mais plutôt parce qu’ils contiennent beaucoup moins de calories que le petit-déjeuner que vous preniez auparavant.

Certains aliments ne contiennent presque pas de calories et leur ingestion et leur digestion demandent probablement autant d’énergie que ce que les humains en tirent. Le céleri, la laitue iceberg et les champignons entrent tous dans cette catégorie. Le problème, c’est que si vous mettez du beurre d’arachide sur le céleri, de la vinaigrette sur la laitue et faites frire les champignons dans du beurre ou de l’huile, ils cessent soudain d’être les aliments peu caloriques qu’ils prétendent être. Nous, les humains, sommes très doués pour apprêter les aliments peu caloriques de façon à les rendre plus savoureux et à leur faire perdre leur faible teneur en calories.

… Les aliments sans matières grasses et les produits diététiques sont la clé de la perte de poids.

De nombreux aliments et condiments vendus dans le commerce contiennent moins de matières grasses et prétendent être moins caloriques que leurs versions classiques. Ils contiennent souvent divers produits chimiques et substituts du sucre destinés à rendre leur goût et leur texture aussi proches que possible de ceux des produits ordinaires.

Les substituts du sucre semblent plus sains que le sucre lorsqu’ils sont utilisés avec modération, mais ils semblent aussi inciter les gens à rechercher des aliments plus sucrés. Des études ont établi un lien entre les édulcorants artificiels et l’apparition d’une intolérance au glucose — un problème susceptible d’entraîner le diabète. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3095502/ Les diététiciens semblent penser que, parmi les différents substituts du sucre, la stévia est la plus sûre.

Dans l’ensemble, notre objectif ne devrait pas être d’essayer de manger les mêmes aliments, mais avec moins de calories, mais plutôt de consommer une variété d’aliments sains et des portions de taille modérée. C’est cela qui améliorera le métabolisme, et non le simple fait de choisir des versions allégées de nos aliments préférés.

… La solution, ce sont les pilules amaigrissantes.

Au fil du temps, j’ai vu beaucoup de gens prendre des médicaments et des compléments, prescrits ou en vente libre, pour essayer de les aider à perdre du poids. Ces médicaments et compléments sont censés avoir différents effets, notamment réduire l’appétit et accélérer le métabolisme.

Ils sont souvent efficaces à court terme. Les gens perdent pas mal de poids au cours des premières semaines et pensent avoir surmonté leurs difficultés. Le problème, c’est qu’avec le temps, ils s’habituent généralement à ce qu’ils prennent, leur appétit revient et leur métabolisme retrouve son rythme normal.

Ce genre de solutions peut apporter une aide à court terme, mais pour être en bonne santé à long terme, il faut établir un programme alimentaire sain et un calendrier d’exercice, puis s’y tenir durablement. L’objectif ne devrait jamais être simplement de « perdre cinq kilos », mais plutôt d’être en aussi bonne santé que possible.

Nous avons abordé beaucoup de choses à ne pas faire et, probablement, en lisant entre les lignes, vous pouvez discerner certaines choses utiles à faire également. Une deuxième partie (si le Seigneur le veut) paraîtra dans le prochain numéro et abordera les mesures positives que nous pouvons prendre pour atteindre un poids sain.

Dans tout cela, il est important de se rappeler que notre objectif n’est pas d’atteindre une quelconque beauté terrestre. Il s’agit plutôt de traiter notre corps comme le temple du Saint-Esprit (1 Corinthiens 6:19). J’ai entendu ce verset invoqué pour expliquer pourquoi nous ne devrions pas boire, fumer ou nous faire tatouer, mais nous devons aussi le respecter en ce qui concerne notre alimentation et l’exercice.

En prenant soin de notre corps, nous serons mieux en mesure de répondre aux besoins des personnes qui nous entourent et nous serons prêts à suivre le plan que Dieu a pour nos vies.

Editor’s Note: Many of our readers may at first be convinced that this topic doesn’t pertain to them. If this is correct, we rejoice with you. However, before simply passing over this article we urge the reader to carefully read what is written here then start asking questions of family, friends, and acquaintances. We are hearing that especially the younger generation is being drawn into para-church events (such as concerts, seminars, Bible Schools, etc.) or special services at neighboring churches, which involve this type of content to one degree or another. Especially prominent are special music groups/concerts, ventriloquism, religious films, and skits. We wish to raise awareness on this issue and stimulate a discussion on the matter.

Religious drama—what is it?

A serious story by actors performing or impersonating any given dialogue in a theatrical manner, or an event of real life with emotional effects which are characteristics of a play, patterned after a religious theme. (American Heritage College Dictionary)

Is this something the church needs to be concerned about? It should be. It usually seems to get its beginning in extended “prayer and praise” services between Sunday school and church services. Or in special services other than on a Sunday morning. It can include such things as instrumental presentations, puppet shows, skits, plays, dances, and religious films.

Religious drama is not something new. It was introduced during the Dark Ages (A.D. 400 to 1200) as dramatic performances with religious themes known as “miracle plays.” These plays became so corrupt that the Catholic Church tried to put a stop to them, but to no avail. In 1242, the Passion play, a performance that depicts the death of Christ, started in Germany and it is still being performed around the world today.

An interesting observation, as we look back through time, is that religious drama was introduced during the darkest time of history (the Dark Ages), but the church emerged from this long era of moral decay through Spirit-filled, Bible-based, New Covenant-focused preaching of the Anabaptist Revival during the Reformation time period.

I. Why Drama Violates True Worship

a. Drama is a violation of the law of hearing.

In a spiritual world, seeing is not as important as hearing (2 Corinthians 4:18). The words hear, heareth, and heard are found over 1,000 times in the Bible. As a matter of fact, the whole Bible is God speaking to man. He wants mankind to hear! “Thus, saith the Lord” is a constant refrain throughout Scripture.

On Mount Sinai (Exodus 19:9), the people heard the message of God through His spokesman, Moses. God’s voice was frightening to them (Exodus 20:18-19) but hearing from Him was essential so that they “sin not.” In Exodus 20, God gave some detailed instructions of what the worship pattern was to be. Ye shall not make with me gods of silver, neither shall ye make unto you gods of gold –Exodus 20:23. These visual aids (idols) were a violation of God’s law of hearing. Through the eye gate comes the temptation to build idols. The altars that God did permit were to be plain and uncut (vss. 24-25). What they did see was not to distract from that which was heard from the altar! What is seen, especially immodesty, tends to be a distraction from what is heard (v. 26).

The preaching of Jesus appealed to the hearing: Who hath ears to hear, let him hear –Matthew 13:9. While He did not use visual aids like speakers do today, Jesus did use verbal aids (parables) as a tool to appeal to the hearing (Mat 13:18).

On the Mount of Transfiguration (Matthew 17), Peter wanted to reinvent the worship experience by building three shrines. He wanted something to see! But the voice in the clouds alerted the disciples to the importance of hearing (v. 5). Worship with visual aids is not endorsed by God!

Jesus said, Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life … The hour is coming, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God: and they that hear shall live. John 5:24-25. Salvation comes by hearing the Word of God, but only when one believes what is heard!

Paul raises some sobering questions: How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher? –Romans 10:14. He answers his own questions: So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God –Romans 10:17. God’s law to experience salvation is either by hearing God’s Word or by reading God’s Word!

In the 2nd and 3rd chapters of Revelation, Jesus repeats seven times: “He that hath an ear, let him hear.” Religious drama is superficial in that it appeals to the soulish part of man, not the spiritual part. The soulish part of man (emotions) can have a great time while the spirit within man remains untouched and unmoved. Satan uses the eye gate to distract man from his real heart issues.

Hebrews 11:6 tells us, “Faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen (or demonstrated).” Real faith comes to the human heart by hearing, not by demonstration. Therefore, religious drama borders on being anti-Christ because it is counterproductive to God’s law of hearing.

b. Drama is a violation of sincerity.

The Scriptures teach the importance of sincerity in all of life (1 Corinthians 5:8; 2 Corinthians 1:12, 2:17; Philippians 1:10). In maintaining our sincerity, it is important for each person to recognize that God has created us as unique individuals (Psalm 139:14-15). We are not and cannot be someone else! To try to be someone else violates our individual uniqueness. And, when one does so, he becomes insincere.

How does this connect with religious drama? Drama employs playacting. Jesus had a constant controversy with the Pharisees. They were constantly playacting, or pretending to be something that they were not. Jesus repeatedly called them hypocrites. The original Greek word means “play actor.”

The Pharisees’ sole motivation to pray in public was to be seen of men (Matthew 6:5-7). They were conscious of their audience, thus their performance. Jesus made it very clear that religious devotion was to be private, in “thy closet.” When a person who expresses his piety becomes more concerned about his performance than his message, he is no longer worshiping, but putting on a show! This can happen to preachers, quartets, choruses, etc. “Prayer walks” also usually fall into this same category of playacting.

When a person makes play-acting a regular habit, he becomes a hypocrite. He violates his own soul, because he injures his own uniqueness, which was given by God.

Jesus addressed the Pharisees as hypocrites seven times in Matthew 23. He informed them that they were walking dead men (Matthew 23:27-28). They had playacted for so long that they did not know the difference between the real and the unreal!

This deception is one reason that professional actors become such extremists about the issues of life. Professionally, they become increasingly detached from truth, sincerity, and reality. In such matters as ecology, animal rights, abortion, gay rights, and global warming, many of them have taken positions that are disconnected from the foundations of truth and are no longer sincere.

To pretend to pray or worship or to act out Bible characters in a play is not only insincere, but it borders on being sacrilegious. Imagine pretending to be Jesus in a play! To pretend to be Jesus is blasphemous because no Christian has ever come anywhere close to His perfection! Or, what about pretending to be the devil? Why, pray tell, would anyone who is sincerely following the teachings of Jesus take upon himself the embodiment of evil? A. W. Tozer concludes, “Playacting embodies a gross moral contradiction in that it calls a lie to the service of the truth.”

Religious drama, those who involve themselves in it, and for that matter those who approve of the very hypocrisy that Jesus condemned, are frauds. The Holy Spirit does not honor pretense and showmanship!

The reason multitudes followed Jesus was that His sincerity was so refreshing in comparison to the constant playacting of the Pharisees.

II. Practical Reasons Why Religious Drama is a Menace

a. Religious drama demoralizes reverence for God.

A person who pretends to be Jesus Christ or any other Bible character erodes his reverence for the Lord. When one playacts enough, his fear of God slowly dies within. After all, if a person can pretend to be equal to Christ, what is the need for reverence to a higher being? The Pharisees did not even suspect that they were walking dead men (Matthew 23:27).

b. Religious drama identifies worship with the theatrical world.

Hollywood has effectively proven that the theatrical world cannot produce godly moral values. Pairing a man and a woman as a pretend husband and wife breaks down the sanctity of marriage. The theatrical world also endorses courtship practices that violate the biblical standards of purity. The theatrical world has become the pacesetter of moral standards in today’s society, and many are following their ungodly pattern.

c. Religious drama does not satisfy the inner man.

When a person’s senses are titillated by outward show, the emotions keep seeking a new high and another feel-good worship experience. It creates a desire within to see yet another show that is more satisfying than the previous one. The emotions are having fun, but the inner man starves and slowly dies because the heart and mind have not been fed with real substance.

d. Religious drama ruins the preacher.

Drama is a friend to the lazy preacher. He no longer needs to: Study to shew thyself approved unto God… –2 Timothy 2:15. It requires no Holy Spirit unction to substitute a play for the sermon. Instead of commanding men to be “the light of the world,” he commands them to “lower the lights, please!” When the projector replaces the prophet, the primary means for man to find salvation is lost (1 Corinthians 1:21).

“As long as the preacher can fall back upon entertainment, the pressure that makes preachers will be wanting. The habit and rhythm which belongs to great preaching will be missing from their ministry.” –A. W. Tozer.

The use of religious drama will doom the preacher to mediocrity! The menace that we face today is that as religious drama multiplies, the heaven-sent revivals of the past will become extinct.

e. True worship will be viewed as inferior.

By using drama in a worship service, churches are training the youth to think that true worship is just another inferior form of amusement. When worship and drama are fused into one, worship is reduced to the lowest common denominator. The danger is that the next generation will not know what true worship is!

III. Patterns of True Worship

a. Prayer

Prayer is a vast subject, a worship pattern that too many times remains untapped. Public prayer in the congregational life is squeezed into our man-made time constraints.

In the early church, public prayers held a consistent pattern in their worship experiences. There was public prayer immediately after Christ’s ascension (Acts 1:14) and the first ordination (Acts 1:24). And they continued stedfastly … in prayers –Acts 2:42. No spirit of apathy was present! Prayer meetings were an evangelistic tool, a means of implementing the fear of God, and a great unifier for the whole church (Acts 2:41-44).

Peter and John attended a midafternoon prayer meeting (Acts 3:1). (Say, fellow saint, when was the last time that you attended a midafternoon prayer meeting?) Their prayer meeting had seismic results (Acts 4:31)! The power and presence of the Holy Spirit in our worship services brings results!

Prayer meeting attendance was not a monthly or a bimonthly option (Act 6:4)! When Peter was in prison, they had a voluntary, round-the-clock, prayer chain (Acts 12:5). They laid hands on their missionaries and prayed for them (Acts 13:3). They gathered at the river for a prayer meeting (Acts 16:13). Please note: this gathering at the river was not for the purpose of any kind of water sports; it was a prayer meeting! They gathered …prayer was wont to be made… –Acts 16:13. They understood that wherever Christians happened to meet, it was a normal activity to pray together.

b. Preaching

Preaching is a worship pattern that dates back to the time of Jonah (Jonah 3:2) and Moses (Acts 15:21). In the Old Testament, preaching was God’s pattern for communicating the will of God to man. When Jesus came on the scene, …[He] came into Galilee, preaching the gospel of the kingdom of God –Mark 1:14. He used the same worship pattern. Jesus used parables as verbal illustrations (not visual ones), which caught the attention of His hearers.

Near the end of His ministry, Jesus extended preaching as a worship pattern to future generations and all world cultures: …Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature –Mark 16:15.

Paul’s call was to preach the gospel (1 Corinthians 1:17-21). Preaching was not to be embellished by the cleverness of man. It pleased God to use the foolishness and simplicity of preaching to minister salvation to those who dared to believe. For this reason, preaching needs to be the focal point of every worship service. Praise services, concerts, and musicals are robbers of time that instead ought to be invested in listening to Holy Spirit-inspired preaching. When religious drama is used to present truth, it bypasses God’s ordained pattern of bringing the message of salvation to man.

Blessed is he that readeth, and they that hear the words of this prophecy, and keep those things which are written therein… –Revelation 1:3. God’s method of communication is the written or spoken Word. Not a picture! Not a play! Not a pageant!

c. Singing

The New Testament leaves no hint of professional singers, choirs, or musical performances. Meaningful singing requires participation by all, and an intelligent involvement of the mind (1 Corinthians 14:15). The context clearly implies that worship or singing is not only an individual experience; it is for the edification of all present. Soloists, who tend to be self-exalting, prohibit the remainder of the audience from entering into a corporate worship experience.

Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord –Colossians 3:16. Spiritual songs move the heart, while soulish songs move the feet and the emotions. Our singing is “to the Lord.” Preaching is from God to man, but singing is from man to God, containing expressions of praise, adoration, honor, and thanksgiving. Singing is for worship, not for entertainment.

Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord –Ephesians 5:19. Spirit-filled singing brings mutual edification, inspiration, and encouragement. Participation in singing has a way of ministering to heartfelt needs, where other methods fail. “Making melody in your heart” involves the accompaniment of the heart. External instrumentation tends to focus on a person’s abilities rather than on the heart. If our singing is not accompanied by our hearts, it becomes just another pharisaical worship show.

Old Testament worship was acceptable to God; nevertheless, it was also ritualistic with animal sacrifices, burning incense, using musical instruments, and dancing before the Lord. New Testament worship, however, is quite different. Jesus teaches us that we …must worship him in spirit and in truth –John 4:24. The spirit of worship replaces the rituals. When we move from intrinsic methods of worship to extrinsic methods, we violate the New Testament “spirit” of worship. Our worship is not to be stimulated by the extrinsic, but rather by the Holy Spirit (Ephesians 5:18).

IV. Essence of True Worship

When Jesus met the woman at the well, she expressed a concern about His change in worship format (John 4:20). She was concerned about how her fathers worshiped. In other words, “this is the way that we have always done it!” Every generation of worshipers must guard against formalistic worship.

There are two attitudes that affect true worship in a wrong way:

  • Formal –becoming so accustomed to the way that we have always done it, that we end up merely going through the motions and losing focus on the One being worshiped.
  • Casual –becoming so aloof to any form of worship that the One being worshiped becomes obscured by indifference.

Both formal and casual worship styles have one root problem: lack of reverence for God!

The fathers of the woman at the well had lost both the focus and the concept of worship: “Ye worship ye know not what” (John 4:22a). Jesus clearly indicated that worship is not thoughtless: “We know what we worship” (4:22b). True worship is the exercise of our mind and intellect. True worship has something to offer: “Salvation is of Jesus” (4:22c). It is life-changing!

The worship location is not as important as the attitude (John 4:23). The emphasis that Jesus gives is not on the outward ceremony, but on the state of the mind and spirit.

God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth –John 4:24. Note the word must! The only acceptable worship is in spirit and in truth. Our attitude must be such that it is in harmony with the Spirit of God. True worship also involves our response to truth. If our spirits are not responding to truth, we are not worshiping! If our minds are somewhere else, or on anything else, our worship is merely cold, dead ritualism!

Conclusion

In the observation of the principles of Scripture, it is clear that religious drama is not God’s pattern to bring faith and life into the human soul!

The pattern of true worship in the New Testament is to gather to hear the Word preached; to pray together and for each other; and to sing songs, hymns, and spiritual songs.

The temptation to introduce new things to worship is very real today. The appeal of Jesus is to worship in spirit and in truth. When each of us sincerely does his part to keep worship services meaningful and spiritual, it reduces the temptation to reintroduce the formal (“the way our fathers worshiped”) or to introduce the casual (any new irreverent worship).

Catatan Editor: Banyak pembaca kami mungkin pada awalnya yakin bahwa topik ini tidak berkaitan dengan mereka. Jika demikian, kami turut bersukacita bersama Anda. Namun, sebelum begitu saja melewatkan artikel ini, kami mendesak pembaca untuk membaca dengan saksama apa yang tertulis di sini, lalu mulai mengajukan pertanyaan kepada keluarga, teman, dan kenalan. Kami mendengar bahwa khususnya generasi muda sedang tertarik untuk menghadiri acara-acara para-gerejawi (seperti konser, seminar, sekolah Alkitab, dan sebagainya) atau kebaktian khusus di gereja-gereja tetangga, yang mencakup jenis isi seperti ini sampai taraf tertentu. Yang terutama menonjol adalah kelompok musik/konser khusus, ventrilokuisme, film-film keagamaan, dan sandiwara pendek. Kami ingin meningkatkan kesadaran akan masalah ini dan mendorong diskusi mengenai hal tersebut.

Drama keagamaan—apakah itu?

Sebuah kisah serius yang dibawakan oleh para aktor dengan memainkan atau menirukan dialog tertentu secara teatrikal, atau suatu peristiwa kehidupan nyata dengan efek emosional yang merupakan ciri khas sebuah drama, yang berpola pada tema keagamaan. (American Heritage College Dictionary)

Apakah ini sesuatu yang perlu menjadi perhatian gereja? Seharusnya demikian. Biasanya hal ini tampak bermula dalam kebaktian “doa dan pujian” yang diperpanjang di antara sekolah Minggu dan kebaktian gereja. Atau dalam kebaktian khusus selain pada Minggu pagi. Hal ini dapat mencakup hal-hal seperti persembahan instrumental, pertunjukan boneka, sandiwara pendek, drama, tarian, dan film keagamaan.

Drama keagamaan bukanlah hal baru. Drama ini diperkenalkan pada Zaman Kegelapan (Masehi 400 hingga 1200) sebagai pertunjukan dramatis bertema keagamaan yang dikenal sebagai “drama mukjizat.” Drama-drama ini menjadi begitu rusak sehingga Gereja Katolik berusaha menghentikannya, tetapi tidak berhasil. Pada 1242, drama Sengsara, sebuah pertunjukan yang menggambarkan kematian Kristus, dimulai di Jerman dan masih dipentaskan di seluruh dunia hingga hari ini.

Satu pengamatan menarik, ketika kita menengok ke masa lalu, ialah bahwa drama keagamaan diperkenalkan pada masa paling gelap dalam sejarah (Zaman Kegelapan), tetapi gereja keluar dari era panjang kemerosotan moral ini melalui khotbah Kebangunan Anabaptis yang dipenuhi Roh, berlandaskan Alkitab, dan berfokus pada Perjanjian Baru, pada masa Reformasi.

I. Mengapa Drama Melanggar Ibadah Sejati

a. Drama melanggar hukum mendengar.

Dalam dunia rohani, melihat tidak sepenting mendengar (2 Korintus 4:18). Kata mendengar, mendengarkan, dan didengar ditemukan lebih dari 1.000 kali dalam Alkitab. Sesungguhnya, seluruh Alkitab adalah Allah berbicara kepada manusia. Dia ingin umat manusia mendengar! “Demikianlah firman Tuhan” adalah seruan yang terus-menerus terdengar di seluruh Kitab Suci.

Di Gunung Sinai (Keluaran 19:9), bangsa itu mendengar pesan Allah melalui juru bicara-Nya, Musa. Suara Allah membuat mereka takut (Keluaran 20:18-19), tetapi mendengar dari-Nya penting agar mereka “jangan berbuat dosa.” Dalam Keluaran 20, Allah memberikan petunjuk terperinci mengenai pola ibadah. Janganlah kamu membuat di samping-Ku allah-allah dari perak, dan janganlah kamu membuat bagimu allah-allah dari emas –Keluaran 20:23. Alat bantu visual ini (berhala) melanggar hukum mendengar yang ditetapkan Allah. Melalui mata, timbul godaan untuk membuat berhala. Mezbah-mezbah yang diizinkan Allah harus sederhana dan tidak dipahat (ay. 24-25). Apa yang mereka lihat tidak boleh mengalihkan perhatian dari apa yang didengar dari mezbah! Apa yang terlihat, khususnya ketidaksopanan dalam berpakaian, cenderung mengalihkan perhatian dari apa yang didengar (ay. 26).

Khotbah Yesus mengimbau orang untuk mendengar: Siapa bertelinga untuk mendengar, hendaklah ia mendengar –Matius 13:9. Walaupun Dia tidak menggunakan alat bantu visual seperti yang digunakan pembicara dewasa ini, Yesus menggunakan alat bantu verbal (perumpamaan) untuk mengimbau orang agar mendengar (Mat 13:18).

Di Gunung Transfigurasi (Matius 17), Petrus ingin menciptakan kembali pengalaman beribadah dengan membangun tiga tempat suci. Ia menginginkan sesuatu untuk dilihat! Namun suara dari awan mengingatkan para murid akan pentingnya mendengar (ay. 5). Ibadah dengan alat bantu visual tidak didukung oleh Allah!

Yesus berkata, Sesungguh-sungguhnya Aku berkata kepadamu: siapa yang mendengar perkataan-Ku dan percaya kepada Dia yang mengutus Aku, ia mempunyai hidup kekal … Saatnya akan tiba, dan sekarang sudah tiba, bahwa orang-orang mati akan mendengar suara Anak Allah, dan mereka yang mendengarnya akan hidup. Yohanes 5:24-25. Keselamatan datang dengan mendengar Firman Allah, tetapi hanya apabila seseorang percaya pada apa yang didengarnya!

Paulus mengajukan beberapa pertanyaan yang patut direnungkan: Bagaimana mereka dapat berseru kepada Dia yang belum mereka percayai? Dan bagaimana mereka dapat percaya kepada Dia yang belum mereka dengar? Dan bagaimana mereka dapat mendengar tanpa ada yang memberitakan? –Roma 10:14. Ia menjawab pertanyaannya sendiri: Jadi, iman timbul dari pendengaran, dan pendengaran oleh firman Allah –Roma 10:17. Hukum Allah untuk mengalami keselamatan ialah melalui mendengar Firman Allah atau membaca Firman Allah!

Dalam pasal 2 dan 3 Wahyu, Yesus mengulangi tujuh kali: “Siapa bertelinga, hendaklah ia mendengar.” Drama keagamaan dangkal karena menarik bagian manusia yang bersifat jiwani, bukan bagian rohaninya. Bagian manusia yang bersifat jiwani (emosi) dapat menikmati waktu yang menyenangkan sementara roh di dalam manusia tetap tak tersentuh dan tak tergugah. Iblis menggunakan mata untuk mengalihkan perhatian manusia dari persoalan hatinya yang sesungguhnya.

Ibrani 11:6 memberi tahu kita, “Iman adalah dasar dari segala sesuatu yang kita harapkan dan bukti dari segala sesuatu yang tidak kelihatan (atau diperagakan).” Iman sejati datang ke hati manusia melalui pendengaran, bukan melalui peragaan. Karena itu, drama keagamaan nyaris bersifat anti-Kristus karena bertentangan dengan hukum Allah tentang mendengar.

b. Drama melanggar ketulusan.

Kitab Suci mengajarkan pentingnya ketulusan dalam seluruh kehidupan (1 Korintus 5:8; 2 Korintus 1:12, 2:17; Filipi 1:10). Untuk menjaga ketulusan kita, penting bagi setiap orang untuk menyadari bahwa Allah telah menciptakan kita sebagai pribadi-pribadi yang unik (Mazmur 139:14-15). Kita bukan dan tidak dapat menjadi orang lain! Berusaha menjadi orang lain melanggar keunikan kita masing-masing. Dan, ketika seseorang melakukannya, ia menjadi tidak tulus.

Apa hubungannya dengan drama keagamaan? Drama menggunakan akting. Yesus terus-menerus berselisih dengan orang-orang Farisi. Mereka terus-menerus berpura-pura, atau berpura-pura menjadi sesuatu yang bukan diri mereka. Yesus berulang kali menyebut mereka orang munafik. Kata asli dalam bahasa Yunani berarti “aktor.”

Satu-satunya motivasi orang-orang Farisi untuk berdoa di depan umum adalah supaya dilihat orang (Matius 6:5-7). Mereka sadar akan penonton mereka, dan karena itu beraksi. Yesus dengan sangat jelas menyatakan bahwa kesalehan harus dilakukan secara pribadi, di “kamarmu.” Ketika seseorang yang menyatakan kesalehannya lebih mementingkan penampilannya daripada pesannya, ia tidak lagi beribadah, melainkan mengadakan pertunjukan! Hal ini dapat terjadi pada para pengkhotbah, kuartet, paduan suara, dan sebagainya. “Berjalan sambil berdoa” juga biasanya termasuk dalam kategori berpura-pura yang sama.

Ketika seseorang menjadikan akting sebagai kebiasaan, ia menjadi munafik. Ia melanggar jiwanya sendiri, karena ia merusak keunikannya sendiri, yang diberikan oleh Allah.

Yesus menyebut orang-orang Farisi munafik sebanyak tujuh kali dalam Matius 23. Dia memberi tahu mereka bahwa mereka adalah orang mati yang berjalan (Matius 23:27-28). Mereka telah berpura-pura begitu lama sehingga tidak mengetahui perbedaan antara yang nyata dan yang tidak nyata!

Penipuan ini adalah salah satu alasan para aktor profesional menjadi begitu ekstrem mengenai persoalan-persoalan kehidupan. Secara profesional, mereka makin menjauh dari kebenaran, ketulusan, dan kenyataan. Dalam perkara seperti ekologi, hak-hak hewan, aborsi, hak-hak kaum gay, dan pemanasan global, banyak dari mereka mengambil sikap yang terlepas dari dasar-dasar kebenaran dan tidak lagi tulus.

Berpura-pura berdoa atau beribadah, atau memerankan tokoh-tokoh Alkitab dalam drama, bukan hanya tidak tulus, melainkan nyaris bersifat menista hal-hal suci. Bayangkan berpura-pura menjadi Yesus dalam sebuah drama! Berpura-pura menjadi Yesus adalah penghujatan karena tidak ada orang Kristen yang pernah mendekati kesempurnaan-Nya! Atau, bagaimana dengan berpura-pura menjadi iblis? Mengapa, bolehkah saya bertanya, orang yang sungguh-sungguh mengikuti ajaran Yesus ingin menjadikan dirinya perwujudan kejahatan? A. W. Tozer menyimpulkan, “Berpura-pura merupakan pertentangan moral yang mencolok, karena menjadikan dusta sebagai pelayan kebenaran.”

Drama keagamaan, mereka yang terlibat di dalamnya, dan, dalam hal ini, mereka yang menyetujui kemunafikan yang justru dikecam Yesus, adalah para penipu. Roh Kudus tidak berkenan pada kepura-puraan dan sikap suka pamer!

Alasan orang banyak mengikuti Yesus ialah karena ketulusan-Nya begitu menyegarkan dibandingkan dengan kepura-puraan orang-orang Farisi yang terus-menerus.

II. Alasan Praktis Mengapa Drama Keagamaan Merupakan Ancaman

a. Drama keagamaan merusak rasa hormat kepada Allah.

Orang yang berpura-pura menjadi Yesus Kristus atau tokoh Alkitab lainnya mengikis rasa hormatnya kepada Tuhan. Jika seseorang cukup sering berpura-pura, rasa takutnya akan Allah perlahan-lahan mati di dalam dirinya. Lagi pula, jika seseorang dapat berpura-pura setara dengan Kristus, apa perlunya menghormati Pribadi yang lebih tinggi? Orang-orang Farisi bahkan tidak menyadari bahwa mereka adalah orang mati yang berjalan (Matius 23:27).

b. Drama keagamaan menyamakan ibadah dengan dunia teater.

Hollywood telah membuktikan dengan efektif bahwa dunia teater tidak dapat menghasilkan nilai-nilai moral yang saleh. Memasangkan seorang pria dan seorang wanita sebagai suami dan istri pura-pura meruntuhkan kesucian pernikahan. Dunia teater juga mendukung praktik berpacaran yang melanggar standar kemurnian Alkitab. Dunia teater telah menjadi penentu standar moral dalam masyarakat dewasa ini, dan banyak orang mengikuti pola mereka yang tidak saleh.

c. Drama keagamaan tidak memuaskan batin manusia.

Ketika indra seseorang dirangsang oleh pertunjukan lahiriah, emosinya terus mencari sensasi baru dan pengalaman ibadah lain yang membuatnya merasa senang. Hal ini menimbulkan keinginan dalam diri untuk melihat pertunjukan lain yang lebih memuaskan daripada yang sebelumnya. Emosi bersenang-senang, tetapi batin manusia kelaparan dan perlahan-lahan mati karena hati dan pikiran tidak diberi makanan yang sungguh berisi.

d. Drama keagamaan merusak pengkhotbah.

Drama adalah sahabat pengkhotbah yang malas. Ia tidak lagi perlu: Berusahalah supaya engkau layak di hadapan Allah… –2 Timotius 2:15. Tidak diperlukan urapan Roh Kudus untuk mengganti khotbah dengan drama. Alih-alih memerintahkan orang menjadi “terang dunia,” ia menyuruh mereka, “Tolong redupkan lampunya!” Ketika proyektor menggantikan nabi, sarana utama bagi manusia untuk menemukan keselamatan pun hilang (1 Korintus 1:21).

“Selama pengkhotbah dapat mengandalkan hiburan, tekanan yang membentuk para pengkhotbah akan hilang. Kebiasaan dan irama yang menjadi ciri khotbah yang agung akan lenyap dari pelayanan mereka.” –A. W. Tozer.

Penggunaan drama keagamaan akan menjerumuskan pengkhotbah ke dalam keadaan biasa-biasa saja! Ancaman yang kita hadapi dewasa ini ialah bahwa ketika drama keagamaan berkembang biak, kebangunan rohani yang diutus dari surga pada masa lalu akan punah.

e. Ibadah sejati akan dipandang rendah.

Dengan menggunakan drama dalam kebaktian, gereja-gereja melatih kaum muda untuk berpikir bahwa ibadah sejati hanyalah bentuk hiburan lain yang lebih rendah. Ketika ibadah dan drama dilebur menjadi satu, ibadah diturunkan ke taraf yang paling rendah. Bahayanya ialah generasi berikutnya tidak akan mengetahui apa itu ibadah sejati!

III. Pola-Pola Ibadah Sejati

a. Doa

Doa adalah pokok bahasan yang luas, suatu pola ibadah yang terlalu sering belum dimanfaatkan. Doa bersama dalam kehidupan jemaat dipadatkan agar sesuai dengan batas waktu yang kita buat sendiri.

Dalam gereja mula-mula, doa bersama memiliki pola yang konsisten dalam pengalaman ibadah mereka. Ada doa bersama segera setelah kenaikan Kristus (Kisah Para Rasul 1:14) dan penahbisan pertama (Kisah Para Rasul 1:24). Dengan tekun mereka … berdoa –Kisah Para Rasul 2:42. Tidak ada semangat apatis! Pertemuan doa merupakan sarana penginjilan, cara untuk menanamkan rasa takut akan Allah, dan pemersatu yang kuat bagi seluruh gereja (Kisah Para Rasul 2:41-44).

Petrus dan Yohanes menghadiri pertemuan doa pada tengah sore (Kisah Para Rasul 3:1). (Coba pikirkan, saudara seiman, kapan terakhir kali Anda menghadiri pertemuan doa pada tengah sore?) Pertemuan doa mereka membuahkan hasil yang mengguncang (Kisah Para Rasul 4:31)! Kuasa dan kehadiran Roh Kudus dalam kebaktian kita mendatangkan hasil!

Kehadiran dalam pertemuan doa bukanlah pilihan bulanan atau dua bulanan (Kisah Para Rasul 6:4)! Ketika Petrus berada di penjara, mereka mengadakan rangkaian doa sukarela sepanjang waktu (Kisah Para Rasul 12:5). Mereka menumpangkan tangan atas para misionaris mereka dan berdoa bagi mereka (Kisah Para Rasul 13:3). Mereka berkumpul di tepi sungai untuk pertemuan doa (Kisah Para Rasul 16:13). Harap perhatikan: perkumpulan di tepi sungai ini bukan untuk melakukan olahraga air dalam bentuk apa pun; ini adalah pertemuan doa! Mereka berkumpul …biasanya diadakan doa… –Kisah Para Rasul 16:13. Mereka memahami bahwa di mana pun orang Kristen kebetulan bertemu, berdoa bersama adalah kegiatan yang lazim.

b. Khotbah

Khotbah adalah pola ibadah yang sudah ada sejak zaman Yunus (Yunus 3:2) dan Musa (Kisah Para Rasul 15:21). Dalam Perjanjian Lama, berkhotbah adalah pola Allah untuk menyampaikan kehendak-Nya kepada manusia. Ketika Yesus tampil, …[Ia] datang ke Galilea memberitakan Injil Allah –Markus 1:14. Dia menggunakan pola ibadah yang sama. Yesus menggunakan perumpamaan sebagai ilustrasi verbal (bukan visual), yang menarik perhatian para pendengar-Nya.

Menjelang akhir pelayanan-Nya, Yesus memperluas khotbah sebagai pola ibadah bagi generasi mendatang dan semua kebudayaan di dunia: …Pergilah ke seluruh dunia, beritakanlah Injil kepada segala makhluk –Markus 16:15.

Panggilan Paulus ialah memberitakan Injil (1 Korintus 1:17-21). Khotbah tidak boleh dihiasi dengan kecerdikan manusia. Allah berkenan menggunakan kebodohan dan kesederhanaan pemberitaan untuk melayani keselamatan bagi mereka yang berani percaya. Karena itu, khotbah perlu menjadi titik fokus setiap kebaktian. Kebaktian pujian, konser, dan pertunjukan musik merampas waktu yang seharusnya digunakan untuk mendengarkan khotbah yang diilhamkan Roh Kudus. Ketika drama keagamaan digunakan untuk menyampaikan kebenaran, hal itu melewati pola yang ditetapkan Allah untuk membawa pesan keselamatan kepada manusia.

Berbahagialah ia yang membacakan dan mereka yang mendengar kata-kata nubuat ini serta menuruti apa yang tertulis di dalamnya… –Wahyu 1:3. Cara Allah berkomunikasi adalah melalui Firman tertulis atau lisan. Bukan gambar! Bukan drama! Bukan pertunjukan kolosal!

c. Bernyanyi

Perjanjian Baru sama sekali tidak memberi petunjuk tentang penyanyi profesional, paduan suara, atau pertunjukan musik. Nyanyian yang bermakna memerlukan partisipasi semua orang dan keterlibatan pikiran yang penuh pengertian (1 Korintus 14:15). Konteksnya jelas menyiratkan bahwa ibadah atau nyanyian bukan hanya pengalaman pribadi; ibadah atau nyanyian itu dimaksudkan untuk membangun semua orang yang hadir. Penyanyi solo, yang cenderung meninggikan diri, menghalangi orang-orang lainnya untuk mengalami ibadah bersama.

Hendaklah perkataan Kristus diam dengan segala kekayaannya di antara kamu, sehingga kamu dengan segala hikmat mengajar dan menegur seorang akan yang lain, sambil menyanyikan mazmur, puji-pujian dan nyanyian rohani, dengan rasa syukur di dalam hatimu kepada Allah –Kolose 3:16. Nyanyian rohani menggerakkan hati, sedangkan nyanyian yang bersifat jiwani menggerakkan kaki dan emosi. Kita bernyanyi “bagi Tuhan.” Khotbah berasal dari Allah kepada manusia, tetapi nyanyian berasal dari manusia kepada Allah, dan berisi ungkapan pujian, penyembahan, penghormatan, dan ucapan syukur. Bernyanyi adalah untuk beribadah, bukan untuk menghibur.

Saling berkata-katalah dalam mazmur, puji-pujian, dan nyanyian rohani, sambil bernyanyi dan melantunkan melodi dalam hatimu kepada Tuhan –Efesus 5:19. Nyanyian yang dipenuhi Roh membawa pembangunan bersama, ilham, dan dorongan. Partisipasi dalam nyanyian memiliki cara tersendiri untuk melayani kebutuhan hati yang terdalam, saat cara-cara lain gagal. “Melantunkan melodi dalam hatimu” berarti hati menjadi pengiringnya. Instrumen musik lahiriah cenderung memusatkan perhatian pada kemampuan seseorang alih-alih pada hati. Jika nyanyian kita tidak disertai hati, nyanyian itu menjadi sekadar pertunjukan ibadah Farisi lainnya.

Ibadah Perjanjian Lama berkenan kepada Allah; namun demikian, ibadah itu juga bersifat ritual, dengan korban binatang, pembakaran kemenyan, penggunaan alat musik, dan tarian di hadapan Tuhan. Namun, ibadah Perjanjian Baru sangat berbeda. Yesus mengajarkan bahwa kita …harus menyembah Dia dalam roh dan kebenaran –Yohanes 4:24. Roh ibadah menggantikan ritual-ritual. Ketika kita beralih dari cara-cara ibadah intrinsik ke cara-cara ekstrinsik, kita melanggar “roh” ibadah Perjanjian Baru. Ibadah kita tidak boleh dirangsang oleh hal-hal ekstrinsik, melainkan oleh Roh Kudus (Efesus 5:18).

IV. Hakikat Ibadah Sejati

Ketika Yesus bertemu dengan perempuan di sumur, ia menyampaikan kekhawatiran tentang perubahan tata cara ibadah yang dilakukan-Nya (Yohanes 4:20). Ia mengkhawatirkan cara nenek moyangnya beribadah. Dengan kata lain, “begitulah cara kami selalu melakukannya!” Setiap generasi penyembah harus waspada terhadap ibadah yang formalistis.

Ada dua sikap yang memengaruhi ibadah sejati dengan cara yang keliru:

  • Formal –terlalu terbiasa dengan cara yang selalu kita lakukan, sehingga akhirnya kita hanya menjalankan rutinitas dan kehilangan fokus pada Dia yang disembah.
  • Santai –terlalu acuh terhadap segala bentuk ibadah sehingga Dia yang disembah menjadi tersamarkan oleh sikap tidak peduli.

Baik gaya ibadah formal maupun santai memiliki satu masalah pokok: kurangnya rasa hormat kepada Allah!

Nenek moyang perempuan di sumur itu telah kehilangan fokus maupun pemahaman tentang ibadah: “Kamu menyembah apa yang tidak kamu kenal” (Yohanes 4:22a). Yesus dengan jelas menyatakan bahwa ibadah bukanlah sesuatu yang dilakukan tanpa berpikir: “Kami menyembah apa yang kami kenal” (4:22b). Ibadah sejati adalah penggunaan pikiran dan intelek kita. Ibadah sejati memiliki sesuatu untuk ditawarkan: “Keselamatan datang dari Yesus” (4:22c). Ibadah sejati mengubah hidup!

Tempat ibadah tidak sepenting sikap (Yohanes 4:23). Penekanan yang diberikan Yesus bukan pada upacara lahiriah, melainkan pada keadaan pikiran dan roh.

Allah itu Roh: dan barangsiapa menyembah Dia harus menyembah-Nya dalam roh dan kebenaran –Yohanes 4:24. Perhatikan kata harus! Satu-satunya ibadah yang dapat diterima adalah ibadah dalam roh dan kebenaran. Sikap kita harus selaras dengan Roh Allah. Ibadah sejati juga melibatkan tanggapan kita terhadap kebenaran. Jika roh kita tidak menanggapi kebenaran, kita tidak sedang beribadah! Jika pikiran kita berada di tempat lain, atau tertuju pada hal lain, ibadah kita hanyalah ritualisme yang dingin dan mati!

Kesimpulan

Dengan mengamati prinsip-prinsip Kitab Suci, jelaslah bahwa drama keagamaan bukanlah pola Allah untuk membawa iman dan kehidupan ke dalam jiwa manusia!

Pola ibadah sejati dalam Perjanjian Baru ialah berkumpul untuk mendengar Firman diberitakan; berdoa bersama dan bagi satu sama lain; serta menyanyikan lagu, puji-pujian, dan nyanyian rohani.

Godaan untuk memperkenalkan hal-hal baru ke dalam ibadah sangat nyata dewasa ini. Seruan Yesus adalah agar kita beribadah dalam roh dan kebenaran. Ketika setiap orang dari kita dengan tulus melakukan bagiannya agar kebaktian tetap bermakna dan rohani, godaan untuk memperkenalkan kembali yang formal (“cara nenek moyang kita beribadah”) atau memperkenalkan yang santai (ibadah baru apa pun yang tidak hormat) akan berkurang.

There He was, the King Himself, standing before Pilate, awaiting His death sentence. A large crowd had gathered outside. There was no mistaking it, these people were angry. They wanted this man, Jesus of Nazareth, dead. “Crucify him! Crucify him!” was all that could be heard. This man must have done something terrible. But who were these people that were so angry at the Son of God? Maybe they were rapists, thieves, and murderers. Possibly they were the local liars, drunks, or some other evildoers. Actually, they were the religious people, the church goers, the ones claiming to be God’s people.

Ever since that infamous day, history has repeated itself. People claiming to be God’s people have seen those who love Jesus and try to follow His teachings as their enemies and have persecuted them any way they could. From the Jews, to the Roman Catholics, to the Protestants, the mainstream church of the day has always been the enemy of those who try to govern their everyday lives by the simple clarity of the Scriptures.

I am concerned that we have signed a deal with the mainstream church of our day—a deal for peace at all costs.

Any Scripture that teaches rebuke, reproof, or correction is considered out-of-date and is not allowed to be used to help shape the faith and practice of today’s Christian. Many individuals, church leaders, and even whole churches have begun to believe that love and acceptance alone is a better way to point others to Christ. Those who would raise a voice of warning are seen to be critical and stirring unrest, so they are quickly silenced.

As we search the Scriptures, we see that Jesus, then the disciples, then the early church, had nothing good to say or think about the false church.

While out witnessing or talking to people about the Lord, I’m amazed at the backlash from the mainstream church of our day. Mainly, the Protestant church.

A simple man walked up to a Christian concert holding a sign reading ‘Jesus saves from sin’. Without him ever saying a word, he was attacked. “Quit judging us!” “You don’t know our hearts!” “You’re a disgrace!” “Bigot!” The man slowly walked away.

Many times, the people who get angry when discussions involving God come up are actually folks who claim to know Jesus. The sinners seem to let the message penetrate their hearts. If you were to go to an intersection in a city and simply hold a sign proclaiming something about Christ, you would soon see that this is true.

As I was standing in line at a fast-food restaurant, I noticed that the young man preparing my sandwich had many interesting tattoos. Some were of tombstones, skulls, and other graphic designs. I calmly asked him if he could explain what the tattoos meant to him. He began going into detail about each one. I then asked the young man if he knew Jesus. He got sober and explained that he wanted to believe in God but couldn’t. I quoted a few Bible verses and told him that God was waiting for him. I noticed that God’s Word was having a great effect on the young man.

Meanwhile, I also noticed that the lady behind me was beginning to get frustrated. Finally, she interrupted our conversation and told the man, “Jesus loves you just the way you are. You don’t have to change for this man.” This lady later told me what church she went to and how judgmental she thought that I had acted. I was amazed. I had only told the young man about the Savior!

Before I left the restaurant, I walked back over to the young man to bid him farewell. As I approached, he looked up with tears in his eyes. “Thank you”, he said “I can tell that you truly care about me. I will go home and really think about what you said.”

That night, as I reflected on the day’s events, I wondered why that professing Christian woman had such a problem with my interaction with the young man. Why did she get so angry? I felt like the Lord gave me an answer: No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon –Matthew 6:24.

She was a nice young lady. And, yes, she professed that she was a Christian, but she clearly did not live a life that was in obedience to God’s Word. Rather, outside of going to church, one would not be able to tell at all that she was a follower of Christ. I’m sure if I would have met her at the park, we could have had a nice chat. I’m sure she would have been courteous and polite. I’m sure she would have presented herself as a good citizen and nice person. But when it came to being excited about Jesus, sharing the gospel, and talking about God’s Word, her true colors came out.

Am I saying that a person must be an Anabaptist to make it to heaven? Absolutely not, but I am saying we must obey the Bible and follow Christ to make it to heaven. Most professing Christians are super nice and seem godly, until you start talking about God.

Since when has the definition of a Christian been ‘a nice person’, or ‘a good citizen’? Is that all there is to it anymore—simply do what you want, find a fun church that doesn’t require anything from you, get a good job, get married, have a few children and just like that you’re a ‘Christian’? God help us!

When He was having a discussion with a group of people about whether or not they were true followers of God, Jesus said, …If ye were Abraham’s children, ye would do the works of Abraham. But now ye seek to kill me, a man that hath told you the truth … Ye do the deeds of your father … Ye are of your father the devil… –John 8:39-44.

Has the true church slipped so far as to not be able to call things as they are? God’s Word gives us clear understanding on the matter: Proving what is acceptable unto the Lord. And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather reprove them. For it is a shame even to speak of those things which are done of them in secret. But all things that are reproved are made manifest by the light: for whatsoever doth make manifest is light –Ephesians 5:10-13.

Jesus says Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid –Matthew 5:14. Do we expose sin and heresy in the same way that light exposes darkness? Or are we too attached to a comfortable life with no enemies? We do not need to be scared of the world, or of the false church, because we know that we have what they need! For years the mainstream churches have been getting farther and farther away from the truth of God’s Word. Are we afraid to recognize this? Are we afraid to separate ourselves from this? Will we stand up against it like the early church did?

There is a reason why the Protestant reformer, Martin Luther, died hating the Anabaptist people—because they rejected his interpretation of the Scriptures. The Anabaptist people were not respecters of people. Rather their only respect was for God and His Word, and that without compromise. It was for this that they were persecuted. It would have been much easier for those godly young men to just be quiet and try to get along with the Catholics and Protestants, but they refused and both groups sought to extinguish them. Still, they lived on, trusting only in their God. When we joined the church of Jesus Christ didn’t we promise to continue fighting the same fight—the same fight that Jesus fought; the same fight the early church fought—the fight against the false church? Or have we agreed to get along, for the sake of peace? After all isn’t it better for business, for friendships, and for reputation?! God forbid!

We can live a life that seems to be without sin, but still be living in disobedience. The Bible calls us to action! We are called to be lights, to be witnesses, to pursue godliness, and to live uprightly, not just to put on a good show. I believe this is what has become popular in our day. Lying, cheating, stealing, and killing are attributes that even the world rejects. It’s the ‘in thing’ to be respectable, to make a nice living, and to be upstanding citizens. But is this the life of a born-again believer? Should we fit in with the American dream? Should the only thing that’s different between us and the Protestant church be a head covering? I think we should prayerfully consider this move, the move to join hands with the mainstream church.

I personally know many Protestant Christians. I’m not trying to say they are bad people; many are good folks. But that is not what we are talking about. I believe we need to draw a line and slow down this draw to join them in any compromising manner. Let’s look at just a few of the differences between the Protestants and Anabaptists.

War

Can you believe in war, killing your enemies, and still be a New Testament Christian? Most Protestants are supporters of fighting for our freedoms and our rights. Many will go as far as calling Anabaptist people cowards for not fighting.

Years ago, a group of professing Christians gathered around the biggest bomb ever made. This bomb was about to be sent into a foreign land to destroy an entire city; this bomb was meant to kill everything in its path. Men, women, and children alike would perish because of this bomb; that was the plan. As this group was gathered around this bomb they began to pray, they asked God’s blessing on this bombing mission. They then thanked Him for its success—killing nearly one quarter of a million souls.

Jesus calls us to love our enemies. This topic clearly separated the churches during the various wars. Most of the ‘Christian’ churches in the world supported the war effort of their country. The Anabaptists would not, and they were sorely persecuted for it. So, can we be a Christian and continue to support war? If we support war, where will it stop? Will we also prepare to defend ourselves and our families against violence and lawlessness? The American church calls ‘defending ourselves’, our families, and our country, heroism or bravery; the Bible calls it.

Entertainment

It seems that most Christians in America have no problem watching as many ballgames and sports events as they desire. Movies and television are found in nearly every home. Going to the beach, casinos, and festivals are commonplace. Spending thousands on big hunting trips and expensive vacations is completed without a second thought. To be honest, there really are no limits to what the Christian in America can do, as long as it seems right to them. Jesus tells us multiple times to deny ourselves. It seems that we look for any loophole possible to indulge in all the self-gratifying activities we want! It’s no wonder the church is struggling with pornography and many other sins of the flesh. When we learn how to deny ourselves, pick up the cross, and follow Jesus, then we will start to see a clear, distinct, and large separation between us and the mainstream church of our day.

Non-conformity

It is common to conform to one’s surroundings. This is one reason we don’t send our children to public schools. Jesus is also very clear that we need to come out from among them and be separate, to say “No” to evil communication and the ways of this world, and to not be afraid of identifying ourselves with the people of God. It almost seems that dress is really the only thing that separates many of us, and that is changing also.

Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world. If any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him. For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world –1 John 2:15-16. Where are the people that hate the world? Where are the people that want to be as separated as possible? Where are the people that are not afraid to be laughed at? Where are the people that are not afraid to be different? Oh, where are God’s people?! If history repeats itself, there will soon be no difference between the church and the world. Oh, where are the men?!

I’ve heard many Anabaptist people say they can’t say that those in the worldly church are not Christians; they just don’t want to go in that direction. Is that truthful? Is that the message we want to send to our youth, and to our children? I don’t believe so. The Bible says that few will make it. If we pass on to our children that the Protestant church is also ok, and that they just do things differently, we are destroying everything that Jesus preached. We are saying that we do what we do, not because the Bible says, but rather we decide what we do based on our circumstances and what others around us think! No wonder our children are more interested in the modern church of today than ever before—there’s no line drawn!

There was a modern church that caught my attention. They seemed to be on fire for the Lord! The pastor preached as a dying man. They were very interested in reaching the lost. But there were so many Bible teachings that they simply ignored! I finally took it to the Lord. “What is going on here God!” It was as if God told me to ‘just wait’.

Soon after that, the pastor was released from his position because he was having an affair. Then it all became clear to me—you can have a nice church, you can preach a good message, and you can help the poor, but if you’re not willing to obey ALL of the New Testament teachings, you’re not a true Christian, and you will not find victory. It’s easy to take Christianity so far, but it is not easy to sell all that you have, put your all on the altar, and follow your Master. I know this is bold, but it is the truth of God’s Word.

I was speaking to a young lady in a Protestant setting, who wanted to give her life to the Lord. She was ready to do what it took, or so she said. I asked her if she was ready to suffer for Jesus, if she was ready to separate herself from her old friends, if she was ready to be hated by the world, and ready to be different. I asked her if she was willing to change how she looked. It didn’t take long before she shockingly responded with an emphatic “No!” “I want to start going to church, but not all that other stuff.” I later noticed her with her friends pointing and laughing at me. Being cool does not define a true Christian but being rejected for the sake of the Gospel does.

This is a tough article to write. It’s not a popular message and not very encouraging. But I think it’s a message we must consider today, not only for our sake, but for our children’s sake, and that of the church of tomorrow. We must draw clear lines of separation, without any compromise. We must honestly evaluate the modern church of our day with the clear teachings of the New Testament. We must call sin, sin. We must call disobedience, sin. We must call compromise, sin. We must once again choose to suffer with the true people of God. This does not mean that we shun people or act distasteful towards them, but with love in our hearts, and a message on our lips, we point the masses to Christ!

For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek –Romans 1:16.
