—Dr. Waldron —me dijo la mujer mientras me preparaba para salir de la sala de examen—. Tengo una pregunta más. ¿Cómo puedo bajar este peso de más?

Suspiré en silencio mientras me sentaba para hablar de la situación con ella. Abordar el aumento de peso no es algo que se pueda añadir fácilmente al final de una consulta, y se han escrito muchos libros extensos sobre el tema.

Los estadounidenses parecen tener dificultades con esto. Gastan un promedio de 33 mil millones de dólares al año en productos para bajar de peso, y el 65 por ciento de los estadounidenses tiene sobrepeso o es obeso.

Todo el tema es complicado. Queremos una solución rápida: tomar una pastilla, añadir un alimento que queme grasa o hacer un ejercicio sencillo que elimine el peso de más de manera simple y rápida. La realidad es que, aunque aumentamos de peso con bastante facilidad, es mucho más difícil bajar ese mismo peso. Mantener la pérdida de peso es aún más difícil.

En el principio

No sabemos mucho acerca de la vida antes de la caída en Génesis 3. Sí sabemos que …vio Dios todo lo que había hecho, y he aquí que era bueno en gran manera… –Génesis 1:31.

Es razonable suponer que Adán y Eva no tenían problemas con su peso antes de que el pecado entrara en el mundo. Fueron creados perfectos, lo cual significaba que no habrían tenido problemas metabólicos. Tampoco tenían el apetito descontrolado por la comida con el que hoy lidian sus descendientes.

Con la caída del hombre en el huerto de Edén ocurrieron dos cosas. Primero, los seres humanos empezaron a sufrir dolencias físicas: sus cuerpos ya no funcionaban tan bien como antes. Adán y Eva aún pudieron vivir mucho más que los seres humanos de hoy, pero empezaron a manifestarse enfermedades metabólicas y otros padecimientos. Lo segundo que ocurrió fue que comenzaron a tener una naturaleza pecaminosa.

Esas dos cosas han provocado muchos problemas… Entre ellos están los problemas metabólicos y de peso.

Lo que dice la Biblia sobre la comida

Nuestro cuerpo necesita alimentos nutritivos; sin comer, se deterioraría y finalmente moriría. No hay cosa mejor para el hombre sino que coma y beba, y que su alma se alegre en su trabajo. También he visto que esto es de la mano de Dios –Eclesiastés 2:24.

La ley del Antiguo Testamento imponía restricciones sobre lo que podía comer el pueblo judío. Según la ley kosher, la cantidad de animales limpios era muy inferior a la de animales impuros. Además, el libro de Proverbios menciona varias veces que comer en exceso es peligroso. No estés entre los bebedores de vino, ni entre los comedores desenfrenados de carne; porque el borracho y el glotón llegarán a la pobreza, y el sueño vestirá al hombre de harapos –Proverbios 23:20-21.

En el Nuevo Testamento vemos que ya no se exigía a los cristianos gentiles de la iglesia primitiva que siguieran las leyes judías sobre la alimentación. El concilio de Jerusalén exigió específicamente …que se abstengan de las contaminaciones de los ídolos, de la fornicación, de lo estrangulado y de la sangre –Hechos 15:20. Por lo demás, parece que eran libres de comer lo que quisieran.

Lo que no cambió en el Nuevo Testamento fue la idea del dominio propio. El fruto del Espíritu menciona la templanza como una de las cualidades que deben tener los cristianos, y Pablo dejó claro que se esforzaba por controlar sus deseos, no fuera que llegara a ser eliminado (véase 1 Corintios 9:27).

¿No sabéis que vuestro cuerpo es templo del Espíritu Santo, que está en vosotros, el cual tenéis de Dios, y que no sois vuestros? Porque habéis sido comprados por precio; glorificad, pues, a Dios en vuestro cuerpo y en vuestro espíritu, los cuales son de Dios –1 Corintios 6:19-20.

¿No sabéis que sois templo de Dios, y que el Espíritu de Dios mora en vosotros? Si alguno destruye el templo de Dios, Dios lo destruirá a él; porque el templo de Dios, el cual sois vosotros, santo es –1 Corintios 3:16-17.

La Escritura deja claro que los cristianos deben cuidar de su cuerpo, someter sus deseos al control de Dios y evitar las cosas que tengan que ver con la idolatría.

Razones por las que las personas aumentan de peso

Es fácil dividir las razones del aumento de peso en dos grandes categorías:

  1. problemas metabólicos
  2. problemas relacionados con el exceso de calorías.

Cuando pensamos en problemas metabólicos, estos incluyen cosas como los trastornos de la tiroides y la diabetes. Estos trastornos afectan la velocidad a la que nuestro cuerpo quema calorías. Una de las principales maneras de aumentar el metabolismo es incrementar nuestro nivel de actividad, en particular haciendo ejercicio que eleve el ritmo cardíaco: ejercicio cardiovascular.

El exceso de calorías proviene principalmente de comer demasiado. Es importante recordar que las personas comen por muchas razones además del hambre. Comen porque están aburridas, solas, tristes y sí, a veces porque tienen hambre. Algunos medicamentos, en particular los esteroides, pueden aumentar el apetito y afectar negativamente el ritmo metabólico.

Llamamos tasa metabólica del cuerpo a la cantidad de calorías que nuestro organismo quema en reposo. Se usan un par de fórmulas diferentes para calcular nuestra tasa metabólica basal. Estas utilizan la estatura, el peso, la edad y el sexo para determinar cuántas calorías quemará el cuerpo en un día promedio. Hay algunas aplicaciones y sitios web que pueden hacer este cálculo por usted. https://www.active.com/fitness/calculators/bmr Lo importante es saber que este es el número de calorías que debe consumir para mantener su peso corporal actual. Si consume menos calorías que esa cantidad, tenderá a bajar de peso; si consume más, aumentará de peso.

¿Es importante el peso?

Desde el punto de vista médico, el sobrepeso se asocia con varias afecciones. Tiende a aumentar la resistencia a la insulina y puede llevar a la diabetes. Eleva la presión arterial. Puede causar apnea obstructiva del sueño y empeora la artritis en la espalda y las piernas.

Tener sobrepeso no necesariamente indica un problema espiritual y, según la genética de cada persona, puede ser difícil alcanzar el peso que debería tener de acuerdo con las tablas. Aunque la mayoría de las personas se sienten mucho mejor cuando se acercan a su peso ideal, la Escritura no indica que exista un peso o índice de masa corporal (IMC) específico que los cristianos no deban superar.

Lo importante es que nuestras vidas estén bajo el control de Dios si nos hemos entregado a Él, con nuestros apetitos y todo lo demás. Debemos procurar estar sanos para poder participar de la mejor manera en la edificación del Reino. Además, debemos intentar dar a los demás el ejemplo de una vida entregada a Dios.

Mitos sobre la pérdida de peso…

La gente cree muchas cosas acerca de la pérdida de peso. Examinaremos una lista de ideas que se repiten. Aunque pueda haber algo de verdad en ellas, no son del todo ciertas y pueden desalentar actividades que ayudarían a una persona que lucha con su peso.

…El ejercicio vigoroso es la única manera de bajar de peso.

Muchas personas creen que no pueden bajar de peso porque no pueden hacer suficiente ejercicio. Lidian con dolor, artritis o alguna afección cardíaca o pulmonar que les impide realizar actividades atléticas vigorosas.

Quizá conocen a alguien que empezó a correr y bajó mucho de peso, y les parece que esa es la manera correcta de hacerlo. Simplemente no se sienten capaces de seguir ese camino y se sienten desesperanzadas ante todo el esfuerzo.

El ejercicio es importante. La mayoría de las asociaciones médicas recomiendan que las personas hagan ejercicio al menos 150 minutos por semana. Aunque el ejercicio acelera nuestro metabolismo y ayuda al corazón y a los pulmones, aun así quizá no cambie mucho el peso de una persona.

La mayoría de las personas quema entre 200 y 300 calorías con media hora de ejercicio. Aunque pueda parecer mucho, el cuerpo debe quemar 3500 calorías para perder una libra (aproximadamente 454 gramos). Además, la mayoría sentimos más hambre después de hacer ejercicio, y es muy fácil comer 200 calorías adicionales, lo que prácticamente anula lo que se quemó durante el ejercicio.

…Los carbohidratos hacen que se aumente de peso.

Carbohidrato es el término médico para los azúcares. Las calorías que consumimos en nuestra dieta provienen de una de tres fuentes: carbohidratos, grasas y proteínas. Los carbohidratos están presentes en los postres, pero también en muchos alimentos ricos en almidón, como el arroz, el maíz, la pasta, el pan y muchas otras cosas.

Hay varias dietas, como la dieta Atkins y la dieta keto, que instan a quienes las siguen a eliminar tantos carbohidratos como sea posible. A menudo las personas sí bajan de peso con este tipo de dietas. Por desgracia, son difíciles de mantener a largo plazo porque son bastante restrictivas.

Lo más saludable es consumir carbohidratos con moderación y optar por las alternativas más saludables. Es importante elegir cereales integrales y carbohidratos más complejos. Un tazón de avena puede tener una cantidad de gramos de carbohidratos similar a la de un cereal azucarado para el desayuno, pero el cuerpo lo descompondrá más lentamente y podrá procesarlo con mayor facilidad.

…Morirse de hambre es la única manera de bajar de peso.

Pasar hambre sí produce pérdida de peso: no hubo personas corpulentas entre quienes salieron de los campos de concentración durante la Segunda Guerra Mundial. Desde luego, no es la única manera de bajar de peso ni es una manera saludable de hacerlo.

Sabemos que cuando las personas pasan hambre durante períodos prolongados, comienzan a perder masa muscular, sus huesos se debilitan y su metabolismo disminuye. La mayoría de quienes se privan de alimento terminan recuperando en unos pocos años todo el peso que perdieron y, como su metabolismo se ha ralentizado, a largo plazo les resultará más difícil mantener el peso bajo.

…¡Solo tiene que comer «___», un alimento que quema grasa, para bajar de peso!

Dejé específicamente en blanco el alimento de arriba porque parece que siempre cambia. Tal vez hayas leído que el yogur griego, la canela o el jugo de bayas de goji te ayudarán a bajar de peso. Los estudios indican que no existe ningún alimento mágico que derrita la grasa.

Si estos alimentos funcionan, es porque has reemplazado algo poco saludable y rico en calorías por algo más saludable. Por ejemplo, si tu desayuno habitual consiste en 5 tiras de tocino, un vaso de jugo de naranja, 2 rebanadas de pan tostado y dos huevos, y lo reemplazas por un vaso de agua y un tazón de avena, probablemente bajarás de peso. No será porque la avena «queme grasa», sino porque tiene muchas menos calorías que el desayuno que comías antes.

Algunos alimentos casi no tienen calorías y probablemente requieren tanta energía para comerlos y digerirlos como la que los seres humanos obtienen de ellos. El apio, la lechuga iceberg y los champiñones pertenecen a esta categoría. El problema es que, si le pones mantequilla de maní al apio, aderezo a la lechuga y fríes los champiñones en mantequilla o aceite, de repente dejan de ser los alimentos bajos en calorías que parecen ser. Los seres humanos somos muy buenos para preparar alimentos bajos en calorías de modo que sepan mejor y dejen de ser bajos en calorías.

…Los alimentos sin grasa y dietéticos son la clave para bajar de peso.

En el mercado hay muchos alimentos y condimentos con menos grasa que afirman tener menos calorías que sus versiones normales. A menudo contienen muchos productos químicos diferentes y sustitutos del azúcar para que su sabor y textura se parezcan lo más posible a los de las versiones habituales.

Los sustitutos del azúcar parecen ser más saludables que el azúcar cuando se usan con moderación, pero también parecen hacer que las personas deseen más los alimentos dulces. Algunos estudios han relacionado los edulcorantes artificiales con la aparición de intolerancia a la glucosa, algo que podría conducir a la diabetes. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3095502/ Los dietistas parecen considerar que, entre los diversos sustitutos del azúcar, la stevia es el más seguro.

En definitiva, nuestro objetivo no debería ser tratar de comer los mismos alimentos, solo con menos calorías, sino consumir una variedad de alimentos saludables y porciones moderadas. Eso es lo que conducirá a un mejor metabolismo, no simplemente elegir versiones reducidas en grasa de nuestros alimentos favoritos.

…La solución son las pastillas para adelgazar.

Con el tiempo he visto a muchas personas tomar medicamentos y suplementos, tanto recetados como de venta libre, para tratar de ayudarles a bajar de peso. Se supone que estos medicamentos y suplementos hacen varias cosas, entre ellas reducir el apetito y aumentar la tasa metabólica.

A menudo funcionan a corto plazo. Las personas bajan bastante de peso durante las primeras semanas y creen que han superado sus dificultades. El problema es que, con el tiempo, por lo general se acostumbran a lo que estén tomando, les vuelve el apetito y su metabolismo regresa a la normalidad.

Aunque este tipo de soluciones pueden ayudar a corto plazo, para estar sano a largo plazo hay que idear un plan de alimentación saludable y un horario de ejercicio, y luego mantenerlos a largo plazo. El objetivo nunca debería ser simplemente «bajar diez libras», sino estar lo más saludable posible.

Hemos tratado muchas cosas que no se deben hacer y, probablemente, leyendo entre líneas puedas ver también algunas de las cosas que sí ayudan. La segunda parte (si el Señor quiere) llegará con el próximo número y tratará sobre medidas positivas que podemos tomar para alcanzar un peso saludable.

Con todo esto, es importante recordar que nuestro objetivo no es alcanzar cierta belleza terrenal. Más bien, se trata de tratar nuestro cuerpo como el templo del Espíritu Santo (1 Corintios 6:19). He oído usar este versículo para explicar por qué no debemos beber, fumar ni hacernos tatuajes, pero también debemos tratarlo con respeto en lo que respecta a la alimentación y el ejercicio.

Al cuidar nuestro cuerpo, estaremos en mejores condiciones de atender las necesidades de quienes nos rodean y preparados para cumplir cualquier plan que Dios tenga para nuestras vidas.

Lord, this pain seems unbearable.
Things once loved now must die.
So many hearts are bleeding.
No one has kept a dry eye.

We’ve wept and writhed and prayed
Asking, Lord, this cup to avoid.
We tried what we thought might change it,
But all attempts seemed to return to us void.

Father, we’ve cried out for mercy,
All would have escaped this pain.
But Lord, You bade us go through it;
Your hand in it all You’ve made plain.

Our minds seem to spin as we ponder,
Just exactly what You’re trying to do.
Yet we know that no matter our feelings,
There’s a reason we this storm must go through.

So Father, we bow at Your feet now,
Acknowledging Your omnipotent might.
We cannot discern all the details,
But we trust in the end, all will be right.

Help us, Father, to be broken,
Releasing our all up to You.
Our rights, dreams, ambitions, and possessions,
Making everything open to Your view.

Grow in us, Lord, a humility,
Quiet, yet deep and true.
It’s a jewel that nothing but trials can teach.
Lord, through this, make us more like You!

May our eyes be set on You, Father,
Not on this o’erwhelming gale.
For You have gone through these deep waters,
Nothing but what You plan will prevail.

Obedient even unto death, Lord,
No matter how high the cost may seem.
Give us a vision of the heavenly treasure,
For which no earthly price can exceed.

–By Adrianna H. Fanton

Here, hierdie pyn voel ondraaglik.
Dinge wat ons eens liefgehad het, moet nou sterf.
Soveel harte bloei.
Niemand het ’n droë oog behou nie.

Ons het gehuil, geworstel en gebid
en gevra: Here, laat hierdie beker verbygaan.
Ons het probeer wat ons gedink het dit dalk kon verander,
maar al ons pogings het skynbaar op niks uitgeloop.

Vader, ons het om genade geroep,
ons almal sou hierdie pyn wou vryspring.
Maar Here, U het ons beveel om daardeur te gaan;
U het dit duidelik gemaak dat U hand in alles is.

Ons gedagtes draai in die rondte terwyl ons nadink
oor presies wat U probeer doen.
Tog weet ons dat daar, ongeag hoe ons voel,
’n rede is waarom ons deur hierdie storm moet gaan.

Vader, daarom buig ons nou aan U voete,
en erken ons U almagtige krag.
Ons kan nie al die besonderhede onderskei nie,
maar ons vertrou dat alles uiteindelik reg sal wees.

Help ons, Vader, om gebroke te wees,
en alles aan U oor te gee.
Ons regte, drome, ambisies en besittings—
en alles vir U oop te stel.

Laat nederigheid in ons groei, Here,
stil, maar diep en opreg.
Dit is ’n juweel wat slegs beproewings ons kan leer.
Here, maak ons hierdeur meer soos U!

Mag ons oë op U gerig wees, Vader,
nie op hierdie oorweldigende stormwind nie.
Want U het deur hierdie diep waters gegaan;
niks behalwe wat U beplan, sal seëvier nie.

Gehoorsaam, selfs tot die dood toe, Here,
ongeag hoe hoog die prys mag lyk.
Gee ons ’n blik op die hemelse skat,
waarmee geen aardse prys kan vergelyk nie.

–Deur Adrianna H. Fanton

The night was still, the air was drear.

A man walked alone; his direction unclear.

A battle raged within his troubled soul.

He was at the crossroads, all his life as a whole.

He believed in God, or at least so he thought.

He obeyed what he knew—all that he’d been taught.

But something’s not right, there’s something I lack.

I’ve lived like most others, as my life plays back.

But I go to church! I sing and I pray!

I even helped the neighbor, just the other day!

He fought with his mind, justifying the wrong.

It was God that was working, He seemed quite strong.

The fact of the matter, it’s confidence I lack.

I believe in myself, not the God from way back.

God wants to show strong, in my life every day.

He wants me to be proved; He’s the Life and the Way.

There’s no better One, in Whom to put all your trust;

Than the almighty God. For all men it’s a must!

–by Barry Grant

קרב התחולל בתוך נפשו המיוסרת.

אבל משהו לא בסדר, משהו חסר לי.

חייתי כמו רוב האחרים, כשחיי חולפים לנגד עיניי.

אבל אני הולך לכנסייה! אני שר ומתפלל!

רק לפני כמה ימים אפילו עזרתי לשכן!

הוא נאבק במחשבותיו, מצדיק את הפסול.

אלוהים הוא שפעל; הוא נראה חזק מאוד.

האמת היא שחסר לי ביטחון.

אני מאמין בעצמי, ולא באלוהים של פעם.

אלוהים רוצה להראות את כוחו בחיי, יום אחר יום.

הוא רוצה שאעמוד במבחן; הוא החיים והדרך.

אין טוב ממנו, לשים בו את כל מבטחך;

באלוהים הכול יכול. כל אדם חייב לבטוח בו!

“Could you come with me to visit my sister and her husband?” a friend asked my husband. “They’re having serious marriage problems. My brother-in-law saw how God is working in our marriage and asked me how it happened. Can you tell them how God could change their marriage, too?”

At dusk that evening, my husband, and I, waited with our friend outside his sister’s home. Half an hour later a dilapidated red pickup chugged up and shuddered to a stop. An overweight man with grease-covered clothes and a perpetual smile heaved himself out from behind the steering wheel, while his pretty, fashionably dressed wife hopped out of the passenger seat.

“Come in! Come in!” they invited, guiding us to the stairway which led to their living quarters.

“Excuse the mess,” the wife apologized, swiping clothes from the couches so we could take seats. The room was elaborately furnished but dirty. A deep layer of dust covered the top of the large-screen television set, the end tables… everything.

“Lord, give us wisdom,” I silently implored as we took seats across from the couple. How could we connect with folks we scarcely knew, and who did not have God in their lives?

The husband talked. His wife had failed him miserably and had cheated on him many times. She was presently meeting with a new boyfriend, a young chap she had learned to know on the street. “But I’ll forgive you all that,” promised the husband, “If you are willing to start over, be my wife, and be a mom to our children. I know you’ve failed, but we all fail. Let’s start over, Dear.”

The wife sat in stony silence. Our friend talked, pleading with his sister and brother-in-law to be reconciled. My husband talked about God and His plan for marriage, urging them to turn to Him.

Finally, the wife opened her mouth. Bitterness poured out; dishonor; old dirt. “You never show me that you care. You never buy me anything. Why should I try to please you anymore?”

The husband joined the fray. Both talked at once, on and on, louder and louder.

We sat with sagging hearts, listening, praying, thinking. I tried to imagine how the wife must have felt. She was pretty and young. Why stay at home to clean, cook, and wash clothes for a hulk of a husband who spent his days leaning over greasy motors and crawling under dirty cars? Why, when she could have fun on the street with a cool, young fellow who made her feel so-o-o special?

Finally, the couple ran out of steam. We sat in sad silence. “I’m sorry,” my husband stated finally, “but we can’t help you. The only one who can help you is God. And if you don’t want His help, there’s no hope for your marriage.”

“Yeah, I really should go to church,” mumbled the husband.

“Ha, ha,” sneered the wife. “Just see you become a Mennonite yet!” We rose and shook hands, promised our prayers, and left.

After we left that evening, more harsh words flew between the couple. Their two children came upon the scene and, siding with their father, drove their mother from the house.

From far in the distance came a sound of music—and what else? Singing. Joyful shouting. A wife threw open the shutter from a window facing the street, leaned out, and peered up the road. Oh, yes, today is the day my husband went to bring the Ark of the Covenant home. But why are they making such a ruckus over it?

Into the city danced the parade, singing, shouting, and blowing trumpets. David danced with all his might, his heart overflowing with thanks to God. After agonizing years of fleeing from Saul, God had established him as king. And now the Ark of the Lord was finally returning to its proper dwelling place… God be praised!

As David leaped and shouted his way up the street, his wife looked down from her perch at the window with a dark scowl on her face. Just look at how his robe flies around as he dances. Doesn’t he have any shame?! And hollering like that… what a way for a king to act! Doesn’t he care what others think?!

David returned home several hours later—tired, but happy—to bless his household. It had been a good day. He could tell his wife, Michal, all about it at the supper table.

But she beat him to the subject. [“My, but didn’t you act gloriously today,”] were her frosty words. David must have looked confused. [“I mean, jumping around like that in front of the maidens, just like a vain fellow from off the streets!”]

David must have been smitten. [“I was doing it to the Lord, to the one who chose me to be king instead of your father.”]

I imagine Michal wincing. Ouch! [“Why do you have to throw that in my face?”]

[“I know I am low in your esteem,”]* continued David, [“but those maidens you mentioned, they esteem me.”]

I think of the wayward lady in town who was chased from home by her children, and I wonder who will care for her forty years from now when her pretty face is wrinkled, and her back is bent.

I picture Michal’s lonely old age. The account ends by saying she had no children until her dying day. I doubt if her king-husband bothered to stop in with her anymore. Why would he? He received honor aplenty from others. I also wonder if Michal’s dishonor and their fall-out weakened King David. Several chapters later tell of his eyes roving to a neighbor’s wife and the resulting sin.

All wives are tempted to dishonor their husbands. We are tempted to dishonor regardless of whether our husband is a king or a mechanic, godly or ungodly.

Every day I choose to honor or dishonor the husband God gave me. I can skip alongside him, supporting with enthusiasm, or I can hang out the window, watching with scorn in my heart. I can focus on what he does well and compliment him, or I can nag about what he does wrong. My choice determines the reciprocating favor or loss. My choice affects, not only my husband and me, but also a cloud of witnesses… my children, my sisters in Christ, and my neighbors.

“And the wife see that she reverence her husband.”
(Ephesians 5:33b)

* This is how the Spanish Bible says it; the thought is clearer than in the English translation.

“Kan jy saam met my gaan om my suster en haar man te besoek?” het ’n vriend my man gevra. “Hulle het ernstige huweliksprobleme. My swaer het gesien hoe God in ons huwelik werk en my gevra hoe dit gebeur het. Kan jy vir hulle vertel hoe God ook hulle huwelik kan verander?”

Teen skemer daardie aand het ek en my man saam met ons vriend buite sy suster se huis gewag. ’n Halfuur later het ’n vervalle rooi bakkie aangepruttel en met ’n ruk tot stilstand gekom. ’n Oorgewig man met klere vol vetvlekke en ’n ewige glimlag het homself agter die stuurwiel uitgebeur, terwyl sy mooi, modieus geklede vrou uit die passasiersitplek gespring het.

“Kom in! Kom in!” het hulle ons genooi en ons na die trap gelei wat na hulle woonkwartiere opgegaan het.

“Verskoon die gemors,” het die vrou om verskoning gevra terwyl sy klere van die rusbanke af wegvee sodat ons kon sit. Die vertrek was weelderig gemeubileer, maar vuil. ’n Dik laag stof het die bokant van die grootskermtelevisie, die sytafels … alles bedek.

“Here, gee ons wysheid,” het ek stilweg gebid toe ons oorkant die egpaar gaan sit. Hoe kon ons ’n band smee met mense wat ons skaars geken het en wat God nie in hulle lewe gehad het nie?

Die man het gepraat. Sy vrou het hom bitterlik teleurgestel en hom baie keer verneuk. Sy was op daardie oomblik besig om ’n nuwe kêrel te ontmoet, ’n jong man wat sy op straat leer ken het. “Maar ek sal jou dit alles vergewe,” het die man belowe, “as jy bereid is om oor te begin, my vrou te wees en ’n ma vir ons kinders te wees. Ek weet jy het gefaal, maar ons almal faal. Kom ons begin oor, Liefie.”

Die vrou het in klipperige stilte gesit. Ons vriend het gepraat en sy suster en swaer gesmeek om hulle te versoen. My man het oor God en sy plan vir die huwelik gepraat en hulle aangespoor om hulle tot Hom te wend.

Uiteindelik het die vrou haar mond oopgemaak. Bitterheid het uitgestort; minagting; ou griewe. “Jy wys nooit dat jy vir my omgee nie. Jy koop nooit iets vir my nie. Hoekom moet ek nog probeer om jou tevrede te stel?”

Die man het ook by die stryery aangesluit. Hulle het albei gelyktydig gepraat, aanhoudend, al hoe harder.

Ons het met swaar harte gesit en luister, bid en dink. Ek het probeer indink hoe die vrou moes voel. Sy was mooi en jonk. Hoekom tuis bly om skoon te maak, kos te kook en klere te was vir ’n groot, lomp man wat sy dae oor vetterige enjins gebuig en onder vuil motors deurgekruip het? Hoekom, wanneer sy op straat pret kon hê saam met ’n aantreklike jong kêrel wat haar so-o-o spesiaal laat voel het?

Uiteindelik het die egpaar se fut opgeraak. Ons het in droewige stilte gesit. “Ek is jammer,” het my man uiteindelik gesê, “maar ons kan julle nie help nie. Die enigste een wat julle kan help, is God. En as julle nie sy hulp wil hê nie, is daar geen hoop vir julle huwelik nie.”

“Ja, ek behoort regtig kerk toe te gaan,” het die man gemompel.

“Ha, ha,” het die vrou gespot. “Kyk net, jy gaan nog ’n Mennoniet word!” Ons het opgestaan en hande geskud, belowe dat ons vir hulle sou bid, en weggegaan.

Nadat ons daardie aand vertrek het, het daar nog harde woorde tussen die egpaar geval. Hulle twee kinders het op die toneel afgekom en hulle pa se kant gekies en hulle ma uit die huis gejaag.

Van ver af het musiek nader gekom—en wat nog? Gesang. Vreugdevolle gejuig. ’n Vrou het die luik van ’n venster wat na die straat uitkyk oopgegooi, vorentoe geleun en in die straat afgekyk. O, ja, vandag is die dag waarop my man die Verbondsark gaan haal het om dit huis toe te bring. Maar hoekom maak hulle so ’n geraas daaroor?

Die optog het dansend die stad binnegekom, singend, juigend en op trompette blaas. Dawid het uit alle mag gedans, sy hart het oorgeloop van dank aan God. Ná kwellende jare waarin hy vir Saul gevlug het, het God hom as koning gevestig. En nou het die Ark van die Here uiteindelik na sy regmatige woonplek teruggekeer … God sy dank!

Terwyl Dawid al springend en juigend in die straat op beweeg het, het sy vrou van haar sitplek by die venster af met ’n donker frons na hom afgekyk. Kyk net hoe wapper sy kleed om hom terwyl hy dans. Skaam hy hom dan glad nie?! En so skreeu … dis darem nie hoe ’n koning hom gedra nie! Gee hy nie om wat ander mense dink nie?!

Dawid het etlike ure later teruggekeer huis toe—moeg, maar gelukkig—om sy huisgesin te seën. Dit was ’n goeie dag. Hy kon alles daarvan tydens ete vir sy vrou, Mikal, vertel.

Maar sy het hom voorgespring. [“Wel, jy het vandag darem heerlik opgetree,”] was haar ysige woorde. Dawid moes verward gelyk het. [“Ek bedoel, so rondspring voor die diensmeisies, nes ’n ydele vent van die straat af!”]

Dawid moes seergemaak gevoel het. [“Ek het dit vir die Here gedoen, vir Hom wat my gekies het om koning te wees in plaas van jou pa.”]

Ek kan my voorstel dat Mikal haar gesig vertrek het. Eina! [“Hoekom moet jy dit in my gesig vryf?”]

[“Ek weet ek staan laag in jou agting,”]* het Dawid voortgegaan, [“maar daardie diensmeisies waarvan jy gepraat het, ag hulle my hoog.”]

Ek dink aan die eiesinnige vrou in die dorp wat deur haar kinders uit die huis gejaag is, en ek wonder wie oor veertig jaar vir haar sal sorg wanneer haar mooi gesig verrimpel en haar rug krom is.

Ek stel my Mikal se eensame ouderdom voor. Die verhaal eindig deur te sê dat sy tot haar sterfdag geen kinders gehad het nie. Ek twyfel of haar koninklike man nog moeite gedoen het om by haar in te loer. Waarom sou hy? Ander mense het hom oorgenoeg eer betoon. Ek wonder ook of Mikal se minagting en hulle vervreemding koning Dawid verswak het. Etlike hoofstukke later lees ons van sy oë wat op ’n buurman se vrou dwaal en van die sonde wat daarop gevolg het.

Alle vroue kom in die versoeking om hulle mans te minag. Ons word versoek om hulle te minag ongeag of ons man ’n koning of ’n werktuigkundige is, godvresend of goddeloos.

Elke dag kies ek of ek die man wat God aan my gegee het, sal eer of minag. Ek kan vrolik langs hom huppel en hom geesdriftig ondersteun, of by die venster uithang en met minagting in my hart toekyk. Ek kan fokus op wat hy goed doen en hom komplimenteer, of kerm oor wat hy verkeerd doen. My keuse bepaal of ek guns terugontvang of dit verloor. My keuse raak nie net my man en my nie, maar ook ’n wolk van getuies … my kinders, my susters in Christus en my bure.

“En die vrou moet haar man eerbiedig.”
(Efesiërs 5:33b)

* So lui dit in die Spaanse Bybel; die gedagte is duideliker as in die Engelse vertaling.

The night was still, the air was drear.

A man walked alone; his direction unclear.

A battle raged within his troubled soul.

He was at the crossroads, all his life as a whole.

He believed in God, or at least so he thought.

He obeyed what he knew—all that he’d been taught.

But something’s not right, there’s something I lack.

I’ve lived like most others, as my life plays back.

But I go to church! I sing and I pray!

I even helped the neighbor, just the other day!

He fought with his mind, justifying the wrong.

It was God that was working, He seemed quite strong.

The fact of the matter, it’s confidence I lack.

I believe in myself, not the God from way back.

God wants to show strong, in my life every day.

He wants me to be proved; He’s the Life and the Way.

There’s no better One, in Whom to put all your trust;

Than the almighty God. For all men it’s a must!

–by Barry Grant

We all have a story. Some feel like Job sometimes. Some have lost parents, or partners, or children, or siblings, or friends. Some suffer from severe illness. Some will never recover from their illnesses. Our loved ones might have a terminal illness. Maybe a husband or parent is abusive or unfaithful. Like Job, our friends might have turned against us. Maybe there are problems in the church that seem impossible to fix. It could be something like a colicky baby, or a hyper child. Maybe we just have a cold and are feeling like everything is going wrong. The list is endless. We can relate to the words of this song.

Till the Storm Passes By

In the dark of the midnight have I oft hid my face,
While the storm howls above me, and there’s no hiding place.
‘Mid the crash of the thunder, Precious Lord, hear my cry,
Keep me safe till the storm passes by.

refrain:

Till the storm passes over, till the thunder sounds no more,
Till the clouds roll forever from the sky;
Hold me fast, let me stand in the hollow of Thy hand,
Keep me safe till the storm passes by.

Many times Satan whispered, “There is no need to try,
For there’s no end of sorrow, there’s no hope by and by”
But I know Thou art with me, and tomorrow I’ll rise
Where the storms never darken the skies.

When the long night has ended and the storms come no more,
Let me stand in Thy presence on the bright peaceful shore;
In that land where the tempest, never comes, Lord, may I
Dwell with Thee when the storm passes by.

–by Mosie Lister

When I was a little girl, I thought the author was referring to thunderstorms. I was afraid of thunderstorms. Now I understand that he was referring to the storms of life we go through. On July 14, 2013, I suddenly ended up in the hospital with a life-threatening heart attack caused by a spontaneous coronary artery dissection. What a shock for a 40-year-old mother. The storm was howling, and the thunder was crashing. There was no hiding place from the danger, for it was within me. I only had one heart and it could not be trusted. What if it happens again? Would I die? Then my children would be motherless.

This song was one I’d pray in the dark of the midnight when I couldn’t sleep, and fear threatened to overwhelm me. The Lord’s presence was very real to me. I came through this storm with a greater awareness of how God reveals Himself to us in a deeper way when we are going through hard times. We must choose to yield ourselves completely to Him, and say, “Not my will, but Thine be done.”

When the disciples were out on the sea in the storm, Jesus was with them. He is with us too. We can trust Him. Nothing will happen that is not according to His will. We do not always understand why things happen, but that’s okay. An old preacher used to quote:

“Not now, but in the coming years,
It may be in the better land
We’ll read the meaning of our tears,
And there, sometime, we’ll understand.”

It is so important that we accept what God allows in our lives. Accepting does not mean we don’t do anything about it. We will go to the doctor if necessary. We will reach out to others for comfort and council. We will still have all kinds of feelings, but we should have peace. We can’t wallow in self-pity and have a “poor me” attitude. And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose –Romans 8:28. I believe that. I can’t always see the good, but God does.

Life is hard sometimes, but the song tells about the time when the long night has ended, and the storms come no more. Dear sisters, let’s remain faithful and lean hard on the Lord through the storms of life.

لكل منا قصة. أحيانًا يشعر بعضنا كما شعر أيوب. فقد بعضهم والديه، أو أزواجهم، أو أبناءهم، أو إخوتهم، أو أصدقاءهم. ويعاني بعضهم مرضًا خطيرًا. ولن يتعافى بعضهم من أمراضهم أبدًا. وقد يكون أحباؤنا مصابين بمرض عضال. وربما يكون الزوج أو أحد الوالدين مسيئًا أو غير مخلص. وكما حدث مع أيوب، ربما انقلب أصدقاؤنا علينا. وربما توجد في الكنيسة مشكلات تبدو مستحيلة الحل. وقد يكون الأمر شيئًا مثل طفل كثير البكاء بسبب المغص، أو طفل مفرط النشاط. وربما لا نعاني سوى زكام، لكننا نشعر أن كل شيء يسير على نحو خاطئ. والقائمة لا تنتهي. نستطيع أن نجد أنفسنا في كلمات هذه الترنيمة.

حتى تعبر العاصفة

في ظلمة منتصف الليل كثيرًا ما أخفيت وجهي،
فيما تعوي العاصفة فوقي، ولا موضع أختبئ فيه.
وسط دوي الرعد، يا ربّي الثمين، اسمع صراخي،
واحفظني آمنًا حتى تعبر العاصفة.

اللازمة:

حتى تمر العاصفة، وحتى لا يعود للرعد صوت،
وحتى تنقشع الغيوم إلى الأبد عن السماء؛
أمسك بي بإحكام، ودعني أقف في جوف كفك،
واحفظني آمنًا حتى تعبر العاصفة.

كثيرًا ما همس الشيطان: «لا حاجة إلى المحاولة،
فالحزن لا نهاية له، ولا أمل في الغد».
لكنني أعلم أنك معي، وغدًا سأقوم
إلى حيث لا تظلم العواصف السماء أبدًا.

حين تنتهي الليلة الطويلة ولا تعود العواصف،
دعني أقف في حضرتك على الشاطئ المشرق الهادئ؛
في تلك الأرض التي لا يأتيها الإعصار، يا رب، ليتني
أقيم معك حين تعبر العاصفة.

– بقلم موزي ليستر

حين كنت فتاة صغيرة، ظننت أن كاتب الترنيمة يشير إلى العواصف الرعدية. كنت أخاف منها. أما الآن فأفهم أنه كان يشير إلى عواصف الحياة التي نمر بها. في 14 يوليو 2013، وجدت نفسي فجأة في المستشفى إثر نوبة قلبية مهددة للحياة، سببها تسلخ تلقائي في أحد الشرايين التاجية. يا لها من صدمة لأم في الأربعين من عمرها. كانت العاصفة تعوي، والرعد يدوي. لم يكن هناك مكان أختبئ فيه من الخطر، لأنه كان في داخلي. لم يكن لدي سوى قلب واحد، ولم يكن بوسعي الوثوق به. ماذا لو حدث ذلك مرة أخرى؟ هل سأموت؟ وحينها سيصبح أطفالي بلا أم.

كنت أصلّي بهذه الترنيمة في ظلمة منتصف الليل حين يعجزني النوم ويهدد الخوف بأن يغمرني. كان حضور الرب حقيقيًا جدًا بالنسبة إليّ. اجتزت هذه العاصفة بإدراك أعمق لكيفية إعلان الله عن نفسه لنا على نحو أعمق حين نمر بأوقات عصيبة. علينا أن نختار أن نسلّم أنفسنا له بالكامل، ونقول: «لتكن لا إرادتي بل إرادتك».

حين كان التلاميذ في البحر وسط العاصفة، كان يسوع معهم. وهو معنا أيضًا. نستطيع أن نثق به. لن يحدث شيء لا يكون بحسب مشيئته. لا نفهم دائمًا لماذا تحدث الأمور، لكن لا بأس بذلك. كان واعظ مسن يقتبس هذه الأبيات:

«ليس الآن، بل في السنوات القادمة،
وربما في الأرض الأفضل،
سنفهم مغزى دموعنا،
وهناك، يومًا ما، سندرك.»

من المهم جدًا أن نقبل ما يسمح الله به في حياتنا. فالقبول لا يعني ألا نفعل شيئًا حياله. سنذهب إلى الطبيب إذا اقتضى الأمر. وسنلجأ إلى الآخرين طلبًا للمواساة والمشورة. وستظل لدينا مشاعر من شتى الأنواع، لكن ينبغي أن يكون لنا سلام. لا يمكننا أن نستغرق في الشفقة على أنفسنا ونتخذ موقف «يا لسوء حالي». ونحن نعلم أن كل الأشياء تعمل معًا للخير للذين يحبون الله، الذين هم مدعوون حسب قصده – رومية 8:28. أنا أؤمن بذلك. لا أستطيع دائمًا أن أرى الخير، لكن الله يراه.

الحياة صعبة أحيانًا، لكن الترنيمة تتحدث عن الوقت الذي تنتهي فيه الليلة الطويلة ولا تعود العواصف. أخواتي العزيزات، فلنبقَ أمينات ونتكل بشدة على الرب خلال عواصف الحياة.

ورأيت سماءً جديدة وأرضًا جديدة، لأن السماء الأولى والأرض الأولى قد مضتا، ولم يعد بحرٌ موجودًا. وأنا يوحنا رأيت المدينة المقدسة، أورشليم الجديدة، نازلة من السماء من عند الله، مهيأة كعروس مزينة لعريسها. وسمعت صوتًا عظيمًا من السماء يقول: «هوذا مسكن الله مع الناس، وهو سيسكن معهم، وهم يكونون له شعبًا، والله نفسه يكون معهم إلهًا لهم. وسيمسح الله كل دمعة من عيونهم، ولن يكون موت في ما بعد، ولا حزن، ولا صراخ، ولا وجع في ما بعد، لأن الأمور الأولى قد مضت». رؤيا 21:1-4.

Lord, this pain seems unbearable.
Things once loved now must die.
So many hearts are bleeding.
No one has kept a dry eye.

We’ve wept and writhed and prayed
Asking, Lord, this cup to avoid.
We tried what we thought might change it,
But all attempts seemed to return to us void.

Father, we’ve cried out for mercy,
All would have escaped this pain.
But Lord, You bade us go through it;
Your hand in it all You’ve made plain.

Our minds seem to spin as we ponder,
Just exactly what You’re trying to do.
Yet we know that no matter our feelings,
There’s a reason we this storm must go through.

So Father, we bow at Your feet now,
Acknowledging Your omnipotent might.
We cannot discern all the details,
But we trust in the end, all will be right.

Help us, Father, to be broken,
Releasing our all up to You.
Our rights, dreams, ambitions, and possessions,
Making everything open to Your view.

Grow in us, Lord, a humility,
Quiet, yet deep and true.
It’s a jewel that nothing but trials can teach.
Lord, through this, make us more like You!

May our eyes be set on You, Father,
Not on this o’erwhelming gale.
For You have gone through these deep waters,
Nothing but what You plan will prevail.

Obedient even unto death, Lord,
No matter how high the cost may seem.
Give us a vision of the heavenly treasure,
For which no earthly price can exceed.

–By Adrianna H. Fanton

Signore, questo dolore sembra insopportabile.
Ciò che un tempo amavamo ora deve morire.
Troppi cuori sanguinano.
Nessuno è riuscito a trattenere le lacrime.

Abbiamo pianto, ci siamo contorti e abbiamo pregato,
chiedendo, Signore, di evitare questo calice.
Abbiamo tentato ciò che pensavamo potesse cambiarlo,
ma ogni tentativo ci è sembrato vano.

Padre, abbiamo implorato la tua misericordia,
tutti avrebbero voluto sfuggire a questo dolore.
Ma, Signore, ci hai fatto attraversare questo dolore;
hai reso chiara la tua mano in tutto questo.

La mente sembra girarci vorticosamente mentre ci chiediamo
che cosa esattamente tu stia cercando di fare.
Eppure sappiamo che, qualunque cosa proviamo,
c’è un motivo per cui dobbiamo attraversare questa tempesta.

Così, Padre, ora ci prostriamo ai tuoi piedi,
riconoscendo la tua onnipotenza.
Non riusciamo a discernere tutti i particolari,
ma confidiamo che alla fine tutto andrà bene.

Aiutaci, Padre, a essere spezzati,
affidandoti tutto ciò che siamo.
I nostri diritti, sogni, ambizioni e possedimenti,
mettendo ogni cosa alla tua luce.

Fa’ crescere in noi, Signore, l’umiltà,
silenziosa, eppure profonda e autentica.
È un gioiello che solo le prove possono insegnare.
Signore, attraverso questo, rendici più simili a te!

Possano i nostri occhi essere rivolti a te, Padre,
e non a questa tempesta travolgente.
Perché tu hai attraversato queste acque profonde,
e nulla se non ciò che hai disposto prevarrà.

Obbedienti fino alla morte, Signore,
per quanto alto possa sembrare il prezzo.
Donaci una visione del tesoro celeste,
il cui valore nessun prezzo terreno può superare.

–Di Adrianna H. Fanton

Editor’s Note: Many of our readers may at first be convinced that this topic doesn’t pertain to them. If this is correct, we rejoice with you. However, before simply passing over this article we urge the reader to carefully read what is written here then start asking questions of family, friends, and acquaintances. We are hearing that especially the younger generation is being drawn into para-church events (such as concerts, seminars, Bible Schools, etc.) or special services at neighboring churches, which involve this type of content to one degree or another. Especially prominent are special music groups/concerts, ventriloquism, religious films, and skits. We wish to raise awareness on this issue and stimulate a discussion on the matter.

Religious drama—what is it?

A serious story by actors performing or impersonating any given dialogue in a theatrical manner, or an event of real life with emotional effects which are characteristics of a play, patterned after a religious theme. (American Heritage College Dictionary)

Is this something the church needs to be concerned about? It should be. It usually seems to get its beginning in extended “prayer and praise” services between Sunday school and church services. Or in special services other than on a Sunday morning. It can include such things as instrumental presentations, puppet shows, skits, plays, dances, and religious films.

Religious drama is not something new. It was introduced during the Dark Ages (A.D. 400 to 1200) as dramatic performances with religious themes known as “miracle plays.” These plays became so corrupt that the Catholic Church tried to put a stop to them, but to no avail. In 1242, the Passion play, a performance that depicts the death of Christ, started in Germany and it is still being performed around the world today.

An interesting observation, as we look back through time, is that religious drama was introduced during the darkest time of history (the Dark Ages), but the church emerged from this long era of moral decay through Spirit-filled, Bible-based, New Covenant-focused preaching of the Anabaptist Revival during the Reformation time period.

I. Why Drama Violates True Worship

a. Drama is a violation of the law of hearing.

In a spiritual world, seeing is not as important as hearing (2 Corinthians 4:18). The words hear, heareth, and heard are found over 1,000 times in the Bible. As a matter of fact, the whole Bible is God speaking to man. He wants mankind to hear! “Thus, saith the Lord” is a constant refrain throughout Scripture.

On Mount Sinai (Exodus 19:9), the people heard the message of God through His spokesman, Moses. God’s voice was frightening to them (Exodus 20:18-19) but hearing from Him was essential so that they “sin not.” In Exodus 20, God gave some detailed instructions of what the worship pattern was to be. Ye shall not make with me gods of silver, neither shall ye make unto you gods of gold –Exodus 20:23. These visual aids (idols) were a violation of God’s law of hearing. Through the eye gate comes the temptation to build idols. The altars that God did permit were to be plain and uncut (vss. 24-25). What they did see was not to distract from that which was heard from the altar! What is seen, especially immodesty, tends to be a distraction from what is heard (v. 26).

The preaching of Jesus appealed to the hearing: Who hath ears to hear, let him hear –Matthew 13:9. While He did not use visual aids like speakers do today, Jesus did use verbal aids (parables) as a tool to appeal to the hearing (Mat 13:18).

On the Mount of Transfiguration (Matthew 17), Peter wanted to reinvent the worship experience by building three shrines. He wanted something to see! But the voice in the clouds alerted the disciples to the importance of hearing (v. 5). Worship with visual aids is not endorsed by God!

Jesus said, Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life … The hour is coming, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God: and they that hear shall live. John 5:24-25. Salvation comes by hearing the Word of God, but only when one believes what is heard!

Paul raises some sobering questions: How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher? –Romans 10:14. He answers his own questions: So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God –Romans 10:17. God’s law to experience salvation is either by hearing God’s Word or by reading God’s Word!

In the 2nd and 3rd chapters of Revelation, Jesus repeats seven times: “He that hath an ear, let him hear.” Religious drama is superficial in that it appeals to the soulish part of man, not the spiritual part. The soulish part of man (emotions) can have a great time while the spirit within man remains untouched and unmoved. Satan uses the eye gate to distract man from his real heart issues.

Hebrews 11:6 tells us, “Faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen (or demonstrated).” Real faith comes to the human heart by hearing, not by demonstration. Therefore, religious drama borders on being anti-Christ because it is counterproductive to God’s law of hearing.

b. Drama is a violation of sincerity.

The Scriptures teach the importance of sincerity in all of life (1 Corinthians 5:8; 2 Corinthians 1:12, 2:17; Philippians 1:10). In maintaining our sincerity, it is important for each person to recognize that God has created us as unique individuals (Psalm 139:14-15). We are not and cannot be someone else! To try to be someone else violates our individual uniqueness. And, when one does so, he becomes insincere.

How does this connect with religious drama? Drama employs playacting. Jesus had a constant controversy with the Pharisees. They were constantly playacting, or pretending to be something that they were not. Jesus repeatedly called them hypocrites. The original Greek word means “play actor.”

The Pharisees’ sole motivation to pray in public was to be seen of men (Matthew 6:5-7). They were conscious of their audience, thus their performance. Jesus made it very clear that religious devotion was to be private, in “thy closet.” When a person who expresses his piety becomes more concerned about his performance than his message, he is no longer worshiping, but putting on a show! This can happen to preachers, quartets, choruses, etc. “Prayer walks” also usually fall into this same category of playacting.

When a person makes play-acting a regular habit, he becomes a hypocrite. He violates his own soul, because he injures his own uniqueness, which was given by God.

Jesus addressed the Pharisees as hypocrites seven times in Matthew 23. He informed them that they were walking dead men (Matthew 23:27-28). They had playacted for so long that they did not know the difference between the real and the unreal!

This deception is one reason that professional actors become such extremists about the issues of life. Professionally, they become increasingly detached from truth, sincerity, and reality. In such matters as ecology, animal rights, abortion, gay rights, and global warming, many of them have taken positions that are disconnected from the foundations of truth and are no longer sincere.

To pretend to pray or worship or to act out Bible characters in a play is not only insincere, but it borders on being sacrilegious. Imagine pretending to be Jesus in a play! To pretend to be Jesus is blasphemous because no Christian has ever come anywhere close to His perfection! Or, what about pretending to be the devil? Why, pray tell, would anyone who is sincerely following the teachings of Jesus take upon himself the embodiment of evil? A. W. Tozer concludes, “Playacting embodies a gross moral contradiction in that it calls a lie to the service of the truth.”

Religious drama, those who involve themselves in it, and for that matter those who approve of the very hypocrisy that Jesus condemned, are frauds. The Holy Spirit does not honor pretense and showmanship!

The reason multitudes followed Jesus was that His sincerity was so refreshing in comparison to the constant playacting of the Pharisees.

II. Practical Reasons Why Religious Drama is a Menace

a. Religious drama demoralizes reverence for God.

A person who pretends to be Jesus Christ or any other Bible character erodes his reverence for the Lord. When one playacts enough, his fear of God slowly dies within. After all, if a person can pretend to be equal to Christ, what is the need for reverence to a higher being? The Pharisees did not even suspect that they were walking dead men (Matthew 23:27).

b. Religious drama identifies worship with the theatrical world.

Hollywood has effectively proven that the theatrical world cannot produce godly moral values. Pairing a man and a woman as a pretend husband and wife breaks down the sanctity of marriage. The theatrical world also endorses courtship practices that violate the biblical standards of purity. The theatrical world has become the pacesetter of moral standards in today’s society, and many are following their ungodly pattern.

c. Religious drama does not satisfy the inner man.

When a person’s senses are titillated by outward show, the emotions keep seeking a new high and another feel-good worship experience. It creates a desire within to see yet another show that is more satisfying than the previous one. The emotions are having fun, but the inner man starves and slowly dies because the heart and mind have not been fed with real substance.

d. Religious drama ruins the preacher.

Drama is a friend to the lazy preacher. He no longer needs to: Study to shew thyself approved unto God… –2 Timothy 2:15. It requires no Holy Spirit unction to substitute a play for the sermon. Instead of commanding men to be “the light of the world,” he commands them to “lower the lights, please!” When the projector replaces the prophet, the primary means for man to find salvation is lost (1 Corinthians 1:21).

“As long as the preacher can fall back upon entertainment, the pressure that makes preachers will be wanting. The habit and rhythm which belongs to great preaching will be missing from their ministry.” –A. W. Tozer.

The use of religious drama will doom the preacher to mediocrity! The menace that we face today is that as religious drama multiplies, the heaven-sent revivals of the past will become extinct.

e. True worship will be viewed as inferior.

By using drama in a worship service, churches are training the youth to think that true worship is just another inferior form of amusement. When worship and drama are fused into one, worship is reduced to the lowest common denominator. The danger is that the next generation will not know what true worship is!

III. Patterns of True Worship

a. Prayer

Prayer is a vast subject, a worship pattern that too many times remains untapped. Public prayer in the congregational life is squeezed into our man-made time constraints.

In the early church, public prayers held a consistent pattern in their worship experiences. There was public prayer immediately after Christ’s ascension (Acts 1:14) and the first ordination (Acts 1:24). And they continued stedfastly … in prayers –Acts 2:42. No spirit of apathy was present! Prayer meetings were an evangelistic tool, a means of implementing the fear of God, and a great unifier for the whole church (Acts 2:41-44).

Peter and John attended a midafternoon prayer meeting (Acts 3:1). (Say, fellow saint, when was the last time that you attended a midafternoon prayer meeting?) Their prayer meeting had seismic results (Acts 4:31)! The power and presence of the Holy Spirit in our worship services brings results!

Prayer meeting attendance was not a monthly or a bimonthly option (Act 6:4)! When Peter was in prison, they had a voluntary, round-the-clock, prayer chain (Acts 12:5). They laid hands on their missionaries and prayed for them (Acts 13:3). They gathered at the river for a prayer meeting (Acts 16:13). Please note: this gathering at the river was not for the purpose of any kind of water sports; it was a prayer meeting! They gathered …prayer was wont to be made… –Acts 16:13. They understood that wherever Christians happened to meet, it was a normal activity to pray together.

b. Preaching

Preaching is a worship pattern that dates back to the time of Jonah (Jonah 3:2) and Moses (Acts 15:21). In the Old Testament, preaching was God’s pattern for communicating the will of God to man. When Jesus came on the scene, …[He] came into Galilee, preaching the gospel of the kingdom of God –Mark 1:14. He used the same worship pattern. Jesus used parables as verbal illustrations (not visual ones), which caught the attention of His hearers.

Near the end of His ministry, Jesus extended preaching as a worship pattern to future generations and all world cultures: …Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature –Mark 16:15.

Paul’s call was to preach the gospel (1 Corinthians 1:17-21). Preaching was not to be embellished by the cleverness of man. It pleased God to use the foolishness and simplicity of preaching to minister salvation to those who dared to believe. For this reason, preaching needs to be the focal point of every worship service. Praise services, concerts, and musicals are robbers of time that instead ought to be invested in listening to Holy Spirit-inspired preaching. When religious drama is used to present truth, it bypasses God’s ordained pattern of bringing the message of salvation to man.

Blessed is he that readeth, and they that hear the words of this prophecy, and keep those things which are written therein… –Revelation 1:3. God’s method of communication is the written or spoken Word. Not a picture! Not a play! Not a pageant!

c. Singing

The New Testament leaves no hint of professional singers, choirs, or musical performances. Meaningful singing requires participation by all, and an intelligent involvement of the mind (1 Corinthians 14:15). The context clearly implies that worship or singing is not only an individual experience; it is for the edification of all present. Soloists, who tend to be self-exalting, prohibit the remainder of the audience from entering into a corporate worship experience.

Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord –Colossians 3:16. Spiritual songs move the heart, while soulish songs move the feet and the emotions. Our singing is “to the Lord.” Preaching is from God to man, but singing is from man to God, containing expressions of praise, adoration, honor, and thanksgiving. Singing is for worship, not for entertainment.

Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord –Ephesians 5:19. Spirit-filled singing brings mutual edification, inspiration, and encouragement. Participation in singing has a way of ministering to heartfelt needs, where other methods fail. “Making melody in your heart” involves the accompaniment of the heart. External instrumentation tends to focus on a person’s abilities rather than on the heart. If our singing is not accompanied by our hearts, it becomes just another pharisaical worship show.

Old Testament worship was acceptable to God; nevertheless, it was also ritualistic with animal sacrifices, burning incense, using musical instruments, and dancing before the Lord. New Testament worship, however, is quite different. Jesus teaches us that we …must worship him in spirit and in truth –John 4:24. The spirit of worship replaces the rituals. When we move from intrinsic methods of worship to extrinsic methods, we violate the New Testament “spirit” of worship. Our worship is not to be stimulated by the extrinsic, but rather by the Holy Spirit (Ephesians 5:18).

IV. Essence of True Worship

When Jesus met the woman at the well, she expressed a concern about His change in worship format (John 4:20). She was concerned about how her fathers worshiped. In other words, “this is the way that we have always done it!” Every generation of worshipers must guard against formalistic worship.

There are two attitudes that affect true worship in a wrong way:

  • Formal –becoming so accustomed to the way that we have always done it, that we end up merely going through the motions and losing focus on the One being worshiped.
  • Casual –becoming so aloof to any form of worship that the One being worshiped becomes obscured by indifference.

Both formal and casual worship styles have one root problem: lack of reverence for God!

The fathers of the woman at the well had lost both the focus and the concept of worship: “Ye worship ye know not what” (John 4:22a). Jesus clearly indicated that worship is not thoughtless: “We know what we worship” (4:22b). True worship is the exercise of our mind and intellect. True worship has something to offer: “Salvation is of Jesus” (4:22c). It is life-changing!

The worship location is not as important as the attitude (John 4:23). The emphasis that Jesus gives is not on the outward ceremony, but on the state of the mind and spirit.

God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth –John 4:24. Note the word must! The only acceptable worship is in spirit and in truth. Our attitude must be such that it is in harmony with the Spirit of God. True worship also involves our response to truth. If our spirits are not responding to truth, we are not worshiping! If our minds are somewhere else, or on anything else, our worship is merely cold, dead ritualism!

Conclusion

In the observation of the principles of Scripture, it is clear that religious drama is not God’s pattern to bring faith and life into the human soul!

The pattern of true worship in the New Testament is to gather to hear the Word preached; to pray together and for each other; and to sing songs, hymns, and spiritual songs.

The temptation to introduce new things to worship is very real today. The appeal of Jesus is to worship in spirit and in truth. When each of us sincerely does his part to keep worship services meaningful and spiritual, it reduces the temptation to reintroduce the formal (“the way our fathers worshiped”) or to introduce the casual (any new irreverent worship).

Hata hivyo, kabla ya kupuuza tu makala hii, tunamhimiza msomaji asome kwa makini yaliyoandikwa hapa, kisha aanze kuwauliza maswali watu wa familia, marafiki na watu anaowafahamu. Tunasikia kwamba hasa kizazi cha vijana kinavutwa kwenye matukio ya mashirika yanayoshirikiana na kanisa (kama vile matamasha, semina, shule za Biblia, n.k.) au ibada maalum katika makanisa ya jirani, ambazo huhusisha maudhui ya aina hii kwa kiwango fulani. Yanayoonekana zaidi ni vikundi maalum vya muziki/matamasha, uigizaji wa sauti kwa kutumia vikaragosi, filamu za kidini na maigizo mafupi. Tunataka kuibua ufahamu kuhusu suala hili na kuchochea majadiliano juu yake.

Drama ya kidini—ni nini?

Hadithi nzito inayowasilishwa na waigizaji wanaoigiza au kujifanya kuwa wahusika katika mazungumzo fulani kwa namna ya maigizo ya jukwaani, au tukio halisi la maisha lenye athari za kihisia ambazo ni sifa za mchezo wa kuigiza, lililoundwa kwa kufuata mada ya kidini. (Kamusi ya Chuo cha American Heritage)

Je, hili ni jambo ambalo kanisa linapaswa kulijali? Linapaswa. Kwa kawaida huonekana kuanza katika ibada za “sala na sifa” zilizoongezwa muda kati ya shule ya Jumapili na ibada za kanisa. Au katika ibada maalum zisizofanyika Jumapili asubuhi. Linaweza kujumuisha mambo kama vile maonyesho ya ala za muziki, maonyesho ya vikaragosi, maigizo mafupi, michezo ya kuigiza, dansi na filamu za kidini.

Drama ya kidini si jambo jipya. Ilianzishwa wakati wa Enzi za Giza (A.D. 400 hadi 1200) kama maonyesho ya maigizo yenye mada za kidini yaliyojulikana kama “michezo ya miujiza.” Michezo hii ilipotoka kiasi kwamba Kanisa Katoliki lilijaribu kuikomesha, lakini halikufanikiwa. Mwaka 1242, mchezo wa Mateso ya Kristo, maonyesho yanayoonyesha kifo cha Kristo, ulianza nchini Ujerumani na bado unaonyeshwa duniani kote leo.

Jambo la kuvutia tunapotazama nyuma katika historia ni kwamba drama ya kidini ilianzishwa wakati wa kipindi cheusi zaidi cha historia (Enzi za Giza), lakini kanisa lilitoka katika kipindi hiki kirefu cha uharibifu wa maadili kupitia mahubiri yaliyojaa Roho, yaliyojengwa juu ya Biblia na kuelekezwa kwenye Agano Jipya, ya Uamsho wa Anabaptisti wakati wa kipindi cha Matengenezo.

I. Kwa Nini Drama Inakiuka Ibada ya Kweli

a. Drama inakiuka kanuni ya kusikia.

Katika ulimwengu wa kiroho, kuona si muhimu kama kusikia (2 Wakorintho 4:18). Maneno sikia, asikiaye na alisikia yanapatikana katika Biblia zaidi ya mara 1,000. Kwa kweli, Biblia nzima ni Mungu akizungumza na mwanadamu. Anataka wanadamu wasikie! “Bwana asema hivi” ni kauli inayorudiwa mara kwa mara katika Maandiko.

Katika Mlima Sinai (Kutoka 19:9), watu walisikia ujumbe wa Mungu kupitia msemaji wake, Musa. Sauti ya Mungu iliwatisha (Kutoka 20:18-19), lakini kumsikia kulikuwa muhimu ili “wasitende dhambi.” Katika Kutoka 20, Mungu alitoa maagizo ya kina kuhusu namna ibada ilivyopaswa kufanywa. Usijifanyie miungu ya fedha pamoja nami, wala usijifanyie miungu ya dhahabu –Kutoka 20:23. Vifaa hivi vya kuona (sanamu) vilikuwa ukiukaji wa kanuni ya Mungu ya kusikia. Kishawishi cha kutengeneza sanamu huingia kupitia jicho. Madhabahu ambazo Mungu aliruhusu zilipaswa kuwa za kawaida na zisizochongwa (mistari ya 24-25). Mambo waliyoyaona hayakupaswa kuvuruga yale yaliyosikiwa kutoka madhabahuni! Kile kinachoonekana, hasa mavazi yasiyo na staha, huwa kinavuruga yale yanayosikiwa (mstari wa 26).

Mahubiri ya Yesu yalilenga kusikia: Aliye na masikio na asikie –Mathayo 13:9. Ingawa hakutumia vielelezo vya kuona kama wahubiri wanavyofanya leo, Yesu alitumia vielelezo vya maneno (mifano) kama njia ya kuelekeza watu kwenye kusikia (Mat 13:18).

Katika Mlima wa Kubadilika Sura (Mathayo 17), Petro alitaka kubuni upya uzoefu wa ibada kwa kujenga vibanda vitatu. Alitaka kitu cha kutazama! Lakini sauti kutoka mawinguni iliwafahamisha wanafunzi umuhimu wa kusikia (mstari wa 5). Ibada inayotumia vielelezo vya kuona haikubaliwi na Mungu!

Yesu alisema, Amin, amin, nawaambia, Yeye alisikiaye neno langu na kumwamini yeye aliyenituma, anao uzima wa milele … Saa inakuja, nayo sasa ipo, wafu watakapoisikia sauti ya Mwana wa Mungu, nao watakaoisikia wataishi. Yohana 5:24-25. Wokovu huja kwa kusikia Neno la Mungu, lakini ni pale tu mtu anapoamini kile alichosikia!

Paulo anauliza maswali yenye kutafakarisha: Basi wamwiteje yeye wasiyemwamini? Tena wamwaminije yeye wasiyemsikia? Tena wamsikieje pasipo mhubiri? –Warumi 10:14. Anajibu maswali yake mwenyewe: Basi imani huja kwa kusikia, na kusikia huja kwa neno la Mungu –Warumi 10:17. Kanuni ya Mungu ya kuupata wokovu ni kwa kusikia Neno la Mungu au kwa kulisoma Neno la Mungu!

Katika sura ya 2 na 3 za Ufunuo, Yesu anarudia mara saba: “Aliye na sikio na asikie.” Drama ya kidini ni ya juu juu kwa kuwa inavutia sehemu ya nafsi ya mwanadamu, si sehemu ya kiroho. Sehemu ya nafsi ya mwanadamu (hisia) inaweza kufurahia sana huku roho iliyo ndani ya mwanadamu ikibaki bila kuguswa na bila kusogezwa. Shetani hutumia jicho kumvuruga mwanadamu asishughulikie masuala halisi ya moyo wake.

Waebrania 11:6 inatuambia, “Imani ni kuwa na hakika ya mambo yatarajiwayo, ni bayana ya mambo yasiyoonekana (au kuonyeshwa).” Imani ya kweli huja moyoni mwa mwanadamu kwa kusikia, si kwa kuonyeshwa. Kwa hiyo, drama ya kidini inakaribia kuwa ya kumpinga Kristo kwa sababu inakwenda kinyume na kanuni ya Mungu ya kusikia.

b. Drama inakiuka unyoofu.

Maandiko yanafundisha umuhimu wa unyoofu katika maisha yote (1 Wakorintho 5:8; 2 Wakorintho 1:12, 2:17; Wafilipi 1:10). Ili kudumisha unyoofu wetu, ni muhimu kwa kila mtu kutambua kwamba Mungu alituumba kuwa watu binafsi wa kipekee (Zaburi 139:14-15). Sisi si mtu mwingine, wala hatuwezi kuwa mtu mwingine! Kujaribu kuwa mtu mwingine kunakiuka upekee wetu. Na mtu anapofanya hivyo, anakosa unyoofu.

Hili linahusianaje na drama ya kidini? Drama hutumia uigizaji. Yesu alikuwa na mabishano ya mara kwa mara na Mafarisayo. Walikuwa wakiigiza kila mara, au kujifanya kuwa kitu ambacho hawakuwa. Yesu aliwaita wanafiki tena na tena. Neno la awali la Kigiriki linamaanisha “muigizaji.”

Sababu pekee iliyowasukuma Mafarisayo kusali hadharani ilikuwa kutazamwa na watu (Mathayo 6:5-7). Walikuwa wakijua hadhira yao, na hivyo walijua jinsi walivyokuwa wakijionyesha. Yesu aliweka wazi kabisa kwamba ibada ya kidini ilipaswa kuwa ya faraghani, “chumbani mwako.” Mtu anayeonyesha uchaji wake anapojali zaidi namna anavyojitokeza kuliko ujumbe wake, basi haabudu tena, bali anafanya maonyesho! Hili linaweza kuwapata wahubiri, vikundi vya waimbaji wanne, kwaya, n.k. “Matembezi ya maombi” pia kwa kawaida huangukia katika kundi hili hili la kujifanya.

Mtu anapofanya uigizaji kuwa mazoea ya kawaida, anakuwa mnafiki. Anaikosea nafsi yake mwenyewe kwa sababu anadhuru upekee wake, aliopewa na Mungu.

Yesu aliwaita Mafarisayo wanafiki mara saba katika Mathayo 23. Aliwaambia kwamba walikuwa watu waliokufa huku wakitembea (Mathayo 23:27-28). Walikuwa wameigiza kwa muda mrefu sana hivi kwamba hawakujua tena tofauti kati ya ukweli na uongo!

Udanganyifu huu ni sababu mojawapo inayowafanya waigizaji wa kitaalamu kuwa wenye msimamo uliopitiliza kuhusu masuala ya maisha. Kitaalamu, wanazidi kujitenga na ukweli, unyoofu na uhalisia. Katika masuala kama vile ikolojia, haki za wanyama, utoaji mimba, haki za mashoga na ongezeko la joto duniani, wengi wao wamechukua misimamo iliyokatika na misingi ya ukweli na hawana tena unyoofu.

Kujifanya kusali au kuabudu, au kuigiza wahusika wa Biblia katika mchezo wa kuigiza, si ukosefu wa unyoofu tu, bali kunakaribia kuwa kufuru. Fikiria kujifanya Yesu katika mchezo wa kuigiza! Kujifanya Yesu ni kumkufuru Mungu kwa sababu hakuna Mkristo aliyewahi hata kukaribia ukamilifu wake! Au vipi kuhusu kujifanya kuwa Ibilisi? Kwa nini, naomba kuuliza, mtu yeyote anayefuata mafundisho ya Yesu kwa unyoofu ajitwike mfano wa uovu? A. W. Tozer anahitimisha, “Uigizaji unajumuisha mkanganyiko mkubwa wa kimaadili kwa kuwa unaifanya uongo uitumikie kweli.”

Drama ya kidini, wale wanaoshiriki humo, na kwa maana hiyo wale wanaoidhinisha unafiki uleule alioulaani Yesu, ni matapeli. Roho Mtakatifu haheshimu kujifanya na kujionyesha!

Sababu iliyofanya makutano wamfuate Yesu ni kwamba unyoofu wake ulikuwa wenye kuburudisha sana ukilinganishwa na uigizaji wa daima wa Mafarisayo.

II. Sababu za Kivitendo Zinazofanya Drama ya Kidini Kuwa Tishio

a. Drama ya kidini inadhoofisha heshima kwa Mungu.

Mtu anayejifanya kuwa Yesu Kristo au mhusika mwingine yeyote wa Biblia hudhoofisha heshima yake kwa Bwana. Mtu anapoigiza vya kutosha, kumcha Mungu hufa polepole ndani yake. Kwani, ikiwa mtu anaweza kujifanya kuwa sawa na Kristo, kuna haja gani ya kumheshimu aliye mkuu zaidi? Mafarisayo hawakutambua hata kwamba walikuwa watu waliokufa huku wakitembea (Mathayo 23:27).

b. Drama ya kidini huunganisha ibada na ulimwengu wa maonyesho ya jukwaani.

Hollywood imethibitisha wazi kwamba ulimwengu wa maonyesho ya jukwaani hauwezi kuzalisha maadili mema ya kiungu. Kumwonyesha mwanamume na mwanamke kana kwamba ni mume na mke wa kujifanya hudhoofisha utakatifu wa ndoa. Ulimwengu wa maonyesho pia huunga mkono desturi za uchumba zinazokiuka viwango vya usafi vya kibiblia. Ulimwengu wa maonyesho umekuwa ndio unaoweka viwango vya maadili katika jamii ya leo, na wengi wanafuata mfano wake usiomcha Mungu.

c. Drama ya kidini haimridhishi mtu wa ndani.

Hisia za mtu zinaposisimuliwa na maonyesho ya nje, hisia hizo huendelea kutafuta msisimko mpya na uzoefu mwingine wa ibada unaomfanya ajisikie vizuri. Hilo hujenga ndani yake hamu ya kutazama onyesho jingine ambalo linaridhisha zaidi ya lile lililotangulia. Hisia zinafurahia, lakini mtu wa ndani ana njaa na hufa polepole kwa sababu moyo na akili havijalishwa chakula chenye kiini halisi.

d. Drama ya kidini humharibu mhubiri.

Drama ni rafiki wa mhubiri mvivu. Hahitaji tena: Jitahidi kujionyesha kuwa umekubaliwa na Mungu… –2 Timotheo 2:15. Haihitaji kutiwa nguvu na Roho Mtakatifu ili kubadilisha mahubiri kwa mchezo wa kuigiza. Badala ya kuwaamuru watu wawe “nuru ya ulimwengu,” anawaamuru “tafadhali, punguzeni mwanga!” Projekta inapochukua nafasi ya nabii, njia kuu ya mwanadamu kuupata wokovu hupotea (1 Wakorintho 1:21).

“Mradi tu mhubiri aweze kutegemea burudani kama njia ya kujinasua, msukumo unaowafanya wahubiri utakosekana. Mazoea na mdundo unaohusishwa na mahubiri makuu vitakosekana katika huduma yao.” –A. W. Tozer.

Matumizi ya drama ya kidini yatamhukumu mhubiri kuwa wa kiwango cha wastani! Tishio tunalokabiliana nalo leo ni kwamba kadiri drama ya kidini inavyozidi kuongezeka, ndivyo uamsho uliotumwa kutoka mbinguni wa zamani utakavyotoweka.

e. Ibada ya kweli itaonekana kuwa duni.

Kwa kutumia drama katika ibada, makanisa yanawazoeza vijana kufikiri kwamba ibada ya kweli ni aina nyingine tu ya burudani duni. Ibada na drama vinapounganishwa kuwa kitu kimoja, ibada hushushwa hadi kiwango cha chini kabisa kinachokubalika na wote. Hatari ni kwamba kizazi kijacho hakitajua ibada ya kweli ni nini!

III. Mifumo ya Ibada ya Kweli

a. Maombi

Maombi ni mada pana, mfumo wa ibada ambao mara nyingi sana hautumiki kikamilifu. Maombi ya hadharani katika maisha ya kusanyiko hubanwa ndani ya mipaka ya muda tuliyojiwekea sisi wenyewe.

Katika kanisa la kwanza, maombi ya hadharani yalifuata mfumo thabiti katika ibada zao. Kulikuwa na maombi ya hadharani mara tu baada ya Kristo kupaa (Matendo 1:14) na wakati wa kuwekwa wakfu kwa mara ya kwanza (Matendo 1:24). Wakawa wakidumu … katika kusali –Matendo 2:42. Hakukuwa na roho ya kutojali! Mikutano ya maombi ilikuwa njia ya uinjilisti, njia ya kuleta hofu ya Mungu, na chombo kikuu cha kuliunganisha kanisa lote (Matendo 2:41-44).

Petro na Yohana walihudhuria mkutano wa maombi katikati ya alasiri (Matendo 3:1). (Hebu, mtakatifu mwenzangu, ni lini mara ya mwisho ulihudhuria mkutano wa maombi katikati ya alasiri?) Mkutano wao wa maombi ulikuwa na matokeo makubwa kama tetemeko la ardhi (Matendo 4:31)! Nguvu na uwepo wa Roho Mtakatifu katika ibada zetu huleta matokeo!

Kuhudhuria mikutano ya maombi halikuwa chaguo la mara moja kwa mwezi au mara mbili kwa mwezi (Matendo 6:4)! Petro alipokuwa gerezani, walikuwa na mnyororo wa maombi wa hiari wa saa zote (Matendo 12:5). Waliwawekea mikono wamisionari wao na kuwaombea (Matendo 13:3). Walikusanyika kando ya mto kwa mkutano wa maombi (Matendo 16:13). Tafadhali zingatia: mkusanyiko huu kando ya mto haukuwa kwa ajili ya shughuli zozote za michezo ya majini; ulikuwa mkutano wa maombi! Walikusanyika …maombi yalikuwa yamezoeleka kufanywa… –Matendo 16:13. Walielewa kwamba popote Wakristo walipokutana, kusali pamoja lilikuwa jambo la kawaida kufanya.

b. Mahubiri

Mahubiri ni mfumo wa ibada ulioanzia wakati wa Yona (Yona 3:2) na Musa (Matendo 15:21). Katika Agano la Kale, mahubiri yalikuwa mfumo wa Mungu wa kumjulisha mwanadamu mapenzi yake. Yesu alipoanza huduma yake, …[Alifika] Galilaya, akihubiri Injili ya ufalme wa Mungu –Marko 1:14. Alitumia mfumo huohuo wa ibada. Yesu alitumia mifano kama vielelezo vya maneno (si vya kuona), vilivyowavutia wasikilizaji wake.

Mwisho wa huduma yake ulipokaribia, Yesu alipanua mahubiri kuwa mfumo wa ibada kwa vizazi vijavyo na tamaduni zote za ulimwengu: …Enendeni ulimwenguni mwote, mkaihubiri Injili kwa kila kiumbe –Marko 16:15.

Wito wa Paulo ulikuwa kuhubiri Injili (1 Wakorintho 1:17-21). Mahubiri hayakupaswa kupambwa kwa werevu wa mwanadamu. Mungu alipendezwa kutumia upumbavu na usahili wa mahubiri kuwahudumia kwa wokovu wale waliothubutu kuamini. Kwa sababu hii, mahubiri yanahitaji kuwa kitovu cha kila ibada. Ibada za sifa, matamasha na maonyesho ya muziki ni wezi wa muda ambao badala yake unapaswa kutumiwa kusikiliza mahubiri yaliyoongozwa na Roho Mtakatifu. Drama ya kidini inapotumiwa kuwasilisha ukweli, hupita pembeni mwa mfumo aliouweka Mungu wa kumfikishia mwanadamu ujumbe wa wokovu.

Heri asomaye, na hao wayasikiao maneno ya unabii huu, na kuyashika yaliyoandikwa humo… –Ufunuo 1:3. Njia ya Mungu ya mawasiliano ni Neno lililoandikwa au kusemwa. Si picha! Si mchezo wa kuigiza! Si tamasha la maigizo!

c. Uimbaji

Agano Jipya halitoi dokezo lolote kuhusu waimbaji wa kitaalamu, kwaya au maonyesho ya muziki. Uimbaji wenye maana huhitaji kila mtu kushiriki, na akili kushiriki kwa ufahamu (1 Wakorintho 14:15). Muktadha unaashiria wazi kwamba ibada au uimbaji si uzoefu wa mtu mmoja tu; ni kwa ajili ya kuwajenga wote waliopo. Waimbaji wa peke yao, ambao mara nyingi hujikuza, huwazuia wasikilizaji wengine kushiriki katika ibada ya pamoja.

Neno la Kristo na likae kwa wingi ndani yenu katika hekima yote, mkifundishana na kuonyana kwa zaburi, na nyimbo, na tenzi za rohoni, huku mkiimba kwa neema mioyoni mwenu kwa Bwana –Wakolosai 3:16. Nyimbo za rohoni hugusa moyo, ilhali nyimbo za nafsi husisimua miguu na hisia. Tunaimba “kwa Bwana.” Mahubiri hutoka kwa Mungu kwenda kwa mwanadamu, lakini uimbaji hutoka kwa mwanadamu kwenda kwa Mungu, ukiwa na maneno ya sifa, kuabudu, heshima na shukrani. Uimbaji ni kwa ajili ya ibada, si burudani.

Mkisemezana kwa zaburi, nyimbo na tenzi za rohoni, mkiimba na kufanya sauti ya muziki mioyoni mwenu kwa Bwana –Waefeso 5:19. Uimbaji uliojaa Roho huleta kujengana, msukumo na kutiana moyo. Kushiriki katika uimbaji kuna namna ya kuhudumia mahitaji ya moyoni, pale njia nyingine zinaposhindwa. “Kufanya sauti ya muziki moyoni mwako” kunahusisha moyo kuandamana na uimbaji. Ala za nje za muziki huelekeza fikira kwenye uwezo wa mtu badala ya moyo. Ikiwa uimbaji wetu hauandamani na mioyo yetu, unakuwa maonyesho mengine tu ya ibada ya kifarisayo.

Ibada ya Agano la Kale ilikubalika kwa Mungu; hata hivyo, ilikuwa pia ya kaida, ikiwa na dhabihu za wanyama, kufukiza uvumba, kutumia ala za muziki na kucheza mbele za Bwana. Hata hivyo, ibada ya Agano Jipya ni tofauti kabisa. Yesu anatufundisha kwamba …imewapasa kumwabudu katika roho na kweli –Yohana 4:24. Roho ya ibada huchukua nafasi ya desturi za ibada. Tunapohama kutoka njia za ndani za ibada kwenda njia za nje, tunakiuka “roho” ya ibada ya Agano Jipya. Ibada yetu haipaswi kuchochewa na mambo ya nje, bali na Roho Mtakatifu (Waefeso 5:18).

IV. Kiini cha Ibada ya Kweli

Yesu alipokutana na mwanamke kisimani, mwanamke huyo alieleza wasiwasi wake kuhusu Yesu kubadili namna ya ibada (Yohana 4:20). Alikuwa na wasiwasi kuhusu jinsi baba zake walivyoabudu. Kwa maneno mengine, “ndivyo tulivyokuwa tukifanya siku zote!” Kila kizazi cha waabudu lazima kijilinde dhidi ya ibada ya kufuata kaida tu.

Kuna mitazamo miwili inayoathiri ibada ya kweli kwa njia isiyofaa:

  • Ya kufuata kaida –kuzoea sana namna ambavyo tumekuwa tukifanya mambo siku zote kiasi cha kuishia kufuata tu mienendo ya kawaida na kupoteza mtazamo wa Yule anayeabudiwa.
  • Ya kupuuza –kuwa mbali sana na namna yoyote ya ibada kiasi kwamba Yule anayeabudiwa anafichwa na kutojali.

Mitindo yote miwili ya ibada, ya kufuata kaida na ya kupuuza, ina tatizo moja la msingi: kukosa heshima kwa Mungu!

Baba za mwanamke kisimani walikuwa wamepoteza mtazamo na dhana ya ibada: “Ninyi mnaabudu msichokijua” (Yohana 4:22a). Yesu alionyesha wazi kwamba ibada si jambo lisilo na fikira: “Sisi tunaabudu tukijuacho” (4:22b). Ibada ya kweli ni kutumia akili na ufahamu wetu. Ibada ya kweli ina kitu cha kutoa: “Wokovu watoka kwa Yesu” (4:22c). Hubadilisha maisha!

Mahali pa ibada si muhimu kama mtazamo (Yohana 4:23). Yesu anakazia si sherehe ya nje, bali hali ya akili na roho.

Mungu ni Roho: nao wamwabuduo yeye imewapasa kumwabudu katika roho na kweli –Yohana 4:24. Zingatia neno imewapasa! Ibada pekee inayokubalika ni ile ya rohoni na kweli. Mtazamo wetu lazima ulingane na Roho wa Mungu. Ibada ya kweli pia inahusisha jinsi tunavyoitikia kweli. Ikiwa roho zetu haziitikii kweli, hatuabudu! Ikiwa akili zetu ziko kwingine, au zinafikiria jambo jingine, ibada yetu ni desturi tu isiyo na uhai na baridi!

Hitimisho

Tunapozingatia kanuni za Maandiko, ni wazi kwamba drama ya kidini si mfumo wa Mungu wa kuleta imani na uzima katika nafsi ya mwanadamu!

Mpangilio wa ibada ya kweli katika Agano Jipya ni kukusanyika ili kusikia Neno likihubiriwa; kusali pamoja na kuombeana; na kuimba nyimbo, tenzi na nyimbo za rohoni.

Kishawishi cha kuingiza mambo mapya katika ibada ni halisi sana leo. Wito wa Yesu ni kuabudu katika roho na kweli. Kila mmoja wetu anapofanya sehemu yake kwa unyoofu ili kudumisha ibada zenye maana na za kiroho, kishawishi cha kurudisha ibada ya kufuata kaida (“jinsi baba zetu walivyoabudu”) au kuanzisha ibada ya kupuuza (ibada yoyote mpya isiyo na heshima) hupungua.
